questions.title: What is the difference between MediShield Life and CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Both MediShield Life and CareShield Life are insurance plans, but they serve different purposes. They complement each other in providing lifetime protection against different types of healthcare expenses.
MediShield Life helps to pay for large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments such as dialysis and chemotherapy for cancer. Whereas CareShield Life provides cash payouts to help severely disabled individuals with their long-term care costs.

questions.title: I am covered by Employer Medical Benefits. Can I claim from MediShield Life as well? Who pays first?
questions.text:
For members who are covered under multiple schemes, the Ministry of Health has set out the following claims protocol to avoid duplicative payouts:
1. Employer, private insurance, other third party pays first
2. Followed by MediShield Life (MSHL)/Integrated Shield Plan (IP)
3. Then MediSave
4. Then Cash
MSHL/IP will pay for the portion of the bill that is not covered by employer, private insurance and other third-party payers, subject to claim limits, deductible and co-insurance. If you have filed a claim under MSHL/IP first and subsequently with a third-party payer, you or the third party payer must reimburse the relevant amount to MSHL/IP, in line with the claims protocol. The public/private healthcare institutions and the insurance industry have been informed of this claims protocol.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Who should be considered as a member of my household? What is the definition of a household?
questions.text:
Only family members related by blood, marriage and/or legal adoption, (e.g. spouse, parents, children, grandparents, grandchildren, siblings, uncles, aunts, cousins and in-laws) and who live at the same residence are considered members of your household.
Domestic helpers, unrelated landlord/tenants, fiancé/fiancee, future in-laws, godparents and friends living at the same address are not considered members of your household. Family members not living at your address are not considered members of your household for the purposes of means-testing.
To view or update the household information used to compute your Premium Subsidies, log in to the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/).
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: How do I find out what is the Annual Value of my Property?
questions.text:
The Annual Value (AV) of HDB properties generally falls below $21,000, while some lower-value private properties have AV between $21,000 and $31,000.
You can find out about the AV of your residence from IRAS e-Valuation List at a nominal fee. You may also check your property tax bill or log in to myTax.iras.gov.sg.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: How can I inform if there is a change in my address?
questions.text:
All notification letters relating to MediShield Life will be sent to the last known address on your Singapore identity card (IC), which is the official address as registered with the Singapore Government. You may update your residential address by accessing the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority of Singapore’s (ICA) change of address e-Service (https://go.gov.sg/ic-address) using your Singpass. Any updates will automatically be transmitted to all participating government organisations via the One-Stop Change of Address Reporting Service (OSCARS).
If you do not hold an identity card but wish to update your address, please write to us (medishieldlife.sg/writetous) and we will further advise you on your request.

questions.title: Where can I get help if I cannot afford my premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life premiums are fully payable by MediSave. If there are insufficient monies in the MediSave account, policyholders can top up their account with cash or their family members with sufficient MediSave balance can step in to support their premium payments.
We understand that changes in one’s household circumstances may mean that one could require additional support for their healthcare expenditure including premiums. In such instances, individuals may call the MediShield Life hotline or visit the MediShield Life e-service website (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg).
Additional Premium Support (APS) is also available for those who face difficulty paying for premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support. The Government will invite individuals with insufficient MediSave balances to apply for APS and help them with the process if they are unable to do so themselves. There is no need for individuals to apply for APS ahead of time.
If approved, APS will cover any outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums for the next two years.
Eligibility for APS is based on, but not limited to the applicants’ and his/her immediate family members’ financial means. Flexibility will be exercised for individuals who may not completely meet the criteria but need help because of extenuating circumstances.
No one will lose coverage from MediShield Life because of an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: How can I apply for Additional Premium Support to pay for my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text: Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their premiums after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support. You will be invited to apply for APS should you have insufficient MediSave, and details on the application process will be included in the invitation letter. There is no need for you to apply for APS ahead of time.

questions.title: What are IP riders and should I consider getting one?
questions.text:
IP riders are optional products designed to cover part of the deductible and co-insurance of your Integrated Shield Plan (IP). Even with a rider, patients will still need to co-pay a minimum of 5% of the claimable amount. Riders may also provide coverage for additional treatments, such as cancer drug treatments not covered under MediShield Life and IPs.
Riders premiums can only be paid in cash.
You may wish to consider the following when deciding whether to buy a rider:
Co-payment: Whether you are willing to pay more premiums to lower your co-pay in the unlikely event you incur hospital bills. If so, consider getting a rider, but do compare whether the rider premiums are worth the likely amount of co-payment they will cover.
Additional benefits: IPs and riders may cover additional treatments and services such as pre-/post-hospitalisation, emergency overseas treatments and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). Again, consider whether the additional premiums are worth the additional coverage.
Premiums: Most importantly, consider whether you can afford a rider in the long run. As you age, your premiums will increase and may strain your finances if not planned for adequately, leading to affordability issues in later years.

questions.title: I am applying for subsidy from another healthcare scheme, but was directed to approach MediShield Life. What can I do to have my means-test result reassessed so that I can be eligible for higher subsidy?
questions.text: To reassess your household and/or means information for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies and/or other selected healthcare schemes, please submit your request via the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/). We will contact you if we require further clarification on your request. Alternatively, you may wish to call the hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: What is Additional Premium Support and what are the eligibility criteria for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their premiums even after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support. This may include low-income single elderly without family support and low-income families with multiple dependants. The Government will invite these individuals to apply for APS and help them with the process if they are unable to do so themselves.
Eligibility for APS is based on, but not limited to the applicants’ and his immediate family members’ financial means. Flexibility will be exercised for individuals who may not completely meet the criteria but need help because of their financial circumstances.
No one will lose their MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) coverage due to the inability to pay premiums.

questions.title: What is the validity period for my subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: In general, your subsidy eligibility will be valid for one year. Your subsidy eligibility may be updated when there are changes to your household information, such as a new-born in your household or when you apply for / renew your status under other healthcare subsidy schemes such as the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).

questions.title: When should I review and update my household information?
questions.text:
You should review and update your household information whenever there are changes to your household (e.g. when you/your household member(s) move house and updated the NRIC address, or when there are new additions to your household).
Please submit the changes via the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg) and click “Login to access the MediShield Life e-Service”. Alternatively, you can call 1800-222-3399.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: Do I need a private Integrated Shield Plan (IP)?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are covered under MediShield Life no matter how long you live, regardless of age or health condition. MediShield Life helps to pay for large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments such as dialysis and chemotherapy for cancer. It is sized for subsidised treatment in B2/C wards of the public hospitals.
You do not need an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) if you plan to stay in B2/C wards in public hospitals which are heavily subsidised. In fact, majority of Singaporeans, even those who had bought IP, chose to stay in B2/C wards. In particular, eight in 10 seniors choose B2/C wards when they are hospitalised.
If you buy an IP but choose to stay in B2/C wards in public hospitals, you might want to reconsider whether you should pay for additional private insurance.
However, if you are firm in choosing B1/A wards in public hospitals or seeking treatment at private hospitals, you can consider getting an IP that matches your ward preference. If so, you should be prepared to pay additional premiums for the additional coverage.

questions.title: How does the Government help those who cannot afford their MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
All Singapore Residents will remain covered under MediShield Life and no one will lose coverage due to an inability to pay premiums. The Government provides Singaporeans with premium subsidies and support, such as Premium Subsidies for the lower- to middle-income, special Pioneer Generation subsidies, additional Merdeka Generation subsidies, and MediSave top-ups.
Policyholders who are unable to afford their premiums even after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support, may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support , which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years.
From 1 April 2025, enhancements will be made to several of these premium support measures to cushion the impact of premium increases. Please refer to press release for more details.

questions.title: I have my own healthcare coverage, why do I need MediShield Life? How is MediShield Life different from other insurance schemes?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are required to join MediShield Life. Under MediShield Life, Singapore Residents will receive lifelong protection for large medical bills. The Government provides support for premiums for the needy who are unable to pay. Even if you incur very large bills over your lifetime, the insurance cover will not be terminated when you get very sick.
Unlike MediShield Life, other healthcare coverage is not guaranteed for life. For example, employees with healthcare coverage from their employers may lose such coverage when they leave employment or retire. Those with other forms of private insurance (e.g., Integrated Shield Plans) may lose this coverage if they are unable to pay for premiums, and they may not be able to re-apply for coverage later or may incur exclusions if they have already developed some health conditions.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: What is the difference between CareShield Life, ElderShield, MediShield Life, CPF LIFE, ElderFund, Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) , Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS) and Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE)?
questions.text:
CareShield Life, ElderShield, MediShield Life, CPF LIFE, CHAS, HCG, PioneerDAS, ElderFund and IDAPE are schemes that help Singaporeans with different types of healthcare and retirement expenses.
CareShield Life and ElderShield are long-term care insurance schemes that will provide Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with some financial protection should one develop severe disability (i.e. unable to perform at least three or more of the six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)), especially in old age.
For CareShield Life, Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later will be automatically covered under CareShield Life on 1 October 2020, or when they turn 30, whichever is later. Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents born in 1979 or earlier can choose to join CareShield Life if they do not develop severe disability. CareShield Life insureds can receive monthly payouts for as long as they are unable to do three or more ADLs. Monthly payout is $649 in 2024 and increases annually until age 67 or when a successful claim is made, whichever is earlier.
For ElderShield, eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who had a MediSave Account when they turned 40 years old in 2019 or earlier were automatically covered under ElderShield. Depending on the plan you have, in the event of severe disability, ElderShield provides monthly cash payouts of $300 per month for up to 60 months (under ElderShield 300 plan), or $400 per month for up to 72 months (under ElderShield 400 plan).
MediShield Life is a basic healthcare insurance plan that protects all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents against large medical bills for life.
CPF LIFE is the national longevity insurance annuity scheme, which insures Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents against the risk of outliving their retirement savings. Under CPF LIFE, members will receive a monthly payout from their payout eligibility age, for as long as they live.
Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) enables all Singapore Citizens, including Pioneer Generation (PG) and Merdeka Generation (MG) cardholders, to receive subsidies for medical and/or dental care at participating General Practitioner (GP) and dental clinics. CHAS was implemented to allow CHAS cardholders to enjoy more subsidies at Specialist Outpatient Clinics (SOCs) in public hospitals when referred by CHAS-partnered clinics or polyclinics.
Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) is a monthly cash grant of $200 to support families caring for loved ones with permanent moderate disability (i.e. always require some assistance with at least three Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)) who reside in the community. The HCG can be used to defray caregiving expenses, such as the cost of eldercare and services in the community or hiring of a foreign domestic worker.
Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS) offers life-long monthly cash assistance of $100 to Pioneers with permanent moderate disability (i.e. always require some assistance with at least three ADLs). Applicants must be a Pioneer to be eligible.
Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE) offers a monthly cash assistance of up to $250 to needy elderly Singapore Citizens living in Singapore who are needy, have developed severe disability and are unable to join ElderShield when it was launched in 2002 either because they had exceeded the maximum entry age or had pre-existing disabilities.
ElderFund is a discretionary government assistance scheme providing monthly cash assistance of up to $250 to lower-income Singapore Citizens, aged 30 and above, who have developed severe disability and are not able to benefit from CareShield Life, ElderShield and Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE), and have low MediSave balances and inadequate personal savings to meet their long-term care needs.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: What is the maximum amount of premium discounts that could be redeemed?
questions.text:
Under the regular conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $1, the maximum value of cumulative Healthpoints that an individual can earn in a calendar year is worth $270.
As the MediShield Life premium discounts have a higher conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $2, the maximum value of premium discounts that could be redeemed per calendar year is $540. Please refer to this webpage for more details.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: Can I get a pro-rated refund of the premiums for my original Integrated Shield Plan (IP) if I downgrade or switch from a higher coverage plan to the Standard IP before my premium renewal date?
questions.text:
If the downgrade or switch takes place before your next premium renewal date, your insurer will provide you with a pro-rated refund of your original Integrated Shield Plan premium.
Please speak to your financial advisor to find out more about the implications of downgrading or switching insurers before making your decision. Please also highlight any medical conditions you have to your financial advisor.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Can I help my family members pay for their CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You can pay the CareShield Life premiums for your family members (i.e. spouse, parents, children, siblings or grandparents) using your MediSave.
To do so, you can visit the Change Premium Payer e-Service and log in using Singpass to complete the application.
Alternatively, you/your family member may top up to your or his/her MediSave via the Top up MediSave Account online form.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Can I opt out from MediShield Life and premium payment?
questions.text: MediShield Life is mandatory for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents. Universal lifelong coverage under MediShield Life ensures that all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents will have assurance against large healthcare bills. This is in line with our move towards a more inclusive society with stronger collective responsibility.

questions.title: Can I opt out of the upcoming enhanced benefits and increased premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is a national health insurance scheme that covers all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents for life. As coverage is mandatory, the benefits and premiums apply to all policyholders and there is no opting out of this scheme.
With rising healthcare costs and changes in the healthcare landscape, MediShield Life benefits and premiums have to be reviewed periodically and updated to ensure the scheme remains sustainable and relevant to the needs of Singaporeans.
The Government will continue to ensure that premiums are kept affordable for all Singaporeans and no one will lose coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: How can I find out if I am covered under MediShield Life or an Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text:
You are covered under MediShield Life if you are a Singaporean or Permanent Resident.
If you are covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), your premium payer will be notified by your private insurer with details about your premiums and subsidies when your IP is up for annual renewal. You will receive applicable subsidies for the MediShield Life portion of your IP, if you meet the eligibility criteria.
You can log in to visit the Healthcare dashboard (cpf.gov.sg/healthcare) 'Coverage and premium details' to check the coverage and premium information for yourself and the dependant(s) you are paying premiums for.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: How do I appeal for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: You can submit your request through the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/) or call our MediShield Life hotline at 1800-222-3399. Do note that supporting documents will be requested for assessment.

questions.title: How do I claim from MediShield Life / Integrated Shield Plan (IP) and MediSave for my medical expenses?
questions.text:
You may inform the participating medical institution(s) that you wish to make a claim from your MediShield Life or Integrated Shield Plan and use your MediSave to pay for your medical expenses. The medical institution will provide you with a copy of the Medical Claims Authorisation Form to complete. It authorises them to check how much you can utilise from your healthcare plans and submit the medical claim on your behalf.
You may use the MediSave and MediShield Life claims calculator to estimate how much you can withdraw from your MediSave and / or claim from MediShield Life.

questions.title: How do I view details of my MediShield Life claims from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
You can view the details of your MediSave withdrawals and MediShield Life claim details for past 15 months online at www.cpf.gov.sg under "Latest healthcare payments and claims".
Following are the steps to take:
(1) Login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass
(2) Proceed to “Latest healthcare payments and claims”
(3) Click on “View past 15 months”
(4) Select the hospitalisation period
(5) Click on the amount at MediSave Payment or MediShield Life/Integrated Shield Plan Payment to view the claim details.
If you would like to view the details of claims prior to the past 15 months, please submit a request to the Central Provident Fund Board via www.cpf.gov.sg/eSvc/Web/FeedbackSubscription/Index .
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: How will my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premium be affected by the MediShield Life review?
questions.text:
Your IP premium is made up of two components – the MediShield Life premium and the premium for the additional private insurance component.
Your MediShield Life premium component will increase.
Revisions to the private insurance component of your IP premium will depend on your insurer, who may make changes based on their own actuarial and commercial considerations, and after accounting for any changes in their product features, if any.

questions.title: I am a Pioneer Generation member. How much subsidies do I receive for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text:
All Pioneer Generation seniors receive special Pioneer Generation Subsidies of 40% to 60%, regardless of income or Annual Value of property. PGs also receive lifetime annual MediSave top-ups of $300 - $1,200 a year, which can be used to pay premiums. With this, PGs born in 1934 and earlier have premiums fully covered by the government, while younger PGs will have about two-thirds of premiums covered. Older PGs (born in 1939 and earlier) who have serious pre-existing conditions also receive an additional one-off annual MediSave top-up of $50-$200, from 2021 to 2025.
PGs who are unable to pay their remaining share of premiums even after the Pioneer Generation Subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support, which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years. No one will lose their MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) coverage because of an inability to pay premiums.

questions.title: What are the Additional Withdrawal Limits?
questions.text:
The Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) refer to the amount of MediSave Singapore Residents can use to pay for the additional private insurance coverage component of their Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums (see Diagram below for illustration).
The AWLs apply to all IPs and differ by age, as follows:
· $300 for those with age next birthday 40 and below;
· $600 for age next birthday 41 to 70; and
· $900 for age next birthday 71 and above

questions.title: What does it mean if I have an exclusion on the additional private insurance coverage component but not on the MediShield Life component? How do I find out what exclusion I have?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) comprise 2 components (i) the MediShield Life component, and (ii) the additional private insurance component.
As MediShield Life covers all pre-existing conditions, all IP policyholders will also enjoy MediShield Life coverage for any pre-existing conditions, even if the private insurer has imposed an exclusion for the pre-existing condition on the additional private insurance coverage component.
If you are hospitalised for the excluded condition, you will not be able to claim for coverage under the additional private insurance component under your IP, but you will be able to claim for coverage under MediShield Life.
To find out more about your specific exclusion, please contact your financial advisor or private insurer.

questions.title: What should I do if one of my household members has disallowed access to his means information for the purpose of means-testing for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
If one of your household members has decided not to allow access to his/her means information for means-testing for MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and any applicable MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life assistance measures, we will not be able to calculate the household's eligibility for MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. As such, we are unable to extend any MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and any applicable assistance measures to all members of your household.
Please discuss with your household member if you have concerns regarding his or her disclosure status. If your household member now wishes to allow access to his means information, please call our hotline at 1800-222-3399 or visit the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/) and click “login to access the MediShield Life e-Service”.

questions.title: Why can’t CareShield Life automatically reimburse long-term care costs like MediShield Life does for hospital bills?
questions.text:
Monthly cash payouts under CareShield Life will provide more flexibility for individuals with severe disability and their caregivers to decide on their desired care arrangements. This is to ensure that they are not limited to certain long-term care services to be eligible to claim.
For example, some individuals may prefer to remain in a familiar home setting and thus opt for home-based care, while others may prefer receiving care from a healthcare provider such as a nursing home.

questions.title: Can I help my family members pay for their MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Spouses, parents, children, siblings or grandchildren who have sufficient MediSave balances may help their insured family members pay their MediShield Life premiums.
Other family members like uncles, aunts, and in-laws may only help pay the premiums for the insured, if the insured’s spouse, parents, children, siblings or grandchildren do not have sufficient MediSave funds to pay for the insured’s MediShield Life premiums.
You can help your family members pay their premiums using your MediSave by submitting a Change of Payer Request (cpf.gov.sg/changepayer).

questions.title: How can Additional Premium Support help me with my MediShield Life and CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If approved, Additional Premium Support (APS) will cover your outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums as well as the premiums for the next two years.
For outstanding premiums, APS will pay the premiums and any interest incurred. Any penalty will also be waived.

questions.title: How can I participate in the programme and earn premium discount?
questions.text:
A person, who on average, does 30 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) almost daily, could earn a total of 6,000 Healthpoints in a year if he clocks these activities on his Healthy 365 app. He can then redeem these Healthpoints for $80 worth of MediShield Life premium discounts.
For residents aged 40 and above who enrol in Healthier SG and complete their first Health Plan consultation, they would be able to redeem $40 worth of MediShield Life premium discounts.
Please refer to the HPB rewards programme FAQs for more information on Healthpoints.

questions.title: How do I switch to a lower Integrated Shield Plan (IP) / terminate my existing IP?
questions.text: You can instruct your private insurer to assist you in switching or terminating your Integrated Shield Plan (IP). You will continue to be covered under MediShield Life.

questions.title: How long do I have to pay for CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If you are 59 and above when you join CareShield Life, you will have to pay premiums over 10 years.
If you are 58 and below when you join CareShield Life, you will have to pay premiums until you reach age 67 (inclusive of the year you turn age 67). Thereafter, you will no longer need to pay for CareShield Life premiums.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: How will the household monthly income per person be computed?
questions.text:
In general, annual income from work from all household members will be used.
For those who are salaried employees, their income will be based on either:
a) the average monthly income over the last available 12-month period, including bonuses, as derived by the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board ; or
b) the average monthly income from work (sum of net employment income and annual trade income before losses brought forward) assessed by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) for the latest available assessment year.
For those who are self-employed, their income will be based on either:
a) the average monthly income from work (sum of net employment income and annual trade income before losses brought forward) assessed by IRAS for the latest available assessment year; or
b) the income declared to the CPF Board or the income assumed under the CPF Legislation within the last year.
Should there be a change in your income or employment status, you may be required to submit supporting documents to reflect this change at a later date.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: I am a MG Senior and have an integrated shield plan, will I benefit from the MediShield Life subsidies?
questions.text:
Yes. Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of (i) a MediShield Life component managed by the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board and (ii) additional private insurance coverage managed by a private insurer. The IP premium comprises the MediShield Life premium and the premium for the additional private insurance coverage.
All MG seniors will benefit from the additional MG premium subsidies – for those with IPs, this will apply to the MediShield Life portion of their IP premium.

questions.title: I am a pensioner retired from the civil service. Can I opt out of MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Universal lifelong coverage under MediShield Life ensures that all Singapore Residents will have assurance against large healthcare bills. It is in line with our move to a more inclusive society with stronger collective responsibility. MediShield Life coverage is mandatory for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, including those who receive benefits from their employer. This enables all Singapore Residents to share in our national risk pool and play our part in supporting our healthcare costs.
If you are a pensioner, you will also be covered under MediShield Life. To ensure that pensioners are not worse off with the introduction of MediShield Life, the Government has been helping pensioners with their MediShield Life premiums by paying for their premiums in full or by providing 2% MediSave contribution, depending on their respective medical benefit schemes.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: I am a Pioneer Generation Member and have an Integrated Shield Plan, will I benefit from the MediShield Life subsidies?
questions.text:
Yes.
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs), are made up of (i) MediShield Life and (ii) an enhanced portion providing better benefits and/or higher coverage (in private or Class A/B1 wards in public hospitals). For those with IPs, the special Pioneer Generation MediShield Life subsidies will apply to the MediShield Life component of their IP premium.

questions.title: I am covered under CareShield Life. What is Additional Premium Support and who can qualify?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) is designed to help Singaporeans who cannot afford CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and payment by MediSave and have insufficient family support to rely on.
This is to ensure that no Singaporeans will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.
Please note that you will not be eligible for APS if you have an additional private medical insurance cover under an Integrated Shield Plan and/or Supplements under CareShield Life/ElderShield. You will also not be eligible for APS if you are paying the premiums of someone else’s Integrated Shield Plan and/or Supplements under CareShield Life/ElderShield.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: I am living at Property A (which I do not own), but I own Property B. Would I still be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: The Annual Value of the address on your NRIC will be used for the eligibility checks for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: I have received a letter from CPF Board/private insurer stating that “The Government is unable to determine the Insured’s eligibility for Premium Subsidies due to incomplete information” and I am currently residing overseas. What information should I provide to review my eligibility for Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
To be eligible for Premium Subsidies, all of the following criteria must be fulfilled:
Household average monthly income per person of $3,600 and below
Living in residences with an Annual Value of $31,000 and below
Individuals who own multiple properties will not be eligible
Should you wish to proceed with the review, please ensure that your NRIC address is updated to your overseas residential address. As you are currently residing overseas, the Government will not be able to automatically determine your eligibility without the relevant supporting documents. In general, the following contains the list of documents required to facilitate the review based on your living and financial circumstances abroad:
Overseas identification documents
Declaration of household member staying at the overseas address
Latest pay slips (for the past 12 months)
Property tax document, property valuation document OR Sales and Purchase Agreement (dated not more than 5 years ago) if you own your place of residence OR a tenancy agreement (valid for the next 6 months) if you are renting your place of residence
Declaration of number of properties owned
If you would like to proceed with the review, please submit your request through this online form and we will advise if any further information/documents are required. Alternatively, you may contact us at 1800-222-3399 if calling from Singapore / +65 6222 3399 if calling from overseas.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: If I am eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies, does this apply for the rest of my life?
questions.text: Your eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies is subject to your household monthly income per person, Annual Value (AV) of residence, multiple property ownership and citizenship. All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are generally means-tested once a year, and will continue to receive MediShield Life Premium Subsidies as long as one continues to meet the eligibility criteria. Premium Subsidies are provided to help the lower- to middle-income households with their MediShield Life premiums. Pioneer Generation subsidies and Merdeka Generation subsidies are applicable for life, regardless of income or place of residence.

questions.title: If I downgrade to an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) with lower coverage or switch insurers, will I need to go through health assessment / underwriting again?
questions.text:
You do not have to go through underwriting again if you downgrade your IP to a plan with lower coverage with the same insurer. However, you will need to undergo underwriting again if you wish to switch to a new insurer, even if the new plan is of the same or lower coverage than your original plan.
Upon the inception of your new plan under your new insurer, your original plan under your original insurer will be automatically terminated. Please note that you may hence lose coverage for existing medical conditions covered by your original plan, depending on the underwriting outcome of the new insurer, and may not be able to re-apply for your original coverage later.
Regardless of any change in your IP insurer, you will remain covered by MediShield Life without any exclusions, for life.
Please speak to your financial advisor to find out more about the implications of switching plans before making your decision. Please also highlight any medical conditions you have to your financial advisor.

questions.title: Must I reimburse my employee if their medical expenses were paid out of their MediSave or MediShield?
questions.text:
If medical costs were paid by your employee using cash, MediSave or MediShield, you must reimburse payment in the following order:
Reimburse the cash portion.
Reimburse the MediSave portion directly into your employee’s MediSave account.
Reimburse the MediShield portion directly to the MediShield insurer.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Work injury compensation

questions.title: What are the Standard Integrated Shield Plan benefits?
questions.text:
The Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) covers large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatments, with coverage targeted at the Ward B1 or equivalent level at public hospitals, and has:
- Claim limits sized to fully cover 9 out of 10 Ward B1 or equivalent bills.
- Co-payment features of claim limits, deductible and co-insurance, in line with ongoing efforts to manage healthcare costs.
For more details, you may refer to the benefit schedule of the Standard IP under “Comparison of Standard IPs (for Class B1 coverage)” at go.gov.sg/moh-compare-ip.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: What happens to the deceased member's CPF LIFE premium?
questions.text: The deceased member's CPF LIFE premium balance (if applicable) will be paid to his nominee(s) together with his CPF savings.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What if I am not able to pay for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
There are various Government subsidies available to help Singaporeans with their CareShield Life premiums. In addition, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support (APS) to help those who are unable to afford their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and have limited family support.
If you are eligible, the Government will send you an application inviting you to apply for Additional Premium Support. The Government will reach out to you to help you with the process if you are unable to make the application by yourself.
For more information on APS, please visit the MediShield Life website or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: What if I am unable to pay for my MediShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
There are various Government subsidies available to help Singaporeans with their MediShield Life premiums. In addition, there is Additional Premium Support (APS) to help those who are unable to afford their MediShield Life premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave use, and if they have limited family support.
The Government will send them application forms to apply for APS, and reach out to them to help them with the process if they are unable to make the applications by themselves.

questions.title: What is the difference between CareShield Life, ElderShield, MediShield Life, CPF LIFE, ElderFund, Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) , Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS) and Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE)?
questions.text:
CareShield Life, ElderShield, MediShield Life, CPF LIFE, CHAS, HCG, PioneerDAS, ElderFund and IDAPE are schemes that help Singaporeans with different types of healthcare and retirement expenses.
CareShield Life and ElderShield are long-term care insurance schemes that will provide Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with some financial protection should one develop severe disability (i.e. unable to perform at least three or more of the six Activities of Daily Living), especially in old age.
For CareShield Life, Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later will be automatically covered under CareShield Life on 1 October 2020, or when they turn 30, whichever is later. Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents born in 1979 or earlier can choose to join CareShield Life if they do not develop severe disability. CareShield Life insureds can receive monthly payouts for as long as they are unable to do three or more ADLs. Monthly payout is $649 in 2024 and increases annually until age 67 or when a successful claim is made, whichever is earlier.
For ElderShield, eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who had a MediSave Account when they turned 40 years old in 2019 or earlier were automatically covered under ElderShield. Depending on the plan you have, in the event of severe disability, ElderShield provides monthly cash payouts of $300 per month for up to 60 months (under ElderShield 300 plan), or $400 per month for up to 72 months (under ElderShield 400 plan).
MediShield Life is a basic healthcare insurance plan that protects all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents against large medical bills for life.
CPF LIFE is the national longevity insurance annuity scheme, which insures Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents against the risk of outliving their retirement savings. Under CPF LIFE, members will receive a monthly payout from their payout eligibility age, for as long as they live.
Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) enables all Singapore Citizens, including Pioneer Generation (PG) and Merdeka Generation (MG) cardholders, to receive subsidies for medical and/or dental care at participating General Practitioner (GP) and dental clinics. CHAS was implemented to allow CHAS cardholders to enjoy more subsidies at Specialist Outpatient Clinics (SOCs) in public hospitals when referred by CHAS-partnered clinics or polyclinics.
Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) is a monthly cash grant of $200 to support families caring for loved ones with permanent moderate disability (i.e. always require some assistance with at least three Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)) who reside in the community. The HCG can be used to defray caregiving expenses, such as the cost of eldercare and services in the community or hiring of a foreign domestic worker.
Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS) offers life-long monthly cash assistance of $100 to Pioneers with permanent moderate disability (i.e. always require some assistance with at least three ADLs). Applicants must be a Pioneer to be eligible.
Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE) offers a monthly cash assistance of up to $250 to needy elderly Singapore Citizens living in Singapore who are needy, have developed severe disability and are unable to join ElderShield when it was launched in 2002 either because they had exceeded the maximum entry age or had pre-existing disabilities.
ElderFund is a discretionary government assistance scheme providing monthly cash assistance of up to $250 to lower-income Singapore Citizens, aged 30 and above, who have developed severe disability and are not able to benefit from CareShield Life, ElderShield and Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE), and have low MediSave balances and inadequate personal savings to meet their long-term care needs.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: Why is MediShield Life covering treatments such as CTGTPs and high-cost drugs that only benefit a small number of patients?
questions.text:
CTGTPs and high-cost drugs have significant potential to treat rare diseases and conditions. However, they can be expensive. Without any financing, Singaporeans will not be able to access these potentially effective treatments.
This is where MediShield Life and risk-pooling can play a useful role. Instead of having every individual save for a CTGTP, which only some may require, MediShield Life works by collecting smaller, annual premiums from individuals, and paying out when one requires high-cost, low-incidence treatments such as CTGTPs. To ensure the scheme remains affordable and sustainable, coverage will only be extended to treatments that are assessed by MOH to be clinically and cost-effective.

questions.title: Annual Value is an assessment criterion for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies. Will there be any flexibility in premium payment for "asset-rich, cash-poor" citizens?
questions.text:
In general, Government subsidies should be targeted at those in greater need. The assessment approach for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies uses the household monthly income per person and Annual Value (AV) of homes as a way to assess the household’s means and better target these subsidies. In addition, those who own multiple properties will not be eligible for Premium Subsidies.
The household assessment process strikes a balance between being more precise in assessing applicants’ means and keeping the process simpler for applicants and administratively practical. The approach aims to provide us with a fair and objective basis to take a person's income and wealth into consideration.
Annual Value is a relevant consideration, as among those with similar income, those who live in homes with a higher AV would generally be better off than those who live in homes with a lower AV. The $31,000 AV threshold covers all HDB flats and some private properties. Similarly, Singapore Residents who own multiple properties would also have more means to pay for their premiums.
Aside from Premium Subsidies, Singapore Citizens who belong to the Pioneer Generation or Merdeka Generation are given subsidies from 40% - 60% or 5% - 10% respectively.
For Singaporeans with difficulties affording MediShield Life premiums even after the various Government subsidies, there will be Additional Premium Support available on a case-by-case basis, in line with family circumstances.
Those living in homes with higher AVs or own multiple properties will also continue to benefit from substantial healthcare subsidies e.g. at polyclinics and public hospitals. From time to time, they also receive MediSave top-ups to help them with healthcare expenses.
Overall, premiums are aimed to be both fair and progressive, with general subsidies available to all Singapore Residents and support tiered to help those in greater need.

questions.title: Are Singapore Permanent Residents eligible for suspension of premium collection?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is a compulsory, basic health insurance which helps members meet the large costs of hospitalisation at Class B2 or C wards and certain outpatient treatments in Singapore’s approved medical institutions. All Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents are required to be covered under MediShield Life. The intent of this insurance is to give all Singapore residents assurance of universal healthcare coverage, including those with pre-existing conditions, for life.
Overseas Singapore Citizens who live abroad permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore can apply for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection. Singapore Permanent Residents will not be eligible for the suspension of premium collection. Permanent Residents have applied to reside in Singapore and should continue to meet their MediShield Life obligations.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Can I cancel or terminate my MediShield Life cover?
questions.text: MediShield Life provides universal healthcare coverage to Singapore Citizens (SCs) and Permanent Residents (PRs) regardless of their pre-existing medical conditions, for life. Coverage is mandatory for SCs/PRs and cannot be cancelled or terminated. With every Singapore resident collectively supporting our healthcare costs by paying premiums and pooling our healthcare risks under MediShield Life, we can keep annual premiums affordable to support payouts for those of us who incur unexpectedly large hospital bills.

questions.title: Can I change my address to receive MediShield Life letters to one not registered under ICA/OSCARS as I am concerned of missing letters or others opening my letters?
questions.text:
MediShield Life letters are sent to your residential address registered with the Immigration Checkpoints Authority (ICA)'s One-Stop Change of Address Reporting Service (OSCARS). It is an offence for another person to wilfully open letters not addressed to them or to intentionally prevent letters from reaching the recipient under the Postal Services Act.
As part of our efforts to facilitate timelier and up-to-date notifications, you will start to receive MediShield Life notifications digitally in place of hardcopy letters from end 2021.
To receive timely notifications on MediShield Life matters, update your contact information with the following steps:
1. On the CPF homepage (cpf.gov.sg), click “Login” to log on to my cpf digital services with Singpass
2. Click the dropdown button from the top right panel and select "Account settings"
3. Select “Update” to update your contact information. An SMS or email One-Time PIN (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile number or email address for verification before the changes take effect.
You can also log in to Healthcare dashboard to check your MediShield Life premiums and subsidies.

questions.title: Can I request an extension for my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium payment if I am facing financial difficulties?
questions.text: If you are unable to pay the outstanding Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium within the given two months grace period due to financial difficulties and need more time for payment, you may request to extend the HPS premium payment deadline online. Your request is subject to approval.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I submit the MediShield Life claim directly to the Central Provident Fund Board after I have settled the bill at the medical institution?
questions.text:
All MediShield Life claims must be e-filed by medical institutions to ensure accountability and efficiency in claims processing, due to the high volume of claims involved. The Central Provident Fund Board does not accept claims submitted by patients.
The medical institution will seek your authorisation to submit your claim for you. If a payout is due, it will be made directly to the medical institution to offset your bill.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my siblings' insurance premiums for schemes such as MediShield Life, Integrated Shield Plans or ElderShield/ElderShield Supplement?
questions.text: Yes. Since 1 June 2019, members may use their MediSave to pay for their siblings' insurance premiums.

questions.title: Can I use my redeemed premium discounts for my Integrated Shield Plan premiums?
questions.text:
You can redeem MediShield Life (MSHL) premium discounts if you are covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP). Your IP premiums are made up of two components – the MSHL portion and the additional private insurance coverage. The premium discounts you redeemed will be applied to the MSHL premiums of your IP policy.
IP policyholders may check with their IP insurers if they separately offer premium discounts or rewards which incentivise healthier behaviours.

questions.title: Can the Government allow us to use more of our MediSave to pay for our Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums? Why aren’t withdrawal limits sized such that IP policyholders do not experience cash outlay for their IP premiums?
questions.text:
MediSave is designed to help with basic healthcare expenses, especially after retirement. MediSave contribution rates and withdrawal limits are set in line with this principle.
MediShield Life premiums are fully payable by MediSave, while there is a limit (the Additional Withdrawal Limit) set on the premiums for the additional private insurance component to strike a balance between helping Singapore Residents pay for IPs, which are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life, and conserving enough MediSave for basic healthcare expenses, especially in old age.

questions.title: Can we use MediSave to pay for Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and Riders?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are payable by MediSave as IPs include both a MediShield Life component and an additional, optional private insurance component that sits on top of MediShield Life. Nevertheless, the payment of IP premiums using MediSave is still subject to the MediSave Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) for the private insurance component.
MediSave savings are intended to be sufficient for basic healthcare needs. The AWLs are set to strike a balance between helping Singapore Residents pay for IPs, which are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life, and conserving enough MediSave for basic healthcare expenses, especially in old age.
Rider premiums are only payable in cash as they are not part of IPs or MediShield Life. In addition, a key feature of riders is to help reduce co-payment. Insufficient co-payment may increase the risk of over-consumption and over-servicing, which could in turn lead to escalation in healthcare costs and insurance premiums for all Singaporeans.

questions.title: Do I have to continue paying for CareShield Life premiums in the event of severe disability?
questions.text:
If you have developed severe disability and are eligible to claim under CareShield Life, you will not need to pay premiums from the time your claim application is approved. However, please note that the first premium payment is still required if you have developed severe disability in the first policy year.
Premium payment will resume if you no longer develop severe disability.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Do I have to continue paying for CareShield Life premiums in the event of severe disability?
questions.text:
If you have developed severe disability and are eligible to claim under CareShield Life, you will not need to pay premiums as long as there is no change in your disability status. However, please note that the first premium payment is still required if you have developed severe disability in the first policy year.
Premium payment will resume if you no longer have severe disability.

questions.title: Do I have to pay Additional Premium (AP) for pre-existing conditions if I have an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), and would these conditions be covered after AP is paid?
questions.text:
An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) comprises two parts, namely the MediShield Life (MSL) and the additional private insurance component. MSL is sized for B2/C wards at Government hospitals, while the additional private insurance is sized for A/B1 wards at Government hospitals and private hospitals.
The 30% Additional Premium (AP) for serious pre-existing medical conditions is only applicable to the MSL component of your IP premiums.
For the additional private insurance coverage component, it will be separately assessed by your IP insurer. Generally, private insurers exclude pre-existing medical conditions from their coverage. You should contact your IP insurer to find out more.

questions.title: How can I access the CareShield Life Premium Checker?
questions.text: You can access the CareShield Life Premium Checker after logging in via your Singpass.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premium Checker

questions.title: How can I apply for Additional Premium Support to pay for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their premiums after premium subsidies and have limited family support.
There is no need for you to apply for APS ahead of time. You will be invited to apply for APS should you have insufficient MediSave savings and limited family support to pay your premiums.
If you are subsequently assessed to be eligible for the scheme, the Government will grant APS to you to pay for your MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) premiums.
For more information on APS, please visit the MediShield Life website or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: How can I tell if I am eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies upon the completion of the means test review / How much are my premiums after the premium subsidies?
questions.text:
You may visit https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/ and log in with your SingPass to check on updates to your latest household and means information. MediShield Life means information includes Annual Value (AV) of the Property, Household Monthly Income Per Person and Multiple Property Ownership.
To determine the subsidies granted to you and your family based on your respective age groups, please refer to the MOH website. Please note that the revised subsidy will apply upon the next policy renewal.
To see your MediShield Life premiums and policy details, please refer to the CPFB’s Healthcare Dashboard.

questions.title: How can one participate in the programme to redeem premium discounts?
questions.text:
Individuals can earn Healthpoints by participating in healthy lifestyle programmes and challenges on the Healthy 365 app, such as tracking their steps, sleep and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA). For participants 40 years old and above, they can redeem these Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts at a conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $2, higher than the regular conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $1.
For instance, an individual who averages 150 minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity weekly for the entire year, could redeem almost $70 worth of discounts off his or her MediShield Life premiums.
Healthier SG enrollees who have received 3,000 Healthpoints from completing their first Health Plan consultation can also redeem these for $40 worth of MediShield Life premium discounts.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: How do I make a cash top-up for my Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text:
You can make a cash top-up for your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium via the following means:
PayNow at CPF website, or
Cash at any Singapore Post branch offices
You may wish to note that the HPS premium top-up is considered a voluntary contribution and is subject to the prevailing CPF Annual Limit.
Alternatively, your family member (that is your spouse, parent, child or sibling) who co-owns the flat with you can authorise us to use their CPF OA savings to pay your HPS premium online using their Singpass.
Find out more on how to top-up the Home Protection Scheme premium shortfall via PayNow QR.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I pay my Dependants' Protection Scheme premiums?
questions.text:
The Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) premium will be automatically deducted from your CPF savings when DPS coverage is first extended to you upon a valid CPF working contribution, and subsequently on your annual policy renewal date.
If your available CPF savings are insufficient for the full sum assured
Partial premiums will be deducted from your CPF savings, and the sum assured will be reduced proportionately (minimum sum assured is $5,000). If you wish to restore to full coverage, you will be required to make a cash top-up to the appointed insurer, Great Eastern Life (GEL). Visit GEL’s website for detailed instructions and forms.
If your available CPF savings are insufficient for the minimum sum assured
A full cash top-up to the appointed DPS insurer, GEL, will be required. Visit GEL’s website for detailed instructions and forms.
To ensure your DPS coverage is renewed in a timely manner, you may wish to consider paying your DPS premiums in cash via GIRO. To set up GIRO payments, please refer to “How do you stay covered under DPS” on GEL’s website.
For further assistance, you may contact GEL directly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How do I stop the MediShield Life premium payment for a dependant's premium?
questions.text:
To stop paying MediShield Life premiums for your dependant(s), submit a Stop Payment for MediShield Life. Your dependant(s) will take over paying his/her own premium from the next policy year.
If your child is under 21 years old, you will not be able to submit an online stop payment request unless the child has sufficient savings in his/her MediSave Account, or another family member takes over the premium payment. Parents are responsible for their children's MediShield Life premiums until they turn 21 years old. If you have been discharged from the liability of maintaining your child after your divorce, please write to us and provide the relevant court documents.
If you have questions, you can call us at 1800 222 3399 or write to us.

questions.title: How long will it take for my appeal request to be completed?
questions.text: In general, the time taken to review your request would be 20 working days upon receiving the full set of supporting documents (if any). For complex cases, more time would be required. An update would be provided to you via the MediShield Life letter sent to your email or NRIC address.

questions.title: How much can I claim from MediShield Life?
questions.text:
MediShield Life has features such as claim limits, deductible and co-insurance. As such, the amount you can claim from MediShield Life for your bill can only be finalised after the Board processes the completed claim information submitted by the medical institution.
In the meantime, you can use the MediSave and MediShield Life claims calculator to estimate the maximum amount you can withdraw from your MediSave and / or claim from MediShield Life.

questions.title: How much is the outpatient deductible? Will I need to pay more out-of-pocket for outpatient consultation?
questions.text:
The outpatient deductible is set at $500 to strike a balance between ensuring that it can sieve out smaller bills meaningfully and moderate the extent to which premiums need to increase by, whilst not overly affecting affordability for patients. It applies for all admissions on or after 1 June 2026 and is fully payable by MediSave. There should generally be no increase in out-of-pocket payable as you may use MediSave to pay for the outpatient deductible.
There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave. Nobody will be denied appropriate care due to an inability to pay.

questions.title: How will the MediShield Life premium discounts I have redeemed be used for my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Any premium discounts you redeem on the Healthy 365 app before and on your MediShield Life (MSHL) or Integrated Shield Plan (IP) renewal date will be applied to your upcoming MSHL premiums, up to the net premium payable. Premium discounts redeemed after your MSHL or IP renewal date will be used for your next policy renewal, so long as these remain valid (premium discounts are valid for one year from the date of redemption).
The premium discount will be reimbursed to you or your payer’s account after the full premium has been paid at policy renewal. You or your payer may check the reimbursement in the CPF Transaction History or contact your IP insurer directly. For information on your premium discounts, you may login to your Healthcare Dashboard.

questions.title: How will those with no income (e.g. needy, not working) be able to afford the MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums? What if they do not have enough MediSave or do not have a MediSave account?
questions.text:
The Government provides Singaporeans with premium subsidies and support, such as Premium Subsidies for the lower- to middle-income, special Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation subsidies. Those who are less well-off will qualify for higher Government subsidies to reduce their premium payment.
MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums may be paid using your MediSave. Immediate family members such as parents and spouse, can help to use their MediSave to pay for their loved ones.
Those who are still unable to afford their MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave, and have limited family support, may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS), which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years
From 1 April 2025, enhancements will be made to several of these premium support measures to cushion the impact of premium increases. Please refer to press release for more details.
No one will lose their MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) coverage because of an inability to pay premiums.

questions.title: I already have an Integrated Shield Plan. How is MediShield Life relevant to me?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) comprise 2 components (i) the MediShield Life component, and (ii) the additional private insurance component that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays.
If you have an IP, you already have MediShield Life, as MediShield Life is a component of your IP.
MediShield Life will cover all pre-existing conditions, even if they are excluded by your private insurer from the additional private insurance coverage of your IP. Should you decide to terminate your IP one day, you will remain covered by MediShield Life.

questions.title: I am currently receiving Additional Premium Support (APS) for MediShield Life coverage, will I also receive APS for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
When approved, Additional Premium Support (APS) will cover MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) premiums for the next two years.
Please note that you will not be eligible for APS if you have an additional private medical insurance cover under an Integrated Shield Plan and/or Supplements under ElderShield/CareShield Life.

questions.title: I am or my household is overseas but have a local NRIC address, should I inform Ministry of Health?
questions.text:
The Ministry of Health (MOH) will assess you and your household members' subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies based on your residential address as reflected on your NRIC.
Please note that if you/your household member has confirmed with MOH as being overseas, MOH will not be able to automatically determine your/your household member’s eligibility for the Premium Subsidies under MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life, as they do not have the relevant information about the Annual Value (AV) of your overseas residence and income abroad. Overseas Singaporeans could submit sufficient documentation to MOH to assess their eligibility for the Premium Subsidies prior to the applicable policy year. Please submit your request through this online form or call our hotline at 1800-222-3399 if calling from Singapore / +65 6222 3399 if calling from overseas for more information.
If you / your family member is overseas for studies or will be returning soon, you may wish to retain him as part of your household. There is no need to inform MOH that you / your family member is overseas.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: I am uncomfortable with my personal information being accessed. Can I choose not to participate in means-testing for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
Yes, you may choose not to allow the Ministry of Health to access your means information, for example, income for means-testing.
If you chose not to allow access to your means information, you and your entire household will not receive any MediShield Life Premium Subsidies as there is insufficient information for us to calculate the subsidies to be given.
Your household will still be covered by MediShield Life.

questions.title: I currently have an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) that covers me for Class A wards / Private Hospitals, but the premiums are getting more expensive especially as I get older. Should I switch to the Standard IP?
questions.text:
If you are concerned with being able to afford the premiums of your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) as you get older, you can consider switching to a more affordable IP, including the Standard IP. If you wish to drop your IP altogether, you will remain covered under MediShield Life.
When switching IPs, you should take into consideration factors such as your preferred ward class and affordability of premiums over the long-term. You can refer to a comparison of IP benefits and premiums at this link.
You may also wish to speak to your financial advisor who will be able to advise on your options.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: I had previously disallowed access to my financial information for the purpose of CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility checks. How do I change this arrangement?
questions.text: If you decide to allow access to your financial information for the purpose of CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility checks, please visit here and click "login to access your household information". If you need further assistance, please call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 (after selecting your preferred language, press 3, and then 2).

questions.title: I have just obtained my Singapore Permanent Resident status. When is the start date of my MediShield Life cover?
questions.text: Your MediShield Life cover will commence on the date that Immigration Checkpoints Authority (ICA) grants you your Permanent Residency status.

questions.title: I have redeemed Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discount but the full MediShield Life premium was still deducted from my payer’s MediSave Account. Why was the discount not applied before premium deduction?
questions.text:
Your premium payer will receive the redeemed premium discount as a reimbursement to their MediSave Account on the same day after the full premium is deducted. The net premium amount paid is the same regardless whether the discount is applied before or after premium deduction.
Your premium payer may check the reimbursement after premium deduction in his/her CPF Transaction History or contact your Integrated Shield Plan insurer directly if needed. You may also view your premium discount information in your Healthcare Dashboard.
For more information on MediShield Life premium discount, please refer to the detailed step-by-step guide under Section 5.

questions.title: If I have appealed for higher subsidies or against the Additional Premium imposed, how will I know if my appeal is successful? Will this be reflected in my Premium Notice Letter?
questions.text:
The premium and subsidies information reflected in your Premium Notice Letter is only accurate as of the date stated in the letter.
If you have appealed, you will receive a letter informing you of the outcome of your appeal.
If there are changes to the premium payable for MediShield Life premiums arising from the change in your subsidy status, you will receive a follow-up letter informing you about the change in premiums.
To check on the status of your appeal, you can write to us (medishieldlife.sg/writetous) or call the MediShield Life hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: If my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved and I decide to renounce my Singapore Citizenship in the future, is any action required on my part to cancel my MediShield Life coverage?
questions.text: No further action is required from you. Your MediShield Life coverage will cease when you renounce your citizenship. The Central Provident Fund Board will automatically be updated about the change in your citizenship status. You will not receive any further notifications on MediShield Life coverage.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: If there are insufficient funds in my MediSave account, can I use my Ordinary Account/Special Account monies to pay for my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The savings in a member's various CPF accounts are for specific uses. Savings in the Ordinary Account and Special Account are primarily for housing and retirement while the savings in the MediSave Account are for payment of MediShield Life premium and medical expenses.
Generally, funds in the accounts are not inter-transferable. Therefore, it is not possible for your Ordinary Account/Special Account to be used for payment of MediShield Life premiums.

questions.title: Many Singapore Residents, especially the elderly, do not receive any payout for their bills, due to the deductible. Why must there be a deductible?
questions.text:
The deductible filters out smaller bills that can be adequately covered via MediSave, and focuses MediShield Life coverage on larger, bills where protection is most critical. This keeps premiums affordable for all policyholders. By avoiding first-dollar coverage, the deductible also encourages prudent use of healthcare.
The deductible can be covered by MediSave. The Government provides MediSave top-ups for the lower-income and elderly Singaporeans through schemes such as Workfare, GST Voucher scheme, and Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation Packages. For those who are unable to afford their healthcare bills after subsidies and MediSave, MediFund assistance is available at public hospitals.
From 1 April 2025, the inpatient deductible will be increased. MediSave withdrawal limits will be raised to help Singaporeans offset the increase in deductible, while the Ward C deductible increase will be phased in gradually. Please refer to the press release for more details.
topics: MediShield Life / Benefits Under Medishield Life

questions.title: The review of my eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies has been completed. Will the updated subsidies be automatically applied to my latest MediShield Life policy or at public healthcare institutions?
questions.text:
The updated Premium Subsidies (if any) will be applied at your next policy renewal date, after the completion of your latest MediShield Life Premium Subsidies’ review. To see your MediShield Life premiums and policy details, please refer to the CPFB’s Healthcare Dashboard.
For more information on other healthcare schemes’ subsidies, please contact your service provider for further advice on this matter, or visit this link.

questions.title: To receive Premium Subsidies, why is the household monthly income per person criteria set at $3,600 (Applicable for Renewals From 1 October 2024)? Does this mean if I earn above $3,600, I am considered high income and cannot receive any Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
The $3,600 figure refers to the household monthly income per person, which is based on the total income earned by a family staying in the same residential address, divided by the number of members of that family.
So, if the total income earned by family members is $14,000, and there are four members in the family, then the household monthly income per person is $3,500, and the family would qualify for subsidies.
This is a fairer way of calculating the need for subsidies, because a family with more members may need more support, even if the total income they make is quite high.
Families in a lower household income category will get a higher subsidy rate. In this way, more help is given to those who have less resources, in line with being a compassionate and inclusive society.

questions.title: What are the new outpatient treatments that will be covered by MediShield Life?
questions.text:
MediShield Life has expanded coverage to more outpatient treatments to support the shift in healthcare delivery from hospitals to outpatient and home settings.
For instance, MediShield Life will cover Outpatient Parenteral Antibiotic Therapy which enables patients to receive antibiotic treatment intravenously in the outpatient setting, thereby avoiding prolonged hospital stays.
Home Ventilation and Respiratory Support Service will also be covered to provide patients with breathing insufficiency mechanical assisted ventilation in the comfort of their own home.
