questions.title: What are the options for me if I am the 1 in 10 whose subsidised bill is not fully covered by MediShield Life and MediSave?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is designed to fully cover nine in ten subsidised bills, with the deductible and co-insurance covered by MediSave. This strikes a balance between protecting Singaporeans against the vast majority of healthcare bills, while keeping premiums affordable.
Singaporeans can be assured that more people will see their subsidised bills fully covered by MediShield Life and MediSave. For the minority of patients whose subsidised bills exceed the claim limit, they will still receive payouts from MediShield Life up to the relevant claim limit. Those who have difficulty affording their bills after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave can also apply for financial assistance such as MediFund, or appeal to MOH for MediSave use beyond limits.

questions.title: What happens to the CPF interest earned on my CPF LIFE premium?
questions.text: Your CPF LIFE premium will continue to earn CPF interest rates, which is factored into your monthly payouts to increase the amount you receive, compared to if there were no interests earned. These payouts continue for life, even after your initial premium is exhausted, ensuring lifelong financial security in retirement.

questions.title: What is premium loading for Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text: Premium loading means additional premium is charged on top of the standard premium to provide insurance coverage for pre-existing medical conditions, given the higher likelihood of claims.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What should I consider when I purchase or review my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) coverage with my insurer?
questions.text:
Buying and maintaining an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is a significant lifetime financial commitment. The degree of protection you need evolves and changes with your circumstances and age. As you reach your retirement years, your earning power is likely to reduce while your premiums will rise sharply and your priorities may shift. Depending on your hospital/ ward preferences, you may not want to pay additional premiums for an IP. You should consider the following carefully:
Are you likely to choose to seek treatment or be hospitalised at a public or private hospital?
If you intend to go to a public hospital, will you choose a B2/C ward (six to eight beds) or Standard B1 ward (four beds) or A ward (single bed), taking into account affordability?
If you intend to stay in B2/C wards, you need not buy an IP. This is because MediShield Life is generally sufficient as payouts are pegged to B2/C wards after government subsidies. The deductible and co-insurance can be paid via MediSave, as well as any remaining co-payment subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits.
If you prefer to go to a private hospital, assess your means and ability to pay the additional premiums throughout your lifetime. Your annual premiums will increase sharply with age, which means that your premiums will be much higher in your retirement years. Based on the median premiums for each IP plan type, you can potentially save a significant sum.
You may also refer to the checklist when reviewing your IP coverage.
Did You Know? Your private medical insurance premiums could be ~5 times of your MediShield Life premiums for someone in their 70/80s. Click this link to find out more.

questions.title: What should I do if I want to avoid/remove such duplication between MediShield Life and health insurance plans that are not Integrated Shield Plans?
questions.text:
You may wish to consider avoiding/removing such duplication by taking up an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), which comprises a MediShield Life component and an additional private insurance coverage component.
Unlike MediShield Life which provides coverage for policyholders with pre-existing conditions, you may be subject to exclusions by private insurers. You may wish to speak to your financial advisor who will be able to share more about your options.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: What should I do if my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved and I later decide to relocate back to Singapore?
questions.text:
Suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is only for those who live outside Singapore permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore.
Please inform the Central Provident Fund Board once you have relocated back to Singapore. Your suspension of premium collection will cease and the accumulated sum of premiums suspended from collection, with compound interest, will be payable.
Should you face any concerns with the affordability of premiums, you may apply to be assessed for financial assistance with your premiums. We will consider requests on a case by case basis.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: What will happen to the MediShield Life or Integrated Shield Plan premiums I paid when I renounce my Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Resident status?
questions.text:
Should you renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status and are only insured under MediShield Life, your MediShield Life cover will cease. The annual premium that you have paid will be pro-rated and the amount for the period after your renouncement date will be refunded to the MediSave Account of the premium payer.
If you are insured under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), please inform your private insurer if you have plans to renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status so that your insurer can advise you on the available coverage options and explain what will happen to the premiums you have paid. If you wish to terminate your IP, you will also need to notify your private insurer in a manner as required by your insurer.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: When will my MediShield Life coverage cease?
questions.text:
Your MediShield Life cover will be terminated when you pass away or renounce your Singapore citizenship/Permanent Residency. Premiums for the unused period will be refunded to the premium payer’s MediSave Account.
The payer may view the refunded premium (if any) at Transaction history statement under “Contributions / Government Cash Grant / Government Top-up".

questions.title: When will the changes to MediShield Life benefits / increased premiums take effect?
questions.text:
The changes to MediShield Life benefits will be implemented progressively from 1 April 2025.
Premiums will be adjusted from 1 April 2025 onwards upon policy renewal or inception. To cushion the premium increases, it will be phased in evenly over these three years. This will be effected through the Phased Support which is provided to all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents for two years. It is applied to the net premium increase between the new MediShield Life premium and the premium before 1 April 2025 (after any applicable Premium Subsidies, Pioneer Generation Subsidies, or Merdeka Generation Subsidies).
The Government will also provide additional support measures, which include increase in premium subsidies, additional Medisave top-ups and expansion of Additional Premium Support. Please refer to the MediShield Life 2024 Review press release for more details.

questions.title: Where can I get help if I cannot afford my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The Government provides means-tested premium subsidies targeted at the lower- and middle-income individuals.
Policyholders’ loved ones may also help with premium payment for policyholders through their MediSave or by topping up to the MediSave accounts of their loved ones.
For those who are unable to pay for their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and family support, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support, so that no one loses CareShield Life coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: Why am I receiving subsidies even though I have withdrawn from the eligibility check for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
There are different types of MediShield Life premium subsidies.
The eligibility check process was used to determine eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies for lower- to middle-income Singapore Residents.
If you did not participate in the eligibility check, the Government will still compute the MediShield Life Premium Subsidies for your household. However, it will be based on existing information in Government records, which may not be up-to-date. For individuals who miss the date to confirm their household information and wish to make changes, please call 1800-222-3399 for further assistance.
Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation Subsidies are given based on your Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation statuses, and are applied automatically to your MediShield Life premium.

questions.title: Why are the CareShield Life premiums collected so high?
questions.text:
CareShield Life premiums are calculated such that each age cohort of insureds pay sufficient premiums to support their expected payouts as a cohort. This ensures the long-term sustainability of the insurance fund.
While CareShield Life insureds are younger, premiums collected are naturally more than payouts in that year due to fewer claims. However, the premiums collected will be carried over to support the payouts in the event of severe disability in the future.
Going forward, an independent CareShield Life Council will regularly review factors like changes in claims experience and longevity and advise the Government on premium adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. The Government will consider affordability of premiums when reviewing the Council’s advice on premium adjustments.
CareShield Life is managed by the Government on a not-for-profit basis. Any excess premiums will be used to benefit insureds and there are legal safeguards to ensure the Government cannot divert CareShield Life and ElderShield Insurance Fund monies for non-prescribed uses.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Why did I receive the Additional Premium Support invitation letter (Ref: APCINV)?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support.
As you have outstanding MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life premiums, the letter was sent to invite you to apply for APS if you wish to. Alternatively, you may top up your MediSave Account to pay your outstanding premiums. Family members can also help pay for your premiums using their MediSave.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: Why do I have to pay MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life provides universal coverage to Singapore residents for life, regardless of their pre-existing health condition. Members uphold their collective responsibility by paying their premiums on time to ensure that MediShield Life is able to meet its commitments and pay out claims to its members.
Defaults on premium payment will translate to bad debts to the MediShield Life Fund and result in higher premiums for all.

questions.title: Why does the Health Insurance Planner not display all benefits in the Integrated Shield Plan (IP) comparison?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner focuses on the most commonly used benefits to make comparisons simpler and more user-friendly. For a complete comparison of all Integrated Shield Plan (IP) benefits across insurers, please visit Ministry of Health (MOH)'s website.
The list of key benefits are:
Inpatient benefits
Daily ward and treatment charges (Normal ward)
Daily ward and treatment charges (ICU)
Outpatient benefits
Cancer drug treatment
Cancer drug services
Kidney dialysis
Pre-hospitalisation
Post-hospitalisation
Co-payment and other features
Deductible
Co-insurance
Pro-ration factors
Pre-authorisation
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why have my Integrated Shield Plan premiums increased?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of 2 components (i) the MediShield Life component, and (ii) the additional private insurance component that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays. The overall IP premium may be affected by both changes in the MediShield Life premiums and premiums for the additional private insurance component.
The Ministry of Health sets the premiums for the MediShield Life component, and provides subsidies to keep MediShield Life premiums affordable.
Premiums for the additional private insurance component of IPs are set, reviewed and adjusted by insurers based on commercial and actuarial considerations. Insurers may adjust premiums upwards or downwards taking into account their claims experience, medical inflation and their own product changes if any. Insurers have an incentive to keep premiums competitive, to attract and retain policyholders. Singaporeans concerned with the affordability of IP premiums may wish to consider switching to more affordable insurance options, in line with their preferences for hospitalisation coverage.

questions.title: Why is my CareShield Life premiums payable until age 67?
questions.text:
Starting the CareShield Life premium payment duration at age 30, and ending at age 67 gives you a longer period to spread your premium payments, hence reducing the annual premiums payable.
The age at which premium payments end may be subsequently reviewed to take into consideration the changes in the re-employment age.

questions.title: Why is the MediShield Life claim limit for a particular combination treatment not the sum of all the claim limits for individual cancer drugs in that combination?
questions.text:
If a particular combination treatment is cost-effective, the MediShield Life (MSHL) claim limit is sized to be sufficient to cover the post-subsidy cost of the entire combination in Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs). In some cases, the claim limit for the entire combination is the same as the highest-cost drug in that combination because the cost of the other drugs in the PHIs are low and can therefore be adequately covered by the same claim limit.
If a particular combination treatment is not cost-effective, the MSHL claim limit is pegged to the highest individual claim limit of the drugs in the combination. Doctors and patients are encouraged to use treatments that have been assessed to be cost-effective, for which MSHL claim limits have been sized for.

questions.title: Will I be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies if I earn more than $3,600?
questions.text:
The $3,600 figure refers to the household monthly income per person, which is based on the total income earned by a family staying in the same residential address, divided by the number of members of that family.
If the total income earned by family members is $14,000, and there are four members in the family, then the household monthly income per person is $3,500, and the family would qualify for subsidies.
Up to two-thirds of the population would qualify for Premium Subsidies. This is a fairer way of calculating the need for subsidies, because a family with more members may need more support, even if the total income they make is quite high. This is because the amount they can spend on each family member will be lower if there are more family members.
Families in a lower household income category will get a higher subsidy rate. In this way, we give more help to those who have less resources and need more help. This is part of being a compassionate and inclusive society.

questions.title: Will I receive subsidies even though I am insured under an Integrated Shield Plan? Do I have to downgrade my insurance plan to MediShield Life to receive subsidies?
questions.text:
You will still be able to receive the applicable MediShield Life subsidies (i.e. Premium Subsidies for lower- to middle-income; Pioneer Generation Subsidies; Merderka Generation Subsidies) if you meet the eligibility criteria, even if you are insured under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP). You do not have to downgrade your plan to receive the subsidies.
For IP policyholders who meet the eligibility criteria for the various subsidies, the subsidies will be applied on the MediShield Life component of their IPs.

questions.title: Will my information which was obtained to check for my eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies be shared with other Government public assistance schemes?
questions.text:
Yes, sharing the subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies will help Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents benefit from other Government assistance schemes easily. However, detailed means and medical information will not be shared beyond MediShield Life, in order to protect the confidentiality of the information.
If you prefer not to share your subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies with other Government public assistance schemes, you can exercise this option via the MediShield Life e-service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/). Alternatively, please call 1800-222-3399 for further assistance.
Do note that if you exercise this option, you may need to re-submit separate applications and/or means information for such schemes in future. This will however, not affect your household’s eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies, unless you and/or your household members have also chosen not to allow MOH access to your means information for the eligibility check for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies.

questions.title: Will the Government make any future changes to the Standard Integrated Shield Plan benefits?
questions.text:
The Ministry of Health will review the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) benefits from time to time to ensure that the benefits remain relevant to policyholders.
Any changes to the Standard IP benefits will apply across all insurers.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: With the introduction of MediShield Life, should I continue to stay on my Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is a basic scheme designed to cover subsidised bills such as Ward B2/C stays.
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are private plans that provide additional private insurance coverage on top of MediShield Life to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays.
We advise you to buy a plan that meets your needs taking into consideration your preferred ward class and affordability of premiums over the long-term.

questions.title: Would changes to my income be taken into consideration immediately for means-testing?
questions.text:
Your income will only be assessed when your subsidy eligibility is due for an update. This will happen nearing the end of the 1 year validity period, and will take into account the latest available 12 months information based on Government records.
If there are changes to your household financial circumstances that you would want us to use before your subsidy eligibility is due for an update, please submit your request through the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg) for a re-assessment of your household’s subsidy eligibility.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: Am I eligible for Additional Premium Support if I have an Integrated Shield Plan and/or active-paying ElderShield/CareShield Life Supplement?
questions.text:
If you were approved for Additional Premium Support (APS) before CareShield Life (CSHL) implementation and have purchased an active-paying ElderShield (ESH) supplement, you will continue to receive APS for premiums for the two years after the approval. However, your APS will cease immediately if you purchase an Integrated Shield Plan (IP).
If you purchase an active-paying ESH / CSHL Supplement after CSHL implementation, you will not be eligible for APS. This is to ensure that APS is targeted at members who are needy and have financial difficulties.
Should you have difficulty paying the premiums for your IP or active-paying ESH/ CSHL Supplement, you may wish to approach your financial advisor to review your health insurance coverage based on your care preferences and long-term affordability of the plans.

questions.title: An individual can also save for his future premiums through his own MediSave account. Why do we opt for this mechanism where monies that are paid ahead are pooled?
questions.text:
Paying ahead for insurance premiums is a more inclusive and collective approach to boost the support for each generation’s future old-age premiums. Under this approach, everyone pools some monies during working ages which are set aside to help support the old-age premiums of those of the same generation. Doing so gives policyholders a pool of pre-paid premiums to tap on in future, to cushion the impact of future increases during the retirement years.
In contrast, while MediSave is useful to help with healthcare costs, including insurance premiums, there are also many competing demands for it such as hospitalisation bills and outpatient treatment for chronic diseases, which all add to pressure on MediSave balances.
topics: MediShield Life / Pre-funding under MediShield Life

questions.title: Apart from the Internet Reimbursement service, are there other ways to submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements?
questions.text:
To support our go green program and the Smart Nation initiative, we only accept reimbursements via our Internet Reimbursement (IR) service.
If you encounter any difficulties while submitting reimbursements via this IR service, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Are checks conducted for new Singapore Residents who are automatically covered under MediShield Life?
questions.text:
For new Singapore Residents who are automatically covered under MediShield Life, we implement a range of checks, including reviewing medical records after they are covered. They are also required to declare their health status upon receipt of the In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter from the Immigrated & Checkpoint Authority of Singapore (ICA). A copy of the form can be found by using this link (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/health-declaration-pr-applicants)
If they are identified to have serious pre-existing conditions, they will be subject to the 30% Additional Premiums for 10 years. Those who make false health declarations will be guilty of an offence under the MediShield Life Scheme Act and will be liable to pay penalties.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: Are Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders which are closed to new business included in the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
If you currently have a closed Integrated Shield Plan (IP) or rider, you can select it in the "Current Plan" section and compare it with other available options.
However, if you are not already covered under a closed plan, these plans will not appear in the IP comparison since they are not open to new subscribers.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Are subsidies applicable to the 30% Additional Premiums for those with serious pre-existing conditions?
questions.text: Yes, all subsidies are applicable to the 30% Additional Premiums for those with serious pre-existing conditions. This includes the Premium Subsidies for the lower- to middle income, Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation subsidies for Singapore Citizens. For Singaporeans who are not able to afford their premiums even after subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support, which will also be applicable to the Additional Premiums.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: Are the increases in CareShield Life payouts and premiums fixed at 2% annually?
questions.text:
To provide greater assurance to Singaporeans, for the first five years of scheme implementation, payouts and premiums* will both increase by 2% per year.
*2% increase of premiums per year excludes GST.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Are the MediShield Life Fund’s liabilities necessary? Why is there a need to set aside liabilities for recurring claims when premiums are paid annually?
questions.text:
The MediShield Life Fund is designed to be self-sustaining based on sound actuarial principles. Premiums are collected to cover current and future payouts, including amounts set aside to support future commitments. These commitments are largely made up of premium rebates that will be paid out in future to keep premiums affordable for Singaporeans in old age. They also include expected payouts for patients who have started on multi-year treatments (e.g. dialysis and chemotherapy), to provide them assurance that they will be covered for as long as they require their treatments.
The liabilities associated with these current and future claim commitments are computed by external actuarial experts in accordance with requirements set by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and are in line with industry standards.

questions.title: Are there any charges for the MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service?
questions.text: The MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service is provided free of charge.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Are those insured with Integrated Shield Plans eligible for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans automatically include a MediShield Life component. You will have to pay the premium (inclusive of the MediShield Life component) to retain your Integrated Shield Plan coverage.
As coverage for Integrated Shield Plans are designed for local treatment, please consider if you wish to retain your Integrated Shield Plan if you are planning to move overseas permanently.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: As I am covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), why are there two transactions made in my Yearly CPF Statement of Account?
questions.text:
An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is made up of two components, namely:
1. The MediShield Life component – reflected as MSL, and
2. The additional private medical insurance component – reflected as PMI.
Hence, there would be two transactions reflected for any deduction/refund of IP.

questions.title: Can a patient claim for cancer drug services from the Cancer Drug Services limit if he is receiving a treatment that is not on the Cancer Drug List?
questions.text: Yes, patients may claim for cancer drug services from the annual Cancer Drug Services limit even if the service was rendered for a cancer treatment not on the Cancer Drug List (CDL) (i.e. the claim limit is not specific to treatments on the CDL).

questions.title: Can I change the bank account to pay for my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: Yes. You will need to submit a new GIRO application with the new bank account details. The new application will generally be processed within 21 working days. We will continue to deduct your healthcare premiums from the current bank account until the new GIRO application is approved.

questions.title: Can I choose to port my previous Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover to my new flat instead of taking up a new HPS cover with premium loading?
questions.text:
Yes, you can decline the offer for a new Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover with premium loading if it does not suit your needs. We will then consider porting your existing HPS coverage (remaining sum assured and term of loan) to your new flat, subject to eligibility conditions.
Find out how you can qualify for porting your previous HPS cover:
How do I qualify for the porting of my previous Home Protection Scheme cover to my new property?
Alternatively, you may also consider applying for insurance coverage from private insurers.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I choose to switch to Annual Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS) if I am currently insured under the Single Premium HPS?
questions.text: If you are currently insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS), you cannot choose to switch to the Annual Premium HPS. The Annual Premium HPS is only applicable to those who joined HPS on or after 1 March 2001.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I claim tax relief for the top-up to my MediSave to pay for CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: Top-ups to MediSave to pay CareShield Life premiums are generally treated as voluntary top-ups and those who are eligible may enjoy tax relief. These top-ups can also be used to offset MediSave liability for Self-Employed Persons.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Can I continue to use my Ordinary Account savings to service my regular premium insurance bought before 1 January 2001, even if my balance falls below $20,000?
questions.text: You can continue to service the future premiums using your Ordinary Account savings, even if your balance falls below $20,000. This applies to you even after age 55 as long as you have set aside the Full Retirement Sum or the Basic Retirement Sum with sufficient property charge/pledge in the Retirement Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I enjoy tax relief for topping up my MediSave Account to pay my MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
Top-ups to MediSave Account to pay MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums are considered voluntary contributions.
Eligible members will enjoy tax relief for these top-ups. You can refer to the IRAS website for details on the eligibility criteria and amount of tax relief for voluntary MediSave contributions.

questions.title: Can I fully pay for the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums using MediSave at all ages?
questions.text:
Based on the current Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) for MediSave use and the current Standard IP premiums across insurers (as of Apr 2024), you can use MediSave to fully pay for the Standard IP premiums until age next birthday 74.
As the Standard IP is a private product that provides additional coverage at the Ward B1 or equivalent level, premiums are higher than MediShield Life premiums. As such, there will still be some cash outlay for older policyholders.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Can I help my family members pay for their ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
You can pay the ElderShield premiums for your family members (i.e. spouse, parents, children, siblings or grandparents) using your MediSave.
To do so, you can visit the Change Premium Payer e-Service and log in using Singpass to complete the application.
Alternatively, you/your family member may top up to your or his/her MediSave via the Top up MediSave Account online form.

questions.title: Can I increase or decrease the premiums to be paid for my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policies?
questions.text:
Academic Staff Provident Fund (ASPF) members are not allowed to make any changes to their Part V insurance policies that will cause an increase in premiums with effect from 28 December 2006 (i.e. the date that National University Singapore issued the official "Dissolution Notice" to all its members). However, if the increase in premiums is due to attained age at renewal of the policies1, or conversion of the policies2, you can use your CPF monies to pay the higher premium.
ASPF members can make any changes to their Part V insurance policies that will result in a decrease in premiums, as long as the insurance companies allow it.
1 When a member exceeds a certain age, he may have to pay a higher premium to renew his insurance policy. In such an instance, he can continue to use his CPF monies to pay the higher premiums.
2 A member's insurance policy contract may allow him to convert: (1) a rider to a new whole life policy, endowment policy or investment-linked insurance product (ILP); or (2) a whole life policy to an endowment policy or vice versa.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I insure my dependent under Integrated Shield Plan (IP), but insure myself under MediShield Life and vice-versa?
questions.text: Yes, you can choose to cover yourself under MediShield Life and get Integrated Shield Plan (IP) from different private insurers for your dependents, or vice versa.

questions.title: Can I pay for CareShield Life premiums using GIRO?
questions.text: Currently, CareShield Life premiums can only be paid via MediSave. You can pay for your premiums from your own MediSave, or your family members may pay for your premiums using their MediSave.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Can I pay my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium by instalments?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme premiums cannot be paid by instalments. The premium is structured to be paid in full at the beginning of each policy year so that the scheme remains viable and the premiums kept affordable for all insured members.
You can find out more on the available payment options.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I pay my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums by instalment through GIRO?
questions.text:
You can pay your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums by monthly GIRO instalments if you have outstanding premiums (excluding renewal premiums). The monthly deductions will be made from your bank account on the 15th of the month (or the next working day if 15th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday).
For MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life renewal premiums, there is no instalment option. The premiums will be deducted from your bank account every year, within a month after the cover is renewed.
Please maintain enough balance in your GIRO bank account. If you have set a payment limit on GIRO deductions, please ensure that the limit takes into account the total premium amount to be deducted. Note that some banks may charge administrative fees for unsuccessful deductions.
Please refer to the following FAQs for guidance on applying for GIRO to pay for your/your dependants' MediShield Life, CareShield Life, and ElderShield premiums:
How do I apply for GIRO for my/my dependant's MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?

questions.title: Can I purchase a regular premium insurance policy under CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: With effect from 1 January 2001, CPF savings cannot be used for new regular premium insurance policies. Only Single Premium or Recurring Single Premium insurance policy is allowed under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account and CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds in cash for a medical bill paid using their MediSave and/or MediShield Life?
questions.text: You cannot reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds in cash if the medical bill was paid using their MediSave and/or MediShield Life. The reimbursement for the utilised amount must be made directly to the employees, platform workers or insureds’ MediSave and/or MediShield Life.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Can I reserve monies in my CPF Ordinary Account to pay the annual renewal premium for my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text: The monies in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), including your incoming CPF contributions, will automatically be reserved up to a period of two months for the full Home Protection Scheme premium amount, when you do not have sufficient funds in your OA at the time of HPS cover renewal.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I still make payment for my outstanding MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums after the deadline stated in the Final Reminder notification?
questions.text:
We advise you to pay your outstanding MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums before the due date to avoid enforcement actions.
Please click on the link below for the payment options.
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)'s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: Can I stop paying premiums for my child?
questions.text:
If your child is below 21 years old, you are legally responsible for your child’s premium payment. You may change payer to your child, if he or she has sufficient balance in his/her MediSave Account e.g. if your child is a Singaporean who has received MediSave Grant for Newborns or if your child has working contributions.
Otherwise, Section 4(1) of MediShield Life Act requires parents to pay their child’s premiums until their child is 21 years old. If you have valid reasons to stop paying premiums for your child, for example you have been discharged from liability to maintain the child after divorce, please write to us (www.medishieldlife.sg/writetous) and attach the relevant court documents to support your case.

questions.title: Can I submit foreign citizenship documents when applying for suspension of premium collection?
questions.text:
No. The Singapore Government does not allow Singapore Citizens, aged 21 and above, to hold dual citizenship. The suspension application will not be processed until your dual citizenship status has been resolved with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
For matters relating to resolving of Singapore Citizenship, please submit your enquiry to ICA.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Can I terminate my standing instruction to use my CPF Ordinary Account savings to pay for my co-owner's Home Protection Scheme premiums?
questions.text: Please write to us if you wish to revoke your standing instruction to use your CPF Ordinary Account savings to pay your co-owner's Home Protection Scheme premium shortfall.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I upgrade to a higher coverage Integrated Shield Plan (IP) in future, if I buy the Standard IP now?
questions.text: When policyholders apply to upgrade to a higher coverage Integrated Shield Plan, they will need to go through another round of underwriting for the new additional coverage that they are purchasing. The insurers are allowed to assess, approve with or without exclusions and/or risk-loading, or reject applications based on their own risk assessment frameworks, as these are essentially business risk decisions.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Can I use different bank accounts to set up different GIRO arrangements for MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield?
questions.text:
No, you can only use one bank account for the premium payment of MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield as they are under a single GIRO arrangement.
Please refer to the following FAQs for guidance on changing your bank account or applying for GIRO to pay for your/your dependants' MediShield Life, CareShield Life, and ElderShield premiums:
Can I change the bank account to pay for my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?
How do I apply for GIRO for my/my dependant's MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay the MediShield Life deductible for outpatient treatment?
questions.text: Yes, you can use your MediSave to pay for your MediShield Life outpatient deductible. There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life, and MediSave. Nobody will be denied appropriate care due to an inability to pay.

questions.title: Can I use more than one of my family members' CPF Ordinary Account savings to pay my Home Protection Scheme premium shortfall?
questions.text:
If you have a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium shortfall, you can only use the CPF Ordinary Account savings of one family member (spouse, parent, child, or sibling), who is a co-owner, to pay the premium at any given time.
If you need help with subsequent HPS renewal premiums, you can approach another family member who is also a co-owner for assistance.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I use my CPF MediSave to pay for the ElderShield premiums for my family members?
questions.text: You can use your MediSave to pay for your own or your family members’ (spouse, parents, children, siblings, and grandparents) premiums for basic ElderShield and ElderShield Supplements. For ElderShield Supplements, usage of MediSave is capped at a limit of $600 per year.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF monies to service the premiums of my Part V Insurance Policy under Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS)?
questions.text: You can use your CPF monies in your Ordinary Account to service the future premiums of your policies (including endowment, whole life or rider policies, and regular premium policies).
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums for my family members, and is there a limit?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums for your family members, including your spouse, parents, children, grandparents and siblings. There is no limit to the number of family members you can help pay for.
However, you should consider the long-term affordability of IP premiums for your family members and whether you will have enough MediSave savings for your own healthcare needs, including during your retirement years.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay MediShield Life, CareShield Life and/or ElderShield premiums for my family members?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay the MediShield Life, CareShield Life and/or ElderShield premiums for yourself and your family members (spouse, parent, child, sibling or grandparent).
You can also pay for other family members (e.g. uncles, aunts, nephews, nieces, parents in-laws), if they meet the following conditions:
They are financially dependent on you; and
Both they and their family members (spouse, parent, child, sibling or grandchild) do not have sufficient MediSave for their premiums.
To become a premium payer, you can submit a Change Payer for MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to purchase an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) for my family member who is a foreigner?
questions.text: Integrated Shield Plan (IP) coverage for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents include the MediShield Life (MSL) component. You can use your MediSave to purchase a similar non-integrated healthcare plan for your foreign dependent. However, such plans for foreigners will not have the MSL component. Please approach your insurer to advise on the plans offered.

questions.title: Can I use my MediShield Life premium discount to pay for my outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text: Premium discounts can only be used for your next MediShield Life premium payments from 18 September 2025 onwards. They cannot be applied to any outstanding premiums from previous policy years.

questions.title: Can I use the monies in my CPF Special Account to pay the annual renewal premium for my Home Protection Scheme cover if I do not have sufficient savings in my CPF Ordinary Account?
questions.text: Home Protection Scheme premiums can only be paid from the savings in your CPF Ordinary Account, and not from your CPF Special Account (SA) savings. The SA savings are meant for retirement needs as they may be the only source of funds that members can turn to for financing their living expenses in old age.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I withdraw my CPF savings if I have unpaid taxes or MediShield Life/CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: If you have unpaid taxes or MediShield Life/CareShield Life premiums, we may be appointed by IRAS to recover the unpaid amount from the CPF savings you are withdrawing. If we are appointed to do so, you will receive an appointment notice from IRAS and we will pay IRAS the outstanding amount from your withdrawable savings to settle your unpaid taxes or MediShield Life/CareShield Life premiums before the balance (if any) is paid to you.

questions.title: Can licensees refer their patients to the relevant websites for fee-related information (e.g., MOH fee benchmarks, CPF MediSave and MediShield Life claims calculator to check on estimate claimable coverage) as part of the financial counselling?
questions.text:
There are no restrictions on a licensee referring a patient or a patient’s authorised representative to the relevant websites on fees related to the treatment or procedure the patient is receiving. However, for avoidance of doubt, such referrals to websites should not substitute financial counselling.
The licensee must still ensure that the patient or the patient’s authorised representative is aware of and understands the estimated price or price range, applicable subsidies, as well as the applicable MediShield Life benefits (e.g., deductible, co-insurance, claim limits, etc) and MediSave withdrawal limits for the patient’s treatment or procedure.
Licensees may share an estimate of MediShield Life payout and MediSave deduction amounts, provided that these estimates are generated by CPFB- or MOH-endorsed sources.
The licensee must obtain the patient’s or the patient’s authorised representative’s acknowledgement of receiving the financial counselling in writing (either paper record, or as an electronic record).

questions.title: Can minors who hold dual citizenship apply for suspension of premium collection?
questions.text:
Minors aged below 21 who hold dual citizenship may apply for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection, subject to the eligibility criteria. Minor dual citizens (DCs) must possess a valid permanent residency permit in their country of residence, or other foreign residency documents permitting them to reside in their country of residence permanently with no end date.
This is considering that Singapore Citizens who have acquired a citizenship of a foreign country can only renounce their Singapore citizenship after they turn 21 years old. If the application is approved, minor DCs will be granted suspension of MediShield Life premiums starting from the next policy year at point of application until the age of 20 years (inclusive).
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Can my insurance policy continue to run on Automatic Premium Loan (APL) and/or Extended Term Insurance (ETI) after the transfer to CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text: Automatic Premium Loan and Extended Term Insurance are allowed to continue after the transfer of your Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy to CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can overseas Singaporean male minors apply for suspension of premium collection before National Service obligations are fulfilled?
questions.text:
National Service is a key institution that is vital to the security and defence of Singapore. Under the Enlistment Act, all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents above the age of 18 years are required to serve National Service.
In line with this, only the following overseas Singaporean males will be eligible to apply for the suspension of MediShield Life premium collection:
a) Those who have completed full-time National Service; or
b) Those who have been informed by MINDEF that they are not required to serve full-time National Service.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Can the Board refund the amount of outstanding MediShield Life premiums recovered from my/my child's MediSave if we qualify for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) is provided to members who have insufficient MediSave and limited family support to pay their outstanding premiums.
The Government will pay your/your child's outstanding and future premiums at the point of APS qualification for the next two years. Hence, there is no refund of any outstanding premiums recovered prior to your APS qualification.

questions.title: Can the CareShield Life/ElderShield claims process be automated further, similar to how MediShield Life claims are automatically filed on behalf of an individual by the hospitals?
questions.text:
MediShield Life covers large bills incurred due to hospitalisation, so it is natural that hospitals automatically file claims on behalf of an individual.
CareShield Life/ElderShield provides monthly cash payouts that can be used for the benefit of an insured with severe disability. As the payouts will be paid to the bank account nominated by the insured, insureds or their caregivers will still need to be involved in the process of filing the claim.
Notwithstanding this, the Government has streamlined the claims process to improve convenience for insureds with severe disability and their caregivers, by increasing the pool of assessors and progressively accepting equivalent disability assessments already conducted by the insured’s care provider. We have also made the claim application process more efficient, for instance, by introducing an electronic application system that insureds with severe disability and their caregivers can access via the internet. The portal, accessible via https://efinance.aic.sg, integrates the application for all MOH disability schemes into a single form. We will continue to review how the process can be further simplified, as we gain more experience in administering the scheme.

questions.title: Can the deadline be extended to pay my outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premium?
questions.text:
You should make payment for your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums before the deadline. If you face difficulties in paying your outstanding premiums, you may apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). APS helps members who cannot pay their MediShield Life premiums after Government subsidies and have limited family support.
You can find out more about APS by calling 1800 222 3399 (or +65 6222 3399) from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8).
Alternatively, you can:
1. Seek a family member's help to perform "Change Payer" to pay your outstanding premiums; or
2. Set up GIRO arrangement to pay your renewal premiums annually. Any outstanding premiums from previous policy years will be paid by monthly instalments.

questions.title: Can the Government allow us to use more of our MediSave to pay for our Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums? Why aren’t withdrawal limits sized such that IP policyholders do not have to pay cash for their IP premiums?
questions.text: MediSave's main purpose is to help you save enough for basic healthcare needs, particularly after retirement. While Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) provide additional coverage, they are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life. The MediSave Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) are carefully balanced to help make IPs more affordable while ensuring you have enough savings for both current and future healthcare needs.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Can the outstanding MediShield Life premiums be waived due to financial difficulty?
questions.text:
Members with financial difficulties may apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). APS helps members who cannot pay their MediShield Life premiums despite Government subsidies and have limited family support.
You can find out more on APS by calling 1800-222-3399 (or +65 6222 3399) from Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:30pm (GMT+8).
The Ministry of Health will assess each application to ensure that assistance is provided to members who need financial support.

questions.title: Can the premium recovery measures for MediShield Life be waived?
questions.text:
Premium recovery measures cannot be waived as premiums must be paid timely. These measures are only imposed if the member defaults on premium payments repeatedly.
By paying on time, members do not cause others to shoulder their premium debts. You can write to us at www.cpf.gov.sg/writetous if you need assistance with premium payments.

questions.title: Can we put up a notice to inform patients of CHAS / MediShield Life / MediSave / etc accreditation?
questions.text:
Yes, a notice stating accreditation would suffice. If a licensee decides to put up a notice of their CHAS/MediShield Life/MediSave accreditation status, licensees are expected to facilitate patients’ claims for these schemes (e.g. by submitting MediShield Life and/or MediSave claims via the relevant portals), where applicable.
Licensees whose accreditation is suspended should not put up a notice of their accreditation status, since they would not be able to make claims for their patients during their suspension period.

questions.title: Can you explain the various premium components and computation for my MediShield Life Cover?
questions.text: You can refer to the MediShield Life Information Booklet for more information on the premium components and computation for more information.

questions.title: Did the Ministry of Health increase MediSave contribution rates due to the introduction of the Additional Withdrawal Limits?
questions.text:
Employer MediSave contribution rates for MediSave were last increased by 1% in Jan 2015. This helps to ensure that Singapore Residents can afford their MediShield Life premiums.
There were no changes to MediSave contribution rates arising from the introduction of the AWLs. MOH will monitor and review the adequacy of MediSave contributions.

questions.title: Do I get additional payouts from buying Integrated Shield Plan (IP)?
questions.text: In the majority of hospitalisation bills, you are unlikely to get additional payout from your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) if you stay in B2/C wards in public hospitals.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are automatically covered under MediShield Life. No application is required.
You will receive a cover issuance or renewal notification about one month before the start or renewal of your MediShield Life cover. The notification will inform you of your MediShield Life premiums and subsidies. If you have children under 21 years old, you will receive their MediShield Life notifications.

questions.title: Do I need to attach the employee, platform worker or insured's hardcopy healthcare payments and claims statement for submitting MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement?
questions.text:
CPF Board does not require any documents from employers, platform operators or insurers to process the MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement.
You should not request a hardcopy Healthcare Payments and Claims Statement from your employee, platform worker or insured. Employers, platform operators or insurers should accept a digital copy of the Healthcare Payments and Claims Statement from your employee, platform worker or insured if required.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Do I need to re-apply for Additional Premium Support (APS)?
questions.text: You will be invited to re-apply for APS if you still have insufficient MediSave to pay your premiums after your current APS ends.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: Do I need to re-apply for Additional Premium Support after the two-year validity period?
questions.text: You will be invited to re-apply for Additional Premium Support (APS) if you have insufficient MediSave savings and limited family support to pay your premiums after the two-year validity period. There is no need for you to re-apply for APS ahead of time.

questions.title: Do I need to reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave and/or MediShield Life within a specific time period?
questions.text: We strongly encourage you to reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds promptly. Timely reimbursement is particularly helpful if they need their MediSave and/or MediShield Life for further treatments.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Do I still need to pay premiums if I am eligible for ElderShield benefit claim payout?
questions.text: If you qualify for ElderShield benefit claim payout, you do not need to pay premiums if there is no change in your disability status.

questions.title: Do I still need to pay premiums if I am eligible for ElderShield benefit claim payout?
questions.text: If you qualify for ElderShield benefit claim payout, you do not need to pay premiums if there is no change in your disability status.

questions.title: Do the claim limits for High-Cost Drugs (HCD) and Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTP) apply if these treatments are administered during an inpatient stay or day surgery?
questions.text: Yes, if a patient receives High-Cost Drugs (HCD) or Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTP) treatment during an inpatient or day surgery admission, the respective HCD/CTGTP claim limit will apply to these treatments, while the daily inpatient hospital limit will apply to the room and board charges. This ensures adequate healthcare financing support by MediShield Life and MediSave for patients who receive HCD or CTGTP treatment in inpatient or day surgery settings.

questions.title: Do the MediSave contribution rates need to be increased because of the higher CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: The current MediSave contribution rates already allow most working households to pay for CareShield Life and MediShield Life premiums from their monthly MediSave contributions. The Government will continually review the MediSave contribution rates to ensure that they are adequate for the future healthcare needs of Singaporeans.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Do the Premium Subsidies differ for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents?
questions.text: Permanent Residents receive half of the subsidy rates applicable to Singapore Citizens.

questions.title: Does MediShield Life cover hospice care?
questions.text: Yes, MediShield Life covers the Inpatient Hospice Palliative Care Service (IHPCS) at inpatient hospices and community hospitals. Please refer to the latest limits here
topics: MediShield Life / Benefits Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Does MediShield Life or MediSave cover the GST charged on my medical bill?
questions.text: Yes, MediShield Life claim payouts and MediSave withdrawals are based on the bill amounts submitted by the medical institution, subject to the applicable limits under the respective schemes. If the bill includes GST, the GST amount will be included in the payout.

questions.title: Does my CPF LIFE premium continue to earn interest?
questions.text: Yes, your CPF LIFE premium will continue to earn CPF interest rates with the floor rate of 4%, and up to 2% extra interest on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances. The interest earned is factored into your monthly payouts and you receive a higher payout from the start.

questions.title: Does the Basic Healthcare Sum need to be increased because of the higher CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the estimated savings required for basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age. As CareShield Life premium payments will stop at the re-employment age of 67 for most Singaporeans, the Government does not expect premiums to have a significant impact on the BHS.
Nevertheless, the Government will review and adjust the BHS regularly to ensure that Singaporeans’ MediSave savings keep pace with growth in MediSave use by the elderly, especially with rising healthcare costs and expansions in MediSave uses.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Does the Cancer Drug List also apply to inpatient cancer drug treatments under MediShield Life and MediSave?
questions.text: Currently, the Cancer Drug List does not apply to inpatient cancer drug treatments as these are covered separately under the inpatient claim limits for MediShield Life and MediSave, together with other costs incurred during the inpatient stay.

questions.title: Does the Government intend to provide additional CareShield Life premium support to help individuals who are financially affected by COVID-19?
questions.text:
The Government has put in place several measures to ensure that CareShield Life premiums remain affordable. In particular, the Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies, Additional Premium Support and other support measures to ensure that premiums remain affordable. This includes the transitional subsidies for the future cohorts joining the new scheme.
We also understand that it may be more challenging to meet living expenses during the current COVID-19 pandemic. There are additional support measures available to support lower- and middle-income families, such as the Temporary Relief Fund and COVID-19 Support Grant.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Does the Health Insurance Planner account for the cost of dependants’ premiums?
questions.text: The Health Insurance Planner includes premium costs for dependants you currently pay for, based on CPF Board’s records. You can specify how many years you plan to continue paying premiums for each dependant.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: For those with serious pre-existing conditions, why do they have to pay Additional Premiums for MediShield Life?
questions.text: Those with serious pre-existing conditions pay a higher MediShield Life premium as a reflection of the higher risks they pose to the pool and to fund part of their coverage. The Government will support most of the cost of extending MediShield Life coverage to all Singapore Residents.

questions.title: For those with serious pre-existing conditions, why do they have to pay Additional Premiums? What is the reason for setting it at 30% over 10 years? Would this be too onerous for some?
questions.text:
The Additional Premiums apply to the first 10 years of premiums paid by Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who newly join the scheme and who have pre-existing conditions.
The Additional Premiums reflect the higher risks of covering these individuals with serious pre-existing conditions while ensuring that premiums remain affordable and are not overly onerous.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: Given that the Fund already has significant assets, why is there a need to increase premiums for MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Majority of the assets in the MediShield Life Fund are set aside as liabilities to honour future commitments such as premium rebates and future claims for patients who have started on multi-year recurrent treatments, such as dialysis and chemotherapy. In addition, capital is also set aside to ensure that MediShield Life can absorb the impact from adverse events and continue to pay out claims, without requiring sudden increases in premiums.
As payouts have increased over the years due to medical inflation and higher claims utilisation, premiums have to be increased in order for the Fund to continue meeting its commitments. Higher premiums will also support the higher claim limits for existing benefits and the expansion to new benefits.

questions.title: How are CareShield Life premiums calculated?
questions.text:
CareShield Life premiums are calculated such that each age cohort of insureds pay sufficient premiums to support their expected payouts as a cohort. This ensures the long-term sustainability of the insurance fund.
While CareShield Life insureds are younger, premiums collected are naturally more than payouts in that year due to fewer claims. However, the premiums collected will be carried over to support the payouts in the event of severe disability in the future.
The CareShield Life Council regularly reviews factors like changes in claims experience and longevity and advises the Government on premium adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. The Government will consider affordability of premiums when reviewing the Council’s advice on premium adjustments.
CareShield Life is managed by the Government on a not-for-profit basis. Any excess premiums will be used to benefit insureds and there are legal safeguards to ensure the Government cannot divert CareShield Life and ElderShield Insurance Fund monies for non-prescribed uses.

questions.title: How are claim limits for MediShield Life and MediSave determined when more than one cancer drug is used in the treatment?
questions.text:
Patients who need more than one cancer drug treatment on the Cancer Drug List (CDL) in a month may claim up to the higher of the MediShield Life, MediSave and Integrated Shield Plan (IPs) claim limits applicable for the individual treatments.
For example, if a patient uses both Treatments X (MediShield Life claim limit of $2,000 & MediSave withdrawal limit of $600) and Y (MediShield Life claim limit of $1,000 & MediSave withdrawal limit of $600) in a month, the patient may claim no more than $2,000 from MediShield Life and withdraw no more than $600 from MediSave in that month.
Please consult your doctor if you wish to clarify the claim limit that will apply for your treatment.

questions.title: How are MediShield Life claim limits sized when more than one cancer drug is used in the treatment?
questions.text:
In general, the MediShield Life (MSHL) claim limits for cost-effective treatments are set based on the post-subsidy bills for subsidised patients in Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs).
The Cancer Drug List (CDL) includes treatments that involve a single drug or multiple drugs (i.e. combination treatments). For combination treatments, the applicable MSHL claim limit depends on whether the combination treatment has been assessed to be cost-effective:
If the combination treatment is cost-effective, the MSHL claim limit is sized to be sufficient to cover the post-subsidy cost of the entire combination in PHIs.
If the combination treatment is not cost-effective, it may be listed on the CDL subject to negotiations with the drug companies. However, the claim limit would be pegged to the highest individual claim limit of the drugs in the combination. Doctors and patients are encouraged to use treatments that have been assessed to be cost-effective.

questions.title: How can I apply for Additional Premium Support to pay for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their CareShield Life premiums after premium subsidies and have limited family support.
There is no need for you to apply for APS ahead of time. You will be invited to apply for APS should you have insufficient MediSave savings and limited family support to pay your premiums.
If you are assessed to be eligible for the scheme, the Government will grant APS to you to pay for your MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) premiums.
For more information on APS, please visit the MediShield Life website or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.

questions.title: How can I apply for reimbursements for my MediSave and/or MediShield Life?
questions.text:
If you have utilised your MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses, and your employer or insurer has contractual obligations to reimburse you for your medical expenses, please approach them to find out how they can reimburse to your MediSave and/or MediShield Life.
Your employer or insurer may require you to provide the following supporting documents:
i. Finalised medical bill - showing the itemised charges and the source of payment (e.g. cash, MediSave, Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life).
ii. Healthcare payments and claims statement - showing the payment information including the Hospital Registration Number (HRN) used to identify the claim details for reimbursement purposes. The HRN is a 13-character alphanumeric registration number (e.g. 522016A02QL6E). You can retrieve this statement online from your Healthcare dashboard.
For claims that have been reimbursed, you will see the message 'You have been reimbursed for this claim. View details'. Click 'View details' to view the reimbursement details on the Healthcare payments and claims statement.
If you do not have Singpass, you can register for an account online.

questions.title: How can I apply for the suspension of MediShield Life premium collection?
questions.text:
The MediShield Life Council (MLC) recognises that there is a small and distinct group of Overseas Singaporeans (OS) who live outside Singapore permanently, have no intention to reside in Singapore, and feel that they will not benefit from MediShield Life.
If you belong to the OS group, you can apply for a suspension of premium collection even though you will remain covered under MediShield Life. You can refer to the Suspension of MediShield Life Premium Collection for more information on the eligibility criteria and application process.

questions.title: How can I check for healthcare GIRO deductions on my bank statement?

questions.title: How can I check the status of my reimbursement if I have already submitted a claim to my insurer after using my MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses?

Simply login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass, and go to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims' to view the recent transactions. You can also click on 'View past 15 months' to see additional transactions.
For reimbursed claims, you will see the message "You have been reimbursed for this claim. View details". Click 'View details' to see the reimbursement details.

If you have insufficient savings in your MediSave, you can make a top-up via the Top up MediSave Account online form.

questions.text:
Your CareShield Life premiums will be automatically deducted from your MediSave. In the event of insufficient savings in the MediSave for premium payment, you can top up your MediSave through the Top up MediSave Account online form.
If you do not have a MediSave Account, you can set up a MediSave Account with CPF Board by making a top-up through the Top up MediSave Account online form.
Alternatively, a family member* can apply to take over as your premium payer using his/her MediSave. To do so, he/she may visit the Change Premium Payer e-Service and log in using his/her own Singpass to complete the “Change Premium Payer” transaction.
*Family member refers to the Insured's spouse, parents, children, siblings or grandchildren.

questions.title: How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)'s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to view your or your dependant(s)’s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life coverage and premium information under the “CareShield Life/ElderShield” and “MediShield Life” section respectively.
Paying your premiums
Premiums are fully payable by MediSave. If you do not have sufficient MediSave, you can pay the premiums by:
Asking a family member to perform a Change Payer request to take over the premium payment using his/her MediSave.
Performing a voluntary top-up to your MediSave Account via the Top up MediSave Account online form.
MediSave top-ups are generally credited immediately and will be deducted for premium payment. You may view the MediSave top-up(s) and premium deduction(s) in your Transaction history. If the top-up amount is not reflected in your MediSave Account, please check your MediSave account balance after five working days as more time may be needed to process some transactions.
No further action will be required from you if payment has been made. We will notify you again if there are insufficient MediSave for premium payment.
As MediSave top-ups could be deducted for healthcare premiums and medical expenses based on when deductions are due, please ensure that you have sufficient MediSave for all payments.
Setting up GIRO arrangement to pay your renewal premiums annually. Any outstanding premiums from previous policy years will be paid by monthly instalments.
More payment options are available in the link below:
I am (i) residing overseas or (ii) have renounced my Singapore Citizenship/Permanent Resident status. How do I pay my CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums?
