questions.title: How did the Government decide what should be covered under MediShield Life in this review?
questions.text:
In MediShield Life Council’s review, there were a few considerations:
First, MediShield Life was created as a national health insurance scheme to fully cover majority of the subsidised bills in public hospitals. Patients use their MediSave savings to pay the deductible and co-insurance. However, as medical bills have increased over the years, this coverage has dropped.
Second, the Government recognises that healthcare is now being provided outside of hospitals — like in outpatient, community, and home settings — areas that MediShield Life mostly doesn’t cover.
Lastly, new medical technologies have introduced life-saving treatments, like Cell, Tissue, and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTPs), which are also not covered by MediShield Life.
The recommended approach balances enhancing affordability for patients while keeping premiums manageable for everyone.

questions.title: How did the Government decide which treatments, conditions, and care settings should be covered under MediShield Life in this review?
How do Government pensioners benefit from MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Government pensioners can use MediShield Life as a complement to their post-retirement medical benefits, to pay for overall out-of-pocket expenses for large hospitalisation bills that are incurred from:
Co-payments for large hospitalisation bills that exceed their post-retirement medical benefits
Ward upgrades beyond their eligibility in Restructured Hospitals e.g. when a pensioner eligible for Class B1 ward chooses to stay in Class A ward
Private hospital expenses, which are not covered by Civil Service medical benefits today.
The Public Service Division has sent letters to pensioners to inform them of their MediShield Life benefits in 2015.

questions.title: How do I apply for GIRO for my/my dependant's MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
You can use your own or a third party's bank account to apply for GIRO for your/your dependant's MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums by clicking on Set up GIRO for healthcare premiums.
Upon approval of your GIRO application, your healthcare renewal premiums will be deducted from your bank account every year, within a month after the cover is renewed. If you/your dependant has outstanding healthcare premiums, it will be paid in monthly instalments from the GIRO bank account.

questions.title: How do I change the payer for my/my dependants' Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums?
questions.text: As your Integrated Shield Plan is administered by the private insurer you have chosen to cover you, please approach your insurer directly to make the change.

questions.title: How do I check that the premium rebate has been successfully credited?
questions.text:
If you are the recipient of the rebate, you will be informed of your personalised rebate amount via email, SMS, or hardcopy based on your registered contact details by end January 2023.
The credited rebate will also be viewable via your MediSave account statements by end January 2023. To view this, access the Transaction History via cpf.gov.sg (Singpass login is required).

questions.title: How do I check the premiums payable under CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The CareShield Life Premium Checker allows individuals to view their personalised CareShield Life premiums and subsidies for the current policy year, and their estimated premiums and subsidies for upcoming policy years.
If you are born in 1945 or earlier, you will face higher annual CareShield Life premiums as you have fewer years to spread your premium payment over, as compared to younger cohorts. Older cohorts also have a higher risk of developing severe disability.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premium Checker

questions.title: How do I check the premiums payable under CareShield Life?
questions.text: The CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service allows individuals to view their personalised CareShield Life premiums and subsidies for the current policy year, and their estimated premiums and subsidies for upcoming policy years.

questions.title: How do I claim from MediShield Life?
questions.text:
The medical institution will ask if you wish to make a claim and request for your authorisation to submit the claim to MediShield Life and your Integrated Shield Plan insurer (if any) on your behalf. If a payout is due, it will be made to the medical institution directly to offset your bill. The remaining balance can be paid by MediSave and/or cash.
To estimate the maximum amount that you can claim from MediSave or MediShield Life, click here
(https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/medisave-medishield-life-claims)
The list of medical institutions participating in MediShield Life is available here.
https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/member/healthcare/documents/MSH_MedicalInstitutions.pdf
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: How do I ensure I am notified of my MediShield Life premiums payable?
questions.text:
To ensure that you are notified of your MediShield Life premiums payable, you can update your residential address with ICA or at the nearest Neighbourhood Police Post. Once updated, participating government agencies and statutory boards like the CPF Board will be informed of the change in address through the One-Stop Change of Address Reporting Service (OSCARS).
You can also log in to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' for information on your and/or your dependants' MediShield Life premiums and subsidies.
You will receive digital notifications regarding your MediShield Life if you have registered your email address and mobile telephone number. For example,
a. If your email address is registered with CPF Board, you will be notified via email;
b. If your email address is not registered, but your mobile number is registered with CPF Board, you will be notified via WhatsApp or SMS depending on whether you have given consent to receive WhatsApp notifications;
c. Additionally, if you have installed the CPF Mobile app and enabled push notifications on your mobile phone, you will receive the CPF Mobile app push notification alerts. This is an additional notification alert.
You can log in to the CPF website and update your contact details under Account Settings.
If you do not have the CPF Mobile app, and did not register your email or mobile number with us, you will continue to receive hardcopy MediShield Life letters.

questions.title: How do I know if Additional Premium Support has been granted to fully pay my outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You will receive a letter to inform you on the outcome of your APS application.
For MediShield Life premiums, you may log in to "Outstanding MediShield Life premium". If you do not have any outstanding premium, you will not be able to view this page.
For CareShield Life premiums, you may log in to ‘Check My Premium’ at careshieldlife.gov.sg via SingPass. If you are eligible for APS, the ‘Net Premium Payable after Additional Premium Support’ field will be reflected as $0.

questions.title: How do I make a top up for my spouse/parent/child/sibling's outstanding Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text:
If you co-own the flat with your spouse/parent/child/sibling, you can authorise us to use your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay the insured’s premium shortfall. You can do this online by logging in with your Singpass.
Once the application is approved by the Board, the premium will be deducted from the available balance in the insured’s CPF OA first, followed by your CPF OA.

questions.title: How do I make payment for my MediShield Life if I am overseas and who should I contact to verify that my payment has been received?
questions.text:
For more information on payment matters for overseas members, please click here.
If you require further assistance, you may contact us at 1800-222-3399 (or +65-6222-3399 from overseas), Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm or write to us.

questions.title: How do I pay my ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: You can use your MediSave to pay for your ElderShield premiums in full. If you do not have enough MediSave savings, you may also use the MediSave savings of your spouse, parents, children, siblings, and grandchildren to pay for the premiums.

questions.title: How do I pay the Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium is automatically deducted from your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) annually.
You can check and view the deduction from your CPF account online using your Singpass. The deduction will also be reflected in your Yearly Statement of Account.
If your OA balance is not enough to pay the premium, you will be notified to top up your OA within a grace period of two months. If you have incoming working contributions that will be credited into your OA within the grace period and can cover your premium shortfall, you may choose not to take any action. We will deduct the shortfall from your new working contributions.
Alternatively, your family member, who is your spouse, parent, child, or sibling, who co-owns the flat with you can authorise the use of their OA savings to pay your premium shortfall.
The attempt to deduct premiums occurs weekly for HPS cover renewal and fortnightly for HPS cover issuance during the two-month grace period. HPS cover issuance or renewal will take place once the full premium is successfully deducted from the insured's OA and/or the co-owner's OA (where authorisation has been provided).
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I pay the MediShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life premiums can be paid for by MediSave and are automatically deducted from the MediSave accounts of members. If there are insufficient monies in your MediSave account, other payment options for MediShield Life premiums include:
A family member performing a "Change of Payer for MediShield Life Cover" (cpf.gov.sg/changepayer) request to take over the premium payment using his/her MediSave.
Voluntary top-up to your or the premium payer’s MediSave Account (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/top-up-medisave-account) .
You can view the premium deduction in your Transaction history at the CPF website.
For further assistance, please contact us at 1800 222 3399 or email us by using this link (www.medishieldlife.sg/writetous).

questions.title: How do I submit the MediShield Life and CareShield Life Health Declaration form for Permanent Residence applicants?
questions.text:
All new Singapore Permanent Residence applicants who have received Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA)'s In-Principle Approval are required to declare their health condition for MediShield Life and CareShield Life before completing formalities with ICA. The health status declared will not affect their Singapore Permanent Residence application.
The health declaration can be submitted via the "MediShield Life and CareShield Life health declaration for permanent residence applicants" form on the CPF website. Upon receiving In-Principle Approval from ICA, please wait one day before submitting the form. Each applicant must submit a separate individual form. Singpass login is required.
Applicants age 21 or older
If you are the applicant, please log in using your Singpass and select “Myself” under the “Select Person to be Insured” section. If you do not have a Singpass account, please apply for one. If you are unable to apply for a Singpass account, please have a family member who is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident log in using their Singpass and select “A Family Member” under the “Select Person to be Insured” section.
Applicants under age 21
Applicants under age 21 must have a parent or legal guardian submit the Health Declaration on their behalf. If the parent or legal guardian is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, they must log in using their Singpass and select “A Family Member” under the “Select Person to be Insured” section. For applicants with a foreign parent or legal guardian, see the “Applicants without Singpass” section below.
Applicants without Singpass
If you are unable to apply for Singpass or do not have a family member who is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident with Singpass who can submit the Health Declaration form on your behalf, please use the Health Declaration form for applicants without Singpass instead. Foreign parents or legal guardians of applicants under age 21 with Singpass should also use this form.
Please note that submissions from applicants age 21 or older who have Singpass will not be processed through this form.
After Submission
You can check the status of your health declaration via "Activities". If you are required to attend a disability assessment for CareShield Life, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will notify you of the details, or you can contact AIC at apply@aic.sg. Please attend the assessment promptly within the specified timeframe. You will be informed of the outcome via email, SMS or hardcopy once your application is processed.

For subsequent policy renewals, you will receive a premium notification about a month before the policy is renewed. You can also log in to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' for information on your and/or your dependants' MediShield Life premiums and subsidies.

questions.title: How do I update my personal particulars (including change of address) for my Integrated Shield Plan (IP)?
questions.text: As your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is administered by the private insurer you have chosen to cover you, please approach your insurer directly on all matters relating to your IP or by updating your particulars on your insurer’s web portal.

questions.title: How do I view the details of my outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You can log in to Outstanding MediShield Life premium to view the breakdown of your outstanding premiums, interest and/or penalties.
If you do not have any outstanding premium for the previous policy years, but your dependants have, you will see a blank section below the premium summary table. Your dependants can view the breakdown of their outstanding premiums by logging into their own Healthcare dashboards.
If you and your dependants (if any) do not have outstanding premium, you will not be able to view this page.

questions.title: How do the CareShield Life premiums and monthly payouts compare against Supplements and other private long-term care insurance plans?
questions.text:
Supplement premiums are not directly comparable as there are inherent differences in the product design of CareShield Life, Supplements and other private long-term care products:
• Currently, there are no Supplement plans with increasing payouts, although there are Supplement plans that have a higher payout quantum and no cap on payout duration, similar to CareShield Life.
• Supplements generally have premium schedules designed to keep annual premiums lower e.g. some of them allow premiums to be paid up to age 80, 100 or over the insured’s lifetime while CareShield Life only requires premiums to be paid up to age 67. Some Supplements offer additional benefits, such as death benefit, lump sum benefit upon claim or payouts upon not being able to perform at least two out of the six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), which CareShield Life does not provide.
As part of CareShield Life, the Government will be providing several premium support measures for those born in 1979 or earlier, including means-tested premium subsidies, participation incentives, and Additional Premium Support for those who are unable to pay their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies. No one will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.
In addition, CareShield Life will be administered by the Government on a not-for-profit basis. Government administration will enable the provision of premium support for lower- and middle-income Singaporeans and offer more flexibility for future scheme enhancements.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: How does the Health Insurance Planner project my insurance premiums?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) uses current age-based premium tables for MediShield Life, Integrated Shield Plans (IPs), and riders to calculate your projections. These rates may change over time and will be updated in HIP annually in January. Please note that the projections do not include premium loading, discounts, or claims-based pricing.
To provide realistic estimates, the planner factors in inflation for healthcare costs. You can adjust the inflation rates to customize your projections. The private medical insurance component of the IP and rider premiums are subject to the annual inflation rate set by you for medical insurance premiums, while CareShield Life and Supplement Plan premiums are subject to the annual inflation rate set by you for long-term care premiums.
For more information on assumptions used in these calculations, you may refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: How is the amount of premium loading determined for my Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text: The amount of premium loading depends on the severity of your pre-existing health condition. If you are offered cover with premium loading, you will receive a notification which shows the total premium amount payable.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How is the Government helping me to cope with the MediShield Life premium increase?
questions.text:
To help Singaporeans manage the premium increases, the Government will provide an additional $4.1 billion in premium support measures, comprising $3.4 billion in MediSave top-ups and $0.7 billion in premium subsidies over the next three years.
In addition, the total premium increase is capped at 35% and the increases will be phased evenly from April 2025 to March 2028. You can refer to the MediShield Life Information Booklet for more information on MediShield Life premiums, Government subsidies and support.
Additional Premium Support is available for Singaporeans who are unable to afford their MediShield Life premiums after premium subsidies and have limited family support. The Government will expand the eligibility criteria to cover more lower-income Singaporeans. No one will be denied coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.
Please refer to press release for more details of the MediShield Life 2024 Review premium support measures.

questions.title: How is the Government Transitional support different from the CareShield Life premium subsidy?
questions.text: Unlike CareShield Life premium subsidies, which are means-tested and targeted at the lower- and middle-income policyholders, all policyholders who see an increase in their gross premiums will benefit from the transitional support to help manage the premium increases from the CareShield Life 2025 Review.

questions.title: How is the Government Transitional support different from the CareShield Life premium subsidy?
questions.text: Unlike CareShield Life premium subsidies, which are means-tested and targeted at the lower- and middle-income policyholders, all policyholders who see an increase in their gross premiums will benefit from the transitional support to help manage the premium increases from the CareShield Life 2025 Review.

questions.title: How is the Home Protection Scheme premium calculated?
questions.text:
The Home Protection Scheme charges a level premium rate (i.e. same amount annually throughout the policy term) and is calculated based on several factors:
Outstanding housing loan on the flat*
Loan repayment period
Type of loan (HDB concessionary or market rate)
Age and gender
Percentage share of cover of the outstanding housing loan
*The computation of the level premium takes into account the monthly reduction in the housing loan.
Premiums are generally higher for greater share of coverage, larger loan amounts, or longer repayment periods. The premiums would be lower for younger persons and females, due to lower mortality risk.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How is the proposed premium discount scheme similar to or different from a no-claims discount?
questions.text:
The idea of introducing incentives to encourage healthier behaviours has been considered in past reviews of MediShield Life. With the launch of Healthier SG and the growing emphasis on preventive health, it is now opportune to introduce premium discounts for MediShield Life policyholders to complement these national efforts.
For a start, we have tied the premium discount to health-seeking behaviours such as exercise. In particular, MediShield Life policyholders will be able to redeem premium discounts from Healthpoints earned from activities on the Healthy 365 app or completion of first Health Plan consult under Healthier SG.
This is different from “no-claims discounts” that some insurers offer to their policyholders, which provide discounts to those who do not make claims in the previous policy year. This approach was not adopted to avoid penalising Singaporeans, especially the elderly, for making claims for healthcare episodes that they may inevitably face throughout their lives. It could also discourage Singaporeans from seeking appropriate care, for fear of losing their discounts.

questions.title: How is the scope of benefits determined? What other treatments have been considered for coverage under MediShield Life?
questions.text: The MediShield Life Council has assessed the scope of benefits and new areas to be covered by MediShield Life, taking in proposals from various stakeholders. Treatments which are recommended for MediShield Life coverage have been prioritised based on suitability for risk-pooling, clinical- and cost-effectiveness, having significant affordability gaps, and/or potential to encourage patients to receive care in appropriate settings.
topics: MediShield Life / Benefits Under Medishield Life

questions.title: How long do I have to pay for CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If you are age 59 and above when you join CareShield Life, you will not have to pay premiums after 10 years.
If you are age 58 and below when you join CareShield Life, you will have to pay premiums until you reach age 67 (inclusive of the year you turn age 67). Thereafter, you will no longer need to pay for CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: How long do I have to pay my Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text:
You will only need to pay the premium for 90% of your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover period.
For example, if your HPS cover period is 30 years, you will only need to pay premium for 27 years.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.text:
As relevant agencies may take some time to verify your permanent residency or other status, the processing of MediShield Life Suspension application may take up to three months or longer, depending on its complexity. We will inform you of the outcome once we have assessed your application.
Please visit our website at cpf.gov.sg/HealthcareFinancing if you need more information or write to us at cpf.gov.sg/writetous.

questions.title: How many reimbursements can I submit via E-File at one time?
questions.text:
You can submit up to 15,000 reimbursements at a time via E-File.
Please note that all 15,000 reimbursements should be submitted in a single Excel file.

questions.title: How may I repay the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) of my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy?
questions.text: You may repay the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) by paying cash to the insurance company directly. The cash balance in your CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account cannot be used to repay the APL.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How much cheaper are the CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums going to be under Government administration, compared to private sector administration?
questions.text:
As the Government will be operating CareShield Life on a not-for-profit basis, CareShield Life premiums will be based on actuarial principles with no profit margins priced in.
For ElderShield, the Government will maintain the current ElderShield premiums and run the scheme on a not-for-profit basis. There will be no change to benefits due under ElderShield. Any excess of premiums over claims will be used for insureds’ benefit. In the event that the actual claims experience turns out better than expected, there will continue to be premium rebates for all insureds.
topics: CareShield Life / Government Administration and Independent Council

questions.title: How much is my ElderShield premium?
questions.text: ElderShield premiums are based on the age at which you join the scheme, and the final premium payable is for the policy year in which you are still age 65 at the start of the policy year. The premium amount does not increase with age. You can find your premiums for ElderShield 400 and ElderShield 300 here.

questions.title: How much is my ElderShield premium?
questions.text: ElderShield premiums are based on the age at which you join the scheme, and the final premium payable is for the policy year in which you are still age 65 at the start of the policy year. The premium amount does not increase with age. You can find your premiums for ElderShield 400 and ElderShield 300.

questions.title: How much is the outpatient deductible? Will I need to pay more out of pocket for outpatient consultation?
questions.text:
The outpatient deductible is set at $500 to strike a balance between ensuring that it can sieve out smaller bills meaningfully and moderate the extent to which premiums need to increase by, whilst not overly affecting affordability for patients. It applies for all admissions on or after 1 Jan 2026 and is fully payable by MediSave. There should generally be no increase in out-of-pocket payable as long as you have sufficient MediSave.
For those with insufficient MediSave, the Government will provide additional support such as MediSave top-ups. There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use to pay for my family member's outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text: You can pay your insured family member's outstanding MediShield Life premiums in full using your MediSave.

questions.title: How much more premium rebates will Singapore Residents get in old age, with premiums distributed more evenly over our lifetime?
questions.text:
Please click here (https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medishield-life/premium-rebates) for more information on the enhanced premium rebate table applicable to incoming cohorts.
The scheme is designed such that younger policyholders who pre-pay more during their working ages will receive greater premium rebates. This will help to offset more of old-age premiums for their generation.
topics: MediShield Life / Pre-funding under MediShield Life

The amount of rebate you receive depends on how much premiums you have paid as of 31 December 2022 (the more premiums you have paid, the higher the rebates you will receive).

questions.title: How much will my CareShield Life premiums be after the premium changes take place, and how much would it increase by?
questions.text:
With the CareShield Life premium support measures, annual CareShield Life premium increases from 2026 to 2030 will be moderated to about $38 on average, and no more than $75.
CareShield Life premiums will continue to be fully payable via MediSave, which will minimise out-of-pocket payments for policyholders.
Lower- and middle-income policyholders will have smaller CareShield Life premium increases, as they will receive means-tested premium subsidies.
Individuals may check their personalised premiums through the CareShield Life premium checker from November 2025 onwards.

questions.title: How much will my CareShield Life premiums be after the premium changes take place, and how much would it increase by?
questions.text:
With the CareShield Life premium support measures, annual CareShield Life premium increases from 2026 to 2030 will be moderated to about $38 on average, and no more than $75.
CareShield Life premiums will continue to be fully payable via MediSave, which will minimise out-of-pocket payments for policyholders.
Lower- and middle-income policyholders will have smaller CareShield Life premium increases, as they will receive means-tested premium subsidies.
Individuals may check their personalised premiums through the CareShield Life premium checker from October 2025 onwards.

questions.title: How much will my CareShield life Premiums increase and what happens after I reach 67?
questions.text:
CareShield Life premiums (excluding GST) will gradually increase by 2%* each year and will stop increasing when you reach 67. If you joined CareShield Life when you are 58 or younger, you won’t have to pay premiums after you reach 67. However, if you joined CareShield Life at 59 or older, you won’t have to pay premiums after 10 years.
It is important to note that if you make a successful claim with CareShield Life, your premium payments will be waived during the time you are receiving payouts.
*The payouts will increase at 2% each year until 2025 where it will be reviewed further.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: How much will my CareShield Life Premiums increase and what happens after I reach 67?
questions.text:
CareShield Life premiums are designed to increase regularly to support the regular increase in payouts. The schedule of premium increases is not fixed, and will be regularly reviewed by the CareShield Life Council to ensure the sustainability of the scheme.
Following CareShield Life 2025 Review, payouts will increase by 4% per year from 2026 to 2030 to help policyholders keep up with rising long-term care costs. To support this, premiums will increase annually, with premium support measures moderating increases from 2026 to 2030 to about $38 on average and no more than $75.
If you are age 59 and above when you join CareShield Life, you will not have to pay premiums after 10 years.
If you are age 58 and below when you join CareShield Life, you will have to pay premiums until you reach age 67 (inclusive of the year you turn age 67). Thereafter, you will no longer need to pay for CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: How much will my premiums be once the premium changes take effect, and how much would it increase by?
questions.text:
You may refer to the premium & subsidy table here for the premium schedule for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
The extent of premium increases will vary across policyholders depending on age group. Information on your MediShield Life premium and applicable subsidies will be sent in writing to the payer of your premium about 1-2 months before your policy renewal date, by the Central Provident Fund Board or your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurer (if you are insured under an IP).
To help Singaporeans manage the premium increases, the Government will provide an additional $4.1 billion in premium support measures over the next three years. With this, more than nine in 10 Singaporeans will be able to more than offset their net increase in premiums for the next three years.

questions.title: How often do I have to pay MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text: MediShield Life cover is renewed yearly. Payers are notified about one month before cover renewal date and premiums are collected within a month after the cover is renewed.

questions.title: How often do I have to pay MediShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If you are the payer of your/your dependants’ MediShield Life premiums, the premiums will be collected annually from your MediSave Account.
You will be notified on the net premium payable and applicable subsidies via the Premium Notice Letter that will be sent about 1 to 2 months before the renewal of your MediShield Life cover.

questions.title: How often will the CareShield Life premiums increase?
questions.text:
To give Singaporeans greater certainty in the first five years, payouts and premiums* for CareShield Life will each increase by 2% per year.
An independent council will be set up to regularly review these trends and advise the Government on CareShield Life premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. The Government will consider affordability of premiums when reviewing the council’s advice on premium adjustments.
*2% increase of premiums per year excludes GST.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: How often will the CareShield Life premiums increase?
questions.text:
CareShield Life premiums increase annually to support the annual increases in payouts, which help protect the value of payouts over time and keep up with rising long-term care costs.
The CareShield Life Council regularly reviews these trends and advises the Government on CareShield Life premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. The Government will consider affordability of premiums when reviewing the council’s advice on premium adjustments.

questions.title: How often will the Government review the Standard Integrated Shield Plan claim limits?
questions.text: The Ministry of Health will regularly review the Standard IP claim limits to ensure that they continue to provide sufficient coverage for Ward B1 or equivalent bills in public hospitals.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: How often will the Ministry of Health (MOH) be reviewing the Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs)? Will MOH be reviewing the AWLs taking into account Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premium increases over time?
questions.text:
The Ministry of Health will review the Additional Withdrawal Limits from time to time as new data and evidence emerge.
The AWLs for IP premiums are set to strike a balance between helping Singapore Residents pay for IPs, which are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life, and conserving enough MediSave for basic healthcare expenses, especially in old age.

questions.text:

questions.title: How was I identified to pay my family member's CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You had previously used your MediSave to help pay the insured’s medical expenses or health insurance premiums. To encourage family responsibility, we will notify family members that they can use their MediSave to help their family member with insufficient MediSave. This makes it convenient for the majority of members who wish to help their family members pay their CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums. To date, more than 90% of family members approached have accepted the arrangement.
Family members who are identified as potential payers will be notified one month before premium deduction takes place. You may reject this payment arrangement by submitting Stop Payment for CareShield Life/MediShield Life or call us at 1800-222-3399.
You can later decide to pay for your family member's MediShield Life premiums by submitting a Change Payer for CareShield Life/MediShield Life.

questions.title: How was I identified to pay my family member’s MediShield Life premiums? On what authority does the Board automatically deduct my MediSave to pay for my family member’s MediShield Life premiums? Can I stop this payment arrangement?
questions.text:
You have been identified as the premium payer as you are the insured’s family member and have previously used your MediSave to pay the insured’s medical expenses or other health insurance premiums.
This option encourages family responsibility by notifying family members that they can use their MediSave to help a family member who has insufficient MediSave to pay MediShield Life premiums. This also makes it convenient for the majority of members who wish to help their family members pay their premiums.
This process to facilitate the payment of an insured family member’s MediShield Life premium is authorised under regulation 10(7)(b) of the MediShield Life Regulations 2015.
Family members identified as potential payers have about one month to consider whether to proceed with this payment arrangement, before premium deduction takes place. To date, the majority of family members approached have continued with this arrangement while allowing a small number of individuals who decline to stop premium payment.
You may stop this payment arrangement by completing the “Stop Premium Payment for Dependant(s)’ MediShield Life Cover” via cpf.gov.sg/changepayer or call us at 1800-222-3399. Once you have indicated your intent, future MediShield Life premiums for the insured family member will not be deducted from your MediSave Account.
Should you subsequently change your mind and wish to take over paying the insured’s premiums after all, you will need to submit a "Change of Payer for MediShield Life Cover" application via cpf.gov.sg/changepayer.

questions.title: How were the Additional Withdrawal Limits determined?
questions.text:
The current Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) range from $300 to $900 depending on age, with higher limits for older policyholders.
The AWLs for IP premiums are set to strike a balance between helping Singapore Residents pay for IPs, which are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life, and conserving enough MediSave for basic healthcare expenses, especially in old age.

questions.title: How were the MediShield Life premium subsidies in my Premium Notice Letter (PNL) determined?
questions.text:
The different types of subsidies are as follows:
(a) Premium Subsidies for lower- to middle-income Singapore Residents. Eligibility for this subsidy will be subject to criteria such as household monthly income per person, Annual Value of residence and multiple property ownership.
(b) Special Pioneer Generation (PG) Subsidies for all PGs ranging from 40% - 60%.
(c) Additional Merdeka Generation (MG) Subsidies for all MGs, of 5% for those age 75 and below, increasing to 10% from 76 years old and above.
You may refer to the information booklet by using this link (medishieldlife.sg/infobooklet) for the computation of the various subsidies.

questions.title: How will I know the amount of premiums that I need to pay for my/ my dependents' Integrated Shield Plan (IP)?
questions.text: Your insurer administering the Integrated Shield Plan (IP) will notify you of your premium details before your policy is renewed. You can log into your insurer's web portal to check your IP premium amount or approach your insurer directly for further clarifications.

questions.title: How will my CareShield Life Supplement premiums be affected by the CareShield Life changes?
questions.text:
CareShield Life Supplements are offered by private insurers, and CareShield Life Supplement premiums are independent of CareShield Life.
Most Supplement benefits also stack independently on top of CareShield Life benefits, and would not be affected.
Supplement policyholders may wish to contact their insurers to enquire about any potential changes or impact to their Supplement policies.

questions.title: How will my CareShield Life Supplement premiums be affected by the CareShield Life changes?
questions.text:
CareShield Life Supplements are offered by private insurers, and CareShield Life Supplement premiums are independent of CareShield Life.
Most Supplement benefits also stack independently on top of CareShield Life benefits, and would not be affected.
Supplement policyholders may wish to contact their insurers to enquire about any potential changes or impact to their Supplement policies.

questions.title: How will Singaporeans' eligibility for CareShield Life means-tested premium subsidies be assessed?
questions.text: Means-tested premium subsidies for CareShield Life will depend on Singaporeans' household per capita income, the annual value of his or her residence, and the number of properties owned. Lower- and lower-middle income Singaporeans who own no more than one property, and live in residences with annual values up to $31,000 will be eligible for means-tested premium subsidies.

questions.title: How will Singaporeans’ eligibility for CareShield Life means-tested premium subsidies be assessed?
questions.text: Means-tested premium subsidies will depend on Singaporeans’ household per capita income, the annual value of his or her residence, and the number of properties owned. Lower- and lower-middle income Singaporeans who own no more than one property and live in residences with annual values up to $25,000 will be eligible for means-tested premium subsidies.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: How will the new Cancer Drug Treatment benefit under MediShield Life and MediSave impact my claims from 1 September 2022?
questions.text:
MediShield Life and MediSave will only cover treatments on the Cancer Drug List (CDL) from 1 September 2022. Each cancer drug treatment on the CDL will have its own MediShield Life claim limits and MediSave withdrawal limits.
You may refer to the CDL for the list of cancer drug treatments that are claimable under MediShield Life and MediSave, and their respective claim and withdrawal limits. Please consult your doctor if you wish to find out whether the treatment that you are currently undergoing is on the CDL.
The CDL will only come into effect for Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) on 1 April 2023, upon renewal or application. If you have an IP, you will continue to be covered under your current policy terms until it is renewed on or after 1 April 2023.

questions.title: I am (i) residing overseas or (ii) have renounced my Singapore Citizenship/Permanent Resident status. How do I pay my CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: I am a bankrupt and I do not have monies to pay the MediShield Life premiums for my child/dependant and myself. Will there be interest and penalty imposed on me?
questions.text:
A claim will be filed with the Private Trustee or Official Assignee for outstanding MediShield Life premiums (including interest and penalties) incurred prior to the date of your Bankruptcy Order.
You are required to pay any MediShield Life premiums incurred after the date of your Bankruptcy Order. Bankrupt parents/guardians remain liable to pay for their child/dependant's premiums.
If you face difficulties paying the premiums, you may apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). APS helps members who cannot pay their MediShield Life premiums after Government subsidies and have limited family support. Find out more information on APS by calling 1800-222-3399 (or +65 6222 3399) from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8).
The Ministry of Health will assess each APS application to ensure that assistance is provided to members who need financial support. They will notify you of your APS application status.

questions.title: I am a bankrupt and I remember I owe more MediShield Life premiums than what is shown in my notification and my Healthcare dashboard. How much should I pay?
questions.text:
We may have filed a claim with the Private Trustee or Official Assignee to recover your outstanding MediShield Life premiums (including interest and penalties) incurred prior to the date of your Bankruptcy Order. The amount filed will not be shown in your notifications as the amount may be recovered from your bankruptcy estate.
The notifications you receive are for the MediShield Life premiums incurred after the date of your Bankruptcy Order. You can apply for a Apply / Change GIRO for Payment of MediShield Life Premiums or seek a family member's help to perform Change of Payer for MediShield Life Cover to pay your outstanding premiums.
To make a voluntary top-up to your MediSave Account, you must obtain approval from the Private Trustee or Official Assignee. You can contact them at 1800 225 5529 (during office hours) or visit www.mlaw.gov.sg.

questions.title: I am a foreigner currently covered under MediShield Life. How can I pay for my MediShield Life Premiums if my CPF Account is closed?
questions.text:
When MediShield was replaced by MediShield Life, the Government had given concession to a small number of foreigners with MediShield cover to continue their coverage under MediShield Life.
With the closure of CPF accounts for all foreigners on 1 April 2024, foreigners covered under MediShield Life would need to pay by alternative means aside from their MediSave. For more information on how to change your payment mode, please write to us. If no alternative arrangements are made to continue paying premiums, the MediShield Life cover will be terminated without refund of past premiums paid.

questions.title: I am a Pioneer Generation member (Pioneers). How much subsidies will I receive for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text:
Pioneers Generation Subsidies range from 40% at age 65 to 60% at age 90.
The Government is committed to helping Pioneer Generation seniors aged 80 and above in 2014 by fully covering their MediShield Life premiums. This is done through a combination of Pioneer Generation Subsidies and MediSave top-ups. For younger Pioneers, their MediShield life premiums will be about half of the MediShield premiums after Pioneer Generation Subsidies and MediSave top-ups.
You can login to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' to check your coverage, premiums and subsidies.

questions.title: I am an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) policyholder. Am I eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies or Additional Premium Support (APS)?
questions.text: Integrated Shield Plan (IP) policyholders will be able to receive MediShield Life premium subsidies if they meet the eligibility criteria. However, they are not eligible for Additional Premium Support (APS), as APS is targeted at those with financial difficulties. Should you have difficulty paying your premiums, you may wish to consider terminating your IP and applying for APS.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Can I choose to receive the CareShield Life participation incentive as one lump sum?
questions.text: The participation incentive is meant to encourage those born in 1979 or earlier to join CareShield Life by helping to offset the annual premiums payable. As such, the Government has designed it to be spread over 10 years of premium payment.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Can I opt out from the CareShield Life scheme after joining (e.g. if I cannot afford the premiums)?
questions.text:
To make joining CareShield Life more convenient, you have been auto-enrolled from 1 December 2021, if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979, covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and did not develop severe disability at the point of auto-enrolment. You can choose to opt out by 31 December 2023 if you do not wish to join the scheme.
Those who are not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life. If you are in this group, you will have a 60-day free-look period from the commencement of your CareShield Life coverage, for you to consider your decision.
The Government will provide participation incentives of up to $2,500 ($250/year) to all Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier who join CareShield Life by 31 December 2023. Additional participation incentives of $1,500 ($150/year) will also be provided to Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens who join CareShield Life by 31 December 2023. The participation incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and will be used to offset premiums payable for each year.
To encourage more Singapore Citizens to join CareShield Life, those who join and are covered between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024 will receive participation incentives of up to $1,875 ($187.50/year). Additional participation incentives of $1,125 ($112.50) will be provided to Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens.
The Government will also provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to those who join CareShield Life, to ensure that no one who joins the scheme loses coverage due to financial difficulties. For this reason, after the applicable free-look periods, you will not be able to opt out from the scheme.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.
If you are a foreigner who become a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident from 1 October 2020 onwards, are born in 1979 or earlier and do not develop severe disability, CareShield Life will be mandatory for you.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Can I opt out from the CareShield Life scheme after joining (e.g. if I cannot afford the premiums)?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born between 1970 and 1979, who were covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and did not develop severe disability, were auto-enrolled to CareShield Life from 1 December 2021. You will not be able to opt out of CareShield Life as the deadline to opt out was 31 December 2023.
Those who are not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life. If you are in this group, you will have a 60-day free-look period from the commencement of your CareShield Life coverage, for you to review your decision.
The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to those who join CareShield Life, to ensure that no one who joins the scheme loses coverage due to financial difficulties. For this reason, after the applicable free-look periods, you will not be able to opt out from the scheme.
You may refer to the types of premium support available for more information. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.
CareShield Life is also mandatory for foreigners who become Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards and are born in 1979 or earlier, provided they do not have severe disability (if granted residency status from 1 October 2020 to 31 December 2025) or any disability (if granted residency status from 1 January 2026 onwards).

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Do I need to back pay premiums from age 30 to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
ElderShield premiums that ElderShield insureds have paid will be taken into account when computing their CareShield Life premiums. Insureds do not need to back pay for CareShield Life coverage starting from 30; they will only be paying for coverage going forward.
However, CareShield Life's annual premiums for older insureds will still be higher than those of younger insureds, as they have less years to spread their premium payment over.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I join CareShield Life, will I get premium rebates?
questions.text:
An independent council has been set up to regularly review and recommend premium and payout adjustments for CareShield Life, in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
Should the amount of claims be lower than expected, the council could recommend adjustments to future payouts and premiums (e.g. to reduce the rate of premium increases, or even lower the premiums). Conversely, if the amount of claims is higher than expected, the council could recommend adjustments (e.g. increase the rate of premium increases) to make the scheme more sustainable. A premium rebate is one possible mechanism within this framework.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I join CareShield Life, will I get premium rebates?
questions.text:
Premium rebates are dependent on the recommendations of the CareShield Life Council. The independent council has been set up to regularly review and recommend premium and payout adjustments for CareShield Life, in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
If there are fewer claims than expected, you might receive premium rebates or have your future premiums adjusted lower. However, if there are more claims than expected, your premiums might need to increase to keep the scheme sustainable.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I paid ElderShield 300/400 premiums previously but my policy lapsed due to non-payment of premiums, how will my CareShield Life premiums be affected?
questions.text:
As your ElderShield 300/400 policies have lapsed due to non-payment of premiums, you are no longer covered under ElderShield 300/400. Your premiums for CareShield Life will be based on the premiums for an uninsured individual.
Those who need assistance with their premium payment after subsidies and incentives will receive Additional Premium Support, and no one who joins CareShield Life will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I paid ESH300/400 premiums previously but my policy lapsed due to non-payment of premiums, how will my CareShield Life premiums be affected?
questions.text:
As your ElderShield 300/400 policies have lapsed, you are no longer covered under ElderShield 300/400. Your premiums for CareShield Life will be based on the premiums for an uninsured individual.
Those who need assistance with their premium payment after subsidies and incentives will receive Additional Premium Support, and no one who joins CareShield Life will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. What are my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You may wish to refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.
For those born in 1979 or earlier, your premium may have two components:
1. Base premium
All those born in 1979 or earlier and who join CareShield Life will pay a base premium. Base premiums are paid from the age you join until age 67, or for a period of 10 years for those who join at age 59 or older from 6 November 2021.
ElderShield 400 insureds who have been consistently on the scheme will only need to pay the base premium component if they join CareShield Life by 31 December 2021.
Base premiums are designed to increase regularly to support the regular increase in payouts but will remain flat after age 67 if they remain payable. From 2020 to 2025, the increase is 2% per year (excluding GST). Beyond that, premium and payout adjustments will be recommended by an independent CareShield Life Council, in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
2. Catch-up Component
You will need to pay a catch-up component, on top of the base premium, if:
i. You are an existing ElderShield 300 insured.
ii. You are not insured under ElderShield or have opted into ElderShield late.
iii. You are an existing ElderShield 400 insured who joined CareShield Life later (from 1 January 2022 onwards).
iv. Your ElderShield 300/400 policies have become reduced paid-up (i.e. you stopped paying premiums after a minimum number of years of premium payment, which qualifies you for a lower payout amount).
This is because you would not have paid as much premiums as those in the same cohort who had been consistently insured under the ElderShield 400 scheme and joined CareShield Life earlier.
The catch-up component will also be applicable to foreigners who become Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards.
The catch-up component is a flat amount paid over across 10 years and is paid on top of the base premium.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. What are my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You may refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.
For those born in 1979 or earlier, your premium may have two components:
1. Base premium
All those born in 1979 or earlier and join CareShield Life will pay a base premium. Base premiums are paid from the age you join until age 67, or for a period of 10 years for those who join at age 59 or older.
Base premiums are designed to increase regularly to support the regular increase in payouts but will remain flat after age 67 if they remain payable.
2. Catch-up Component
You will need to pay a catch-up component, on top of the base premium, if your ElderShield profile is any of the following prior to joining CareShield Life:
You are an existing ElderShield 300 insured.
You are not insured under ElderShield or have opted into ElderShield late.
You are an existing ElderShield 400 insured who joined CareShield Life from 1 January 2022 onwards.
Your ElderShield 300/400 policies have become reduced paid-up (i.e. you stopped paying premiums after a minimum number of years of premium payment, which qualifies you for a lower payout amount).
The catch-up component ensures consistency with those in the same cohort who had been consistently insured under the ElderShield 400 scheme and joined CareShield Life earlier.
The catch-up component will also be applicable to foreigners who become Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards.
The catch-up component is a flat amount paid across 10 years and is paid on top of the base premium.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Why are there no subsidies for the catch-up component when it looks so substantial?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1979 or earlier who join CareShield Life will pay a base premium that takes into account the premiums existing ElderShield 400 insureds in their cohort have already paid for ElderShield.
You will need to pay a catch-up component, on top of the base premium, if:
i. You are an existing ElderShield 300 insured.
ii. You are not insured under ElderShield or have opted into ElderShield late.
iii. You are an existing ElderShield 400 insured who joined CareShield Life later (from 1 January 2022 onwards).
iv. Your ElderShield 300/400 policies have become reduced paid-up (i.e. you stopped paying premiums after a minimum number of years of premium payment, which qualifies you for a lower payout amount).
The catch-up component will also be applicable to foreigners who become Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards.
The catch-up component is not subsidised to ensure parity in premium subsidies across different groups within those born in 1979 or earlier.
Nonetheless, for those who are unable to pay for their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support, so that no one who joins CareShield Life loses coverage due to financial difficulties.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Will I have to pay extra premiums if I join CareShield Life with pre-existing medical conditions?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1979 or earlier and have pre-existing medical conditions, you can choose to join CareShield Life if you do not develop severe disability. You will not need to pay additional premiums for pre-existing medical conditions.
You may wish to refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Will I have to pay extra premiums if I join CareShield Life with pre-existing medical conditions?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1979 or earlier and do not have disability, you can choose to join CareShield Life. You will not need to pay additional premiums for pre-existing medical conditions.
You may refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Will the premiums I had already paid under ElderShield be taken into account when I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: ElderShield premiums that ElderShield 300/400 insureds have already paid will be taken into account when computing their CareShield Life premiums. ElderShield Supplement premiums will not be taken into account when computing CareShield Life premiums. ElderShield Supplements provide coverage beyond ElderShield, and their benefits will continue to be recognised even if an ElderShield insured upgrades to CareShield Life, as long as the insured continues paying his Supplement premiums and does not terminate his Supplement coverage.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later and I have pre-existing severe disabilities. Will I need to pay premiums for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1980 or later, you will be able to enjoy protection under CareShield Life, regardless of your ability to pay premiums, even if you have pre-existing disabilities.
As part of collective responsibility, those with pre-existing disabilities should contribute one premium payment to join the scheme. The payment amount is less than the first monthly CareShield Life payout you will receive. Upon joining the scheme, you will continue to receive monthly payouts for as long as you are unable to do three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies, and Additional Premium Support to help those who are still unable to afford premiums even after subsidies. Claims will be paid out as long as insureds meet the claims criteria.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later, and I have pre-existing severe disabilities or medical conditions. Do I need to pay additional CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
All Singaporean Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, including those with pre-existing severe disabilities, will be able to enjoy benefits under CareShield Life, regardless of your ability to pay premiums. As such, you will not have to pay additional CareShield Life premiums.
As part of collective responsibility, those with pre-existing severe disabilities should contribute one premium to join the scheme. The payment amount is less than the first monthly CareShield Life payout you will receive. Upon joining the scheme, you will continue to receive monthly payouts for as long as you are unable to do three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies, and Additional Premium Support to help those who are still unable to afford premiums even after subsidies. Claims will be paid out as long as insureds meet the claims criteria.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: I am covered under CareShield Life. What is Additional Premium Support and who can qualify?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) is designed to help Singaporeans who cannot afford CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and payment by MediSave and have insufficient family support to rely on.
Please note that you will not be eligible for APS if you have an additional private medical insurance cover under an Integrated Shield Plan and/or Supplements under CareShield Life/ElderShield. You will also not be eligible for APS if you are paying the premiums of someone else's Integrated Shield Plan and/or Supplements under CareShield Life/ElderShield.

questions.title: I am currently covered under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) at standard premium rates. Will my premium increase after the introduction of premium loading?
questions.text: There will be no impact on your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premiums. Your HPS premium will remain the same.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I am currently insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS). Do I have to pay additional premiums when my HPS cover is extended to age 65?
questions.text: If you are insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme and wish to extend your coverage to age 65, you will need to pay additional premiums. This premium will be paid annually.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I am currently insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS). How can I extend my HPS cover until age 65?
questions.text:
Your Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will only insure you up to age 55 or 60. If your original housing loan is still outstanding by then, we will extend your HPS cover to age 65 by issuing you an Annual Premium (AP) HPS cover when your Single Premium HPS cover expires.
However, if you had restructured your housing loan and had been previously rejected by CPF Board for an increase to your HPS cover period or sum assured arising from the changes to your housing loan, you will not be eligible for the additional AP cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I am currently paying outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums through monthly GIRO instalments. Can I continue this arrangement to pay my future premiums?
questions.text:
If you have set up GIRO for healthcare renewal premiums, your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield renewal premiums shall be deducted from your GIRO bank account every year.
In the event of unsuccessful GIRO/ MediSave deduction for your renewal premiums, and you have an ongoing monthly GIRO arrangement, the renewal premiums will be included in your monthly GIRO payment plan.
Monthly GIRO instalment is only for payment of outstanding premiums (excluding renewal premiums). If your monthly payment arrangement has ended, you can request a new monthly instalment arrangement by writing to us at cpf.gov.sg/writetous.
If you have terminated your previous GIRO arrangement with the bank, you may re-apply by clicking on "Setting up GIRO arrangement".

questions.title: I am currently receiving Additional Premium Support under MediShield Life. Would I be given Additional Premium Support under CareShield Life?
questions.text:
An individual’s Additional Premium Support (APS) status will be shared across both CareShield Life and MediShield Life scheme. Therefore, MediShield Life insureds who are receiving APS will automatically receive APS for CareShield Life if it is within their APS validity period.
You will be notified in your premium notification letter of your APS status.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: I am currently receiving Additional Premium Support under MediShield Life. Would I be given Additional Premium Support under CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) status applies to both CareShield Life and MediShield Life schemes. If you currently receive APS for MediShield Life, you will automatically be granted APS for CareShield Life during your existing APS validity period.
Your premium notification letter will inform you of your APS status.

questions.title: I am living in Property A and have my registered address on my NRIC here. However, I own Property B too. Which Property address will be used for means-testing for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
The Annual Value (AV) of the address on your NRIC will be used. In this example, AV of Property A will be used for the eligibility checks for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies.
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who own two or more properties will not be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies. Other members of their households (who are not multiple property owners) will still be assessed for their eligibility for subsidies.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: I am on a Government Financial Assistance Scheme. Can I conserve my MediSave and apply Additional Premium Support to pay my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If you are currently on a Government financial assistance scheme, there is no need for you to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). You will automatically be granted APS if you have insufficient MediSave to pay your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums.
APS is a financial assistance scheme designed to support members who cannot afford their premiums even after subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support. If you have sufficient MediSave to pay your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums, you will not be eligible for APS.

questions.title: I am paying ElderShield premiums for myself and my dependants. How do I check the transaction details?
questions.text: You may view the deduction and refund transactions for ElderShield policies via the payer’s Transaction History at cpf.gov.sg (Singpass login is required).

questions.title: I am paying ElderShield premiums for myself and my dependants. How do I check the transaction details?
questions.text: If you are paying the ElderShield premiums for yourself and your dependants using your MediSave, you may view the deduction and refund transactions for the policies via Transaction History.

questions.title: I am paying the Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums for my dependants. Why is this information not reflected on my Yearly CPF Statement of Account?
questions.text: Your dependants’ details would not be reflected if you are not using your MediSave to pay for their Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums. However, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to view your dependants’ coverage information. The information is available under “Health insurance - Coverage and premiums details”.

questions.title: I am paying the premium for my family member's CareShield Life policy. How can I find out more information about their policy?
questions.text: If you are paying for your family members' CareShield Life premiums, you can log in to Healthcare dashboard 'CareShield Life/ElderShield' section for information on your and/or your dependants' CareShield Life premiums and subsidies.

questions.title: I am paying the premium for my family member’s CareShield Life policy. How can I find out more information about their policy?
questions.text: If you are paying for your family members’ CareShield Life premiums, you can view the details via Policies I Am Paying For.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: I am planning to live overseas permanently from next year onwards. Can I apply for the suspension of MediShield Life premium collection now?
questions.text: In order to qualify for suspension of premium collection, you must have resided outside Singapore for at least five years immediately preceding your application, except for short visits back to Singapore (not exceeding 140 days in total during the five years). As such, you may wish to apply only after you have fulfilled all the criteria.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: I am prescribed a drug that is not on the Cancer Drug List. Can I claim under the Cancer Drug Services Limit?
questions.text:
The cancer drug services limit is meant to cover ancillary services that patients may require as part of their cancer drug treatment.
If the drug you are prescribed is a supportive medication to manage the symptoms and side effects of your cancer drug treatment (e.g. antibiotics to reduce risk of infection, pain medication or anti-nausea medication), it is claimable under the Cancer Drug Services limit.
However, if the drug is used for the treatment of the cancer / tumour itself (e.g. chemotherapy, immunotherapy or targeted therapy), it should be claimed under the Cancer Drug Treatment limit instead. Cancer Drug Treatments that are not listed on the Cancer Drug List are not eligible for MediShield Life, MediSave and Integrated Shield Plan claims and should not be claimed under Cancer Drug Services limit.

questions.title: I am unsure of how to fill up the Additional Premium Support (APS) application form. Can I request an officer to help me with my APS application?
questions.text: If you require assistance to fill up or submit the Additional Premium Support (APS) application form, you may call us at 1800-222-3399 (or +65 6222 3399 from overseas) from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8) or write in through this online form. Our officers will guide you through the steps to fill up the APS application form.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I am using a family member’s MediSave to pay for my CareShield Life’s premium as I do not have a CPF account. What happens when my family member passes away?
questions.text:
Your CPF account will be automatically created when you make a top-up to MediSave using cash via the Top up MediSave Account online form with your Singpass.
Alternatively, other family members* can apply to take over as your premium payer using his/her MediSave. To do so, he/she may visit the Change Premium Payer e-Service and log in using his/her own Singpass to complete the “Change Premium Payer” transaction.
*Family member refers to the Insured's spouse, parents, children, siblings, or grandchildren.
Those who are unable to afford their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and have limited family support will be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support. No one will lose coverage under CareShield Life due to an inability to pay premiums.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: I am using a GIRO arrangement to pay my MediShield Life premiums. What happens to my GIRO when I upgrade to an Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text:
If you have applied for GIRO arrangement for your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums and upgrade to an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) subsequently, the GIRO arrangement for your MediShield Life premiums will cease. Your existing GIRO arrangement for CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums (if any) will remain unchanged. You will need to have a separate premium payment arrangement with the IP insurer.
If you switch back to MediShield Life subsequently and would like to use GIRO for your MediShield Life premiums, you must re-apply.

questions.title: I am using GIRO for my MediShield Life and/or ElderShield premiums. Do I need to re-apply when joining CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Yes, you must re-apply for GIRO when joining CareShield Life. Your current MediShield Life and/or ElderShield GIRO arrangement will not automatically extend to cover CareShield Life premiums.
If you opt out of CareShield Life and return to ElderShield, you do not need to re-apply as your earlier GIRO application was extended to ElderShield.

questions.title: I had previously disallowed access to my financial information for the purpose of CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility checks. How do I change this arrangement?
questions.text: To allow access to your financial information for the purpose of CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility checks, please update your status via this link and click "login to access your household information". If you need further assistance, please call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 (after selecting your preferred language, press 3, and then 2).

questions.title: I have a Letter of Guarantee (LOG) from my employer/insurer. How do I use it to pay for my medical expenses?
questions.text:
You may provide the Letter of Guarantee (LOG) to the hospital at admission. The hospital will be able to advise you on the billing arrangements and send the bill to your employer/insurer. If your employer/insurer is paying only part of your hospital expenses, the hospital will also assist you to submit the MediShield and MediSave claims on your behalf.
Please review the terms of your LOG carefully. For clarifications about your LOG or payment arrangements, please approach the hospital and/or employer/insurer directly.

questions.title: I have already paid for ElderShield premiums for this year. Will I get any refund if I apply to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The ElderShield premiums will be refunded if you join CareShield Life and your CareShield Life commencement date is in the same year as your ElderShield policy renewal.
For example, if you paid ElderShield Premiums in September 2021 (for your ElderShield policy renewal in 2021), and later joined CareShield Life in December 2021, the ElderShield premiums you have paid in September 2021 will be refunded to you.
The refund of ElderShield premiums (if any) will take place upon collection of the first CareShield Life premium.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have already paid for ElderShield premiums for this year. Will I get any refund if I apply to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The ElderShield premiums will be refunded if you join CareShield Life and your CareShield Life commencement date is in the same year as your ElderShield policy renewal.
For example, if you paid ElderShield Premiums in September 2021 (for your ElderShield policy renewal in 2021), and later joined CareShield Life in December 2021, the ElderShield premiums you have paid in September 2021 will be refunded to you.
The refund of ElderShield premiums (if any) will take place upon collection of the first CareShield Life premium.

questions.title: I have already submitted my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection. It is pending approval. Why am I still receiving reminder letters to pay my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The premiums for your MediShield Life cover are still payable while your application is being processed. If your application is successful, premium collection will be suspended prospectively from the next policy year based on the date of receipt of your application.
Any outstanding premiums prior to the start of the Suspension Period remain payable. Please make payment promptly with the payment modes available on CPF's website (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/i-am-i-residing-overseas-or-ii-have-renounced-my-singapore-citizenship-permanent-resident-status-how-do-i-pay-my-careshield-life-eldershield-medishield-life-premiums) to avoid any further enforcement action.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection
