questions.title: I have already submitted my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection. It is pending approval. Why am I still receiving reminder letters to pay my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The premiums for your MediShield Life cover are still payable while your application is being processed. If your application is successful, premium collection will be suspended prospectively from the next policy year based on the date of receipt of your application.
Any outstanding premiums prior to the start of the Suspension Period remain payable. Please make payment promptly with the payment modes available to avoid any further enforcement action.

questions.title: I have an ongoing monthly GIRO instalment plan. My MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life cover has been renewed and has incurred new outstanding premiums. Will interest be imposed on me?
questions.text: Interest will not be imposed on the new outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums while you have an ongoing monthly GIRO instalment arrangement. Your existing GIRO payment plan will be revised to include the new outstanding premiums. You will be notified of the revised instalment to be paid.

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. When will my premiums be deducted?
questions.text: Your CareShield Life premium will be automatically deducted from your or your payer’s MediSave within two months from your policy start date. Please ensure you have sufficient funds in your MediSave for CareShield Life premium payment.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. When will my premiums be deducted?
questions.text: Your CareShield Life premium will be automatically deducted from your or your payer's MediSave within two months from your policy start date. Please ensure you have sufficient funds in your MediSave for CareShield Life premium payment.

questions.title: I have been insured for many years but have not made a claim. Why should I remain insured under MediShield Life?
questions.text: Insurance provides protection against the risk of undesirable outcomes and financial costs. MediShield Life provides greater peace-of-mind if policyholders fall sick and incur a large bill. They can enjoy better protection, with payouts to reduce the amount that they need to pay using MediSave and/or cash.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: I have completed the review of my means-test eligibility under MediShield Life and would like to appeal for higher subsidies for other heathcare schemes. How can I do so?
questions.text: Please contact your service provider for further advice.

questions.title: I have received a call claiming to be from MediShield Life. What should I do if this is a scam and my contact details are shared with external agencies?
questions.text:
The MediShield Life Team does not contact members to request sensitive personal information or engage any external agencies to call members on MediShield Life matters. The MediShield Life Team will not disclose members’ contact details to external agencies without members’ consent.
If you receive an unexpected phone call from someone who claims to be from the MediShield Life Team, please be vigilant and do not provide your sensitive personal information (E.g. Singpass ID/password, bank account or credit card details). When in doubt, you may end the conversation with the individual and check with the organisation which the caller claims to represent directly. To verify the authenticity of such calls, you can call us directly at 1800 222 3399 or write to us.
topics: Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I have received a letter from MOH stating that my Additional Premium Support (APS) application was rejected. Why was I rejected and how do I appeal for APS?
questions.text:
Eligibility for Additional Premium Support (APS) is based on, but not limited to the applicants’ and his/her immediate family members’ financial means. As individuals’ circumstances differ from one another, each application will be assessed on a case-by-case basis to ensure that assistance is targeted at members who are needy.
You may submit your enquiry and reason(s) for APS appeal, with any relevant supporting documents through this online form.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I have received an Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore's (IRAS) notice and applied for GIRO payment arrangement for my healthcare premiums. Will interest be imposed on me?
questions.text: Interest and penalties will not be imposed on your outstanding MediShield Life and/ or CareShield Life premiums if CPF Board receives your GIRO application before the due date stated in IRAS' notice.

questions.title: I have recently bought an Integrated Shield Plan. Why was there more than one deduction made from my MediSave Account this year?
questions.text:
The first deduction from your MediSave Account (MA) was for the renewal of your MediShield Life (MSHL) coverage, which is mandatory for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
When you purchase an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), deductions were made for your IP, which comprises both the MSHL and additional private insurance components.
Since you have paid for your MSHL renewal, you will receive a pro-rated refund of the unused MSHL premiums for the remaining policy year.
For example, your MSHL coverage period was 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 and the annual MSHL premium of $435 was deducted in January 2025. You subsequently purchased an IP in February 2025 with an annual premium of $1,035. After you purchase the IP, the unused premium from your MSHL coverage of $398.75, will be refunded back to your MA.
*PMI = Additional private insurance coverage portion of an Integrated Shield Plan

questions.title: I have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. Why is it not reflected in the CareShield Life Premium Checker?
questions.text: If you have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, your appeal may still be processing and the outcome may not be reflected here. If you require assistance with your latest appeal or form submission, please contact us at Write to us or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premium Checker

questions.title: I have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. Why is it not reflected in the CareShield Life Premium Checker?
questions.text: If you have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, your appeal may still be processing and the outcome may not be reflected. If you require assistance with your latest appeal or form submission, please contact us at Write to us or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: I have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. Why is it not reflected in the CareShield Life Premium Checker?
questions.text:
If you have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, your appeal may still be processing and the outcome may not be reflected here.
If you require assistance with your latest appeal or form submission, please contact careshieldlife.gov.sg/writetous or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays). Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: I have redeemed $70 worth of premium discount but only $50 was used for my MediShield Life premiums. What happens to the remaining $20 of premium discount?
questions.text:
Any unused premium discounts will be carried forward and used for your MediShield Life premium at your next policy renewal, so long as these remain valid (premium discounts are valid for one year from the date of redemption).
For information on your premium discount, you may login to your Healthcare Dashboard.

questions.title: I have redeemed my Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts on the Healthy 365 app, but my Healthcare Dashboard shows no redemption. How long will it take for my Healthcare Dashboard to be updated?
questions.text:
After you have redeemed your Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts, your Healthcare Dashboard will be updated with your premium discount information instantly.
If the information does not appear, please log out of the CPF digital services and log back in to refresh your session.

questions.title: I have redeemed my Healthpoints on the Healthy 365 app for MediShield Life premium discounts. Can I use it to pay for my dependant’s MediShield Life or Integrated Shield Plan premiums?
questions.text:
The premium discounts you earn are designated for your own personal MediShield Life (MSHL) premiums and cannot be used to pay for your dependant’s MSHL or Integrated Shield Plan premiums.
Similarly, the premium discounts redeemed by your family members can only be applied to their respective MSHL premiums, regardless of who their premium payer is.

questions.title: I have renounced my citizenship and applied to withdraw my CPF savings. Will my application be affected if I choose not to pay the outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Your withdrawal application will be processed even if you have outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums.
However, you are advised to fully pay your outstanding premiums to avoid enforcement actions by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). To do so, please click on the link below to view the payment options.
I have renounced my citizenship/am residing overseas without local bank account. How do I pay my outstanding MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: I intend to visit a clinic/hospital. How do I know if I can use MediShield Life coverage in that clinic/hospital?
questions.text:
You can refer to this list of medical institutions participating in MediShield Life.
To make a claim, please inform the staff handling your hospital admission or outpatient treatment that you wish to do so. The staff will submit your claim for you after your authorisation.

questions.title: I made a top-up to my MediSave for payment of CareShield Life premium. Has the top-up been credited?
questions.text: You may view the top-up you made to your MediSave via Transaction History at cpf.gov.sg (Singpass login is required).
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: I need to submit a reimbursement to my employee, platform worker or insured's MediSave and/or MediShield Life. How do I go about doing it?
questions.text:
You can submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements to your employee, platform worker or insured quickly and easily via CPF's online reimbursement system, also known as the Internet Reimbursement (IR) service.
Learn more about how to submit a reimbursement via the IR service.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I noticed that I need to fill in the Hospital Registration Number (HRN) for submitting reimbursement via E-File. How do I obtain the HRN?
questions.text:
The Hospital Registration Number (HRN) can be found in the following documents:
Your employee, platform worker or insured’s final medical bill
Your employee, platform worker or insured’s Healthcare Payments and Claims Statement
Your employee, platform worker or insured’s MediSave Transaction Statement
Please refer to this guide for more information on where to find the HRN.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I only turn 40 in December, but my policy year renewal is in November, will I be able to redeem premium discounts before that?
questions.text: You will be able to redeem MediShield Life premium discounts in the year that you turn 40, regardless of when your birthday is.

questions.title: I previously applied for Additional Premium Support but was rejected. Can I apply for assistance again to help pay my premiums for the next policy year?
questions.text:
As you were previously assessed to be ineligible to receive Additional Premium Support (APS), we encourage you to pay your outstanding premiums (if any) via any of the options enclosed in the Rejection for Additional Premium Support Application Letter (Ref: APCREJ).
You may re-apply for APS if there is a change in your financial circumstances or if you face any extenuating circumstances that were not highlighted during your previous application.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I purchased an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) for my employee. Can they downgrade to MediShield Life again?
questions.text: Yes, employees can choose to downgrade from their IP to MediShield Life at any time. Their MediShield cover will not be subject to further underwriting.

questions.title: I realised that I submitted the same reimbursement multiple times via E-File. What should I do?
questions.text:
If you submit duplicate reimbursements on the same day before 5:30pm, the most recent submission will override the previous one, and only the latest file will be processed.
If you have submitted duplicate reimbursements on different days, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I received a Final Reminder notification regarding my outstanding CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums, will the amount payable still be increased?
questions.text:
The Final Reminder notification shows the amount of your outstanding CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums as at the date sent.
Please pay your full outstanding premiums by the deadline indicated in the notification. Otherwise, the amount payable will increase as the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) will impose compounded interest of 4% and penalties of up to 17% on your outstanding premiums. To do so, please click on the link below for the payment options.
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)s' CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: I received an application form each for myself and my child. I wish to apply for myself and my child. Can I submit only one application form?
questions.text:
You only need to submit one application form for yourself if your child is below 21 years old. Please indicate in the application form that you are applying for Additional Premium Support (APS) for yourself (Main Applicant). If you are assessed to be eligible for APS, we will automatically extend APS to your child.
However, if your child is above 21 years old, he/she will need to submit a separate application form with himself/herself as the Main Applicant.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I received the Additional Premium Support application form. Who are considered as my immediate family members to be included in the application form?
questions.text: Immediate family members refer to parents, spouse and children who is/are related to the Main Applicant by blood, marriage and/or legal adoption, but does not refer to other family members such as siblings, grandparents and grandchildren.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I submitted reimbursements via E-File today, but realised there was a mistake in my submission after submitting the Excel file. What should I do?
questions.text:
You can override your previous submission by resubmitting the corrected file before 5:30pm on the same day.
For further clarification, please write to us.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I turned 55 before 2016 and joined CPF LIFE at 55. Will the premium deducted for CPF LIFE continue to earn interest?
questions.text: Yes, regardless of the age that you join CPF LIFE, the amount deducted from your Retirement Account savings for the CPF LIFE premium continues to earn CPF interest rates with the floor rate of 4% and up to 2% extra interest on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances. The interest earned is factored into your monthly payouts, allowing you to receive higher lifelong payouts compared to other annuities offered in the market.

questions.title: I want to appeal for higher CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. Where can I do so?
questions.text:
If you wish to have your eligibility for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies reassessed, you may submit your request via the MediShield Life e-Service. You may also contact us at careshieldlife.gov.sg/writetous or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays).
Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: I want to appeal for higher MediShield Life Premium Subsidies. Where/How can I do so?
questions.text:
If you wish to have your eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies reassessed, you may submit your request via the MediShield Life e-Service. You may also write to us at medishieldlife.sg/writetous or call our hotline at 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays).
Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: I want to get the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) but my insurer’s premiums are higher than other insurers. Should I switch to a Standard IP under another insurer?
questions.text:
If you switch to a Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) with another insurer, your original IP under your original insurer will be automatically terminated.
You will also need to undergo underwriting when you switch to the plan under the new insurer. As such, you may lose coverage for existing medical conditions covered by your original plan, and may not be able to re-apply for your original coverage later.
Please speak to your financial advisor to find out more about the implications of switching insurers before making your decision. Please also highlight any medical conditions you have to your financial advisor.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: I was admitted to a Class A/B1 ward. Why are the pro-ration factors lowered from 1 April 2025 and how will this affect my MediShield Life claim?
questions.text:
As private hospital bills and Class A/B1 bills in public hospitals are generally higher than the Class B2/C bills that MediShield Life is designed for, they are pro-rated or normalised to the equivalent level of a Class B2/C bill before MediShield Life payouts are computed to ensure payouts are comparable.
With private and unsubsidised bills growing faster than subsidised bills, the pro-ration factors have been reduced to ensure MediShield Life payouts are comparable across different settings and to reduce cross-subsidisation .
Patients who seek private or unsubsidised care should now see comparable payouts to subsidised patients.

questions.title: I was born in 1979 or earlier and would like to opt out of CareShield Life. When will the premiums be refunded to my MediSave if I opt out?
questions.text:
You will not be able to opt out from CareShield Life after the applicable opt-out/free-look period. If you choose to opt out of CareShield Life within the applicable opt-out/free-look period, you will be given a full premium refund after one working day. If you were covered by ElderShield prior to your enrolment into CareShield Life, you will be automatically placed back onto your original ElderShield scheme.
You may view the refund made to your MediSave via Transaction History at cpf.gov.sg (Singpass login is required).
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I was born in 1979 or earlier. Will the ElderShield premiums I have already paid be taken into account when I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you were continuously insured under ElderShield before joining CareShield Life, your past ElderShield premiums will be taken into account when computing your CareShield Life premiums, resulting in lower premiums. Your premiums will be lower compared to those in the same cohort who were not insured under ElderShield.

questions.title: I was notified by the Medical Institution that my employee, platform worker or insured's medical bill was cancelled or amended. How can I make changes to the reimbursement I submitted earlier?
questions.text: If you need to amend the MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement you previously submitted, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I wish to check the amount claimed from my MediShield Life coverage for my recent hospitalisation. How can I do so?
questions.text:
You can view the details of your MediShield Life claims (with transaction dates within the last 15 months from the date of enquiry) at cpf.gov.sg/healthcare:
1. Login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass
2. Proceed to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims'
3. Select and view the details of your recent healthcare payments and claims. To view more claims, click on 'View past 15 months'.
4. Click on 'View details' under MediShield Life to view the claim details.

questions.title: I would like to check my latest subsidy eligibility for other healthcare schemes. How can I do so?
questions.text:
Please contact your service provider to find out more information on your current or latest subsidy eligibility.
For more information on other healthcare schemes, their eligibility criteria and corresponding subsidy framework, please visit https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies.

questions.title: I'm residing overseas and do not require MediShield Life, how do I withdraw from MediShield Life?
questions.text:
MediShield Life provides universal coverage to Singapore Citizens (SCs) and Permanent Residents (PRs) so that they have assurance against large healthcare bills. MediShield Life is mandatory for all SCs and PRs, as by sharing in the national risk pool, Singapore residents collectively play our part in supporting our healthcare costs.
The MediShield Life Council (MLC) recognises that there is a small and distinct group of Overseas Singaporeans (OS) who live outside Singapore permanently, have no intention to reside in Singapore, and feel that they will not benefit from MediShield Life.
If you belong to the OS group, you can apply for a suspension of premium collection even though you will remain covered under MediShield Life. You can refer to the Suspension of MediShield Life Premium Collection for more information on the eligibility criteria and application process.

questions.title: If I am currently insured under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS), how much premium refund will I get if my application to be exempted from HPS is approved?
questions.text: If you are successful in the exemption application, your existing HPS cover will be terminated. You will get a full premium refund into your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) provided that the exemption application is received (by the Board) within one month from the issuance of the HPS cover. Otherwise, a pro-rated refund will be credited to your OA upon the termination of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I am currently using GIRO to pay premiums, can I top up my MediSave to pay my MediShield Life/CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
You can top up your MediSave Account at any time, but your healthcare renewal premiums will continue to be deducted from your GIRO bank account unless you terminate the GIRO arrangement with your bank.
If you are currently on monthly GIRO instalments, topping up your MediSave Account will help pay off outstanding premiums. Your monthly GIRO deduction amount will remain unchanged, but the payment plan will end earlier once all outstanding premiums are fully paid.
You can top up your MediSave Account via the Top up MediSave Account online form. MediSave top-ups are generally credited within three working days and will be automatically deducted for premium payment(s). You can check your premium amounts on your Healthcare dashboard under the "Long-term care insurance" and "Health insurance" sections to determine how much to top up.
You may view the MediSave top-up(s) and premium deduction(s) in your Transaction history at cpf.gov.sg.
As MediSave top-ups could be deducted for healthcare premiums and medical expenses based on when deductions are due, please ensure that you have sufficient MediSave for all payments.

questions.title: If I am currently using my Special Account (SA) for Dependants' Protection Scheme premiums, how would I be impacted by the closure of SA?
questions.text:
After your Special Account (SA) closes at age 55, your Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) premiums can only be paid from your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), subject to available balance, or in cash directly to the appointed DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life.
Transition measures are in place to provide short-term support to members immediately affected by the SA closure. These members will be notified directly and advised on the necessary steps to take.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: If I am offered a Home Protection Scheme cover with premium loading, what will be my premium payable?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme premiums are calculated based on several factors:
Outstanding housing loan on the flat
Loan repayment period
Type of loan (HDB concessionary or market rate)
Age and gender
Percentage share of cover of the outstanding housing loan
The amount of premium loading depends on the seriousness of your pre-existing health condition. If you are offered cover with premium loading, the Board will inform you of the total premium amount payable and you may decide whether to take it up.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I am self-employed/retired/become unemployed before age 67, will I be able to afford CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: The Government will provide CareShield Life premium subsidies for lower- and middle-income insureds. Singaporeans who are unable to afford premiums even after premium subsidies can be assisted by Additional Premium Support. No one will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: If I am self-employed/retired/become unemployed before age 67, will I be able to afford CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: The Government will provide CareShield Life premium subsidies for lower- and middle-income insureds. For those who are unable to pay for their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support. No one will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.

questions.title: If I have an existing regular premium insurance policy bought using cash, can I continue to service the future premiums using CPF under the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA)?
questions.text: With effect from 1 January 2001, CPF savings cannot be used for new regular premium insurance policies, regardless of whether the policies are converted from cash or newly bought from insurance companies.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: If I have renounced my citizenship, will interest and penalty still be imposed on my outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text: You need to pay your MediShield Life premiums incurred prior to your renouncement date of your citizenship. If your premiums remain outstanding, compounded interest of 4% and penalties of up to 17% will be imposed and enforcement actions will be taken.

questions.title: If I have terminated my insurance policy bought using CPF, can I reinstate the policy and pay the outstanding premiums and future premiums using CPF?
questions.text: You need to liaise with your insurance company on the reinstatement of the policy. Upon reinstatement, you may pay the outstanding and future premiums using CPF. However, no CPF can be used to pay any outstanding interest owing to the insurance company.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: If I received a payout from MediShield or MediShield Life during the past five years, can I apply for suspension of premium collection?
questions.text: The suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is meant for Singapore Citizens living outside Singapore permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore. One of the eligibility criteria for the suspension of premium collection is that the applicant has adequate healthcare coverage in their country of residence and does not need to rely on MediShield Life. If you have received a payout and benefitted from MediShield or MediShield Life in the five years preceding your application, you will not be eligible for suspension of premium collection.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: If I reside overseas, can I suspend my premium payment for CareShield Life?
questions.text: CareShield Life will provide monthly cash payouts in the event of severe disability. Today, overseas Singaporeans are able to file ElderShield claims from abroad and receive payouts to support their care costs wherever they may be. This applies even for those who have permanently relocated abroad. This will continue to apply for CareShield Life. Hence, premium payments for overseas Singaporeans cannot be suspended.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: If I reside overseas, can I suspend my premium payment for CareShield Life?
questions.text: Premium payments for CareShield Life cannot be suspended for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents residing overseas. Individuals insured under CareShield Life will receive monthly cash payouts in the event of severe disability even when residing overseas. Similarly, insured under ElderShield can file claims from abroad and receive payouts to support their care costs wherever they may be. This applies even for those who have permanently relocated abroad.

questions.title: If I run out of CPF monies to pay the premiums of my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policies, what should I do?
questions.text:
You have the following options:
Use cash to pay the premiums;
Convert your Part V insurance policies to a paid-up mode1; or
Activate the Automatic Premium Loan (APL)2 or Extended Term Insurance (ETI)3 feature(s) of your Part V insurance policies, if they have such features and if your insurance company allows you to do so.
1 Converting a policy to paid-up mode means that the policyholder will not need to pay premiums anymore. The sum assured of a paid-up policy is usually lower than that of the original policy. All supplementary riders attached will be terminated.
2 APL means that once the policy has accumulated sufficient cash value, if the policyholder is unable to pay the premium, he can borrow from the cash value. However, he is required to pay back the loan and compound interest. Once the loan plus compound interest exceeds the cash value of the policy, the policy will lapse.
3 ETI means that if the policyholder still wants the insurance protection but doesn't want to pay any more premiums, the existing cash value of his policy is treated as a single premium which is used to buy protection for future years. The number of years of protection he will get varies directly with the quantum of the cash value.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: If I switch from a higher coverage Integrated Shield Plan (IP) to the Standard IP with the same insurer, will I need to go through additional underwriting and will my previous exclusions remain?
questions.text:
If you are intending to switch to a plan with lower coverage within the same insurer, you will not need to go through additional underwriting.
However, any exclusions on medical conditions you had on your original Integrated Shield Plan (IP) will be retained when you switch to a new plan.
You may wish to speak to your financial advisor who will be able to advise on your options.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: If I top up my MediSave to pay my CareShield Life premiums, does it count towards the MediSave amount that a self-employed person needs to contribute?
questions.text: The top-up to your MediSave to pay for your CareShield Life premiums is a Voluntary Top-up and can be used to offset the MediSave payable for the Self-Employed Scheme.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: If I top up my MediSave to pay my Healthcare premiums, does it count towards the MediSave amount that a self-employed person needs to contribute?
questions.text: The top-up to your MediSave for the purpose of paying your Healthcare premiums, cannot be used to offset your MediSave payable under the Self-Employed scheme. For self-employed persons who wish to make payment for your outstanding MediSave payable, please visit Manage your MediSave payable.

questions.title: If I used cash, MediSave and MediShield Life for my medical bill, is there a specific order in which my employer or insurer should perform the reimbursement?
questions.text:
Subject to contractual obligations, your employer or insurer should reimburse you in the following order:
i. Cash reimbursement - For the amount you paid in cash.
ii. MediSave reimbursement - For the amount utilised from your payer's or your MediSave Account.
iii. MediShield Life reimbursement - For the amount utilised from your MediSave-approved Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life.
This order minimises your cash outlay and restores the balances in your MediSave Account.

questions.title: If my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved, what happens if I wish to return to Singapore to seek medical treatment and claim from MediShield Life in future?
questions.text:
One of the eligibility criteria for the suspension of premium collection is that the applicant has adequate healthcare coverage in their country of residence and does not need to rely on MediShield Life. Hence, if you return to Singapore to seek medical treatment and claim from MediShield Life, your suspension of premium collection will be terminated. You will have to pay the full sum of premiums suspended from collection, with compound interest.
Please contact the Central Provident Fund Board for further information.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: If my application is approved, when will suspension of MediShield Life premium collection start?
questions.text: If your application is approved, suspension of MediShield Life premium collection will start prospectively from the next policy year based on the date of receipt of the application by the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: If my caregiver is currently the payer for my MediShield Life premiums, will he automatically become the payer for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Your caregiver will not automatically become the payer for your CareShield Life premiums.
Caregivers can apply to take over as the family member’s* premium payer using his/her MediSave. To do so, he/she may visit the Change Premium Payer e-Service and log in using his/her own Singpass to complete the “Change Premium Payer” transaction.
*Family member refers to the Insured's spouse, parents, children, siblings or grandchildren.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: If my employees, platform workers or insureds have used their MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses, do I need to reimburse them?
questions.text: As an employer, platform operator or insurer, you are required to reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave and/or MediShield Life if you have a contractual obligation to cover their medical expenses.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: If my health condition is such that I am offered a Home Protection Scheme cover with premium loading, is it compulsory to take up this cover?
questions.text: Members who are offered Home Protection Scheme (HPS) covers with premium loading can decide whether or not to take up the HPS cover. Participation in this scheme will be on an opt-in basis for them.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If my medical condition has improved, how can I request a review of the premium loading on my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover?
questions.text:
If your medical condition has improved, you may request a review of your Home Protection Scheme premium loading. Write to us with your request and provide a medical report at your own cost.
Your medical report must be up-to-date from a medical institution in Singapore, clearly indicate improvement in your medical condition and include the following information:
Diagnosis and diagnosis date
Reason(s) of hospitalisation, if any
Details of treatment(s)
Date(s) and details of surgery, if any
Details of complications, if any, and treatment rendered
Current condition and treatment(s)
Investigation test results
If your current condition still presents similar health risks, your premium loading will remain unchanged. We will assess your request and notify you of the outcome.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If there are insufficient funds in my MediSave Account, can I use my Ordinary Account/Special Account monies to pay for my MediShield Life, CareShield Life or ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
The savings in your CPF accounts are for specific uses. Savings in your Ordinary Account and Special Account are primarily for housing and retirement, while savings in your MediSave are for the payment of selected healthcare insurance premiums (such as MediShield Life and CareShield Life or ElderShield premiums) and hospitalisation expenses.
Thus, you are unable to use the savings in your Ordinary Account and Special Account to pay for your healthcare insurance premiums.
If you do not have sufficient MediSave to pay your premiums, you will be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS).
Alternatively, you may also top up your MediSave Account (visit Top up MediSave Account form with your Singpass) or approach a family member to help you pay the premiums using his/her MediSave by visiting the Change Payer e-Service to complete the transaction.

questions.title: If there are insufficient funds in my MediSave, can I use my Ordinary/Special Account monies to pay for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The savings in your CPF accounts are for specific uses. Savings in your Ordinary Account and Special Account are primarily for housing and retirement, while savings in your MediSave are for the payment of selected healthcare insurance premiums (such as MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums) and hospitalisation expenses.
Thus, you are unable to use the savings in your Ordinary Account and Special Account to pay for your CareShield Life premiums.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: In what order should I reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds if they have paid for medical expenses using cash, MediSave and MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Subject to contractual obligations, the reimbursement order should be as follows:
Amount paid in cash
Amount utilised from your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave
Amount utilised from your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave-approved Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life
This order minimises your employees, platform workers or insureds' cash outlay, and preserves their MediSave for future use.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Is it compulsory to reflect MediShield Life computations in all financial counselling materials?
questions.text:
It is not compulsory to compute estimated MediShield Life payouts in all financial counselling materials. Licensees are, however, required to share the applicable MediShield Life benefits (e.g., deductible, co-insurance, claim limits, etc) and MediSave withdrawal limits for the treatment or procedure that the patient is undergoing to the patient or the patient’s authorised representative.
Licensees may share an estimate of MediShield Life payout and MediSave deduction amounts, and should ensure that these estimates are reasonably accurate. A calculator for such estimates is currently available on the CPFB website, and within public licensees’ systems.

questions.title: Is there an age limit for existing CPF LIFE members to increase their CPF LIFE premium?
questions.text: Existing CPF LIFE members can increase their CPF LIFE premium at any age which will help to increase their CPF LIFE monthly payouts.

questions.title: Many individuals purchase Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders despite MediShield Life provides adequate protection for subsidised care in public hospitals. What is being done to improve consumer education around IPs and riders?
questions.text:
Ministry of Health (MOH) and CPF Board (CPFB) are enhancing public education about healthcare financing through several initiatives.
The Health Insurance Planner helps you evaluate your coverage needs and long-term affordability based on your care preferences and financial situation.
MOH launched a healthcare financing education campaign in June 2024 to explain how different insurance schemes work together. They also started publishing comparisons of lifetime premiums across Integrated Shield Plans (IPs). These complement existing resources on MOH's website about IP benefits, features, premiums, and insurer service indicators like claims processing times.
Additionally, MOH and CPFB collaborate with MoneySense, Singapore's national financial education programme, to provide guidance on IP purchases through educational articles and resources.
These efforts aim to help Singaporeans understand how MediShield Life coverage can meet their needs for subsidised care in public hospitals, and to weigh the costs and benefits of additional private coverage.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: My cancer drug treatment is on a 3-weekly cycle. Is the cancer drug limit sufficient for months when I need to undergo 2 rounds of treatment?
questions.text:
For cost-effective cancer drug treatments on 3-weekly cycles, the MediShield Life (MSHL) claim limits have typically been sized to cover the post-subsidy costs of two treatment courses in a month.
For other cancer drug treatments, the MSHL claim limit has been sized to cover up to the monthly cost of the cost-effective alternative.

questions.title: My child is less than five years old. How will he meet the overseas residency qualifying period of five years?
questions.text: Minors less than five years old will have their overseas residency qualifying period eligibility criteria correspondingly reduced, according to their age. All other criteria will apply. Parents may submit the application on behalf of minors below 21 years old.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: My employee is currently covered under MediShield Life. What will happen to their MediShield Life cover if I buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) for them?
questions.text: All Integrated Shield Plans (IP) have a MediShield Life component and an additional private insurance component. Hence, your employee’s MediShield Life cover will continue when you buy them an IP. In addition, they will not have exclusions for their MediShield Life cover, even if there are exclusions for the additional private insurance component of their IP.

questions.title: My family member is covered under the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS). Can I pay their DPS premium using my CPF savings?
questions.text:
No, your CPF savings cannot be used to pay your family member's Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) premium. This is to ensure that your CPF savings, which are generally meant to meet your retirement needs, are not depleted prematurely.
However, if you wish to help your family member, you may do so by paying their premium in cash directly to the appointed DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life (GEL). Visit GEL’s website for detailed instructions and forms.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: My family members are covered with free Integrated Shield Plan (IPs) provided by a private insurer. Do I still need to pay MediShield Life premiums for them?
questions.text: If your family members are covered with free Integrated Shield Plans (IPs), please check directly with your insurer who is administering the IPs if you still need to pay MediShield Life premiums for them.

questions.title: My reimbursement submission via E-File is unsuccessful, and I received a rejection reason. How should I correct my submission?
questions.text: Please refer to the common rejected reasons and their corresponding corrective actions before resubmitting.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Some riders have claims-based pricing, where premiums are adjusted based on claims made by the policyholder in the preceding year. Is this considered in the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: The Health Insurance Planner does not account for claims-based pricing in riders. For specific information about how your claims history might affect your rider premiums, please contact your insurer or financial advisor.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: The Health Insurance Planner shows that I may have insufficient MediSave for my healthcare expenses and insurance premiums. Will I lose my insurance coverage?
questions.text:
No one will lose coverage to MediShield Life, our national health insurance scheme, due to an inability to pay their premiums.
If you face difficulty paying for MediShield Life premiums even after subsidies and MediSave, help is available through schemes like Additional Premium Support.
When choosing or renewing Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders, consider both your coverage needs and long-term financial ability. Think about whether you have enough income and cash savings to cover expenses beyond what MediSave can pay.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: The majority of Singapore Residents are covered under Integrated Shield Plans. Are they eligible for subsidies?
questions.text:
Yes, Singapore Residents covered under Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) will also receive the applicable subsidies for MediShield Life premiums if they meet the eligibility criteria.
IPs are made up of 2 components: (i) the MediShield Life component and (ii) the additional private insurance component providing additional coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays.
Subsidies for those who are insured under IPs will be applied only on the MediShield Life component of the IP premiums.

questions.title: The use of Annual Value / Multiple Property Ownership as an assessment criterion for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies will overlook ‘asset-rich, cash-poor’ citizens. Is there any flexibility that can be extended to these citizens if they face difficulty with their premiums?
questions.text:
In general, Government subsidies are targeted at those in greater need. The assessment approach for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies uses the household monthly income per person and Annual Value (AV) of homes as a way to assess the household’s means and better target these subsidies. In addition, those who own multiple properties will not be eligible for Premium Subsidies.
The household assessment process strikes a balance between being more precise in assessing applicants’ means and keeping the process simpler for applicants and administratively practical. While the approach is not perfect, it provides us with a fair and objective basis to take a person's income and wealth into consideration.
Policyholders who are unable to afford their premiums even after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support, may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support, which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years. In the event of extenuating circumstances, appeals will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

questions.title: Under what circumstances would I be required to pay the accumulated sum of premiums suspended from collection with compound interest?
questions.text: You would only have to pay the accumulated sum of premiums suspended from collection with compound interest if (a) you choose to relocate back to Singapore, (b) no longer meet the eligibility criteria for suspension of premium collection, or (c) choose to claim and benefit from MediShield Life payouts. Once this happens, your suspension of MediShield Life premium collection will cease and you will have to pay the full sum of premiums suspended from collection, with compound interest.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: What are Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) for Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums?
questions.text:
MediSave is sized to help Singaporeans pay lifelong healthcare expenses. This include paying for hospitalisation bills and healthcare insurance premiums.
The premiums you pay for your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) consist of both the MediShield Life (MSL) and additional private insurance components. MSL premiums can be paid fully using MediSave. However, premiums for the additional private insurance component that is offered by private insurers are subject to the Additional Withdrawal Limit (AWL). The AWL strikes a balance between the use of MediSave for the higher private insurance coverage and preserving MediSave for future healthcare expenses during retirement.
The AWLs that apply to the additional private insurance coverage component of your IP premiums vary according to age as follows:
Age Next BirthdayAWLs
1 - 40$300
41 – 70$600
>= 71$900
Your IP insurer will collect the portion of your private insurance component premium that exceeds the AWL from you in cash.
As healthcare needs and premiums increase with age, planning for these costs is essential. Consider whether co-paying the higher IP premiums using cash is affordable for you over the long-term without straining your retirement savings.

questions.title: What are CPF LIFE premiums invested in and are the investments safe?
questions.text: CPF LIFE premiums are invested in Special Singapore Government Securities (SSGS), which are safe instruments because they are issued and guaranteed by the Government, and shielded from financial market fluctuations.

questions.title: What are Integrated Shield Plans and should I consider getting one?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) provide additional coverage beyond MediShield Life. IPs comprise 2 components:
(i) the MediShield Life component administered by the Central Provident Fund Board, and
(ii) the additional private insurance component by private insurers that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays. There is no duplicate coverage between MediShield Life and IPs.
The list of IPs and comparison of their coverage and premiums can be found here.
As IPs provide additional coverage, premiums for IPs are higher than MediShield Life’s, and they are only payable by MediSave up to the Additional Withdrawal Limits below.
