questions.title: What is the priority of Home Protection Scheme deduction if my family member has authorised the Board to deduct my premium from their CPF Ordinary Account?
questions.text: The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium will first be deducted from the available balance in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) followed by your family member's OA.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What is the pro-ration factor? How does it affect my claim?
questions.text: As private hospital bills and Ward A/B1 bills in public hospitals are generally higher than the Ward B2/C bills that MediShield Life is designed for, they are pro-rated to the equivalent level of a Ward B2/C bill before MediShield Life payouts are computed. This ensures comparable payouts for subsidised and private patients.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: What is the processing time for my Additional Premium Support (APS) Application?
questions.text:
Your application will be processed upon receipt of your completed application form and supporting documents where relevant.
The processing time is generally up to 20 working days for most cases as each APS application undergoes a thorough and careful assessment, including taking into consideration any extenuating circumstances that the applicant may be facing.
You will receive a letter to inform you on the outcome of your APS application.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: What is the rationale for imposing Goods and Services Tax (GST) on CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: We have a broad-based Goods and Services Tax (GST) system, with minimal exemptions as this approach helps to keep the GST rate relatively low. GST is a tax on domestic consumption of goods and services, and is payable on insurance contracts such as health, motor, and fire insurance. GST is therefore payable on premiums for CareShield Life.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: What is the rationale for imposing Goods and Services Tax (GST) on ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: We have a broad-based Goods and Services Tax (GST) system, with minimal exemptions as this approach helps to keep the GST rate relatively low. GST is a tax on domestic consumption of goods and services, and is payable on insurance contracts such as health, motor, and fire insurance. GST is therefore payable on premiums for ElderShield.

questions.title: What is the rationale for imposing Goods and Services Tax (GST) on MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: We have a broad-based Goods and Services Tax (GST) system, with minimal exemptions as this approach helps to keep the GST rate relatively low. GST is a tax on domestic consumption of goods and services, and is payable on insurance contracts such as health, motor, and fire insurance. Therefore, it applies to MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums.

questions.title: What is the Standard Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text:
The Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is an IP offered by private insurers targeted at covering Ward B1 or equivalent bills in public hospitals.
As the Standard IP benefits are set by the Government and identical across all IP insurers, the Standard IP gives Singapore Residents a standardised option for additional coverage beyond MediShield Life. It is also a viable option for those who want to switch from their Class A IP and Private Hospital IP to a more affordable plan.
Similar to other IPs, the Standard IP comprises the MediShield Life component and the additional private insurance component. Premiums for the additional private insurance component are set by the private insurers.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: What should I do if I want to get advice or make changes to my coverage (e.g. Integrated Shield Plan (IP) and rider) after using the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
After using the Health Insurance Planner, you can download a report containing your personalised projections and Integrated Shield Plan (IP) comparisons for reference during discussions with your insurer or financial advisor.
Please note that the planner's projections are for illustration only and should not be taken as financial advice from CPF Board or Ministry of Health. To make changes to your coverage:
If you are staying with your current insurer but want to downgrade to a lower ward class IP, no new premium loading or exclusions will apply.
If you are switching insurers, you may need new medical underwriting, which could result in premium loading, new exclusions, or application rejection.
Before making any changes, please consult your financial advisor to understand all implications.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: What should I do if my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved and I do not renew my permanent residency permit in my country of residence in future?
questions.text:
Please inform the Central Provident Fund Board if your permanent residency permit in your overseas country of residence is no longer valid.
Suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is only for those who live abroad permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore. Obtaining permanent residency in another country is one of the indicators required to demonstrate an individual’s intention to reside in another country permanently. Therefore, if you do not renew your permanent residency permit in your overseas country of residence, it is an indication that you may not be able to permanently reside in that country. Your suspension of premium collection will cease and the accumulated sum of premiums suspended from collection, with compound interest, will be payable.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: What should I do if my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved and I later decide to relocate back to Singapore?
questions.text:
If you have relocated back to Singapore, please inform us via cpf.gov.sg/writetous. We will cease the suspension of MediShield Life premium collection. The accumulated sum of premiums that were suspended from collection, with compound interest, will be payable.
We will provide you with details of the total premiums, the amount deducted from your MediSave Account and inform you if there is any outstanding balance to be paid.
You may refer to the Terms & Conditions for more information.

questions.title: What should I do if my Home Protection Scheme cover has lapsed due to non-payment of premium?
questions.text:
You may continue receiving financial protection on your outstanding housing loan through Home Protection Scheme (HPS) by reinstating your lapsed cover or applying for a new one, depending on your eligibility:
When did your HPS cover lapse or end*?Next steps
Ended 6 months or lessApply to reinstate your HPS cover online.
Ended more than 6 months but less than or equal to 1 year ago
Apply to reinstate your HPS cover online with supporting reason and health declaration.
Your eligibility to reinstate your previous HPS cover is subject to approval.
Ended more than 1 year ago
Apply for a new HPS cover with health declaration.
Your eligibility for the new HPS cover is subject to approval and you being in good health.
*You may check your HPS cover end date from the hardcopy lapse letter (Ref: HPS/Lapse) sent to you.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What should I do if one of my household members has disallowed access to his financial information for the purpose of CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility checks?
questions.text:
If one of your household members has decided not to allow access to his/her financial information for eligibility checks for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and any applicable CareShield Life assistance measures, we will not be able to calculate the household's eligibility for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. As such, we are unable to extend any CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and any applicable assistance measures to all members of your household.
Please discuss with your household member if you have concerns regarding his/her disclosure status. If your household member now wishes to allow access to his financial information, please call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 (after selecting your preferred language, press 3, and then 2) or visit here and click “login to access your household information”.

questions.title: What should I do if one of my household members has disallowed access to his financial information for the purpose of CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility checks?
questions.text:
If a household member disallows access to their financial information, we are unable to assess your household's eligibility for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and other assistance measures. As such, we are unable to extend any CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and other assistance measures to all members of your household.
Please discuss with your household member if you have concerns regarding his/her disclosure status. If your household member now wishes to allow access to his financial information, please call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 (after selecting your preferred language, press 3, and then 2). Otherwise, you may visit the link and click "login to access your household information".

questions.title: What types of properties are considered for the multiple property ownership criterion for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: All types of properties, e.g., HDB flat, private residential property and non-residential property, are taken into account in determining the subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: What will be my total CareShield Life premiums payable for the full premium payment term?
questions.text:
To ensure sustainability and affordability of CareShield Life, an independent CareShield Life Council, which comprises 14 members from a variety of fields, such as accountancy, actuarial science, investment, medicine, law, union, and government, will consider the prevailing trends and regularly advise the Government on adjusting the premiums and payouts in line with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
Hence, the Government is unable to provide the total CareShield Life premiums payable for the full premium payment term, as actual future premiums and payouts will vary depending on the regular adjustments.
However, to provide Singaporeans with greater assurance and certainty, CareShield Life premiums* and payouts increment have been fixed at 2% per year for the first five years of scheme implementation. The Government will also publish any relevant information on the premiums and payouts adjustment when available.
*2% increase of premiums per year excludes GST.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: What will be my total CareShield Life premiums payable for the full premium payment term?
questions.text:
To ensure sustainability and affordability of CareShield Life, the CareShield Life Council will consider the prevailing trends and regularly advise the Government on adjusting the premiums and payouts in line with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
Hence, the Government is unable to provide the total CareShield Life premiums payable for the full premium payment term, as actual future premiums and payouts will vary depending on the regular adjustments.

questions.title: What will be the CareShield Life premiums when a 30-year-old today reaches 67 years old?
questions.text:
For those born in 1980 or later, starting premiums vary by joining age and sex. CareShield Life premiums are designed to increase regularly to support the regular increase in payouts. The schedule of premium increases is not fixed, and will be regularly reviewed by an independent council to ensure the sustainability of the scheme.
As an illustration, for a 30-year-old who joins the CareShield Life scheme upon its launch, his premiums would increase from $17/month to $36/month when he reaches 67 years old, assuming a non-guaranteed 2% premium increase per annum (excluding GST). His payouts would have correspondingly increased from $600/month at scheme launch to around $1,200/month. Actual future premiums and payouts will vary depending on the adjustment each year.
However, to provide greater assurance to Singaporeans, for the first five years of scheme implementation, payouts and premiums* will both increase by 2% per year. An independent council will be set up to regularly review these trends thereafter and advise the Government on premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
*2% increase of premiums per year excludes GST.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: What will be the rate of premium and payout increases for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The rate of premium and payout increases for CareShield Life will be reviewed regularly based on actuarial principles, taking into account factors such as changes in claims experience and longevity. This is important to keep the fund sustainable.
The CareShield Life Council regularly reviews these trends and advises the Government on premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. Actual future premiums and monthly payouts will vary depending on the regular adjustments.
Following CareShield Life 2025 Review, payouts will increase by 4% per year from 2026 to 2030 to help policyholders keep up with rising long-term care costs. With the premium support measures, annual CareShield Life premium increases* from 2026 to 2030 will be moderated to about $38 on average, and no more than $75.
*Premiums increase per year excludes GST.

questions.title: What will be the rate of premium and payout increment for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The rate of premium and payout increases for CareShield Life will have to be reviewed regularly based on actuarial principles, taking into account factors like changes in claims experience and longevity. This is important to keep the fund sustainable.
An independent council has been set up to regularly review these trends and advise the Government on premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. Actual future premiums and monthly payouts will vary depending on the regular adjustments.
To give Singaporeans greater certainty in the first five years, payouts and premiums* will each increase by 2% per year.
*2% increase of premiums per year excludes GST.

questions.title: What will happen if I have insufficient MediSave to pay for my Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text: Your insurer will notify you of the outstanding amount payable for your Integrated Shield Plan and advise you how to make payment to the insurer. Please contact your insurer if you require further assistance.

questions.title: What will happen to my CareShield Life premiums that I paid should I pass away before claiming?
questions.text: There is no death benefit for CareShield Life. As such, there will be no payouts upon insureds' passing. If you wish to obtain insurance that provides death benefits, you may purchase Supplements that provide this option.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme cover if I do not pay the annual premium?
questions.text:
If you do not pay the annual premium for your Home Protection Scheme (HPS), your coverage will lapse and you will no longer be protected by HPS. This means that in the unfortunate event of death, terminal illness, or total permanent disability, you will not be able to make a claim under HPS.
You will need to reapply for an HPS cover if you wish to be covered under HPS in future. However, please note that your eligibility for the new HPS cover will be subject to approval and you being in good health at the time of application.
It is important to ensure that your HPS premiums are paid on time to avoid any lapse in coverage.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my MediShield Life or Integrated Shield Plan cover when I renounce my Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Resident status?
questions.text:
Today, all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are covered by MediShield Life.
Should you renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status and are only insured under MediShield Life, you will lose MediShield Life cover.
If you are insured under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), you will either no longer have a MediShield Life component (which may include coverage of any pre-existing conditions) in your IP or have your IP terminated. Please inform your private insurer if you have plans to renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status so that your insurer can advise you on the available coverage options. If you wish to terminate your IP, you will also need to notify your private insurer in a manner as required by your insurer.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: What will happen to my Single Premium Home Protection Scheme cover if I change my share of cover but there are no changes to my outstanding housing loan?
questions.text:
If you have changed your share of Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover without making any changes to your outstanding housing loan, you will remain covered under the Single Premium (SP) HPS.
Once the adjustment is approved, your SP HPS cover will be adjusted accordingly to the new percentage declared. However, please note that any increase in your HPS coverage is subject to approval and you being in good health.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Single Premium Home Protection Scheme cover if there are changes to my outstanding housing loan?
questions.text:
If your loan repayment period or loan amount has reduced, your Single Premium (SP) Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will be terminated. We will issue you an Annual Premium (AP) HPS cover based on your new outstanding housing loan. Any surrender value of your SP HPS cover will be paid to your CPF Ordinary Account.
However, if the changes to your housing loan result in an increase in your HPS cover, such as an increase in cover period or sum assured, obtaining an additional AP cover will be subject to you being in good health. If you are not eligible for the additional cover, you will remain insured under your SP cover.
Do I need to inform the Board to adjust my Home Protection Scheme cover if I make a partial repayment of my loan?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to the premiums that policyholders have pre-paid in their working years should they pass away early? Will the monies be returned to their family members?
questions.text: The premiums that are pre-paid are pooled together by age group to help cushion the future increases in premiums during older ages. While some members may pass on earlier, the remaining pool of funds will help those of the same age group who live longer and need to draw on more rebates.
topics: MediShield Life / Pre-funding under MediShield Life

questions.title: When can I expect more information on my CareShield Life premiums so I can make a decision?
questions.text: You may wish to refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: When do I have to pay for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: Your CareShield Life premium is payable annually. The premium payable will be automatically deducted from your or your premium payer’s MediSave within one month from your policy anniversary. You can refer to the My Policy e-Service to check if you have any premiums payable.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: When do I have to pay for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Your CareShield Life premium is payable annually. The premium payable will be automatically deducted from you or your premium payer’s MediSave within one month from your policy anniversary.
You can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to view your or your dependant(s)’s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life coverage and premium information under the “CareShield Life/ElderShield” and “MediShield Life” section respectively.

questions.title: When do I need to apply for reimbursement to my MediSave and/or MediShield Life from my third-party-payers for my healthcare expense?
questions.text:
Please submit your reimbursement request to your employer or insurer once your MediSave and/or MediShield Life claims have been processed and reflected in your Healthcare payments and claims statement. Your employer or insurer may need your Healthcare payments and claim statement to assess your request. Find out more on how to retrieve your Healthcare payments and claims statements and apply for reimbursement.
Please note that your Healthcare payments and claims statement will no longer be available for retrieval once it is older than 15 months.

questions.title: When is the last premium payable for ElderShield? Why did I receive a request for premiums payment after I turned 65 last year?
questions.text:
The ElderShield scheme collects premiums based on the insured’s age as at their last birthday. The annual premium is payable until the policy year in which you are still age 65 at the start of the policy year.
For example, for a 40-year-old male (date of birth: 30 June 1978) on ElderShield400, the final premium payable will be for the policy starting 30 April 2044. This is because the insured is still age 65 on 30 April 2044 even though he turned age 65 on 30 June 2043.

questions.title: When is the last premium payable for ElderShield? Why did I receive a request for premiums payment after I turned 65 last year?
questions.text:
The ElderShield scheme collects premiums based on the insured's age as at their last birthday. The annual premium is payable until the policy year in which you are still age 65 at the start of the policy year.
For example, for a 40-year-old male (date of birth: 30 June 1978) on ElderShield 400, the final premium payable will be for the policy starting 30 April 2044. This is because the insured is still age 65 on 30 April 2044 even though he turned age 65 on 30 June 2043.

questions.title: When will I find out whether my application has been approved?
questions.text: The Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board will notify you once your application has been processed.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: When will the deduction from my MediSave Account take place after I submit the Change Payer request?
questions.text:
If the insured has outstanding MediShield Life premiums, the deduction will be made from your MediSave Account soon after you have submitted the request.
Thereafter, the insured(s)' MediShield Life premiums will automatically be deducted from your MediSave Account once a year, within a month after the Insured(s)’ cover renewal date.

questions.title: When will the Government revise the Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) and Annual Value (AV) thresholds for MediShield Life or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, and how will I receive the updated premium subsidies?
questions.text:
The Government periodically reviews and updates the Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) and Annual Value (AV) thresholds used to determine subsidy levels and grant support, to ensure households with greater needs receive continued support. The revisions aim to improve affordability and help more households receive the healthcare subsidies and grant support they need, taking into account changes in household incomes and property AVs.
You do not need to take any action for your Premium Subsidies to be updated. Your Premium Subsidies will automatically be applied based on your eligibility under the revised criteria when your policy commences or renews. You can log in to MediShield Life e-Service with your Singpass to check your MediShield Life or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility.

questions.title: When will the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) be expanded to cover more members with certain pre-existing health conditions to obtain HPS coverage at a higher premium rate (i.e. with premium loading)?
questions.text: From 26 May 2025, the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) expands to cover members with certain pre-existing health conditions that are not so severe, such as certain types of stroke and heart disorder, who are currently not offered coverage. CPF Board will assess each application and offer eligible members an HPS cover with premium loading.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: When will the MediShield Life cover of my newborn baby start? Will I be notified?
questions.text: Newborns who are registered as Singapore Citizens at birth are insured under MediShield Life from birth. The Central Provident Fund Board will notify his/her parent (usually the father) of the new-born’s MediShield Life coverage details generally within 1 month of the start of the MediShield Life cover.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: When will the pilot end?
questions.text: The three-year pilot programme will start on 18 September 2025 and end on 17 September 2028. This means that the last day to redeem Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts would be 17 September 2028. Premium discounts redeemed on and before 17 September 2028 will still be valid for 12 months from redemption, even after the pilot ends.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: Where can I check and view my Home Protection Scheme premium deduction?
questions.text: You can check and view the Home Protection Scheme premium deduction from your CPF Ordinary Account online using your Singpass. The deduction will also be shown in your Yearly Statement of Account.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Where can I check my MediShield Life / Integrated Shield Plan premium and subsidies?
questions.text: Information on your MediShield Life premium and applicable subsidies will be sent in writing to the payer of your premium about 1-2 months before your policy renewal date, by the Central Provident Fund Board or your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurer (if you are insured under an IP).

questions.title: Where can I check the premium payable to renew my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) charges a level premium rate (i.e. same amount annually throughout the policy term). This means that you pay the same annual premium throughout 90% of your HPS coverage period. You can find the premium amount on your HPS certificate, which was sent to you when the HPS cover was first issued to you.
Your HPS premium is deducted from your CPF Ordinary Account every year during your policy anniversary month. You can also check the premium payable by viewing the previous premium deductions online using your Singpass or from the Yearly Statement of Account.
To find out more on how long you need to pay your HPS premium, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Where can I find MediShield Life claim examples?
questions.text:
For examples of MediShield Life claims, please refer to pages 29 to 31 of the MediShield Life Information Booklet.
For more information about MediShield Life, visit MOH website.

questions.title: Where can I find more information on Additional Premium Support (APS)?
questions.text: For more information on APS, please visit this website or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Where can I find more information on Additional Premium Support?
questions.text: For further information on Additional Premium Support, please visit this link or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.

questions.title: Where can I find my CareShield Life premiums information?
questions.text: You may refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.

questions.title: Where can I find the application form? When can I start applying for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection?
questions.text: To apply for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection, please complete the application form (https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medishield-life/e-services-for-medishield-life/). When submitting your application, please ensure that your application form is duly completed with the necessary supporting documents uploaded. If you face any difficulty submitting the online application, please write to us (medishieldlife.sg/writetous).
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Where can I get help if I cannot afford my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The Government provides means-tested premium subsidies targeted at the lower- and middle-income individuals.
Policyholders’ loved ones may also help with premium payment for policyholders through their MediSave or by topping up to their MediSave accounts of their loved ones.
For those who are unable to pay for their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and family support, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support, so that no one loses CareShield Life coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: Where can I view the status of my GIRO application for my Healthcare premiums payment?
questions.text:
You can log in to Activities to track the status of your GIRO payment arrangement request for your healthcare premiums.
Please refer to the following FAQ for guidance on termination of GIRO arrangement for your/your dependants' MediShield Life, CareShield Life, and ElderShield premiums:
How do I terminate my/my dependant's GIRO arrangement for MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?

questions.title: Where does the Health Insurance Planner obtain information on Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders?
questions.text: The information on Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders is provided by the insurers and is updated annually in January. For a comparison of IPs across all insurers, you may refer to Ministry of Health (MOH)’s website.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Which CPF account would the premium be refunded to if my family member has used their CPF savings to pay for my Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text: If your family member (that is your spouse, parent, child or sibling) has used their CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings for your Home Protection Scheme premium, any premium refund will be paid into your OA.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Who are the Council members and how were they chosen?
questions.text: The MediShield Life Council currently comprises 11 members who have been appointed by the Minister for Health based on the relevance of their expertise, experience and public standing. The members come from diverse backgrounds, with professional experience in areas such as accountancy, insurance, investment, medicine, the law, union and government. This ensures that the Council can benefit from the wide-ranging expertise and experience of the members in the administration and review of MediShield Life. Please refer to this link (https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medishield-life/medishield-life-council) for the list of members and their profile.

questions.title: Who can I contact if I have further enquiries about MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement?
questions.text: For any further enquiries about MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement, please write to us and we will assist you with your enquiries.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Who is covered under MediShield Life? Do I need to apply for MediShield Life?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are automatically covered under MediShield Life. No application is required.
If you are covered by MediShield Life only, when your plan is up for annual renewal, the current payer (who may be yourself or your family member) will receive a letter from the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board with details about your MediShield Life premiums and subsidies.
If you are covered by an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), when your IP is up for annual renewal, the current payer (who may be yourself or your family member) will receive a letter from your private insurer with details about your premiums and subsidies. You will receive subsidies for the MediShield Life portion of your IP if you are eligible.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: Who manages MediShield Life?
questions.text: MediShield Life is administered by the Central Provident Fund Board on behalf of the Ministry of Health.

questions.title: Who needs to declare their health status under CareShield Life/MediShield Life?
questions.text: All new Permanent Resident applicants aged 30 or older who have received the In-Principle Approval for their Singapore Permanent Residence application are required to declare their health condition before completing Formalities with the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority. The health status declared will not affect their application for Singapore Permanent Residence.

questions.title: Who receives the ElderShield rebate?
questions.text:
ElderShield policyholders with active/in-force policies and who are not claiming from ElderShield as of 31 December 2022 are eligible for the rebate.
For policies paid for by the insured, or where premiums no longer need to be paid, the rebate will be credited to the insured’s MediSave to support the insured’s future healthcare needs.
For policies paid for by an individual who is not the insured (for example, a family member) via MediSave, the rebate will be credited to the payer’s MediSave to support future ElderShield premium payments.

questions.title: Why am I given an ElderShield rebate?
questions.text: In the last 5 years of the scheme, ElderShield claims have been lower than projected. Hence, existing ElderShield policyholders whose policies are in force and who are not claiming from ElderShield as of 31 December 2022 will be given premium rebates.

questions.title: Why am I identified to pay for my own MediShield Life premiums when my payer has been paying my premiums?
questions.text: You have been identified to take over paying your own premiums because there are sufficient funds in your MediSave Account. This helps to preserve your previous payer’s MediSave for his/her own healthcare needs. We have notified your previous payer. If the previous payer or a new payer wishes to help with your premium payment, he/she can submit a Change Payer for MediShield Life.

questions.title: Why am I responsible for my child's outstanding MediShield Life premiums, and whose MediSave account will be used for the deduction?
questions.text:
Generally, parents of children under age 21 would be informed of their children's MediShield Life coverage and premium matters.
Under the MediShield Life Act or Regulations, parents are legally liable to pay for their child's MediShield Life premiums until the child reaches age 21. Should the children's premiums remain outstanding and unpaid, premiums may automatically be deducted from parents' MediSave Accounts.
Alternatively, you can top up your child's MediSave Account by referring to:
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)'s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?
For divorced parents who do not have custody and are not liable to maintain their child, you can write to us with a copy of court documents for assessment.

questions.title: Why am I unable to view claim details of my hospitalisation from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
Claim details displayed online are accurate as at the date of enquiry. They will be reflected only after the medical institution submits your claim and the MediSave and/or MediShield Life claim is processed.
Please note that the medical institution can only submit your claim after the medical bill has been finalised. Claim details of your hospitalisation will only be available after your MediSave and/or MediShield Life claim is processed.
You can check the status of your MediShield Life claim via 'My Activities' after you log onto "my cpf Online Services" with your SingPass.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Why are CareShield Life premiums for females higher although their payouts are the same as males?
questions.text:
CareShield Life provides the same amount of expected benefits per dollar of premium paid for both women and men over their lifetimes. Compared to men, women generally live longer and have higher chances of developing severe disability, hence they are likely to receive longer CareShield Life coverage and more payouts over their lifetime. As men and women pay premiums for CareShield Life for the same number of years, the annual premiums for women need to be higher to account for their longer expected duration of payout over their lifetime.
We will provide support to lower-income women through the existing social support schemes for lower-income Singaporeans. For CareShield Life, the Government will also provide premium subsidies and support based on one’s financial circumstances to ensure that premiums are affordable.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Why are CareShield Life premiums for females higher although their payouts are the same as males?
questions.text:
CareShield Life provides the same amount of expected benefits per dollar of premium paid for both women and men over their lifetimes. Compared to men, women generally live longer and have higher chances of developing severe disability, hence they are likely to receive longer CareShield Life coverage and more payouts over their lifetime. As men and women pay premiums for CareShield Life for the same number of years, the annual premiums for women need to be higher to account for their longer expected duration of payout over their lifetime.
We will provide support to lower-income women through the existing social support schemes for lower-income Singaporeans. For CareShield Life, the Government will also provide premium subsidies and support based on one's financial circumstances to ensure that premiums are affordable.

questions.title: Why are CareShield Life premiums for older cohorts higher than younger cohorts?
questions.text:
The estimated premiums for all cohorts are actuarially determined and are designed to be not-for-profit.
CareShield Life premiums are meant to be paid from age 30 to 67, or until the insured makes a claim. Older cohorts joining CareShield Life will face higher annual premiums as they have fewer years to spread their premium payments as compared to younger cohorts. Older cohorts also have a higher risk of developing severe disability.
The Government will provide premium support for those born 1979 or earlier:
1. Lower- to middle-income Singapore residents will receive Means-tested Subsidies. Up to two-thirds of Singapore resident households will be eligible for CareShield Life subsidies of up to 30%.
2. Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier will receive Participation Incentives, spread over the first 10 years of their policy if they join and are covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024. Participation Incentives of up to $4,000 ($400/year) will be provided to those who join and are covered by 31 December 2023, and up to $3,000 ($300/year) for those who join and are covered before 31 December 2024. The participation incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and will be used to offset premiums payable for each year.
3. Those in financial need who are unable to pay for their premiums after premium subsidies can apply for Additional Premium Support from the Government.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Why are CareShield Life premiums for older cohorts higher than younger cohorts?
questions.text:
The estimated CareShield Life premiums for all cohorts are actuarially determined and are designed to be not-for-profit.
CareShield Life premiums are meant to be paid from age 30 to 67, or until the insured makes a claim. Older cohorts joining CareShield Life will face higher annual premiums as they have fewer years to spread their premium payments as compared to younger cohorts. Older cohorts also have a higher risk of developing severe disability.
The Government will provide premium support for those born 1979 or earlier:
Lower- to middle-income Singapore residents will receive Means-tested Subsidies. Up to two-thirds of Singapore resident households will be eligible for CareShield Life subsidies of up to 30%.
Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier will receive Participation Incentives, spread over the first 10 years of their policy if they joined and were covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024.
Those in financial need who are unable to pay for their premiums after premium subsidies can apply for Additional Premium Support from the Government.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.

questions.title: Why are my full healthcare renewal premiums deducted from my GIRO bank account when I have set up monthly GIRO instalments?
questions.text:
If you have set up GIRO for healthcare renewal premiums, your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield renewal premiums will be deducted from your GIRO bank account every year. Monthly GIRO instalments are only for payment of past policy year’s outstanding premiums (excluding renewal premiums).
This arrangement was outlined in your GIRO application form.

questions.title: Why are my future MediShield Life premiums so high?
questions.text:
The projected MediShield Life premiums you see reflect expected medical inflation over time and increases with age. Your actual future premiums may differ based on factors like real medical inflation, how much people claim, and any changes in coverage benefits.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) works with the MediShield Life Council to actively review MediShield Life coverage and premiums to ensure that healthcare remains accessible and affordable.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why are my MediSave and MediShield Life claims not processed after my visit/hospital discharge?
questions.text:
Medical institutions may take up to about two weeks from the date of your visit/hospital discharge to submit your MediShield Life and MediSave claims. If you are on an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), it may take longer than two weeks as your claim(s) will first be submitted to your IP insurer for assessment.
Please refer to the table of processing time from the day CPFB receives the claims from your Medical Institution or insurer.

questions.title: Why are only certain individuals allowed to pay my Home Protection Scheme premium using their CPF Ordinary Account savings?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premiums are consumptive in nature, which means that when your family member (who is your spouse, parent, child, or sibling) uses their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to help with your HPS premium payment, they will have less CPF savings for their retirement.
This is why only certain family members, who are co-owners of the flat, are allowed to use their CPF OA savings to pay your HPS premium. By doing so, they can help to secure the family home while limiting the impact on their retirement savings.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why are some funds reserved in my CPF Ordinary Account for the Dependants' Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text:
To ensure that working CPF members are financially protected by the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS), the necessary amount will be reserved in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) during the premium payment grace period. This means that you will not be able to use or withdraw up to that amount of OA savings during this period.
If you prefer to pay your premiums in cash, contact the DPS insurer (Great Eastern Life) to top up the full premium in cash. The reserved amount in your CPF OA will be released after your cash payment is processed.
In the event that you need to use the reserved amount for other purposes, please write to us for assistance. However, please note that your DPS cover could lapse if no payment is made within the grace period stipulated by the DPS insurer.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Why are the deductible and co-insurance features necessary under the MediShield Life scheme?
questions.text:
The deductible sieves out smaller medical bills that can be paid via MediSave or cash, and focuses MediShield Life coverage on larger, catastrophic medical bills to keep premiums sustainable and affordable. The co-insurance encourages responsible and appropriate consumption of healthcare services, while managing the financial burden on the patient. Both the deductible and co-insurance can also be covered by MediSave, up to respective withdrawal limits. This strikes a balance between protecting Singaporeans against the vast majority of healthcare bills, while keeping premiums affordable.
Those who have difficulty affording their bills after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave can also apply for financial assistance such as MediFund.

questions.title: Why are the MediShield Life Premium Subsidies I am eligible for, as seen in CFPB's Healthcare Dashboard, different from those shown in "Your Benefit"@LifeSG?
questions.text:
"Your Benefits"@ LifeSG shows the total amount of subsidies that you have received for your MediShield Life policies starting in 2023 and 2024. The total amount of subsidies might include the following types of MediShield Life subsidies (depending on your eligibility):
1. Means-tested Premium Subsidies for lower- to middle-income Singapore Residents.
2. Pioneer Generation Subsidies for the Pioneer Generation seniors.
3. Merdeka Generation Subsidies for the Merdeka Generation seniors.
You may wish to log in to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' to find out more about the specific type and amount of MediShield Life subsidies you are currently eligible for.

questions.title: Why are the Standard Integrated Shield Plan premiums different across all the insurers, even though benefits are the same?
questions.text:
While the Ministry of Health has worked with the private insurers to standardise the Standard Integrated Shield Plan’s (IP) benefits, the plan is provided and administered by insurers, and remains a private product.
Insurance companies compete in a competitive market and the products need to remain commercially viable. As such, similar to other existing IPs, premiums and underwriting for the additional private insurance component of the Standard IP are determined by insurers based on their own commercial considerations and risk assessment frameworks. There is therefore variance in the premiums, depending on each insurer’s approach and their respective risk pools.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why are there changes to cancer treatment financing?
questions.text:
Before 1 September 2022, MediShield Life paid up to $3,000/month for all cancer drugs, and Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) often covered costs above that on an as-charged basis (i.e. no claim limit), with a small co-payment.
Such a design meant that drug companies had no incentive to charge lower prices for drug treatments that cost less. As a result, we paid higher prices for many cancer drugs as compared to other countries such as Australia, South Korea and the United Kingdom.
The changes to cancer treatment financing allow us to negotiate lower prices for cancer drugs and ensure that cancer treatment costs and insurance premiums remain affordable for Singapore residents in the long term.

questions.title: Why can’t CareShield Life/ElderShield automatically reimburse long-term care costs the way MediShield Life does for hospital bills?
questions.text:
Unlike MediShield Life, which covers large hospital bills, CareShield Life/ElderShield provides monthly cash payouts to offer individuals and their caregivers greater flexibility in choosing their preferred care arrangements. This ensures that they are not restricted to specific long-term care services in order to receive support.
For example, some may prefer to stay in a familiar home environment and opt for home-based care, while others may choose to receive care from a healthcare provider such as a nursing home.
Given long-term care needs and preferences differ widely, cash payouts allow you to decide how best to use the support.

questions.title: Why can't I see the amount of Additional Premium Support my child received in the LifeSG application/website? Where can I find this information?
questions.text:
If you are the payer for your child's MediShield Life premiums, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to find out how much Additional Premium Support your child has received.
Alternatively, please write to medishieldlife.sg/writetous or call 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays). Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: Why can't I see the amount of MediShield Life Premium Subsidies my child received in the LifeSG application/website? Where can I find this information?
questions.text:
If you are the payer for your child's MediShield Life premiums, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to find out how much MediShield Life Premium Subsidies your child has received.
Alternatively, contact CPFB at medishieldlife.sg/writetous or 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays).
Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: Why can’t the Government provide and administer the Standard Integrated Shield Plan, to ensure that premiums are more affordable and to cover pre-existing conditions with risk-loading, similar to MediShield Life?
questions.text:
The Government’s focus is to provide basic and affordable health insurance coverage for all Singapore Residents through MediShield Life, regardless of their health condition.
As the Standard IP is an optional plan designed for higher coverage in Class B1 wards and is not a basic product, it is provided by private insurers. Similar to all other IPs, premiums and underwriting decisions are determined by insurers based on their own commercial considerations and risk assessment frameworks. Nevertheless, the Standard IP was designed to have standardised features to facilitate comparison of premiums by consumers. IP insurers also have the incentive to ensure that their premiums remain competitive to attract new policyholders.
The Ministry of Health will continue to review MediShield Life and the Standard IP, to ensure that they remain relevant to Singapore Residents with different needs.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why did I not receive any premium rebates?
questions.text:
Under MediShield Life, Singapore Residents pay more premiums while they are working, and in return enjoy premium rebates during their older ages. The additional amounts paid during working age are set aside in the MediShield Life Fund, to provide for future premium rebates which will help to moderate premium increases experienced at older ages.
For policyholders born before 1950 and have been insured continuously under the scheme, they will receive premium rebates from age 71 to 90 (based on age next birthday). For policyholders born in or after 1950, they will receive premium rebates from age 66 to 90 (based on age next birthday).
Please click here (www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/medishield-life/medishield-life-premiums-and-subsidies/premium-rebates) for more information on premium rebates.
From 1 April 2025, changes will be made to the indicative premium rebates for policyholders born in or after 1950. Please refer to the MediShield Life 2024 Review press release for more details.

questions.title: Why did I receive a call from someone who claimed to be an officer from the Ministry Of Health (MOH) asking me to apply for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text: As the Ministry of Health (MOH) has not received your Additional Premium Support (APS) application form after sending letter(s) to invite you to apply for APS, the MOH officer had contacted you to find out if you need assistance with the APS application. This is to ensure that adequate assistance is extended to members who are unable to afford their premiums.

questions.title: Why did I receive a MediShield Life letter when I have applied to review my means-test result for other healthcare schemes?
questions.text:
Other healthcare schemes may use MediShield Life means information to determine your eligibility for their schemes. Upon the completion of the review, a MediShield Life letter sent to your email or NRIC address would be provided as an update to your request.
You may also visit https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/ and log in with your SingPass to check on updates to your latest household and means information. MediShield Life means information includes Annual Value (AV) of the Property, Household Monthly Income Per Person and Multiple Property Ownership.
Based on the MediShield Life means information, you may visit https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies for more information regarding other healthcare schemes and their eligibility criteria/corresponding subsidy framework.

questions.title: Why did I receive an error message when trying to redeem Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts?
questions.text:
To redeem Healthpoints for MediShield Life (MSHL) premium discounts, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident covered under MediShield Life or an Integrated Shield Plan, and aged 40 and above. You could be ineligible due to the following reasons (non-exhaustive):
1. You have been granted suspension of MSHL premium collection; or
2. You are a new Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident whose MSHL cover is still being issued.
For members who are assessed as eligible for Additional Premium Support (APS) or on the Fixed Amount on Ward (FAW) and Co-payment on Ward (CPW) Pensioner schemes, redemption of Healthpoints for MSHL premium discounts is not applicable as you are not required to pay MSHL premiums.
If your premiums are fully covered by APS or FAW or CPW Pensioner schemes, you can redeem your Healthpoints for other rewards such as grocery vouchers, transport credits, or lifestyle benefits instead.

questions.title: Why did I receive calls or visits from the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) officers?
questions.text:
These officers from the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) are part of the Additional Premium Support (APS) outreach team.
As you have outstanding MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life premiums and MOH has not received your APS application form after sending letter(s) to invite you to apply for APS, the MSF officer has called / visited you to explain about MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life and how to apply for APS to help you pay your premiums.

questions.title: Why did the CareShield Life Welcome Package state that I was previously invited to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS)?
questions.text:
As you have an outstanding MediShield Life premium, a letter (Ref: APCINV) was sent earlier on to inform you to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS) if you need assistance to pay your outstanding premiums. If you still require assistance to pay for your premiums, you may complete the APS application form that was enclosed with the letter and mail it to us using the Business Reply Envelope provided.
For more information on APS, please visit the MediShield Life website or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Why did the CareShield Life Welcome Package state that I was previously invited to apply for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) is designed to help members who are unable to afford their MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums after Government subsidies and have limited family support. As you have an outstanding MediShield Life premium, a letter (Ref: APCINV) was sent earlier to invite you to apply for APS if you need assistance to pay your outstanding premiums. Alternatively, you may visit cpf.gov.sg/APSapplication to apply for APS online. This link does not require Singpass login.
For more information on APS, please visit the MediShield Life website or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.

questions.title: Why did the Government design the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) to have claim limits, instead of as-charged coverage? Since it is not as-charged, is the Standard IP enough for Class B1?
questions.text:
The Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) was designed with claim limits to balance between providing adequate coverage and ensuring that premiums remain affordable.
In general, claim limits in insurance plans are useful to serve as protection against over-servicing, over-consumption and overcharging, which contribute to claims escalation, premium increases and rising healthcare costs in the long-run.
The Standard IP’s claim limits are sized to cover 9 out of 10 Ward B1 bills. It will therefore be sufficient for most policyholders who stay in a Class B1 ward in public hospitals. Patients can tap on MediSave to help pay for the deductible and co-insurance.
The Ministry of Health will regularly review the Standard IP benefits to ensure that they continue to provide sufficient coverage at the Ward B1 or equivalent level.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why do CareShield Life payouts stop increasing once insureds stop paying premiums (e.g., when they make a claim or turn 67)?
questions.text:
Increases in CareShield Life payouts are supported by premium adjustments to ensure the scheme remains financially sustainable. Those who wish to have payouts that continue to increase throughout their lifetime may consider purchasing Supplements. Insurers designing these Supplements may also take into account the features of CareShield Life.
CareShield Life payouts are designed to complement existing Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support, helping the insured meet their basic long-term care costs. Additionally, they can make monthly cash withdrawals of up to $200 from their and/or their spouse’s MediSave Account(s) under MediSave Care.
For Singaporeans who are still unable to afford their care even after Government subsidies, CareShield Life payouts and personal savings, further assistance is available through Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare.

questions.title: Why do CareShield Life payouts stop increasing once insureds stop paying premiums e.g. when they make a claim or turn 67?
questions.text:
CareShield Life payout increases will need to be supported by premium adjustments, to keep the scheme sustainable. Those who wish to have payouts that increase for life may opt to purchase Supplements. Insurers may also wish to take note of CareShield Life features when designing Supplements.
CareShield Life payouts should also not be seen in isolation, but complement existing Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support, to better assist Singaporeans with their basic long-term care costs. They can also make monthly cash withdrawals of up to $200 from their and/or their spouse’s MediSave Account(s) under MediSave Care.
For Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies, CareShield Life payouts and personal savings, there are Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare which can provide further assistance.

questions.title: Why do CareShield Life premiums increase over time, and by how much annually?
questions.text:
Annual increases in CareShield Life payouts help protect the value of CareShield Life payouts over time. This needs to be supported by annual increases in CareShield Life premiums. To give Singaporeans greater certainty in the first five years, payouts and premiums* each increased by 2% per year from 2021 to 2025.
Following CareShield Life 2025 Review, payouts will increase by 4% per year from 2026 to 2030 to help policyholders keep up with rising long-term care costs. To support this, premiums will increase annually, with premium support measures moderating increases from 2026 to 2030 to about $38 on average and no more than $75.
The CareShield Life Council regularly reviews these trends and advises the Government on CareShield Life premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. The Government will consider affordability of premiums when reviewing the council’s advice on premium adjustments.
*Premiums increase per year excludes GST.

questions.title: Why do CareShield Life premiums increase over time?
questions.text:
Annual increases in CareShield Life payouts help protect the value of CareShield Life payouts over time. This needs to be supported by annual increases in CareShield Life premiums. To give Singaporeans greater certainty in the first five years, payouts and premiums* will each increase by 2% per year.
An independent council will be set up to regularly review these trends and advise the Government on CareShield Life premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. The Government will consider affordability of premiums when reviewing the council’s advice on premium adjustments.
*2% increase of premiums per year excludes GST.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Why do I need to fill in the policy number and claim number of my employee, platform worker or insured in the E-File Excel for MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement?
questions.text: The policy number and claim number fields were added based on requests from companies to help track their MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement submissions and match them with their records. These fields are optional and not compulsory.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Why do I still see outstanding MediShield Life premiums in my Healthcare dashboard after making payment, or continue to receive payment notifications?
questions.text: If you have already made payment for your MediShield Life premiums, no further action is needed. We will notify you again if there is insufficient MediSave for premium payment. Allow five working days for the payment to be processed and reflected in the system before logging in to your Healthcare dashboard to check again.

questions.title: Why do my household members have different subsidy amounts for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
Your household members may have different subsidy amounts for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies due to the following reasons:
a. Age-based Premium Subsidies structure - Subsidy amounts are higher for older insured members, as compared to younger insured members, for those with the same subsidy eligibility.
b. Maximum subsidy for selected group identified - You or your household member may have been assessed previously and are eligible under other Government assistance schemes (e.g. Public Assistance Scheme).
c. Assessed separately - Information from your application and/or renewal for other healthcare subsidy schemes (e.g. Community Health Assist Scheme) will be used for the eligibility checks for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies.
Selected household member(s) may have been assessed separately due to extenuating circumstances, e.g. those living overseas and are unable to provide consent in the previous applications.
If you and your household wish to be reassessed for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies, please write to us at www.cpf.gov.sg/writetous or call our hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: Why do my Projected MediSave Savings differ when comparing MediShield Life (Projection 1) versus Integrated Shield Plan (Projection 2) and Integrated Shield Plan with Rider (Projection 3)?
questions.text:
Your Cumulative MediSave Savings are calculated differently based on your insurance coverage choices. If you have an existing Integrated Shield Plan (IP) with rider, the planner will show you three scenarios:
1. Projection 1: MediShield Life only
2. Projection 2: Existing IP
3. Projection 3: Existing IP with rider
Your Cumulative MediSave Savings include your current MediSave Account balance plus projected inflows for up to 30 years or age 90 (whichever comes first), rounded to the nearest decade (e.g., 50, 60, or 70).
The differences between Projection 1 and Projection 2 can arise for two reasons. When your MediSave reaches the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS), paying IP premiums creates room for additional MediSave contributions, potentially increasing your savings. However, these higher premium payments can also reduce your MediSave balance and earned interest, potentially decreasing your savings. These effects can happen at the same time, and their overall impact depends on your specific circumstances.
The projections for IP with and without riders show the same MediSave savings because rider premiums cannot be paid using MediSave.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why do premium rebates stop at age 90?
questions.text:
Under MediShield, the premium rebate schedule was designed to support premium rebates up to age 90, which was the maximum coverage age under MediShield. With MediShield Life, Pioneers above age 90 will not need to pay any premiums after the Pioneer Generation subsidies and MediSave top-ups. In view of this, there is no immediate need to extend the last coverage age of the premium rebates.
The Ministry of Health will review the premium rebates from time to time so that the distribution of rebates is able to meet the needs of the elderly.
topics: MediShield Life / Pre-funding under MediShield Life

questions.title: Why does my child not have a MediShield Life cover to claim for the hospitalisation bills incurred before he passed away?
questions.text:
We are sorry to hear of your child's demise. The MediShield Life claims can be submitted by the medical institution and will be processed if your child was a Singaporean/Singapore Permanent Resident.
Please contact us at 1800-222-3399 or write to us with your child's details.

questions.title: Why does my Healthcare dashboard state that my MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums may be recovered from my bankruptcy estate?
questions.text:
Outstanding MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums incurred prior to your bankruptcy date may be recovered from your bankruptcy estate. These premiums will therefore not be reflected as outstanding premiums payable in your Healthcare dashboard.
To pay your outstanding premiums incurred prior to the date of your Bankruptcy Order, please obtain approval from the Private Trustee or Official Assignee. You can contact them at 1800 225 5529 (during office hours) or visit www.mlaw.gov.sg.

questions.title: Why does the Standard Integrated Shield Plan not cover pre-existing conditions with risk-loading?
questions.text:
Similar to all other Integrated Shield Plans (IPs), the additional private insurance component of the Standard IP is provided by private insurers. Coverage under the Standard IP is therefore a business decision based on the risk assessment framework of each insurer.
Since the launch of MediShield Life, the Ministry of Health has allowed all IP insurers to introduce risk-loading options for policyholders who would like coverage for their pre-existing conditions. You may wish to check with your insurer if risk-loaded options are available for your plan.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why does the Standard Integrated Shield Plan not provide additional benefits (e.g. pre- and post-hospitalisation)?
questions.text:
In designing the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP), it was important to balance between providing adequate coverage and ensuring premiums remain affordable.
The Standard IP was thus intended to be a “no-frills”, affordable product targeted at large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why does the status of my Home Protection Scheme cover show “pending renewal” in the Home ownership dashboard when I have sufficient monies in my CPF Ordinary Account for the premium?
questions.text:
The deduction of premiums for the renewal of Home Protection Scheme (HPS) covers takes place on a weekly basis.
If your HPS cover renewal date falls between the weekly deduction runs, the status of your HPS cover will show as "pending renewal" in the Home ownership dashboard. Once the premium has been successfully deducted, the status of your HPS cover will change to "Active".
In the event that you do not have enough Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay the premium, we will inform you to top-up the premium shortfall.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why have I received a notice from the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) informing me that I owe MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
IRAS is authorised under the MediShield Life Scheme Act and the CareShield Life Scheme Act to carry out enforcement actions to recover MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums.
The amount stated in IRAS' notice includes any outstanding MediShield Life premiums, interest and penalties as at the print date.
You should pay your outstanding premiums by the deadline indicated by IRAS to avoid further enforcement actions or apply for assistance to help you pay the premiums. Find out more on the payment options.

questions.title: Why is Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) allowed to recover unpaid taxes/ MediShield Life premiums when I withdraw my CPF savings?
questions.text:
Taxes go towards funding of government expenditure; and to support the government's economic and social programme to ensure quality growth and an inclusive society. Most taxpayers pay their taxes on time. To encourage voluntary compliance where every taxpayer contributes their fair share of tax, there are penalties if taxes are not paid on time. Actions to recover the unpaid taxes may include appointment of agents such as CPF Board.
Under the law, IRAS is empowered to appoint CPF Board as an agent for the recovery of unpaid taxes/MediShield Life premiums. IRAS would have informed you that CPF Board has been appointed as agent to recover the unpaid taxes/MediShield Life premiums when you withdraw your CPF savings.
You may approach IRAS at 6356 7012 to discuss alternative arrangements to settle your unpaid taxes/MediShield Life premiums before submitting your withdrawal application.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: Why is MediShield Life applying a differentiated pro-ration factor for ward charges and surgical fees?
questions.text: As ward charges and surgical fees can differ, having a single pro-ration factor could result in over- or under-proration of individual bills. Having a differentiated pro-ration factor will allow private and unsubsidised bills to be better normalise to the subsidised equivalent.

questions.title: Why is MediShield Life covering treatments such as Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTPs) and high-cost drugs which might only benefit a small number of patients?
questions.text:
Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTPs) and high-cost drugs have significant potential to treat rare diseases and conditions. However, they can be expensive. Without any financing, Singaporeans will not be able to access these potentially life-saving treatments.
MediShield Life and risk-pooling essentially make healthcare more accessible for everyone. Rather than having each person save individually for costly treatments like CTGTPs that only a few may need, MediShield Life collects smaller, annual premiums from all. This approach allows the scheme to provide financial support for high-cost, low-incidence treatments when they are needed.
To keep the scheme affordable and sustainable, coverage will focus on treatments that the Ministry of Health (MOH) has assessed to be clinically effective and cost-efficient. This ensures that everyone benefits from shared resources, reducing the financial burden on individuals while maintaining quality care for those who truly need it.

questions.title: Why is my participation incentive $0 for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: Participation Incentives were only extended to Singapore Citizens (SCs) born in 1979 or earlier who joined and were covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024. However, both SCs and Permanent Residents (PRs) will be entitled to Government subsidies, if you are from a lower- to middle-income household. PRs enjoy half the applicable subsidies that SCs enjoy.

questions.title: Why is permanent residency in our country of residence a supporting indicator for eligibility?
questions.text: The administrative arrangement is only for those who live abroad permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore. Obtaining permanent residency in another country is one of the indicators required to demonstrate an individual’s intention to reside in another country permanently.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Why is the Home Protection Scheme premium not refundable if I did not make a claim?
questions.text: Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premiums paid for past policy years are not refundable. This is because you have received insurance protection during the period of cover and would have been eligible to receive the HPS benefits in the event of a claim.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why is the pilot only open to individuals who are 40 years old and above? Are there plans for the programme to be rolled out to younger individuals in the future?
questions.text:
This pilot programme is introduced in support of Healthier SG. As such, for a start, the pilot will focus on those aged 40 and above, which is the age criteria for the Healthier SG enrolment programme.
We will study the outcomes of the pilot before deciding whether premium discounts should be made a permanent feature of the MediShield Life scheme, and whether the discounts should be extended to younger individuals.
Under Healthier SG, all Singapore residents are encouraged to stay active and live healthily, such as by participating in programmes offered by the People’s Association (PA), Sport SG and the Health Promotion Board (HPB). All Singapore residents can participate in Healthy 365 programmes and challenges, to earn and redeem Healthpoints. Regardless of age, healthier lifestyles generally lead to better health outcomes and reduced healthcare utilisation.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: Why is the pilot only open to individuals who are 40 years old and above? Are there plans for the programme to be rolled out to younger individuals in the future?
questions.text:
This pilot programme is introduced in support of Healthier SG. As such, for a start, the pilot will focus on those aged 40 and above, which is the age criteria for the Healthier SG enrolment programme.
We will study the outcomes of the pilot before deciding whether premium discounts should be made a permanent feature of the MediShield Life scheme, and whether the discounts should be extended to younger individuals.
