Regardless of age, healthier lifestyles generally lead to better health outcomes and reduced healthcare utilisation.

questions.title: Why is the premium for my new Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover higher than my old HPS cover even though I have made a partial repayment of my loan?
questions.text:
Your Home Protection Scheme premium is higher than before because you had extended your repayment period to a longer tenure, after you made the partial repayment of your loan.
Find out more:
How is the Home Protection Scheme premium calculated?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why is the premium information shown on the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service different from details in my welcome letter?
questions.text: The information reflected on the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service is based on the latest information available while the information reflected in your welcome letter is accurate as at the date reflected on the first page of your welcome letter. The information may differ if you have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, and the appeal was successful. Otherwise, there should not be any changes in your premium information and do contact us at 1800-222-3399 to allow us to investigate further.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premium Checker

questions.title: Why is the premium information shown on the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service different from details in my welcome letter?
questions.text: The CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service is based on the latest information available when you log in while your welcome letter is accurate as of the date shown on the first page. The information may differ if you have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, and the appeal was successful. For further enquiries, please contact us at Write to us or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: Why is the private insurer writing to me about MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of 2 components – (i) the MediShield Life component administered by the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board and (ii) the additional private insurance component, which is managed by private insurers.
Your private insurer is writing to you about the MediShield Life component of your IP as they act as a single point-of-contact and take care of all communications with IP policyholders.

questions.title: Why is the validity period of the premium discounts capped at 12 months?
questions.text: Once the premium discounts have been redeemed, they are valid for a period of 12 months. The discounts will automatically apply to the policyholder’s premium payment at the next MediShield Life policy renewal, which takes place every 12 months.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: Why is there a cap on the number of days I visit Singapore? How did you decide on 140 days over five years?
questions.text:
Universal lifelong coverage under MediShield Life is in line with our move to a more inclusive society with stronger collective responsibility. MediShield Life coverage is thus mandatory for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
The MediShield Life Council’s recommended administrative arrangement is targeted at overseas Singaporeans who live abroad permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore. The criterion of 140 days over five years was included to help to determine administratively who can be regarded as permanently away, save for short visits to Singapore. The duration takes into consideration the general length of stay granted to tourists coming to Singapore for short visits, but with flexibility to be assessed on a cumulative basis over five years.
For those who live abroad permanently but need to stay in Singapore for a longer period of time than the specified limit, we can review their specific circumstances on a case by case basis.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Why is there a difference between the premium discounts shown on my MediShield Life/ Integrated Shield Plan Premium Notice Letter and the amount I redeemed?
questions.text: The premium discount shown on the Premium Notice Letter reflects the amount you had redeemed as of the letter printing date. If you had redeemed more premium discounts after receiving the Premium Notice Letter, these will be reflected in your Healthcare Dashboard. Please log in for more details. The information is available under “Health insurance – MediShield Life premium discount”.

questions.title: Why is there a need for an increase in the deductible?
questions.text:
Although healthcare costs have increased, the deductible hasn’t changed since 2015. An increase in the deductible helps to keep premiums affordable for all policyholders.
The deductible sieves out smaller bills that can be paid via MediSave, and focuses MediShield Life coverage on larger, catastrophic bills. By not covering small healthcare costs right away (first-dollar coverage), the deductible encourages the prudent use of healthcare services.
To help Singaporeans cope with the increase in deductible, the Ministry of Health will increase MediSave limits such that those with sufficient MediSave will generally not see an increase in cash out-of-pocket.
For those with insufficient MediSave savings, the Government will provide additional support such as MediSave top-ups. There is also MediFund, an endowment fund set up by the Government to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave.

questions.title: Why is there a need for strong premium recovery measures?
questions.text:
With universal MediShield Life coverage, as part of collective responsibility, all Singapore Residents should play their part in paying their premiums in a timely manner. This ensures that MediShield Life is able to meet its commitments to all its members and pay out on claims.
The Government will provide strong support through various subsidies to help Singaporeans with their premiums. Active measures will also be taken to facilitate the payment of premiums, including deduction of premiums fully from MediSave balances, regular reminders, switch of payment arrangement to family members and Additional Premium Support for the genuinely needy.
However, there may be a small group of defaulters who have means but choose not to pay premiums. The premium recovery measures are targeted at this group to discourage freeloading and ensure that they also pay their fair share of premiums. Otherwise, premium defaults will translate to bad debts to the MediShield Life Fund and higher premiums for all.

questions.title: Why is there a need to impose interest?
questions.text:
Interest may be imposed on outstanding premiums where appropriate, e.g. defaulters with premium arrears outstanding for prolonged periods. The interest may be compounded and recovered together with the outstanding premiums.
This fairly reflects the opportunity cost to the MediShield Life Fund, which would otherwise be invested in order to support future payments (e.g. MediShield Life claims) from the MediShield Life Fund. This loss translates to higher premiums for the rest of the insured if they are not recovered in a timely manner.

questions.title: Why is there an error message stating that I am not paying for my family member's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life coverage when I tried to stop premium payment?
questions.text:
If you encountered an error message stating that you are not paying your family member's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums, it could be due to several reasons:
1. Not the Payer: The error may arise if you are not the payer for your family member's healthcare insurance.
2. Coverage Under Integrated Shield Plan (IP) or Supplement Plan: If your family member has an Integrated Shield Plan or Supplement Plan, please contact the insured's private insurer directly for payer arrangements.
3. Inactive Coverage: Your family member's healthcare coverage is inactive.

questions.title: Why is there an error message stating that my MediSave balance is insufficient to take over paying an insured's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
If you received an error message stating that your MediSave balance is insufficient to take over paying an insured's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums, it could be because your MediSave balance has been reserved for upcoming premium payments for yourself and/or your dependants' healthcare insurance coverage.
If you do not have enough MediSave balance to take over paying another insured's CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediShield Life premiums, you may top up your MediSave balance or arrange for another family member to take over the insured's premiums. This will ensure that you have sufficient MediSave balance reserved for your own healthcare needs.

questions.title: Why is there an increase in my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life premiums increase with age as they are set in line with the risks for each age group. This is to avoid intergenerational cross-subsidy, where the young have to pay for the old. If premiums were not priced by age, they would keep escalating as a growing number of elderly would need to be supported by a decreasing number of younger members, imposing an increasing burden on future generations. Instead, the Government provides subsidies and premium assistance to those who are unable to afford their premiums.
Premiums may also be adjusted periodically to support enhancements to the scheme, such as expanded coverage and increased claim limits. From April 2025, premiums will increase upon policy renewal to support MediShield Life enhancements. You can refer to the MediShield Life premium rate table for policy periods commencing or renewing on or after 1 April 2025.
For more information, visit the MSHL 2024 Review page.

questions.title: Why is there an increase in the deductible?
questions.text:
The deductible sieves out smaller bills that can be paid via MediSave, and focuses MediShield Life coverage on larger, catastrophic bills. This keeps premiums affordable for all policyholders. By avoiding first-dollar coverage, the deductible also encourages prudent use of healthcare.
The deductible has not been adjusted since 2015. With rising bill sizes, the deductible has become less effective over time in filtering out smaller bills. If the deductible is not increased, the scheme will pay out for many more smaller bills, and premiums will have to increase even more.
To help Singaporeans cope with the increase in deductible, MOH will increase MediSave limits such that those with sufficient MediSave will generally not see an increase in cash out of pocket.
For those with insufficient MediSave, the Government will provide additional support such as MediSave top-ups. There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave.

questions.title: Why not extend premium payment for life for CareShield Life, like MediShield Life?
questions.text: Lengthening the premium payment duration by bringing down the start age to age 30 and extending the end age to 67 is sufficient to improve CareShield Life premium affordability, while still keeping premium payment largely during one’s working years.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Why not extend premium payment for life for CareShield Life, like MediShield Life?
questions.text: The current premium payment duration is sufficient to improve CareShield Life premium affordability, while still keeping premium payment largely during one’s working years.

questions.title: Why was the CareShield Life premium payment term extended to age 67?
questions.text:
Starting the CareShield Life premium payment duration at age 30, and ending at age 67 lengthens the premium payment duration. A longer duration of premium payment allows insureds to spread premium payment over more years, so as to reduce annual premiums payable.
The premium payment end age might be subsequently reviewed to take into consideration the changes in the re-employment age. Ample notice will be given to cohorts who are affected by any changes to the premium payment end age.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Why was the payment for my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) / MediShield Life (MSL) unsuccessful even though there are sufficient funds in my MediSave Account (MA)?
questions.text: The funds in your MediSave Account (MA) may be reserved for other healthcare payments, such as ElderShield/CareShield Life premiums, hospitalisation bills, or premium payments for your dependents’ healthcare policies. These may have resulted in insufficient funds in your MA to pay for your Integrated Shield Plan / MediShield Life.

questions.title: Will CareShield Life premiums increase due to the increase in GST?
questions.text:
CareShield Life premiums are inclusive of the prevailing GST rate.
In Budget 2022, the Minister for Finance announced that the GST rate will be increased from 7% to 8% with effect from 1 January 2023 and from 8% to 9% with effect from 1 January 2024. As GST is levied on CareShield Life premiums at the prevailing GST rate, the premiums will increase accordingly.
You will be able to view your personalised premiums and subsidies via the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Will checks be conducted for new Singapore Residents who are covered under MediShield Life?
questions.text:
For new Singapore Residents who are covered under MediShield Life, we will have a range of checks, including reviewing medical records after they are covered. They are required to declare their health status upon receipt of the In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter from the Immigration Checkpoint Authority of Singapore (ICA).
If they are identified to have serious pre-existing medical conditions, they will be subjected to 30% Additional Premiums for 10 years. Those who make false health declarations will be guilty of an offence under the MediShield Life Scheme Act and will be liable to pay penalties.

questions.title: Will ElderShield 300 or 400 insureds receive premium subsidies if they upgrade to CareShield Life?
questions.text: CareShield Life premium subsidies will be extended to eligible Singaporeans, including those currently on ElderShield 300 or 400 (born in 1979 or earlier), if they upgrade to CareShield Life. These subsidies are intended to support the increased benefits under CareShield Life and ensure that CareShield Life premiums remain affordable. You can refer to the types of premium support available for more information.

questions.title: Will ElderShield premiums increase due to the increase in GST?
questions.text:
ElderShield premiums are inclusive of the prevailing GST rate.
In Budget 2022, the Minister for Finance announced that the GST rate will be increased from 7% to 8% with effect from 1 January 2023 and from 8% to 9% with effect from 1 January 2024. As GST is levied on ElderShield premiums at the prevailing GST rate, the premiums will increase accordingly.
The new ElderShield premium rate table (for policy periods on or after 1 Jan 2023) can be found on CPF website, under ElderShield premiums table.

questions.title: Will I be able to view claim details of my dependant(s) from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
You will be able to view claim details of your dependant(s) if
(i) You are the MediSave payer for your dependant’s hospitalisation; or
(ii) You are the MediShield Life premium payer for the dependant who is less than 16 years old.
If your dependants are 16 years old and above, they may apply for SingPass here and login to view their own healthcare payment details.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will I be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies for the lower- to middle-income for the rest of my life?
questions.text:
Premium Subsidies are provided to help the lower- to middle-income households with their MediShield Life premiums as long as you meet the eligibility criteria. Pioneer Generation Subsidies are applicable for the rest of the Pioneer's life.
The Government will ensure that the process for subsidies is as simple and convenient as possible, so that those who meet the eligibility criteria can get the subsidies easily.

questions.title: Will I be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
You will receive MediShield Life Premium Subsidies (up to 60%) if you meet the following eligibility criteria:
Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.
Household monthly income per person of $3,600 and below
Living in a property with an Annual Value of $31,000 and below.
Those who are either older, have lower income or live in residences with lower Annual Value will enjoy higher subsidy rates. Individuals who own multiple properties will not be eligible.
Permanent Residents will receive half of the subsidy rates applicable to Singapore Citizens. This is aligned to the subsidy policy in public healthcare institutions.

questions.title: Will I be informed of how much I have claimed to date from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text: You will be able to view the total amount that you have claimed for the current policy year, as at the date of enquiry.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will I be notified about the status of my Direct Debit Authorisation application?
questions.text: You will be notified once the bank has approved your Direct Debit Authorisation (DDA) application, which generally takes four to six weeks. Once your DDA is approved, you can begin submitting reimbursements online.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Will I continue getting ElderShield premium rebates in the future?
questions.text: This will depend on the claims experience of the ElderShield scheme. Premium rebates are only given if subsequent ElderShield claims are lower than projected.

questions.title: Will I continue getting premium rebates in the future?
questions.text: This will depend on the claims experience of the ElderShield scheme. Premium rebates are only given if subsequent ElderShield claims are lower than projected.

questions.title: Will I continue to be covered under the same premium rates for my existing Home Protection Scheme cover if I have developed new health condition(s) after my cover has been issued to me?
questions.text: If you have developed new health condition(s) after your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover has been issued, you will continue to be covered at the same premium rate under your existing HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Will I get an ElderShield premium rebate if I have already joined CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you upgraded to CareShield Life on or before 31 December 2022, the ElderShield rebate would have been incorporated into your CareShield Life premiums, which would become lower as a result. Please be assured that you did not lose your ElderShield premium rebate by upgrading to CareShield Life.
Those who joined CareShield Life on or after 1 January 2023, should get the ElderShield premium rebate.

questions.title: Will I get higher subsidies if I am of an older age since my CareShield Life premiums will be higher?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1979 or earlier, you will receive means-tested subsidies of up to 30% on your base premiums for CareShield Life. Given that premiums increase with age, the annual subsidies for older Singaporeans will also be higher to offset the higher annual premiums.
The Government will also be providing participation incentives of between $500 ($50/year) and $2500 ($250/year) to encourage those born in 1979 or earlier to join the scheme by 31 December 2023. The incentive amount is tiered by age, and older Singaporeans will receive higher incentives. Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens will receive additional participation incentives of $1,500 ($150/year), with the total participation incentives coming up to $4,000 ($400/year). The participation incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and will be used to offset premiums payable for each year.
To encourage more Singapore Citizens to join CareShield Life, those who join and are covered between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024 will receive participation incentives of up to $1,875 ($187.50/year). Additional participation incentives of $1,125 ($112.50/year) will be provided to Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens.
Those who need more assistance with their premium payment after subsidies and the participation incentives will receive Additional Premium Support, and no one who joins CareShield Life will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Will I get higher subsidies if I am of an older age since my CareShield Life premiums will be higher?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1979 or earlier, you will receive means-tested subsidies of up to 30% on your base premiums for CareShield Life. Given that premiums increase with age, the annual subsidies for older Singaporeans will also be higher to offset the higher annual premiums.
Those who need more assistance with their premium payment after subsidies will receive Additional Premium Support.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.

questions.title: Will I receive any premium subsidies as an ElderShield 300/400 insured if I upgrade to CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you are an ElderShield insured, you can receive CareShield Life premium subsidies if you upgrade to CareShield Life. CareShield Life is a new scheme, and these subsidies will ensure that the premiums remain affordable even as the new scheme offers better protection and benefits.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Will I receive premium subsidies even if I am not the one paying for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text: You will be able to receive subsidies if you meet the eligibility criteria, regardless of who is paying for your premiums.

questions.title: Will I receive premium subsidies if my child / payer is paying for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text: You will receive the subsidies you are eligible for regardless of who is paying your MediShield Life premiums. You can login to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' to check your eligible subsidies.

questions.title: Will individuals with developmental disorders have to pay the Additional Premiums?
questions.text: Developmental conditions such as Down Syndrome and Autism alone do not have Additional Premiums imposed on them. However, if an individual with these conditions also presents with serious pre-existing medical complications, such as heart or kidney disease, which elevate the risk of claims, MediShield Life will apply Additional Premiums based on these medical conditions.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: Will interest and penalties be imposed if I make partial payment for my outstanding MediShield Life or CareShield Life premiums before the IRAS deadline?
questions.text:
Yes, paying only part of your outstanding MediShield Life or CareShield Life premiums would not stop interest and penalties from being charged. To avoid these charges, you will need to pay the full amount by the deadline stated in your IRAS notice.
If any MediShield Life or CareShield Life premiums remain unpaid, you may continue to be charged annual interest of 4% (compounded) and penalties of up to 17% of the outstanding amount.
We encourage you to pay your premiums in full by the deadline to avoid any further charges or enforcement action. For payment options, refer to "How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)s' CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?"

questions.title: Will my ElderShield premiums change due to Government administration?
questions.text: You will continue to pay the same premiums and enjoy the same benefits under ElderShield for as long as you are covered even after the Government takes over the administration. In the event that the actual claims experience turns out better than expected, there will continue to be premium rebates for ElderShield insureds.
topics: ElderShield / Government Administration of ElderShield in 2021

questions.title: Will my ElderShield premiums change due to Government administration?
questions.text: Since November 2021, the Government has taken over the administration of ElderShield from insurers. You will continue to pay the same premiums and enjoy the same benefits under ElderShield for as long as you are covered. In the event that the actual claims are lower than projected, premium rebates will be given to eligible ElderShield insureds.

questions.title: Will my hospitalisation claims still be processed after renouncement or citizenship or permanent resident status?
questions.text:
If you are insured by MediShield Life only, you can claim for medical treatments consumed prior to the renouncement date of your citizenship.
Please inform your private insurer if you have plans to renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status so that your insurer can advise you on the available coverage options, and on the processing of your claims under your Integrated Shield Plan.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) benefits be affected by the MediShield Life review?
questions.text: Whether your IP benefits will be affected will depend on your insurer, as the IP benefits are set, reviewed and adjusted by insurers based on their own commercial and actuarial considerations.

questions.title: Will my Integrated Shield Plan premiums be affected by changes in MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of two components: (i) the MediShield Life component and (ii) the additional private insurance component that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays. Correspondingly, IP premiums are made up of MediShield Life premiums and premiums for the additional private insurance component.
Hence, your overall IP premium will be affected by both changes in the MediShield Life premiums and premiums for the additional private insurance component:
If MediShield premiums increase/decrease, the premiums for the MediShield Life component of IPs will be increased/decreased accordingly.
Premiums for the additional private insurance component of IPs are set, reviewed and adjusted by private insurers based on commercial and actuarial considerations. Insurers may adjust their premiums upwards/downwards taking into account the impact of their claims experience, medical inflation and their own product changes if any. Insurers have an incentive to keep premiums competitive, to attract and retain policyholders. Singaporeans concerned with the affordability of IP premiums may wish to consider switching to more affordable insurance options, in line with their preferences for hospitalisation coverage.

questions.title: Will my MediSave be deducted if the amount is less than my/my dependant's outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The amount deducted from your MediSave Account will be your/your dependant’s outstanding premium, or your MediSave balance, whichever is lower.
If you have insufficient MediSave for premium payment, please click on the link below to view the payment options.
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)'s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: Will my new CPF working contribution partially pay off my outstanding MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums if I am on a monthly GIRO instalment plan?
questions.text:
Yes, your new CPF working contributions will be used to pay your outstanding MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums. This helps to reduce the outstanding amount and avoid enforcement actions.
If you are currently on a monthly GIRO payment arrangement, your monthly GIRO deduction amount will remain unchanged, but the payment plan will end earlier once outstanding premiums are fully paid.

questions.title: Will new Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents be required to join MediShield Life?
questions.text:
New Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents will be required to join MediShield Life, in line with the principle of universal coverage. New Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with serious pre-existing conditions may have to pay Additional Premiums upon joining MediShield Life. They will be eligible for Government subsidies for their MediShield Life premiums if they meet the eligibility criteria and will receive premium rebates in line with their age of entry.
They will be notified of their MediShield Life cover by Central Provident Fund Board when their covers have been issued, generally within 1 month of attaining permanent residence.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: Will overseas Singaporeans in financial difficulties be eligible for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text:
Overseas Singaporeans who have insufficient MediSave and limited family support to pay their MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life premiums will be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). Please note that all APS applications will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.
If you require further clarification, please call us at 1800-222-3399 (or +65 6222 3399 from overseas) from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8) or write in to us through this online form.

questions.title: Will overseas Singaporeans receive Premium Subsidies?
Will overseas Singaporeans who relocate back to Singapore be eligible for the subsidies for all premiums?
questions.text:
Overseas Singaporeans approved for suspension of premium collection will be treated similar to other Singaporeans and receive all prevailing subsidies, if eligible. They will automatically receive Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Transitional Subsidies for the applicable policy years. They will receive Premium Subsidies if they apply and submit sufficient documentation for MOH to assess their eligibility for Premium Subsidies prior to the applicable policy year. These subsidies will be factored into the total net amount to be paid should the overseas Singaporean relocate back to Singapore.
Besides subsidies, financial assistance may be available on a case by case basis upon return and the Insured may apply for assessment.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Will premium recovery measures for MediShield Life include chasing the next of kin?
questions.text:
Premium recovery measures will not be levied on the next of kin. Members are responsible for their own MediShield Life premiums.
The Government will implement measures such as imposition of interest and penalty on outstanding premiums on members who default premium payments repeatedly.

questions.title: Will the 2024 increase in Annual Value (AV) impact my eligibility for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: The disbursement of social support schemes (e.g. CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, MediShield Life Premium Subsidies) will not be affected by the revision of Annual Values (AVs) in 2024 as AVs as of 2023 will be used to determine scheme eligibility in 2024. The Government will continue to review our social support schemes to ensure that Singaporeans in need of support receive it.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Will the 2025 increase in Annual Value (AV) impact my eligibility for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: The disbursement of social support schemes (e.g. CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, MediShield Life Premium Subsidies) will not be affected by the revision of Annual Values (AVs) in 2025 as AVs as of 2024 will be used to determine scheme eligibility in 2025. The Government will continue to review our social support schemes to ensure that Singaporeans in need of support receive it.

questions.title: Will the CareShield Life premium payment end age go up further based on the prevailing re-employment age?
questions.text: The premium payment end age of CareShield Life will be set taking into account any changes to the re-employment age in future. Ample notice will be given to you if you are affected by any changes to the premium payment end age.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Will the claim details on the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements be changed if the hospital adjusts my bill size?
questions.text: Yes, the online statements will take into account any adjustments made to the hospital bills, if the hospital has informed the Central Provident Fund Board about the change before the date of enquiry.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will the Supplement premiums that I have already paid, be taken into account when I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Supplement products are strictly run by the private insurers and the premiums that have already been paid for Supplements will not be taken into account when you upgrade to CareShield Life. These Supplement policies will stay in-force as long as you continue to contribute premiums and do not terminate their coverage.
Nonetheless, ElderShield premiums that ElderShield insureds have paid will be taken into account when computing their CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: Will there be any fees for unsuccessful GIRO deduction of MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: CPF Board (Billing Organization) will not impose any charges for unsuccessful deductions of MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums. However, some banks will impose service charges as an unsuccessful deduction may be treated like a bounced cheque. Please contact your bank for further details on the fees and charges (if applicable).

questions.title: Will those who are less well-off and unable to pay their premiums face these premium recovery measures?
questions.text:
In addition to premium support measures from the Government to help the lower-income ensure that premiums are affordable (e.g. Additional Premium Support), these are some other measures that have been implemented:
a. Helping to keep MediSave contributions current. As MediShield Life premiums are deducted from a policyholder’s MediSave account, the first step is to ensure that MediSave contributions are kept current. The Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board has in place arrangements with multiple government agencies to ensure employers, employees and especially self-employed persons meet contribution requirements.
b. Supporting switch of payment to other family members’ MediSave accounts. If an insured person has insufficient MediSave balance, immediate family members such as parents and spouses can use their MediSave to help pay for their family member’s premiums.
c. Regular reminder letters to top up the insured’s MediSave account and to pay MediShield Life premiums.
These measures ensure that premium recovery measures are targeted at those who have the means to pay but choose not to do so. There is Additional Premium Support (APS) to help those who are unable to afford their MediShield Life premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave use, and if they have limited family support. No one will be denied MediShield Life coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: With MediShield Life, will the Integrated Shield Plans cover pre-existing conditions? Can I now get coverage under Integrated Shield Plans for my pre-existing conditions?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of two components: (i) the MediShield Life component and (ii) the additional private insurance component that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays.
You can get coverage for pre-existing conditions, and be assured of lifelong coverage, under the MediShield Life component of your IP.
This is even if the condition is excluded from the additional private insurance coverage by your IP insurer.
Underwriting decisions on the additional private insurance component of IPs are separately determined by the private IP insurers. Private insurers assess applications for the additional private insurance component of the IP based on their own risk assessment frameworks, as these are commercial decisions. You may wish to check with your private insurer or financial advisor on coverage for pre-existing conditions.

questions.title: With the availability of the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements, will I still receive hardcopy statements?
questions.text:
You will not receive a hardcopy statement when deductions are made from your MediSave Account to pay for your dependents or your own medical bills. Instead, you will be informed of any deductions via one of the following mobile notifications:
a. If you have the Singpass Mobile App, you will be notified via the Singpass Mobile App Inbox;
b. If you do not have the Singpass Mobile App, but have registered your mobile number with Singpass, you will be notified via SMS.
If you still prefer to receive a hardcopy of your MediSave transaction statement, please write to us. If you do not have a Singpass account and or a registered mobile number, you will continue to receive the hardcopy MediSave transaction statement. No further action is required.
If your claim was only for MediShield Life and there was no deduction made from your MediSave account for the claim, you will not receive a hardcopy statement. For these cases, you will be able to access the claim details from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements.
If you would like to have the claim statements but are unable to log in online, you may approach our customer service officers over the counter or contact us at 1800 222 3399 for assistance.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: With the GST increase, what is being done to help Singaporeans cushion the impact of premium increase?
questions.text:
The Government has announced the enhanced Assurance Package for GST to cushion the impact of the planned GST increase for at least 5 years for most Singaporean households. This includes MediSave top-up of $150 each year from 2023 to 2025, for Singaporeans aged 20 years and below, or 55 years old and above, which may be used to offset the premium increase.
The Assurance Package for GST also includes cash payouts of $700 to $1,600 over five years, for all Singaporeans aged 21 years and above.
Older Singaporeans aged 65 and above, whose residential address is a property that does not exceed an Annual Value of $21,000 and who own only one property will also continue to receive an annual MediSave top-up of up to $450. This is beyond the transitional support covered by the Assurance Package.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: With the GST increase, what is being done to help Singaporeans cushion the impact of premium increase?
questions.text:
The Government has announced the enhanced Assurance Package for GST to cushion the impact of the planned GST increase for at least 5 years for most Singaporean households. This includes MediSave top-up of $150 each year from 2023 to 2025, for Singaporeans aged 20 years and below, or 55 years old and above, which may be used to offset the premium increase.
The Assurance Package for GST also includes cash payouts of $700 to $1,600 over five years, for all Singaporeans aged 21 years and above.
Older Singaporeans aged 65 and above, whose residential address is a property that does not exceed an Annual Value of $21,000 and who own only one property will also continue to receive an annual MediSave top-up of up to $450. This is beyond the transitional support covered by the Assurance Package.

questions.title: Would I have duplicate coverage or pay double premiums if I buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) when I am already covered under MediShield Life?
questions.text: There is no duplication in coverage and you are not paying double premiums. Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are automatically covered under MediShield Life for life. When you buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) through a private insurer, the IP consists of two components: your existing MediShield Life component and an additional private insurance coverage component. You will continue to be able to enjoy MediShield Life benefits when you buy an IP.

questions.title: How does the Matched MediSave Scheme work?
questions.text:
Members’ eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) will be automatically assessed annually. No application by members is needed.
Each year, if you are eligible, we will notify you at the beginning of the year. You can also check your eligibility via the Healthcare dashboard.
Cash top-ups to MA can be made by yourself, loved ones, employers or members of the community.
If you are eligible and have received cash top-ups to your MediSave Account (MA) by 31 December of the year, you will receive a matching grant at the beginning of the following year.
MMSS is implemented from January 2026. Cash top-ups made before 2026 is not eligible for matching grants under this scheme.
Individual givers will not receive tax relief for cash top-ups that attract the MMSS matching grant.
Members may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $8,000 per year for eligible cash top-ups to their own Special Account, Retirement Account or MA, and another $8,000 per year for cash top-ups to such accounts of their loved ones, that do not attract the matching grant for MMSS or the Matched Retirement Saving Scheme (MRSS).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Is there a maximum amount that I can save in my MediSave Account?
questions.text:
You can save up to the prevailing Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) in your MediSave Account (MA) if you have not turned age 65. It is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA.
From 1 January 2026, the BHS is $79,000 for all CPF members aged 65 years and below. The BHS applicable to you will be adjusted yearly to keep pace with rising healthcare consumption until you turn age 65. For example, if you are aged 65 years old in 2026, your applicable BHS will be fixed at $79,000 for the rest of your life. questions.title: How can I check whether I have any MediSave payable as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
You can check your MediSave payable by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
You can apply for your Singpass online if you do not have one.

questions.title: If I do not have enough in my MediSave, and I am not able to pay the remaining co-payment, are there other ways to receive the vaccination?
questions.text:
At CHAS GP clinics, these nationally recommended vaccinations are fully subsidised for those who hold the Public Assistance card.
Patients who go to the polyclinics for their vaccination(s) and have financial difficulties in paying for their bills can approach the social worker at polyclinics to enquire for assistance.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my family member’s hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
If your approved dependants do not have sufficient MediSave for their hospitalisation expenses, you may consider using your MediSave to pay for them. Approved dependants refer to a member’s spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. They can be of any nationality except for grandparents and siblings who must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
It is important to note that while your approved dependants can tap on your MediSave, the amount they can use is still subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per hospitalisation episode basis. If they still have outstanding hospitalisation expenses after using up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, they would have to pay the remainder in cash.
For more information, please speak to the staff at the hospital's Business Office.
You should use your MediSave prudently to provide for your own and your approved dependants’ hospitalisation needs. This is because you may require more medical care in your old age.
Should you wish to use your MediSave for your approved dependants’ hospitalisation expenses, you may approach the hospital where they are receiving treatment at to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF). The hospital will then submit the claim to us and payment from your MediSave will be made directly to the hospital.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my family member’s outpatient treatment expenses?
questions.text:
If your approved dependants do not have sufficient MediSave for their outpatient treatment expenses, you may consider using your MediSave to pay for them. Approved dependants refer to a member’s spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. They can be of any nationality except for grandparents and siblings who must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
While they can tap on your MediSave, the amount they can use is subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per patient basis regardless of the number of payers. If they still have outstanding medical expenses after utilising up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, they would have to pay the remainder in cash.
Should you wish to use your MediSave for your approved dependants’ medical expenses, you may approach the Medical Institution (MI) where they are receiving treatment at to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF). The hospital will then submit the claim to us and payment from your MediSave will be made directly to the MI.

questions.title: Can MediSave be used for the co-payment after subsidy for vaccinations?
questions.text:
Those eligible for subsidised vaccination may also use their MediSave to cover the out-of-pocket expense at CHAS GP clinics and polyclinics.
Please check with your preferred clinic if the clinic is able to process the remaining co-payment via MediSave. If they do, please check with them on your eligibility to pay via MediSave.

questions.title: How do I check my voluntary top-up limit to my MediSave Account?
questions.text:
When you make a MediSave top-up online, you will be shown the amount of MediSave top-up you can receive before you reach the top-up limit.
You can follow these steps to check how much you can top up to your MediSave Account:
Go to the Top up MediSave Account form
Log in with your Singpass
Select “I wish to make a top-up to Myself” under “Recipient details”
Your top-up limit will then be displayed.
If you are making a top-up to your loved ones, please check with your recipient directly on the amount he can receive.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: I visited a clinic for an outpatient treatment that can be paid by my MediSave. How do I go about utilising my MediSave?
questions.text:
To use your MediSave to pay for your outpatient medical treatment cost:
1. Inform the clinic that you wish to use MediSave to pay for your outpatient medical treatment. The staff will require your NRIC/Passport. If you are paying for your approved dependant, please also produce his/her NRIC/Passport. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
2. The clinic may require information on how much MediSave is available for payment of the outpatient treatment. You will be able to obtain this information by logging in to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass. This is not needed if the clinic can check on your behalf.
3. You and the patient (if applicable) must sign a Medical Claims Authorisation Form to allow the clinic to use your MediSave to pay for the outpatient medical treatment bill.
4. If your employer or insurer is also paying for your outpatient treatment, please bring along your Letter of Guarantee or Employer Identity Pass (i.e. if your clinic has an existing arrangement with your employer or insurer).

questions.title: If I am hospitalised, how much MediSave can I use to pay for my hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
For daily hospital charges1, you can use up to $1,130 per day from MediSave for the first two days of inpatient stays, and $400 per day thereafter.
If you had undergone a surgery, you can use your MediSave to cover part of, or the whole surgery cost. The amount of MediSave you can use depends on the complexity of your surgery, as listed in the Table of Surgical Procedures. You may refer to the MOH website for more information on withdrawal limits for MediSave.
It is useful to note that you are considered hospitalised if you have been admitted for at least eight hours. This requirement does not apply to day surgeries.
1 Includes eligible Mobile Inpatient Care @ Home stays

questions.title: What happens to my MediSave if I do not use it?
questions.text:
Any unused MediSave savings will remain in your MediSave Account and grow with interest.
Learn more about CPF interest rates.

questions.title: What if I have insufficient MediSave balances for my healthcare and long-term care expenses?
questions.text:
The minimum MediSave Account balance of $5,000 under MediSave Care is carefully set to help individuals maintain some savings to pay for for their healthcare bills.
If you have depleted your MediSave account, you may tap on your spouse's MediSave for long-term care withdrawals, and your family members' MediSave for your other healthcare treatments.
You may also apply for other forms of assistance such as means-tested Government assistance schemes (ElderFund, Home Caregiving Grant) to meet your long-term care costs needs. If you are still unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, there are other forms of assistance such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for the removal of my wisdom tooth?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave savings to pay for the removal of your wisdom tooth incurred at a participating private dental clinic under the MediSave Scheme, provided that it is a surgical procedure. The day surgery limits are:
1) Day surgeryUp to a maximum of $830 per day for daily hospital charges, including investigations, medicines and doctor's attendance fees.
2) OperationA fixed limit for operations ranging from $240 to $5,290 depending on the type of operations performed.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for my siblings' medical expenses?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave to pay for your siblings' medical expenses, as long as they are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents (SC/PR). You would have to provide proof to the medical institutions that your siblings are SC/PR (e.g. NRICs).

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for outpatient treatment of chronic diseases?
questions.text:
You can use MediSave for outpatient treatments of the chronic diseases listed below.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) regularly reviews the list of conditions covered under the Chronic Disease Management Programme, to ensure that they continue to meet the needs of Singaporeans.
For more information, please visit the Ministry of Health website.

questions.title: Can I voluntarily top-up to my Ordinary Account only?
questions.text:
Voluntary top-ups cannot be made solely to the Ordinary Account.
You can make voluntary top-ups to your:
Special / Retirement Account only under the Retirement Sum Topping Up Scheme (RSTU) (tax relief available).
MediSave Account only (tax relief available)1
3 CPF accounts2
Voluntary top-up is applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents only.
You can find out more on the different voluntary top-ups.
1For self-employed persons who wish to make a voluntary top up to MediSave Account, you must have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable as a self-employed person.
2Tax relief is only applicable to self-employed persons, based on their assessable net trade income for the year of assessment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How do I request an instalment plan for my MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
You can request an instalment plan to make your MediSave contributions in monthly instalments via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
If you have an existing instalment plan and wish to lower your existing monthly instalment amount, you can submit a request via the same form.
Please note that your request is subject to the Board’s approval. You may be required to provide additional information or supporting documents, if necessary.

questions.title: I've used up my Flexi-MediSave limit of $400, but my spouse needs medical treatment too. Can I use my MediSave for his/her medical bills?
questions.text:
Seniors aged 60 and older can use up to $400 per year under Flexi-MediSave for their own outpatient treatments, using their own MediSave or their spouse’s MediSave (spouse has to be aged 60 and older too).
If a senior has already used up their own $400 limit for outpatient treatments, they may still use their MediSave savings to pay for their spouse’s outpatient treatments, subject to the spouse’s $400 limit.
The $400 withdrawal limit applies to each patient per year, regardless whose MediSave account is used.

questions.title: What happens if I do not have the Basic Healthcare Sum when I turn age 65?
questions.text: The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the estimated savings you need in your MediSave Account (MA) to cover your basic subsidised healthcare expenses in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA. If your balance is less than the cohort BHS at age 65, you are not required to top up your MA. However, if you wish to build up your healthcare savings, you can choose to top up your MA with cash. You can do so via this form to make cash top-ups to your own or your loved ones’ MA.

questions.title: What is the minimum balance I need to set aside in my MediSave Account?
questions.text: There is no minimum amount required to set aside in your MediSave Account (MA). A portion of your working contributions will be allocated to your MA until your balance reaches the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). The BHS is the estimated savings you need in your MA to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA. Any amount above the BHS will be channelled to your other CPF accounts, depending on your age. You can find out how MediSave contributions above the BHS are channelled to other CPF accounts via this link.

questions.title: When will my eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme be assessed and do I need to apply?
questions.text:
Members’ eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) will be automatically assessed annually. You do not need to apply for the scheme.
MMSS is implemented in January 2026 for five years. You will be notified at the beginning of each year if you are eligible for the scheme for the year via email or post. Eligibility information will be available around the 2nd or 3rd week of January of each year and notifications to eligible members will be sent out around end January.
You can also check your eligibility for the MMSS via the Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Who administers MediSave Care?
questions.text: MediSave Care is jointly administered by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB).

questions.title: Are my MediSave Account savings covered under CPF Nomination?
questions.text: CPF Nomination covers all savings in your MediSave Account, including those in your Ordinary, Special and Retirement Accounts.

questions.title: As a bankrupt, can I still use my MediSave?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave to pay for your own or your approved dependants' healthcare expenses even if you have declared bankruptcy. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

questions.title: Can I sign up for CareShield Life on behalf of my parent/spouse/sibling?
questions.text:
Your family member’s Singpass will be required to sign up for CareShield Life.
You can guide your family member to use his/her Singpass to apply for CareShield Life via the Application to join CareShield Life form. Some applicants may need to undergo a disability assessment. Your family member will be informed by Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) if a disability assessment is required, after his/her application.
If they are facing difficulties, you can accompany them to the Community Clubs/Centres to sign up.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my dental implant?
questions.text:
You can use MediSave to pay for your dental implant insertion or removal as long as it is a surgical procedure.
For a dental surgery with insertion or removal of dental implants, you can use MediSave to pay for your dental implants, up to the following limits:
Insertion of Dental Implants
Number of implant(s) inserted x $1,120 Operation limit of Table 2C
Removal of Dental Implants
Number of implant(s) removed x $490 Operation limit of Table 1C
For example, if you have to insert two dental implants, you can use up to $2,240 (2 x $1,120) for payment of your dental implants.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for optional/cosmetic treatments like liposuction, orthodontics treatment or laser surgery to correct short-sightedness?
questions.text: Generally, MediSave cannot be used for optional/cosmetic treatments. Please check with your attending doctor if the cost of your treatment can be covered by your MediSave.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for overseas treatment/hospitalisation?
questions.text:
Use of MediSave for Overseas Treatment - Elective
Patients who are Singaporeans (SC) or Permanent Residents (PR) may use their own or their immediate family member's MediSave for overseas elective treatments at accredited hospitals, subject to the applicable MediSave withdrawal limits. Immediate family members include spouses, children, parents, siblings and/or grandchildren.
To use MediSave for overseas treatment, patients must obtain a referral from MediSave-accredited healthcare provider, Health Management International (HMI). They can contact HMI directly to check if HMI has affiliated hospital(s) in the country where they wish to receive treatment. Please visit the HMI website or call HMI at 6322 6333 for more information.
Use of MediSave for Overseas Treatment - Medical Emergency/Treatment not Available in Singapore
MediSave is primarily meant to help Singaporeans and Permanent Residents pay for their major inpatient hospitalisation expenses and selected outpatient expenses locally. When travelling overseas, CPF members should consider purchasing travel insurance to protect against the risk of incurring unforeseen medical expenses.
Requests to use MediSave for overseas emergency treatments will be considered on a case-by-case basis if the following conditions are first fulfilled:
The patient must be a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR) of Singapore (Please note that the patient may appeal to use his/her or their immediate family members' MediSave to pay for their own overseas hospitalisations. Immediate family members include member’s spouse, children, parents, siblings and/or grandparents.); and
The use of MediSave is only limited to inpatient admission that exceeds a minimum of eight hours or day surgery, which has been assessed to be a medical emergency by our Medical Advisors. It cannot be used for outpatient treatments.
If the above conditions are fufilled, please submit your request along with the following supporting documents through the Ministry of Health (MOH) feedback form:
Original copy (Certified true copy by Hospital is accepted) of the patient's medical records - Discharge summary, operation notes (if any) or clinical notes showing the history, diagnosis and treatment plan for the patient.
Original copy (Certified true copy by Hospital is accepted) of the final hospital bill for the patient.
Passport information - showing passport holder and the entry/departure of the foreign country.
Completed Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF), to authorise the use of MediSave upon an approval. You may find a copy of the MCAF on the MOH website.
NRIC – Front and back copy belonging to patient and MediSave payer (if applicable).
The above documents must be in English, or be officially translated into English.
Should your request be approved by MOH, CPF Board will process the MediSave deduction and pay the money to the MediSave payer’s bank account as maintained in CPF Board’s records. The MediSave payer may confirm or update his/her bank account via my cpf digital services – Account settings.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for Traditional Chinese Medicine?
questions.text: If you are aged 60 and above, you may withdraw up to $400 per year from your own, or your spouse’s MediSave Account under the Flexi-MediSave scheme to pay for acupuncture treatment for lower back pain and neck pain at specialist outpatient clinics in public hospitals.

questions.title: Do I have to top up my MediSave Account to the Basic Healthcare Sum if I start withdrawing my CPF savings from age 55?
questions.text: You do not need to top up your MediSave Account (MA) when you begin withdrawing your CPF savings from age 55. The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the estimated savings you need in your MA to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA.

questions.title: Do I need to wait for my 30th birthday before I can apply for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
To be qualified for MediSave Care, you need to be at least 30 years old and fulfil all the following criteria.
a. Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.
b. Certified by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to have developed severe disability (i.e. unable to perform three (3) or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). You can find the list of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors here.
c. Have a minimum MediSave balance of $5,000.

questions.title: Do I still have to contribute to MediSave as a self-employed person even though my MediSave balance has reached the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS)?
questions.text:
As a self-employed person, you are required to make mandatory MediSave contributions even if you have met the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). Your MediSave contributions are computed based on your assessable net trade income.
This is no different from employees and platform workers, who continue to make CPF contributions, based on their employee wages or platform worker net earnings, even after reaching BHS and/or the Full Retirement Sum (FRS).
MediSave Account (MA) savings above the BHS will first be channelled to your CPF Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA), depending on your age, to build up your retirement savings. Once you have met the FRS in your SA or RA, the MA savings in excess of the BHS will be channelled to your Ordinary Account, which you can tap on for your housing needs. This overflow arrangement prevents excessive accumulation in your MA and helps to enhance your retirement and housing adequacy.

questions.title: How can I check my and my loved ones’ eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is implemented in January 2026. Eligibility is automatically assessed annually, and eligible members will be notified at the beginning of each year. Eligibility information will be available around the 2nd or 3rd week of January of each year, and the notifications are expected to be sent to eligible members around end January.
Checking your own eligibility:
Only members aged 55 to 70 (inclusive) may be eligible for MMSS. You can check your eligibility via the Healthcare dashboard by logging into your CPF account with Singpass.
Alternatively, when you are making cash top-up to your MediSave Account (MA), the online application form will display information on your eligibility.
Please refer to the following illustrations on how to read the information provided.
Logging on to your own Healthcare dashboard
Through the online application form to top up MediSave Account
Checking your loved ones’ eligibility:
When you are making a cash top-up for your loved one, the online application form will display information on their eligibility. If they are eligible for MMSS, the form will also display the estimated matching grant that your loved ones may receive on your intended cash top-up for them.
Please refer to the following illustrations on how to read the information provided.

For top ups to other loved ones,
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I make a CareShield Life claim?
questions.text:
If you are covered under CareShield Life and would like to make a claim, you can arrange for a severe disability assessment with an MOH-accredited assessor and submit your application through the AIC’s eService portal (eFASS) using your Singpass.
If you are a caregiver submitting a claim for a mentally incapacitated CareShield insured, you can log in eFASS using your Singpass to submit the application on his/her behalf.

questions.title: I develop severe disability. Can I make MediSave withdrawals under MediSave Care from my spouse's MediSave?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident with severe disability, you can make MediSave withdrawals under MediSave Care from your own and your spouse’s MediSave.
If you are not a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident and have developed severe disability, your application to make withdrawal from your own and/or your spouse’s MediSave under MediSave Care will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.
To apply for MediSave Care, you should submit an application to the Agency for Integrated Care, and arrange for disability assessment by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.

questions.title: I have outstanding MediSave payable but I am unable to contribute the full amount. Can I make a partial contribution using the Manage your MediSave Payable form (MMSP)?
questions.text: You can make contributions of any amount using the Manage your MediSave Payable (MMSP) form, if you are contributing to your MediSave monthly via an instalment plan. This enables you to shorten your instalment duration and fulfil your MediSave payable sooner by making additional contributions as and when you wish to.

questions.title: I have saved the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) in my MediSave Account (MA). What happens to the savings in my MA above the BHS?
questions.text:
Any savings in your MediSave Account (MA) above the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) will be channelled to your CPF Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA), depending on your age. The BHS cap and overflow arrangement are designed to prevent excessive saving in your MA while helping to supplement your retirement savings, which can be withdrawn according to the CPF withdrawal rules.
If your MA savings exceed the BHS, the excess will be channelled to your Ordinary Account (OA) if you are:
Below 55 years old and have met the current Full Retirement Sum (FRS) (consisting of your SA balance and any active CPFIS-SA investments) in your SA; or
55 years old or older and have set aside your FRS (which can be entirely in cash or a combination of property and cash) in your RA.
Savings in the OA can be used for other purposes, such as housing repayment or withdrawn if you meet the withdrawal requirements.

questions.title: I have used my MediSave to pay for my medical expenses. Can my employer or insurer reimburse me in cash?
questions.text: Your employer or insurer cannot reimburse you in cash for the portion of your medical expenses paid using your MediSave and/or MediShield Life. The reimbursement for the respective amount must be credited back to your MediSave Account and/or MediShield Life.

questions.title: I paid my medical bill in full using cash, but my employer or insurer has since made a payment to the medical institution for the same bill. How can I be reimbursed for the cash I paid?
questions.text:
Cash reimbursements for medical claims are handled between the patients and their employers or insurers.
You may wish to contact your Medical Institution and/or employer or insurer for assistance in processing the reimbursement for the cash you paid.

questions.title: If I have used up other MediSave limits - for example, for scans or for cancer drug treatment, can I use Flexi-MediSave to pay?
questions.text:
If you are already using MediSave to pay for outpatient treatment but have reached your withdrawal limit, you can use Flexi-MediSave to further lower your cash payment, provided that treatment was sought at a polyclinic, public specialist outpatient clinic or general practitioner clinic participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).
Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for cancer drug treatments using cancer drugs that are not on the Cancer Drug List.
However, as Flexi-MediSave covers a much wider range of outpatient treatments than other limits, you may want to save the use of your Flexi-MediSave for treatments that are not already covered by MediSave so as to lower your total cash payments.

questions.title: If I work after age 65, do I still need to contribute to my MediSave Account?
questions.text: As long as you continue to work, you will need to contribute to your MediSave Account (MA). These contributions will accumulate up to the Basic Healthcare Sum and help cover your medical expenses during retirement.

questions.title: Is there a hotline for the CareShield Life, ElderShield or MediSave Care schemes?
questions.text: You can call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399. The operating hours are from Monday to Friday (excluding public holidays), 8.30am to 5.30pm. Alternatively, you can also write to us.

questions.title: My approved dependant is a foreigner, while I am a Singapore Permanent Resident. He/She has incurred medical expenses in Singapore. Can I use my MediSave to pay for his/her bills?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave to pay for your approved dependant's medical bills, if it is a MediSave-approved treatment incurred at any of the approved medical institutions in Singapore. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

questions.title: My CareShield Life coverage status on my Healthcare dashboard is reflected as 'Waiting for Cover'. Will I be able to claim from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
As your CareShield Life application has been approved, you will be eligible to claim if the onset of severe disability falls on or after your CareShield Life policy start date. This applies even if the premiums have not been deducted.
If you wish to claim from CareShield Life, you can submit your application via the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS) Application Portal using your Singpass.

questions.title: What are the benefits of the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), the Government will match every dollar of cash-top up to the MediSave Account (MA) of eligible members up to $1,000 per year.
Please see below examples for illustration:
Your cash top-upMatching grant from the Government (disbursed the following year)Total increase in your healthcare savings
$2,000 in a lump sumCapped at $1,000$3,000 ($2,000 + $1,000)
$100 monthly for 6 months = $600$600$1,200 ($600 + $600)
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What if I am in financial hardship and is unable to set aside monies for MediSave via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme?
questions.text: We understand that some self-employed persons (SEPs) may be facing financial difficulties and may not be able to cope with Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). Thus, if you do not have outstanding MediSave payable or are contributing via GIRO instalments, you may set your CAYE contribution rate to 0%. This means that you’ll receive your service payment in full, and CAYE contribution will not be deducted from your service payment. Please write to us if you wish to apply for a 0% CAYE contribution rate. CPF Board will assess your eligibility and inform you of the outcome in writing.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What is not covered under the MediSave scheme?
questions.text: MediSave generally does not cover optional and cosmetic treatments, accident and emergency (A&E) fees and non-medical treatments such as ambulance transport. Please approach the medical institution to find out whether your treatment can be covered under MediSave.

questions.title: What is outpatient Flexi-MediSave?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave allows members aged 60 years old and above to use their MediSave or their spouse's MediSave (if the spouse is also aged 60 and above), up to $400 a year, for outpatient medical treatments at polyclinics, public hospital Specialist Outpatient Clinics and general practitioner clinics participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).
Please note that the $400 is applied on a per patient basis, regardless whether you are using your MediSave or your spouse's MediSave.

questions.title: What is the Basic Healthcare Sum when I turn 65 years old?
questions.text:
For each cohort turning 65 years old, the applicable Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is fixed at that year's amount for the rest of their life. It is the maximum amount you can hold in your MediSave Account (MA). For example, if you are 65 years old in 2026, your applicable BHS is $79,000 and will remain unchanged for life.

questions.title: What is the Basic Healthcare Sum?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the estimated savings you need in your MediSave Account (MA) to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA.
For CPF members below age 65, the BHS is adjusted annually to keep pace with rising healthcare consumption. This ensures that the BHS remains relevant when each cohort reaches retirement age.
Once CPF members reach age 65, their BHS is fixed and will remain unchanged for the rest of their lives.

questions.title: What is the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) aims to help Singapore Citizens aged 55 to 70 (inclusive) with lower MediSave savings to boost their healthcare savings by matching voluntary cash top-ups made to their MediSave Account (MA). The scheme is implemented in 2026 for a period of five years.
Under the MMSS, the Government will match every dollar of cash top-up to the MA of eligible members up to $1,000 per year. The matching grant by the Government will be disbursed to eligible members in the following year.
The scheme helps eligible members pay for approved healthcare insurance premiums and approved medical treatments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What is the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF)?
questions.text:
When you seek medical treatment at a Medical Institution (MI) participating in the MediSave scheme, the MI staff will inform you if your MediSave can be used for the treatment as well as the amount you may use.
If you intend to use MediSave for your treatment, you will need to complete the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) provided by the MI staff, and authorise them to submit the claim on your behalf.
There are two types of MCAF available:
1. MCAF (Single Institution)
To authorise a specific Medical Institution (MI) to submit MediSave claim(s) for your own and/or your family member(s) medical expenses that can tap on MediSave. If you have ongoing outpatient treatments at the MI, you can provide authorisation for a specific visit, a specific time period, or a standing authorisation until you revoke it.
2. MCAF (Multiple Institutions)
To authorise all Public Healthcare Institutions (PHI) from now on to submit MediSave claims for your own medical expenses that can tap on MediSave. This means that if you have authorised via MCAF (Multiple Institutions) at one PHI – for example, a hospital, and subsequently visited another PHI such as a polyclinic, the polyclinic need not seek your consent again to claim the medical expenses on your behalf from your MediSave. The authorisation will remain valid until you revoke it.

questions.title: What is the monthly payout amount for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Successful CareShield Life claimant can receive monthly payouts for as long as they develop severe disability and remain insured under CareShield Life. This is designed to provide better protection against the uncertainty of long-term care costs.
The monthly payout is $689 in 2026, and increases annually until the insured reaches age 67 or makes a successful claim, whichever comes first.
For example, if a 30-year-old individual joins CareShield Life in 2026, develops severe disability and makes a claim in 2026, he/she will receive $689 per month for the entire duration of severe disability. However, if a 30-year-old individual joins CareShield Life in 2026, and only develops severe disability at age 67 or later, he/she will receive $2,941 per month upon a successful claim, for the entire duration of severe disability.
For insureds born in 1954 and earlier who joined CareShield Life at age 67 or above, the monthly payout will be fixed at $612 per month once a successful claim is made.

questions.title: Who are the MOH-accredited severe disability assessors for CareShield Life and MediSave Care?
questions.text:
