MOH-accredited severe disability assessors are Singapore-registered doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses who have undergone a rigorous training programme to assess a Patient’s level of disability.
For a list of the MOH-accredited severe disability assessors, please visit the AIC’s website.

questions.title: Who are the MOH-accredited severe disability assessors for CareShield Life and MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MOH-accredited severe disability assessors are Singapore-registered doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses who have undergone a rigorous training programme to assess a patient’s level of disability.
For a list of the MOH-accredited severe disability assessors, please visit the AIC’s website.

questions.title: Why am I unable to undergo a severe disability assessment for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care at a hospital?
questions.text:
While you are undergoing treatment in the hospital, your disability status may change, and this may impact your long-term care scheme application. As such, we do not recommend the patients to attend the severe disability assessment while hospitalised.
Our focus is to accredit healthcare professionals in the community, including the GPs, and clinicians in the long-term care sector to assess individuals’ level of disability when their condition has stabilised.

questions.title: Why are MediSave withdrawal limits imposed?
questions.text:
MediSave is used to pay for a wide range of expenses, including health insurance premiums, hospitalisation, day surgery and outpatient bills like chemotherapy and dialysis.
To ensure that Singaporeans have sufficient savings in their MediSave Account for their basic healthcare needs in old age, MediSave withdrawal limits have been carefully set to strike a balance between the affordability of current treatments and future healthcare needs. These limits, after taking into account Government subsidies and applicable MediShield Life payouts, are generally adequate to cover most of the charges incurred at subsidised inpatient wards and outpatient treatments.
The Ministry of Health reviews the MediSave withdrawal limits from time to time to ensure that they remain relevant to healthcare costs and Singaporeans’ needs.

questions.title: Why is Flexi-MediSave only applicable to elderly members aged 60 years old and above?
questions.text:
MediSave is meant to help Singaporeans pay for their more costly medical expenses, especially after retirement. Older Singaporeans usually incur more healthcare expenses as outpatient medical treatments tends to be more expensive for them, while having lower or no income if they have retired. The Flexi-MediSave scheme helps them by allowing them to use MediSave more flexibly to reduce their out-of-pocket expenses for outpatient medical care.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) will regularly review Flexi-MediSave and other financing policies to ensure that outpatient care remains affordable for all Singaporeans.

questions.title: Why is there a need to set aside the MediSave balance of at least $5,000 to be eligible for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave is primarily designed to help Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents put aside sufficient savings for their hospitalisation expenses and selected outpatient treatments such as cancer treatments that are more expensive in nature.
The minimum MediSave balance of $5,000 set aside by MediSave Care is to help individuals maintain some savings to pay for their other healthcare bills.

questions.title: Why was my GIRO deduction for MediSave contributions unsuccessful and how can I ensure my future deductions are successful?
questions.text:
Your GIRO deductions may be unsuccessful due to insufficient funds in your bank account, or if the 'Payment Limit' or 'Amount Allowed' set with your bank during your GIRO application is lower than your current monthly instalment amount. You can check your current monthly instalment amount on the Self-employment dashboard.
Some banks may impose administrative charges for unsuccessful deductions. To ensure future deductions are successful:
Ensure you have sufficient funds in your bank account before the scheduled GIRO deductions, which take place on the 25th of each month (or the next working day if the 25th falls on a weekend or public holiday)
Ensure that the GIRO payment limit which you have set with your bank is higher than your monthly instalment, or leave the 'Payment Limit'/'Amount Allowed' field blank during GIRO application to accommodate any future changes in your monthly instalments
If your GIRO deduction was unsuccessful, the next deduction will take place in the following month. You will be notified of your revised instalment plan before the subsequent month’s deduction. Your monthly instalment amount will be revised based on the total outstanding MediSave contributions and the remaining duration of your instalment plan.
If your GIRO deductions were suspended following unsuccessful deductions, you can reinstate your GIRO deductions within 14 days of the suspension via the “Reinstate GIRO deduction for MediSave contributions” form.

questions.title: Will the interest rates on savings in the Special, MediSave and Retirement Account be maintained at a floor rate?
questions.text:
To help CPF members grow their savings, the Government has decided to further extend the 4% floor rate for interest earned on all Special, MediSave and Retirement Account (SMRA) savings for another year until 31 December 2026.
SMRA savings will earn a minimum 4% interest rate per annum until 31 December 2026.
Please refer to our FAQ on how CPF interest rates are determined for more information.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF interest rates

questions.title: Am I able to use my MediSave for pre-delivery medical expenses before my delivery?
questions.text:
You can only use MediSave for pre-delivery expenses after you have delivered.
You will have to present the bills incurred for pre-delivery medical care to the hospital where you delivered. The hospital will submit these bills, together with the bill for the delivery expenses, for MediSave withdrawal under the MediSave Maternity Package on your behalf.

questions.title: Am I still eligible to be covered under CareShield Life if I have pre-existing disabilities?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, including those with pre-existing severe disabilities, are covered under CareShield Life from 1 October 2020 or when they turn 30, whichever is later.
As part of collective responsibility, those with pre-existing severe disabilities are required to pay one year premium to join the scheme. This payment amount is less than the first monthly CareShield Life payout they will receive. Upon joining the scheme, they will continue to receive monthly payouts for as long as they are unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living. The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to help those who are still unable to afford premiums even after subsidies.

questions.title: Are corporate service buyers required to make MediSave contributions under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) for vendors who are both an employee and self-employed person?
questions.text:
Corporate service buyers are required to make MediSave contributions via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) for vendors who provide their services as self-employed persons, regardless of whether they are concurrently an employee.
If payment is made to the vendor’s company (which hires the vendor as an employee), CAYE is not required. The vendor will continue to receive employee CPF contributions from his/her employer.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Are Singaporeans who are residing overseas eligible for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident who is living overseas, you will be qualified for MediSave Care if you fulfil the following criteria:
a. Aged 30 and above.
b. Certified by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to have developed severe disability (i.e. unable to perform three (3) or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). You can find the list of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors here.
c. Have a minimum MediSave balance of $5,000.

questions.title: Are there additional charges for using my MediSave to pay for my medical expenses?
questions.text: CPF Board does not impose any administrative fee for using MediSave.

questions.title: Are there alternative documents I can submit for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claims in place of a severe disability assessment?
questions.text:
The Government is exploring the recognition of equivalent assessments conducted by qualified healthcare professionals such as doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses who provide care to the patient. In such cases, patients need not undergo a separate severe disability assessment. Today, patients staying in a nursing home can already seek assistance from their nursing home to submit the Resident’s Assessment Form in place of the severe disability assessment.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will publish more information on their respective websites.

questions.title: Are there any alternative documents that I can submit for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claims instead of a severe disability assessment?
questions.text:
The Government is looking into recognising equivalent assessments that have been performed by a qualified healthcare professional (doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses) providing care to the patient. In such cases, the patient need not undergo a separate severe disability assessment. Today, those who are staying in a nursing home can already approach their nursing home for assistance to submit the Resident’s Assessment Form in place of the severe disability assessment.
MOH and AIC will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will make the information available via the MOH and AIC website.

questions.title: Are there any alternative documents that I can submit for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claims instead of a severe disability assessment?
questions.text:
The Government is looking into recognising equivalent assessments that have been performed by a qualified healthcare professional (doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses) providing care to the patient. In such cases, the patient need not undergo a separate severe disability assessment. Today, those who are staying in a nursing home can already approach their nursing home for assistance to submit the Resident’s Assessment Form in place of the severe disability assessment.
MOH and AIC will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will make the information available via the MOH and AIC website.

questions.title: Are there any alternative documents that I can submit for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claims instead of a severe disability assessment?
questions.text:
The Government is looking into recognising equivalent assessments that have been performed by a qualified healthcare professional (doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses) providing care to the patient. In such cases, the patient need not undergo a separate severe disability assessment. Today, those who are staying in a nursing home can already approach their nursing home for assistance to submit the Resident’s Assessment Form in place of the severe disability assessment.
MOH and AIC will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will make the information available via the MOH and AIC website.

questions.title: Are there any medical expenses that Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave aims to help elderly patients reduce their cash payment, with the focus on outpatient medical treatment.
It cannot be used for treatments that are for non-medical purposes, such as those for cosmetic or lifestyle purposes (e.g. hair loss, slimming, and erectile dysfunction). It also cannot be used to pay for items from the retail pharmacies, such as skincare products. Non-medical charges such as administrative fees are also not covered.
Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for admissions to the Accident and Emergency department and cancer drug treatments using cancer drugs that are not on the Cancer Drug List.

questions.title: Are we eligible for higher subsidies if I/my family member am/is placed in a nursing home with higher fees?
questions.text:
For individuals who require nursing home care, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will work closely with the individual and family members to identify a suitable nursing home, taking into account the individual's needs and family's preferences, including financial considerations.
The Government provides subsidies to help with the costs of long-term care. The amount of subsidies each individual is eligible for is determined by means-testing and is not dependent on the fees charged by the nursing homes. Individuals from lower-income households who meet the eligibility criteria will receive higher subsidies under the means-testing framework.
If you require additional assistance, you can tap on financial assistance schemes such as MediFund. Many nursing homes are also run by voluntary welfare organisations, and they may tap on charitable donations to provide further financial support to their residents after all other means of financial assistance and resources are exhausted.

questions.title: As a pensioner, can I receive any special benefits under CareShield Life?
questions.text: There are no special benefits for pensioners under CareShield Life. As a pensioner, your participation in CareShield Life is optional. You can join CareShield Life if you do not have severe disability. If you are interested in CareShield Life, you may access information on your personalised premiums and premium support using the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service (Singpass login is required).

questions.title: As an employee, how much do I contribute to my MediSave Account (MA)?
questions.text: A portion of your monthly CPF contributions is allocated to your MediSave Account depending on your age group. You can refer to the CPF contribution and allocation rates.

questions.title: Can an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor certify the applicant’s mental capacity for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claims?
questions.text:
A mental capacity assessment can be carried out by any doctor registered with the Singapore Medical Council for the purpose of claiming under CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care. If you require a mental capacity assessment, it is advisable to check with your assessor beforehand to confirm whether they are able to perform it, before booking a disability assessment appointment.
Depending on the applicant’s condition and needs, some cases may require a more detailed or complex mental capacity assessment that could take more time. In such cases, the assessor may charge an additional fee on top of the disability assessment fee.

questions.title: Can an overseas insurance company disburse the approved reimbursement to my MediSave Account via telegraphic transfer, or is it only by cheque?
questions.text: Your insurer may submit reimbursements to MediSave and/or MediShield Life electronically via the MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service.

questions.title: Can anyone, including entities, make voluntary top ups to my MediSave Account? How do I check if anyone has topped up for me?
questions.text:
Anyone, including entities (Community Partners, NGO, etc.) can make voluntary top-ups to your MediSave Account (MA). Entities will need to submit their intention to make voluntary top-ups to your MA. See more here.
If you are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), you can check if anyone has topped up to your MA on your Healthcare dashboard. The estimated cash top-ups you have received this year which will qualify you for the matching grant will be reflected.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Can I apply for a licence/renew my licence if I have outstanding MediSave payable?
questions.text:
Licensing authorities will only process your licence application/renewal if you have an active GIRO arrangement with the Board to settle your MediSave payable via monthly instalments or have fully settled your MediSave payable.
To make your MediSave contributions via monthly instalments, you can request an instalment plan via the Manage your MediSave payable form. You will be cleared for licence application/renewal two working days after the first successful GIRO deduction. GIRO deductions take place on the 25th of each month (or next working day if the 25th is a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday). Please allow two working days after the GIRO deduction for the amount to be credited to your MediSave account before proceeding with your licence application/renewal.
To make your MediSave contributions in full, please use the Manage your MediSave payable form to make your contributions via Paynow. The transaction will be processed almost instantly and you will be cleared for licence application/renewal thereafter.
To check your outstanding MediSave payable or your eligibility for licence application/renewal, you may log in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
Refer to this guide for step-by-step instructions on retrieving information on your eligibility for licence application/ renewal.

questions.title: Can I be assessed by my own doctor or therapist for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claim eligibility?
questions.text: To apply for any of the severe disability schemes, you need to undergo a disability assessment by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. You can check whether your family doctor (GP)/own doctor/healthcare professional is on the list of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors available on the AIC website. If they are not, you will need to make an appointment with one of the assessors on the list for the assessment.

questions.title: Can I choose to opt-out of the online Daily Withdrawal Limit?
questions.text: As part of CPF Board’s ongoing efforts to safeguard CPF members’ savings against unauthorised online withdrawals, all members aged 55 and above will be subject to the online Daily Withdrawal Limit. You can set the Daily Withdrawal Limit to your preferred amount, from $0 up to $50,000.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: Can I choose to receive both digital notification and a hardcopy MediSave transaction statement?
questions.text: You will not be receiving hardcopies of your MediSave transaction statement once you receive notifications digitally. This will aid us in our pursuit to reduce the use of paper.

questions.title: Can I choose to receive the hardcopy MediSave transaction statement instead?
questions.text:
Notification through hardcopy statements will result in a delay in informing you of deductions made from your MediSave account. It will also contribute to the usage of paper, which is not environmentally friendly.
We encourage members to join us in our efforts to go digital and reduce our environmental footprint, while enjoying the convenience of timely notifications.

questions.title: Can I choose to retain my excess Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions in my MediSave Account?
questions.text: Yes, you can choose to retain your excess Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions in your MediSave Account. You may apply to do so by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Can I engage my family doctor (GP) OR own doctor/healthcare professional for the CareShield Life/MediSave Care severe disability assessment?
questions.text: If you wish to apply for any of the severe disability schemes, you need to undergo a severe disability assessment by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. You may wish to check if your own doctor or healthcare professional is on the list of MOH accredited severe disability assessors. This can be found on the AIC’s website. If they are not, you will need to make an appointment with one of the assessors on the list for an assessment.

questions.title: Can I engage my family doctor (GP) OR own doctor/healthcare professional for the CareShield Life/MediSave Care severe disability assessment?
questions.text: If you wish to apply for any of the severe disability schemes, you need to undergo a severe disability assessment by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. You may wish to check if your family doctor (GP)/own doctor/healthcare professional is on the list of MOH accredited severe disability assessors. This can be found on the AIC’s website. If they are not, you will need to make an appointment with one of the assessors on the list for an assessment.

questions.title: Can I enjoy tax relief as a self-employed person when I make mandatory MediSave contributions or make voluntary top-ups to my CPF accounts?
questions.text:
As a self-employed person (SEP), you can enjoy full tax relief on your mandatory MediSave contributions.
You can also enjoy tax relief as an SEP for the following voluntary contributions:
MediSave contributions made to offset future MediSave payable, made via the Manage your MediSave Payable form; and
Voluntary top-ups to 3 CPF accounts
The tax relief for these voluntary contributions will be capped at the lowest of:
37% of your net trade income1 2 or
CPF annual limit of $37,7402 or
Actual voluntary amount contributed by you
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards if you are a mandatory or opt in platform worker
2Amount less tax relief allowed on mandatory MediSave contributions
Please visit the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website for more information.

questions.title: Can I join both CareShield Life and ElderShield to get double the protection?
questions.text:
You will not be able to be on both CareShield Life and ElderShield.
However, upgrading to CareShield Life will not affect your ElderShield Supplement plan if you already have one. If you are currently covered under ElderShield, you can upgrade to CareShield Life for higher and lifetime payouts. Your ElderShield coverage will be terminated upon joining CareShield Life. For more coverage, you can also purchase Supplement plans from private insurers.

questions.title: Can I make a one-time authorisation to use my MediSave for my immediate family members' medical expenses in different Medical Institutions without signing a new form at each Medical Institution?
questions.text: You will need to authorise the use of your MediSave for your immediate family member's medical expenses by signing the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (Single Institution) at each Medical Institution. This is to reduce the likelihood that your MediSave is used for subsequent treatments at the same institution and/or other institutions without your knowledge.

questions.title: Can I nominate a joint bank account with the Mentally Incapacitated (MI) Patient to receive the monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts?
questions.text: A joint bank account with the Mentally Incapacitated (MI) patient can be nominated to receive the monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts, provided the MI patient remains a joint account holder. You will need to specify in the application form that the patient is a joint owner of the account.

questions.title: Can I nominate the Mentally Incapacitated (MI) Patient’s own bank account to receive the monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts?
questions.text: You can nominate the Mentally Incapacitated (MI) patient's bank account to receive the monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts and should specify in the application form that the account belongs to the MI patient.

questions.title: Can I opt out from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
I am a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1980 or later
CareShield Life is universal and mandatory for Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later. You will not be able to opt out.
CareShield Life is a long-term care insurance that provides basic financial support should an insured develop severe disability. CareShield Life will provide you with better protection and assurance for basic long-term care needs with:
Lifetime cash payouts, for as long as the insured is unable to do three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs);
Increasing monthly payouts, at $689/month in 2026 and increases annually until age 67 or when a successful claim is made, whichever is earlier;
Government subsidies to make it affordable, with no one losing coverage if they cannot pay premiums;
Premiums can be fully paid by MediSave.
I am a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier
Singapore Citizen and Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979, who were covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and did not develop severe disability, were auto-enrolled to CareShield Life from 1 December 2021. You will not be able to opt out of CareShield Life as the deadline to opt out was 31 December 2023. Find out how CareShield Life protects you for life.
If you were not auto-enrolled and had chosen to join CareShield Life, please note that you will not be able to opt out from CareShield Life after the 60-day free-look period.
CareShield Life is also mandatory for foreigners who become Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards and are born in 1979 or earlier, provided they do not have severe disability (if granted residency status from 1 October 2020 to 31 December 2025) or any disability (if granted residency status from 1 January 2026 onwards).
If you wish to opt out of CareShield Life, you can submit an appeal via Opt-out of CareShield Life e-Service (Singpass login required). Please note that all appeals undergo a rigorous assessment process, and only those with substantiated grounds will be considered.
If you would like to find out the premiums payable, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to view your projected premiums. There are several options available to pay your CareShield Life premiums, including through GIRO or having a family member take over the payment.
Government subsidies are also available to ensure that no one loses coverage due to an inability to pay. Find out more about your payment options.

questions.title: Can I opt out of the upcoming CareShield Life enhancement?
questions.text:
Maintaining the enhancement as a standard feature for all policyholders helps keep the scheme fair and sustainable, and premiums affordable. This helps to:
Reduce adverse selection risk, where those who are more likely to claim are more likely to opt into the scheme
Keep administrative processes simple and efficient
Hence, the CareShield Life Council has recommended to apply the enhancements to all policyholders, striking a fair balance between stronger protection and premium affordability for all.

questions.title: Can I purchase CareShield Life Supplement(s) if I have pre-existing illnesses?
questions.text:
CareShield Life Supplements are products by private insurers who set the underwriting decisions based on commercial and actuarial considerations.
You may refer to a comparison of Supplement plans offered by private insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance). For more information about Supplement plans, you may consider speaking to a financial advisor from one of the private insurers.

questions.title: Can I still receive Matched MediSave Scheme grants if I am a recipient of Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) or Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS)?
questions.text: If you are a recipient of either the Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) or Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS), the cash top-ups used to qualify you for SHB or LBS will not be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) grant. Any voluntary cash top-ups to the MediSave Account that do not qualify for LBS or SHB may attract MMSS grant.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Can I submit a claim for both CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediSave Care concurrently?
questions.text: You may submit a claim for both schemes concurrently. CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediSave Care are not mutually exclusive.

questions.title: Can I submit a claim for both CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediSave Care concurrently?
questions.text: You can submit a claim for both schemes concurrently as CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediSave Care are not mutually exclusive.

questions.title: Can I transfer my cash top-up to MediSave Account for Matched MediSave Scheme to be used for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme instead?
questions.text:
Cash top-ups to MediSave Account made for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) cannot be transferred to Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) as the top-ups are irreversible. If you prefer to receive matching grants for retirement savings, you may consider making cash top-ups via this link for MRSS instead.
If you qualify for both MMSS and MRSS, but have limited funds to top up, you may refer to this FAQ for useful pointers.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Can I upgrade or downgrade between ElderShield 300 and ElderShield 400?
questions.text: Switching between ElderShield plans is not possible. ElderShield 300 insureds were given a one-time option to upgrade to ElderShield 400 in 2007, and this option is no longer available. Downgrading from ElderShield 400 to ElderShield 300 is also not allowed.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to fully pay for my chronic diseases treatment?
questions.text: You only need to co-pay 15% of the bill for your chronic diseases treatment in cash before using MediSave to pay the rest, except for treatments received at your enrolled Healthier SG clinic. You may find out more about Healthier SG and search for a clinic near you to enrol into one. This is to help you conserve some of your MediSave savings for future healthcare needs.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for Accident and Emergency (A&E) expenses?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for Accident and Emergency (A&E) expenses if you are subsequently admitted to the hospital after seeking care at the A&E department, subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits applicable to your inpatient or day surgery bill.
If you are not admitted, you cannot use MediSave to pay for standalone A&E expenses. However, if you have incurred A&E expenses for a CT scan performed for traumatic brain injury at the A&E department of an approved medical institution in Singapore, you can withdraw from your MediSave through the medical institution under the MediSave withdrawal limit for outpatient scans.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my colonoscopy screening?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for colonoscopy screening at all public healthcare institutions and approved private hospitals and medical institutions, provided you are aged 50 years old and above and it is a day surgery procedure. The day surgery limits are:
1) Day Surgery
Up to a maximum of $830 per day for daily hospital charges, including investigations, medicines and doctor's attendance fees.
2) Operation
A fixed operation limit of either $1,120 or $1,390, depending on the type of operations performed.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my mammogram screening?
questions.text:
If you are aged 50 years old or above, you can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave or your immediate family members' MediSave for your mammogram screening.
Your immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. To use your grandchildren's or siblings' MediSave, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my overseas medical treatment if I am living overseas for the long term?
questions.text:
As MediSave is primarily meant for medical treatment in Singapore, it does not cover overseas medical expenses for those residing overseas for the long term. This is a common feature of national healthcare systems in many countries.
If you are residing overseas for the long term, please consider obtaining medical coverage to meet your overseas healthcare needs.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay the remainder of my medical bill that is not covered under my pensioner benefits?
questions.text:
You can use your own or your immediate family members' (i.e. spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings) MediSave to pay the remainder of your medical bill that is not covered under your pensioner benefits, up to the MediSave withdrawal limits. The expenses incurred must be for medical treatments approved under the MediSave scheme.
If you would like to use your MediSave to pay the remainder of your medical bill, please inform the Medical Institution (MI). You will be required to complete the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF), which authorises the MI to use your MediSave to pay the bill. Please note that any amount above the MediSave withdrawal limits would need to be paid in cash.

questions.title: Can I use more than one of my immediate family member's MediSave for my hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
You can tap on one or more of your immediate family member's MediSave for your hospitalisation expenses. Immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident if you wish to tap on your grandchildren or sibling's MediSave.
While you can tap on your family member's MediSave, the amount you can use is still subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per hospitalisation episode basis regardless of the number of payers. If you still have outstanding hospitalisation expenses after utilising up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, you would have to pay the remainder in cash.

questions.title: Can I use my excess Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions to offset my outstanding MediSave payable?
questions.text:
Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions in excess of your MediSave payable for the year will be automatically used to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years, if any1. Any excess thereafter will be refunded to your bank account.
You can also choose to boost your healthcare savings by retaining the excess CAYE contributions in your MediSave Account to earn up to 6% interest per annum, and to offset future MediSave payable. To do so, please apply via the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
1This will take effect for CAYE contributions made from 2023. Please write to us if you do not wish to use your CAYE contributions to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave Care withdrawal for overseas treatment?
questions.text: Withdrawals of up to $200 monthly under the MediSave Care scheme are in cash, and applicants can choose to utilise the cash locally or overseas for their long-term care needs.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for hearing aids?
questions.text:
MediSave cannot be used for the purchase of hearing aids. This is because MediSave is primarily designed to help Singaporeans offset costly hospitalisations, day surgeries and selected outpatient treatments.
However, you may apply for the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF) which provides subsidies to eligible seniors for a range of assistive devices, including hearing aids. You can call the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) at 1800 650 6060* or visit AIC website for more details.
* Airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for my maternity expenses?
questions.text:
MediSave can be used to pay for the delivery and pre-delivery medical expenses.
Pre-delivery expenses have to be claimed under the MediSave Maternity Package. However, post-natal consultation fees cannot be claimed under MediSave.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for the cost of terminating my pregnancy?
questions.text:
The use of MediSave for termination of pregnancy (TOP) is subject to the MediSave Maternity Package guidelines. This includes a $900 withdrawal limit for your pre-delivery expenses. In addition, if the procedure was conducted in a day surgery setting, you may claim an additional $830 per day for Daily Hospital Charges.
Please approach the medical institution where you have received or will be receiving the treatment from to check the specific value of MediSave that can be used. The medical institution is best-placed to advise you on the MediSave usage towards your specific treatment(s) and the expected expenses.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for dental treatments?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave for selected complex dental procedures that involve surgery and are performed for medical reasons, subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits applicable for day surgeries.
If you are aged 60 or older, you can also use your available withdrawal limit under Flexi-MediSave for selected non-surgical dental procedures such as permanent crowns and root canal treatments.
Please check with your dentist whether your dental treatments are MediSave-claimable.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my approved dependant's renal dialysis?
questions.text:
You may use your MediSave to pay for approved dependent’s renal dialysis treatment costs, up to a limit of $450 per month per patient.
Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
To use your MediSave to pay for your approved dependant’s renal dialysis treatment costs, please complete a Medical Claims Authorisation Form at dialysis centres.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my step/adopted children's hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
If your step children are under your custody, they are considered your approved dependants, and you can use your MediSave for their hospitalisation expenses.
To use your MediSave for your adopted children, you need to submit legal documentary proof of your relationship to the hospital. If the legal process of adoption is still underway, you should submit the following documents to the hospital:
a. A lawyer's letter stating that the legal adoption is underway, and
b. The birth certificate within one year of your child's date of birth.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for the medical treatments received by dependants other than my approved dependants (spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings)?
questions.text:
MediSave is meant to help you save for your personal or approved dependant's healthcare expenses incurred in any of the participating medical institutions (MIs) under the MediSave Scheme.
You can apply to use your MediSave for a dependant who is not your approved dependant, if the dependant is receiving treatment in a public healthcare institution or voluntary welfare organisation in Singapore. Please approach the medical institution's Business Office for more details on the eligibility criteria and the application process. Such applications will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to top-up my family member’s MediSave Account?
questions.text:
You may use your MediSave for your family members in different ways. Here are the options depending on your intent :
1. If you would like to pay for your family member's hospitalisation/outpatient expenses,
You can approach the Medical Institution (MI) where your immediate family member is receiving treatment, to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) and authorise the use of your MediSave directly. Find out more on how to pay for your family member’s hospitalisation and outpatient expenses.
2. If you would like to pay for your family member's Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums,
You can use your MediSave to pay for your family member's IP premiums by changing the payer. Find out more on how to pay for your family member's premium.
3. If you would like to make voluntary cash top-ups to your family member’s MediSave Account (MA),
You can find out more on voluntary cash top ups to MA.
4. If you are 55 and above and have withdrawable savings in your Ordinary Account (OA) that you would like to top up your own or a loved one’s MA using savings from your OA,
You can complete the “Top up My / My Loved Ones’ MediSave Account using CPF Savings” form.

questions.title: Can I withdraw more than $200 per month under MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave is a personal savings Account without risk-pooling benefits, and withdrawals are limited to the amount saved during your working years. The $200 monthly withdrawal limit under MediSave Care was set to ensure that sufficient MediSave is set aside for other medical purposes such as hospitalisation expenses and selected outpatient treatments. Hence, you will not be able to withdraw more than $200 per month under MediSave Care.
If you are unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, additional assistance is available through Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare.
The Government also regularly reviews the MediSave Care withdrawal limits to ensure that basic long-term care costs remain affordable for Singaporeans.

questions.title: Can I withdraw my MediSave in cash?
questions.text:
MediSave is primarily designed to help Singaporeans save up during their working years for their healthcare needs in old age. Generally, MediSave cannot be withdrawn in cash and are instead paid directly to MediSave-accredited medical institutions for approved medical treatments.
However, under MediSave Care, Singaporeans with severe disability aged 30 and above may withdraw up to $200 per month in cash from their own and/or their spouse’s MediSave account(s). This is because long-term care needs vary significantly across such individuals, and cash withdrawals will provide patients and their caregivers the flexibility to decide on their desired care arrangements and long-term care services. You may refer to AIC’s website and our FAQ for more details on MediSave Care.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) will continue to review their financing policies to ensure that care remains affordable for our citizens, while MediSave balances are not depleted prematurely.

questions.title: Can I withdraw under MediSave Care for overseas treatment?
questions.text: Withdrawals of up to $200 per month under the MediSave Care scheme are provided in cash, and claimants have the option to use the cash for their long-term care needs, either locally or overseas.

questions.title: Can lump sum payouts, death benefits or "No-claim Bonus” be provided as incentives for healthy living or meeting the two Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) criteria under CareShield Life/ElderShield?
questions.text:
CareShield Life/ElderShield is designed to provide basic financial protection against long-term care costs through monthly cash payouts to insureds with severe disability to cover their ongoing costs. It is not designed or priced to cover payouts to insureds who remain healthy.
If you would like additional coverage such as lump sum payouts and death benefits, you can consider purchasing Supplements from the private insurers.

questions.title: Can MediSave be used for a deceased member's last hospitalisation bill?
questions.text:
The deceased member's MediSave can be used fully, without being subjected to the existing MediSave withdrawal limits to pay the last medical bill, if the member has passed away during his hospitalisation.
If the deceased member had not signed the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) before his death, his spouse, parent or child aged 21 and above, or Donee/Deputy appointed under the Mental Capacity Act, has to quickly sign the MCAF on behalf of the deceased member to authorise the hospital to submit a claim, before the deceased's CPF funds including MediSave, is disbursed to his nominees or the Public Trustee Office.
If the deceased member does not have a spouse, parent or child aged 21 and above, or Donee/Deputy, a next of kin (NOK) who has been taking care of the deceased can inform the hospital of his intention to sign the MCAF on behalf of the deceased member. The hospital will then seek approval from MOH on behalf of the NOK, before the NOK signs the MCAF.
If more than one MediSave Account (MA) holders had authorised the use of their MediSave to pay the medical bill of the deceased member before his demise and one of the MA belongs to the deceased, the protocol on the use of MediSave from the various accounts are as follows:
The deceased member's MediSave will be used first to pay off the last medical bill without being subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits.
If the deceased member's MediSave is not sufficient to pay the last medical bill, the MediSave from the other account holder(s) can then be used, provided that the MediSave withdrawn from the deceased member's account does not exceed the MediSave withdrawal limits.
Example whereby the MediSave withdrawal limit has been reached
Patient passes away with a final hospitalisation bill of $5,000, after staying in the hospital for five days without surgical treatment.
Patient's MediSave Balance = $4,000
$4,000 can be paid from the patient's MediSave and the remainder of $1,000 must be paid by cash. The patient's spouse, child, parent, grandchild or sibling's MediSave cannot be used as the maximum MediSave Withdrawal Limit of $2,300 has been reached.
Example whereby the MediSave withdrawal limit has not been reached
Patient passes away with a final hospitalisation bill of $5,000, after staying in the hospital for five days without surgical treatment.
Patient's MediSave Balance = $1,500
$1,500 can be paid from the patient's MediSave and a further $800 can be paid from the MediSave of the patient's spouse, child, parent, grandchild or sibling, up to the maximum MediSave Withdrawal Limit of $2,300. The remaining $2,700 of the bill needs to be settled with cash.

questions.title: Can MediSave be used for the disability assessments?
questions.text: MediSave cannot be used to pay for the cost of the disability assessments. However, if you are applying for multiple severe disability schemes, such as CareShield Life and MediSave Care, you will only need to go for one disability assessment.

questions.title: Can my MediSave be used to pay for severe disability assessments?
questions.text:
MediSave cannot be used to cover the cost of any severe disability assessments.
However, all severe disability schemes (i.e. CareShield Life, MediSave Care, ElderShield, ElderFund and IDAPE) use the same severe disability assessment. If you are a CareShield Life policyholder undergoing a severe disability assessment for the first time, the cost of that assessment by an MOH-accredited assessor will be waived.
In other cases, the full cost of the severe disability assessment will be reimbursed if you are assessed to have severe disability. AIC will send you a letter with details of the reimbursement and the bank account it will be credited to.

questions.title: Can my MediSave be used to pay for the CareShield Life severe disability assessments?
questions.text:
MediSave cannot be used to pay for the cost of any disability assessments.
However, all severe disability schemes (i.e. CareShield Life, MediSave Care, ElderShield, ElderFund and IDAPE) share the same disability assessment. If you are a CareShield Life policyholder and are undergoing a severe disability assessment for the first time, the cost of your first severe disability assessment by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor will be waived. Otherwise severe disability assessments will be fully reimbursed if you are assessed to have developed severe disability. AIC will send you a letter to inform you about details of the reimbursement and the account to which the reimbursement will be made.

questions.title: Can my platform operator’s contributions be used to offset outstanding MediSave contributions from my past self-employed work?
questions.text:
Your CPF contributions (including platform operator’s share, if any) are meant for platform work done from 2025.
You will need to make separate arrangements to settle any outstanding MediSave contributions on past income earned as a self-employed person.
You may reach out to CPFB to arrange affordable instalment plans on your past MediSave obligations.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can taxi principal hirers who are not liable to make a MediSave contribution qualify for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution from their taxi operators?
questions.text:
Taxi principal hirers who do not have outstanding MediSave payable can still receive Drive and Save co-contributions if they make contributions to pre-pay their future MediSave payable1:
A contribution of at least $20 to their MediSave Account monthly, or
A lump sum MediSave contribution of at least $240 in the past 12 months.
1 Taxi principal hirers may make MediSave contributions to pre-pay their MediSave payable as self-employed persons via Manage your MediSave payable.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / Drive and Save Scheme

questions.title: Can the deceased member's MediSave be used to pay his final hospitalisation bill?
questions.text:
Yes, the deceased member’s entire MediSave can be used to pay the last hospital bill if he had signed the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF), which authorises the use of the deceased member’s MediSave to pay the hospitalisation bill, before his passing.
Any remaining MediSave after the payment of the last medical bill will be distributed to the deceased member’s nominee(s) if he had a valid nomination. This is provided that the MediSave deduction is completed before the distribution of the deceased member’s CPF balances.
If the deceased member had not signed the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF), his spouse, parents, child (if age 21 or older), or donee/deputy can sign the form at the hospital. You are encouraged to do this as soon as possible as hospitals have to submit the MediSave claim before the deceased member’s MediSave is distributed (typically within two weeks of the member’s passing). If the deceased member’s MediSave has been distributed, you will not be able to use his MediSave for the last hospital bill.
If there is no immediate family or donee/deputy, a caregiver who has been taking care of the deceased member during his lifetime may write to the Ministry of Health through the hospital to seek approval for the use of the deceased member’s MediSave for the last hospital bill.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Can the pool of assessors for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care be expanded to include Singapore-registered doctors, therapists or nurses?
questions.text:
If you have developed severe disability and wish to make a claim, you will need to undergo a disability assessment by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.
A trained and accredited severe disability assessor will determine whether you meet the criteria for being unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). To enhance accessibility, we have expanded the pool of assessors to include trained therapists and nurses.
All assessors have undergone a rigorous training programme to learn how to assess a patient’s level of disability. Through the training, assessors are equipped to assess an individual’s ability to perform the six ADLs, including specific components of each ADL to take into account, what factors to consider when an individual is cognitively impaired, and what should be done if any individual’s functional ability fluctuates over time. As this is a complex process, the training and accreditation is necessary to ensure that disability assessments are conducted with a high degree of rigour and consistency.
The Government is also exploring the recognition of equivalent assessments conducted by qualified healthcare professionals such as doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses who are providing care to the patient. In such cases, the patients do not need a separate disability assessment. Today, residents of nursing home can approach their nursing home to submit the Resident's Assessment Form in place of the disability assessment.
MOH and AIC will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will publish more information on their respective websites.

questions.title: Can the pool of assessors for MediSave Care be expanded to include any Singapore-registered doctor, therapist or nurse?
questions.text:
Individuals with severe disability who wish to apply for MediSave Care will need to undergo a severe disability assessment by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. A trained, accredited severe disability assessor will be able to assess whether the applicant meets the severe disability criteria of being unable to perform three or more of the six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). We have expanded the list of accredited assessors to include therapists and nurses who have been trained.
All MOH-accredited assessors have undergone a rigorous training programme to learn how to assess a patient’s level of disability. Through the training, assessors are equipped to assess an individual’s ability to perform the six ADLs, including specific components of each ADL to take into account, what factors to consider when an individual is cognitively impaired, and what should be done if any individual’s functional ability fluctuates over time. As this is a complex process, the training and accreditation is necessary to ensure that disability assessments are conducted with a high degree of rigour and consistency.
The Government is also looking into recognising equivalent assessments that have been performed by a qualified healthcare professional (doctor, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses) providing care to the patient. In such cases, the patient need not undergo a separate severe disability assessment. Today, those who are staying in a nursing home can already approach their nursing home for assistance to submit the Resident's Assessment Form in place of the severe disability assessment.
MOH and AIC will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will make the information available via MOH and AIC website.

questions.title: Can the Supplements work with both CareShield Life and ElderShield?
questions.text: Specific Supplements may work with either ElderShield, CareShield Life, or both schemes. For more information on specific Supplement product, please approach your insurer or financial advisor.

questions.title: CareShield Life is still targeted at those with severe disability i.e. unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living. Why was this retained?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is targeted at severe disability, so that premiums can be kept affordable for all insured.
If you are a Singaporean with mild or moderate disabilities, and need long-term care, you can tap on means-tested Government subsidies for long-term care services, as well as other Government assistance schemes (e.g. the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund) to complement your personal savings and family support.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund/ComCare can also help you pay for these long-term care costs, should you be unable to afford long-term care services.
If you wish to cover yourself for less severe disabilities, you can consider purchasing Supplements from the private insurers.

questions.title: Do I get tax relief for voluntary top-ups to the MediSave Account?
questions.text:
Yes, you can receive tax relief for voluntary top-ups to MediSave Account (MA), subject to specific conditions and limits:
ScenarioTax relief per yearConditions
You make a top-up to your MAUp to $8,000 for bothThe maximum top-up amount you can receive to your MA is the difference between your Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) and your current MediSave balance.
You are an employee/platform worker receiving a MA top-up from your employer/platform operator
You make a MA top-up to your loved onesUp to $8,000
The maximum top-up amount your loved one can receive to his/her MA is the difference between his/her Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) and his/her current MediSave balance.
Spouse/sibling must have annual income ≤ $8,000 in previous year or is handicapped*
*Handicapped refers to people who are incapacitated because of physical or mental infirmity.
Important notes
Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS): From 1 January 2026, cash top-ups that qualify for the MMSS matching grant (up to $1,000/year) will not attract tax relief. Find out more on how this works.
Shared cap with Special Account (SA)/ Retirement Account (RA): $8,000 tax relief cap shared across top-ups to SA/ RA or MA.
Overall tax relief cap: Your total personal income tax relief (including CPF top-ups) is capped at $80,000/year.
Learn more about tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: Do I have to pay my MediSave payable when I am no longer self-employed?
questions.text: You’re still required to settle any outstanding MediSave payable, as it is compulsory under the CPF Act to contribute to your MediSave Account for the years that you were self-employed.

questions.title: Do I have to top up in a lump sum to be eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: No, you can make multiple cash top-ups throughout the year. The matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme is based on the total amount of top-ups you have received throughout the year, up to $1,000 per year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Do I have to undergo a disability assessment before joining CareShield Life?
questions.text: You may be required to undergo a disability assessment prior to joining CareShield Life. Should you be required to attend a disability assessment, you will receive a letter with instructions on how to do so.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for the MediSave Grant for Newborns for my child?
questions.text:
All eligible newborns will receive the MediSave Grant for Newborns automatically within a week from the registration of birth1, or from the date when Singapore Citizenship was granted2. You will receive a notification letter after the grant has been deposited and may check your child's CPF statement online by logging in with your Singpass at cpf.gov.sg/childdashboard.
If your child is born overseas, you can register his or her birth with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority directly, or through the relevant Overseas Missions.
If your child is eligible for the grant but has not received it within one week of their birth registration, please write to the Central Provident Fund Board at cpf.gov.sg/writetous.
1 If your child is a Singapore Citizen at birth.
2 If your child is a Singapore Citizen by registration.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for the MediSave Grant for Newborns for my child?
questions.text:
All eligible newborns will receive the grant automatically after birth registration. You can check your child's CPF statement online by logging in with your Singpass at cpf.gov.sg/childdashboard.
If your child is born overseas, you can register his or her birth with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority directly, or through the relevant Overseas Missions.
If your child is eligible but did not receive the grant a week after registering his or her birth, please write to the Central Provident Fund Board at cpf.gov.sg/writetous.

questions.title: Do I need to pay for the CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care disability assessment?
questions.text:
The fees for clinic-based and non-clinic-based severe disability assessments are $100 and $250 respectively.
If you are applying for CareShield Life:
The fee for your first severe disability assessment will be waived, regardless of the outcome. For any subsequent assessments, you will only be reimbursed if you are assessed to have a severe disability.
If you are applying for other severe disability schemes (i.e., ElderShield or MediSave Care):
You will need to pay the assessment fee upfront to the MOH-accredited assessor. The fee will be reimbursed if you are assessed to have a severe disability.

questions.title: Do I need to submit/check/reveal my and/or my spouse’s MediSave balances before submitting an application for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
You are not required to check your MediSave Account balances before submitting an application for MediSave Care. To be qualified for MediSave Care, you need to fulfil all of the following criteria.
a. Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.
b. Aged 30 and above.
c. Certified by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to have developed severe disability (i.e. unable to perform three (3) or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). You can find the list of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors here.
d. Have a minimum MediSave balance of $5,000.
If your MediSave balance is more than $5,000, the withdrawal will automatically be made from your own MediSave first.
If your MediSave balance is insufficient (i.e. below $5,000) or you wish to supplement your MediSave Care withdrawals, you may apply to withdraw from your spouse’s MediSave. Your spouse has to be at least 30 years old, and his/her MediSave balance should also be more than $5,000 to be eligible for withdrawals. Similarly, there is no need for you to check your spouse’s MediSave Account balance before submitting an application. If you have previously submitted an application without applying to withdraw from your spouse’s MediSave Account, you would have to submit a new application.

questions.title: Do I still have to contribute to my MediSave if I am a self-employed person and an employee and/or a platform worker?
questions.text:
If your annual net trade income1 (NTI) exceeds $6,000, you are required to contribute to your MediSave Account as a self-employed person (SEP), in addition to the CPF contributions you have made on your employment/platform work.
This is the same as how employees with multiple jobs are required to make CPF contributions for all the wages from each job.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards
You can apply to limit your MediSave payable as an SEP, if your total income from all employment (excluding Additional Wages2) and platform work for the year3 exceeds the maximum total annual income.
Learn more about the conditions for limiting your MediSave payable as an SEP at this FAQ.
2Additional Wages are wage supplements which are not granted wholly and exclusively for the month. Examples are the annual bonus, leave pay, incentive and other payments made at intervals of more than a month.
3Applicable from work year 2025 onwards
If you are a platform worker concurrently working as an employee, you can refer to this FAQ on refunding your share of excess CPF contributions (if any) on your platform earnings.

questions.title: Does having dementia automatically qualify an individual for CareShield Life/ElderShield claims?
questions.text: Applicants with dementia or other cognitive impairments will not automatically qualify for CareShield Life/ElderShield claims and must still undergo a severe disability assessment, as the impact of dementia/cognitive impairment on their functional abilities may vary.

questions.title: Does the Health Insurance Planner include riders?
questions.text:
Similar to Ministry of Health (MOH)'s website, the Health Insurance Planner (HIP) focuses on comparing Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) that are MediSave-payable and complement your MediShield Life coverage.
While HIP shows premium projections for co-payment riders if you choose to include them, it does not compare rider features and benefits. If you have other types of riders such as deductible cover, additional cancer coverage, daily cash, or global riders, your actual premiums may be higher than projected.
For existing policies, HIP uses your current rider information for projections. For new plans you are considering, it shows estimates based on the most expensive rider available for each IP. This helps you understand the potential cash outlay for rider premiums.
Please contact your insurer or financial advisor for detailed information about rider coverage and options.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Does the nursing home charge for performing the Resident Assessment Form (RAF) for the applicant?
questions.text: Nursing homes do not charge for performing the Resident Assessment Form (RAF) for their residents. If an individual resides in a nursing home and would like to undergo the RAF in place of a disability assessment conducted by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor, he/she should approach the nursing home for further assistance.

questions.title: Does the online Daily Withdrawal Limit affect the total amount that I can withdraw from my CPF account?
questions.text: No, the online Daily Withdrawal Limit does not affect your total withdrawable amount. There is no change to the withdrawal rules under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: For platform workers who opt in, why is the allocation of CPF contributions into the MediSave account higher than the Ordinary and Special or Retirement Accounts in 2025? How will platform workers be better off by opting in?
questions.text:
It is important that platform workers (PWs) have sufficient savings to meet their healthcare needs, unlike salaried employees who have healthcare protections from their employers.
Hence, the MediSave allocation rate of between 8% – 10.5% remains the same whether PWs opt in to increased CPF contribution or not (see chart below).
The increase in PWs’ CPF contributions will then be allocated to the Ordinary and Special or Retirement accounts respectively. You can view the allocation rates for 2025 - 2028.
By opting in for increased CPF contributions, PWs will receive the platform operator (PO) share of CPF contributions of 3.5% in 2025 which increases to up to 17% in 2029. These are additional savings for platform workers’ housing and retirement needs.
PWs who use the Ordinary account (OA) contributions for mortgage instalments can free up more cash for other expenses. This is because the CPF contributions allocated to the OA (PW and PO share) will be higher than the increase in CPF contributions that the PW has to make.
For example, in 2025, a 40-year-old PW with monthly net earnings of $3,000 who opts in to higher CPF contributions would receive 4.5% of his net earnings ($135) in his OA – which can be used to pay for his mortgage instalments. This is higher than the total increase in his own share of CPF contributions, at 2.5% of his income ($75).
In other words, for every additional $1 in CPF that he contributes, he gets $1.80 in his OA which can be used to pay for his mortgage instalments!
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: How accurate are the projections within the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner provides illustrative estimates to help with your financial planning. Your actual premiums and coverage may vary if you have special circumstances such as exclusions, premium loading, discounts, or claims-based pricing from your insurer. The projections also may not reflect costs of additional riders beyond co-payment riders, such as deductible cover, cancer coverage, daily cash, or global riders.
Please note that these projections should not replace professional financial advice. For specific guidance about your situation, please consult a financial advisor.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: How are my monthly CareShield Life payouts determined?
questions.text:
Monthly CareShield Life payouts are designed to help cover basic long-term care costs, which can vary depending on your care needs and arrangements, whether you live at home, go to a care centre, or move into residential care. Individuals finance these costs differently, depending on their personal financial resources and circumstances.
The starting payout from CareShield Life is about $600 per month. This helps reduce out-of-pocket expenses by supplementing your personal savings (including MediSave) and family support. Additional support is also available through government subsidies, assistance schemes, and community support, especially for lower income Singaporeans. If you wish to have additional insurance coverage, you can consider purchasing supplements on top of CareShield Life.
You are strongly encouraged to plan early and consider your future income, long-term care arrangements, and how much insurance coverage and personal savings you may need to support your choices.

questions.title: How are the matching grants and tax relief determined for my cash top-ups made to a recipient eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
If you are making a cash top-up to a recipient eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), your cash top-up of $1,000 will first enable your recipient to enjoy the matching grant of up to $1,000 per year from the Government and will thus not be eligible for tax relief. You can continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for your cash top-ups that do not attract the MMSS matching grant and the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) matching grant ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).
For example, if you make a cash top-up of $3,000 to your MMSS-eligible loved one (and made no other top ups), your loved one will first enjoy a matching grant of $1,000 from the Government, and you will be eligible for $2,000 of tax relief on your cash top-up that did not attract the matching grant.
For more information on the conditions for tax relief, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How can I apply for MediSave Care?
questions.text: To apply for MediSave Care, you may submit an application to the Agency for Integrated Care, and arrange for a disability assessment by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my top-up application?
questions.text:
You may login to your CPF account and check the status of your online application under “Activities”. If your top-up application is successful, it will be reflected in your CPF accounts.
If you have made multiple top-up applications, do check the status of all your applications to see which transactions have been successfully processed and make a new application if necessary.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How can I find out if my Large Family MediSave Grant is successfully credited?
questions.text: You can log in to your CPF account using your Singpass to view your Transaction history to check if the Large Family MediSave Grant has been credited into your MediSave Account.
topics: Large Families Scheme / Large Family MediSave Grant (LFMG)

questions.title: How can I join CareShield Life if I am a foreigner?
questions.text: CareShield Life is applicable only to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.

questions.title: How can I make my MediSave contributions?
questions.text: You can request an instalment plan or make contributions to your outstanding MediSave payable using the Manage your MediSave payable form using your Singpass.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How can I retrieve my Healthcare payments and claims statement online?
questions.text:
You can view your healthcare payments and claims details (containing information such as the name of patient, hospital registration number (HRN), hospitalisation period, etc), with transaction dates within the last 15 months at cpf.gov.sg/healthcare:
Log in to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass
Proceed to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims' and select 'View past 15 months'
Select the period you require and click 'Search'.
Select the PDF icon at the top-right-hand corner of the page to save/print the statement.
Here is a step-by-step guide on how you can retrieve the Healthcare payments and claims statement. To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
Please note that your claim details are available on your Healthcare dashboard for up to 15 months, after which they will no longer be retrievable. Download your statement in a timely manner to ensure you always have a copy for your own records or future use.
When submitting reimbursement claims to your employer or insurer, a digital copy should be sufficient.

questions.title: How can I top up to myself, my children or my loved ones' MediSave Account?
questions.text:
You can make a top-up via Top up MediSave Account using PayNow QR1. Alternatively, you can also use the CPF mobile app and complete your payment via PayNow QR or OCBC Digital (if installed).
You will be prompted to key in your Recipient’s NRIC/CPF Account Number if you are making a top-up to your loved ones.
You are encouraged to make top-ups early. All applications and payments should reach CPF Board by the last day of the calendar year to enjoy tax relief for the following year’s Tax Assessment. Backdating of top-ups to previous years is not allowed.
Please note that there is no tax relief for top-ups made to your children. Find out more about tax relief for your MediSave top-ups.
You can find out more on which voluntary top-up is applicable to you.
To make MediSave top-ups to yourself or a loved one, you are required to have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable under the Self-Employed Scheme. You may make payment for your MediSave payable via the payment modes.
1Subsequent or duplicate payments made using the same PayNow QR code will be refunded. To ensure that your cash top-ups are processed successfully, please only scan the PayNow QR code and make payment once. You will need to submit a new application each time you wish to make another top-up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: How can parents check their child's MediSave balance?
questions.text:
You can view your child's Transaction History statement for the last 15 months by logging in with your Singpass at cpf.gov.sg/childdashboard if:
1. You and your child are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents, and
2. Your child is below the age of 21 and has received CPF contributions (including Government grants such as the MediSave Grant for Newborns).
If you do not see your child's name listed in the Child dashboard, please submit a request to include your child via cpf.gov.sg/writetous.

questions.title: How do I access long-term care services?
questions.text:
If you have long-term care needs assessed by qualified healthcare professionals, medical social workers and/or administrative staff at public hospitals and/or Government-funded long-term care service providers can assist you with your referral to long-term care services. They can also assist with your application for Government subsidies for long-term care services, and advise on the subsidy quantum you are eligible for.
You can also contact the Agency for Integrated Care at 1800-650-6060 or via the AIC website to find out more about long-term care services.

questions.title: How do I appeal if I believe I qualify all criteria but was deemed ineligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: Please refer to the eligibility criteria under the Matched MediSave Scheme and assess if you qualify every criterion. You can submit an appeal via Write-To-Us.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I apply for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
To apply for MediSave Care, you can arrange for a severe disability assessment with an MOH-accredited assessor and submit your application through the AIC’s eService portal (eFASS) using your Singpass.
If you are a caregiver submitting a claim for a mentally incapacitated member, you can log in eFASS using your Singpass to submit the application on his/her behalf.

questions.title: How do I change my bank account for GIRO instalments for my MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
The quickest and easiest way to change your bank account for GIRO instalments for your MediSave contributions is to apply online! If your bank account is with these participating banks, please complete the Set up GIRO for MediSave contributions using your Singpass – Your application will be approved immediately, with no forms or paperwork needed. You will be re-directed to the bank's ibanking portal to complete the application. You can check the status of your online application through my cpf digital services - Activities with your Singpass.
If you would like to use an account from other banks, please download and submit the "Apply for GIRO for MediSave Contributions" (PDF, 0.2MB) to the Board.
Deduction will be made from the existing bank account until the new GIRO arrangement takes effect.

questions.title: How do I check the amount of matching grant that I will receive under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
To find out the grant amount that you will receive under the Matched MediSave Scheme at the beginning of the following year based on this year’s cash top-ups, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard.
In addition, the dashboard will provide you with the remaining grant amount, if any, that you can receive if you make further top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I check the types of CareShield Life and ElderShield Supplement plans I have purchased for myself or dependants?
questions.text:
To check the types of CareShield Life (CSHL) and ElderShield (ESH) supplement plans you have purchased, please contact your insurer directly or log in to your insurer's web portal.
