If you are unsure which insurer you are with, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass to view your supplement plan insurer. Your dependants will need to log in to their own Healthcare dashboard to view their supplement plan insurer.

questions.title: How do I claim from both CareShield Life or ElderShield and Supplements?
questions.text:
You may submit claims for CareShield Life or ElderShield with Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), and your Supplement plan with private insurers.
Contact your private insurer directly for claims process and payouts details:
Singlife: 6827 9933
Great Eastern: 1800 248 2888
Income Insurance: 6788 1777

questions.title: How do I compute my tax relief for voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave Account?
questions.text:
The tax relief calculation depends on whether your recipient is eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS).
If your recipient is not eligible for MMSS:
You can enjoy tax relief of up to $8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones.
If your recipient is eligible for MMSS:
Your first $1,000 in annual cash top-ups receives government matching grant and no tax relief
For additional top-ups beyond the matched amount, you can enjoy tax relief of up to $8,000* per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000* per year for top-ups to your loved ones.
* The above tax relief cap applies to voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave Account and Special/Retirement Account.
Below are some examples of tax relief computation.
Example 1: In the year, you made cash top-ups totalling $3,000 to an MMSS-eligible recipient (yourself/loved one) who did not receive any other cash top-ups in the year. You did not make any other cash top-ups to yourself or others.
Calculation:
Estimated matching grant your recipient will enjoy: $1,000
Estimated tax relief you may enjoy: Total top-up amount ($3000) - Matching grant amount ($1000) = $2,000
Example 2: In the year, you made cash top-ups totalling $3,000 to an MMSS-eligible recipient (yourself/loved one) who has already received $1,000 cash top-ups and a matching grant from another giver in the same year. You did not make any other cash top-ups to yourself or others.
Calculation:
Estimated matching grant your recipient will enjoy from your cash top-up = $0
Estimated tax relief amount you may enjoy = Total top-up amount ($3000) - Matching grant amount ($0) = $3,000
To find out if your recipient is eligible for MMSS, your recipient can check his/her eligibility via the Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: How do I deactivate the CPF Withdrawal Lock?
questions.text:
If you would like to deactivate the CPF Withdrawal Lock, you may increase the online Daily Withdrawal Limit to your desired amount (up to the maximum withdrawal limit), via Account settings; which requires 12 hours to take effect and may require enhanced authentication. Thereafter, you will be able to make online CPF withdrawal applications.
Alternatively, if you wish to make a CPF withdrawal without deactivating the CPF Withdrawal Lock, you can book an appointment to visit us to withdraw your preferred amount in-person at any CPF Service Centre. Generally, the next available appointment for withdrawal transactions would be in a week’s time; subsequently, members will receive their withdrawn CPF savings generally within five working days.
Please visit the FAQ below to find out more on what is the CPF Withdrawal Lock, and how to activate it:
What is the CPF Withdrawal Lock, and how can I activate it?

questions.title: How do I derive my MediSave contributions amount as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
Your MediSave contributions are computed based on your age and net trade income1 for the year.
You can use the Self-Employed MediSave Contribution Calculator to calculate the amount of MediSave you need to contribute.

questions.title: How do I disable my online CPF withdrawal?
questions.text: You can activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock to instantly disable your online CPF withdrawal. This activation sets the Daily Withdrawal Limit to $0. Please refer to the three simple steps to activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: How do I find out about the various healthcare financing schemes and subsidies in Singapore?
questions.text: You may refer to the Ministry of Health website Schemes and subsidies | Ministry of Health (moh.gov.sg) for more information on MediSave, MediShield Life, and many other schemes and subsidies.

questions.title: How do I join ElderShield?
questions.text:
The ElderShield scheme is no longer open for new applications.
If you are born in 1979 or earlier and do not have disability, you may join CareShield Life via the Application to join CareShield Life form and log in using your Singpass to complete the application.
If you are born in 1980 or later, you will be automatically covered under CareShield Life.

questions.title: How do I know how much subsidies I will receive for the long-term care service(s) that I use?
questions.text: Qualified healthcare professionals, medical social workers and/or administrative staff at public hospitals and/or Government-funded long-term care service providers can assist with your application for Government subsidies for long-term care services, and advise on the subsidy quantum you are eligible for.

questions.title: How do I know if I am eligible for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are aged 30 and above and have developed severe disability (unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)) can apply to make such withdrawals after setting aside a minimum amount.
You may submit an application to the Agency for Integrated Care and arrange for a disability assessment by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.

questions.title: How do I know if I am eligible for the higher withdrawal limit of $700 under MediSave500/700?
questions.text:
The withdrawal limit under the MediSave500/700 is determined based on the complexity of your chronic condition(s).
You will be eligible for the higher withdrawal limit of $700 per year, if you were treated for two or more conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), or one CDMP condition with complications within a year.
You can check if you are eligible for the higher withdrawal limit of $700 through:
a. my cpf digital services
• Log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass
• Select "Utilisation of healthcare benefits" from the menu bar or scroll down to the "Utilisation of healthcare benefits" section for "Treatments for chronic illnesses (MediSave500/700)"
• Check if the "Total withdrawal limit" is $700
b. CPF Mobile app
• Download CPF Mobile app
• Log in using your Singpass
• Select "My Healthcare" from the menu bar and check if the limit is $700 under "Outpatient Treatment"

questions.title: How do I know if my loved one meets the severe disability criteria for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
He/ she will need to see an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor who will determine their disability level.
There is an assessment fee you will need to pay first, which will be reimbursed if your loved one is assessed to be severely disabled.
If he/ she is found to have mild or moderate disability instead, there are other financial assistance schemes that you can turn to for help, like the Home Caregiving Grant or MDW Levy Concession. Please find out more about the other financial assistance schemes here.
Click here to read more information about MediSave Care.

questions.title: How do I know if my MediSave can be used for the medical treatment that I have received or will be receiving?
questions.text: Please approach the medical institution where you have received or will be receiving medical treatments from to check if MediSave can be used to pay for the expenses. Please refer to the list of medical institutions participating in the MediSave scheme. The medical institution is best-placed to advise you whether MediSave can be used for the specific medical treatment it is providing and the expected expenses.

questions.title: How do I make a cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
You can make a cash top-up to your own or your loved one’s MediSave Account (MA) via the Top up MediSave Account using PayNow QR1. Your cash top-up will be credited upon successful payment.
For more information on how to make a cash top-up to MediSave Account, please refer to this FAQ.
You may want to check whether you or your loved ones are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) before making a cash top-up.
1Subsequent or duplicate payments made using the same PayNow QR code will be refunded. To ensure that your cash top-ups are processed successfully, please only scan the PayNow QR code and make payment once. You will need to submit a new application each time you wish to make another top-up.
For more information on how to check my and my loved ones’ eligibility for Matched MediSave, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I make a top up to my MediSave Account?
questions.text:
You can make a top up to your MediSave Account using the Top up MediSave Account form and complete your payment using PayNow QR. Alternatively, you can also use the CPF mobile app and complete your payment via PayNow QR or OCBC Digital (if installed).
We have guides available in multiple languages to help you through the process:
Guide (PDF)

topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: How do I make an ElderShield claim?
questions.text:
If you are covered under ElderShield and would like to make a claim, you can arrange for a severe disability assessment with an MOH-accredited assessor and submit your application through the AIC’s eService portal (eFASS) using your Singpass.
If you are a caregiver submitting a claim for a mentally incapacitated ElderShield insured, you can log in eFASS using your Singpass to submit the application on his/her behalf.

questions.title: How do I reverse the cash top up to my own MediSave Account?
questions.text: Voluntary top-ups made are irreversible.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I revoke the authorisation for the use of MediSave savings for my own and/or family member(s)' medical expenses?
questions.text:
The steps to revoke your authorisation for the use of MediSave savings for your own and/or family member(s)’ medical expenses depend on the type of Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) that you had previously signed:
If you signed the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (Single Institution) [MCAF(S)]
Please approach the Medical Institution where you signed the form to revoke your authorisation.
If you signed the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (Multiple Institutions) [MCAF(M)]
You may obtain a copy of the revocation form from any Public Healthcare Institution. Alternatively, you may download the revocation form and email the completed form to mohh.mcaf@mohh.com.sg.
Important:
Revoking your MCAF(M) authorisation revokes only the authorisation provided under the MCAF(M). Any MCAF(S) authorisations separately provided to individual Medical Institutions will remain valid and must be revoked directly with the respective Medical Institution(s).

questions.title: How do I terminate my ElderShield policy?
questions.text: You can terminate your ElderShield via the Termination of ElderShield e-Service if you do not wish to continue to be covered under the scheme. However, you will lose all existing benefits, and you may have to go for a medical assessment if you wish to join CareShield Life. We encourage you to consider keeping your ElderShield policy to ensure you continue to have basic protection for long-term care.

questions.title: How do I update my bank account details for my CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts?
questions.text:
You can log in to AIC’s eService portal (eFASS) with your Singpass on and go to “Manage My Schemes” > “Change in Scheme Details” to update your bank account information for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claim payouts.
If you are updating the bank account on behalf of a care recipient who lacks mental capacity, you will need to submit a Mental Incapacity Certification if you have not already done so. For more details, please refer to the Frequently Asked Questions on AIC’s website.

questions.title: How do regular MediSave co-contributions received under the Drive and Save Scheme benefit me?
questions.text:
Under the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme, the regular MediSave co-contributions from your taxi operator can:
Offset your mandatory MediSave contributions under the Self-Employed Scheme
Earn up to 6% interest per annum on your MediSave savings
Use of MediSave savings to pay for medical expenses and healthcare insurance
Qualify for Workfare Income Supplement scheme for lower-wage workers

questions.title: How do Supplement plans and other private insurance plans for disability differ from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Supplement plans and other private insurance plans for disability differ from CareShield Life in several ways.
Most private insurance plans for disability cover total and permanent disability, or are meant to insure against loss of income when one develops a disability and is unable to work. This is why they typically cease coverage between ages 60 and 70, when most insureds retire. CareShield Life, however, provides lifetime coverage and continues to cover you even if you develop severe disability in your later years.
Unlike private insurance plans, which cease coverage if insureds are unable to pay premiums, CareShield Life coverage will not lapse if you are unable to pay premiums due to financial difficulties. The Government will provide premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support.

questions.title: How does the Matched MediSave Scheme compare with the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
The table below outlines the key differences between the Matched MediSave Scheme and the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.
Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)
Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS)
What are the top-ups and matching grant used for?
Boost monthly payouts in retirement
Payment of approved healthcare insurance premiums (e.g. MediShield Life and CareShield Life) and approved medical treatments.
Where are my cash top-ups and the government matching grant credited to?
Retirement / Special Account (RA/SA)
MediSave Account (MA)
How much grant can I receive?
Up to $2,000 per year, with a lifetime limit of $20,000
Up to $1,000 per year
Who is eligible?
(The following conditions must all be met for the respective scheme)
Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above or verified persons with disabilities aged below 55
RA/SA savings*# less than current Basic Retirement Sum
Singapore Citizens aged 55-70 (inclusive)
MA balances less than 50% of current Basic Healthcare Sum
Self-employed persons must have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable
Average monthly income# is not more than $4,000
Annual Value of Residence# not more than $21,000
Owns not more than one property#
How can eligible members receive the matching grant?
Make cash top up to RA/SA
Make cash top up to MA
The two schemes complement each other to help support the lower-income seniors with their retirement and healthcare needs. For more information about MRSS and MMSS, please refer to cpf.gov.sg/mrss and cpf.gov.sg/mmss respectively.
*RA savings refers to the RA balances (excluding amounts such as interest earned), plus retirement withdrawals and CPF LIFE premium deducted. If you are below 55 or turning 55 in the assessment year and your RA has not been created at the time we assess your eligibility, your total Special Account and Ordinary Account savings will be used for the eligibility assessment instead.
#Previous year’s data is utilised to assess your eligibility as these are the latest data available.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How is the Basic Healthcare Sum determined?
questions.text: The Basic Healthcare Sum is an estimate of your likely medical expenses from age 65 onwards. It is determined based on past trends in MediSave usage among the elderly and is intended to cover your own basic subsidised healthcare expenses, as well as health and long-term care insurance premiums during old age.

questions.title: How long does it take to process voluntary top-ups application to my MediSave Account?
questions.text:
The application relating to voluntary top-ups to MediSave Account will be processed as stated in the table below.
Service
Processing Time
Top up MediSave Account
Almost immediately
If the top-up amount is not reflected in your CPF accounts, please check your CPF account balance after five working days as more time may be needed to process the transaction. Such cases may arise due to intermittent network connectivity issues beyond CPF Board's control.
Please alert us immediately if your payment is still not updated in your CPF account balance after five working days.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: How long will I be covered under ElderShield?
questions.text: ElderShield provides lifetime coverage to its insureds. You will be covered under ElderShield once you start paying your premiums. Coverage continues for the rest of your life upon completion of all premium payments under the Regular Premium Plan or a lump sum premium under the Single Premium Plan. You can submit a claim if you develop severe disability, so long as your total claims have not exceeded 60 months (for ElderShield 300) or 72 months (for ElderShield 400).

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use for my maternity expenses?
questions.text:
Under the MediSave Maternity Package, you can use your MediSave for pre-delivery medical expenses, delivery expenses and daily hospital charges.
Each MediSave Maternity Package has a different MediSave withdrawal limit, depending on the delivery procedure (e.g. caesarean or vaginal delivery). If you do not wish to claim for pre-delivery expenses, you can still use your MediSave savings for the delivery procedure and daily hospital charges. Each delivery procedure has a different withdrawal limit.
You may refer to the details on the withdrawal limits for maternity expenses (PDF, 0.1MB).

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use for my outpatient treatments of chronic diseases?
questions.text:
You can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave or your immediate family members' MediSave.
Your immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. To use your grandchildren's or siblings' MediSave, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use to pay for approved vaccinations for myself?
questions.text:
You can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave or your immediate family members' MediSave.
Your immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. To use your grandchildren's or siblings' MediSave, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident. The same yearly withdrawal limit applies for approved chronic disease treatments and health screening.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use to pay for my own or an approved dependant's day surgery bills?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave:
Up to $830 per day for ward charges; and
Between $240 and $5,290 for your surgical procedures, depending on the type of procedures performed.
You can use up to the same withdrawal limit for each approved dependant. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

questions.title: How much should I set aside for my long-term care needs?
questions.text:
Long-term care costs will vary across individuals due to differing care needs and arrangements.
Individuals will also have different financing sources. For instance, Singaporeans with higher incomes will qualify for a lower level of subsidies for their care, and will need to draw more from other financing sources. In addition to existing Government subsidies and assistance schemes, those who require additional funding can also make monthly cash withdrawals of up to $200 from their MediSave from 1 October 2020. You can also consider supplementing your basic CareShield Life/ElderShield insurance with private savings or Supplements from the private insurers.
You are strongly encouraged to plan early and consider your future income, long term care arrangement preferences and how much insurance coverage and personal savings will be needed to finance these arrangements.

questions.title: How was the MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit sized?
questions.text: The MediSave withdrawal limits are generally sized to cover subsidised bills, so that the healthcare costs remain affordable.

questions.title: How was the starting payout of $600 per month for CareShield Life determined?
questions.text:
Long-term care costs vary depending on an individual's needs, care arrangements, and available financial resources.
In determining the enhanced payout amount, the ElderShield Review Committee considered the basic long-term care costs across different services and settings, other sources of long-term care funding, such as Government subsidies and assistance schemes, community support, personal savings, family support and Government-funded safety nets like MediFund or ComCare, as well as the need to balance benefits with premium affordability. As part of the overall enhancements to long-term care financing, CareShield Life provides better protection and assurance for Singaporean's basic long-term care needs.
If you would like additional coverage, you may consider purchasing Supplements from the private insurers.

questions.title: How will participating in Contribute As You Earn affect my MediSave contributions payable?
questions.text:
Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) does not change the amount of MediSave contributions you have to make based on your net trade income (NTI). Self-employed persons (SEPs) are required to contribute to their MediSave Account (MA) if their annual NTI1 exceeds $6,000.
The only change is in how the contributions are made. Under CAYE, the agency/company you provided a service to will help to deduct a portion of your service payment and contribute the amount to your MediSave Account, as and when it makes a service payment to you.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.
Your CAYE contributions are based on your estimated annual revenue and expenses. Thus, CAYE contributions are an estimate of your MediSave payable. After you declare your NTI for the year, your MediSave payable will be computed.
If your total CAYE contributions are higher than your MediSave payable for the latest year, your excess CAYE contributions will be used to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years2. Any remaining CAYE contributions will then be refunded to you.
If your total CAYE contributions are lower than your MediSave payable, you’ll be required to top up the remaining amount. You’ll be notified accordingly, and you can choose to make payment via lump-sum payment(s) or sign up for GIRO instalments.
2This will take effect for CAYE contributions made from 2023. Please write to us if you do not wish to use your CAYE contributions to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: I already went for a severe disability assessment recently, why is the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) requesting me to go for another?
questions.text: Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) may require you to attend a disability review to ascertain your continued eligibility for scheme payouts. Your letter will include instructions on how to complete the disability assessment.

questions.title: I am a government pensioner receiving lifelong medical benefits. Is the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) applicable to me?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) for government pensioners differs from that of other CPF members in the same cohort, depending on the coverage of their Post-Retirement Medical Benefits Schemes.
The BHS does not apply to government pensioners under the Fixed Amount on Ward Charges Scheme (FAW). All working contributions allocated to their MediSave Account (MA) and any MediSave top-ups will be transferred to their other CPF accounts.
Pensioners under the Co-payment on Ward Charges Scheme (CPW) have a lower BHS than other CPF members in their cohort. Once this BHS is reached, any working contributions allocated to their MA and any MediSave top-ups will be transferred to their other CPF accounts.
Pensioners under the Comprehensive Co-Payment Scheme (CCS) and MediSave-cum-Subsidised Outpatient (MSO) Scheme will have the same BHS as other CPF members in their cohort.
Dependants of pensioners will also have the same BHS as other CPF members in their cohort. They can refer to the FAQ ‘What is the Basic Healthcare Sum when I turn 65 years old?’ to find out their applicable BHS.

questions.title: I am a patient with a complex chronic condition. Will I enjoy the higher withdrawal limit of $700 under MediSave500/700 even after my condition improves?
questions.text: The MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit is a yearly limit. This means that you will continue to be able to withdraw up to $700 in the new year if you have had visits for two or more conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), or one CDMP condition with complications in that year.

questions.title: I am a self-employed person. Can I contribute to my MediSave together with my employees' CPF using CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
As self-employed person, you are required to make your MediSave payable separately from your employees' CPF. This is because payments made using CPF EZPay will be credited as employer contributions and will not be recognized as self-employed payments.
If you would like to make CPF contributions as a self-employed person, there are various ways to do so.

questions.title: I am a self-employed person. How do I ensure that I have fully settled or are on a monthly instalment plan for my MediSave payable, so I can benefit from the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
You may check if you have fully settled or are on an active GIRO arrangement with CPF Board for your MediSave payable by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
If you have not made any arrangements to settle your MediSave payable, you may make full payment for your MediSave payable or request an instalment plan via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am a taxi driver receiving contributions under the Drive and Save Scheme. Will these contributions be counted towards the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: Contributions made under the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme are specifically designated to fulfil your mandatory MediSave contributions as a Self-Employed Person (SEP). Hence, any contributions made under the DAS Scheme will not count towards the Matched MediSave Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am aged 65 years old, and I would like to use my Flexi-MediSave to pay for my father's outpatient medical treatment cost at a polyclinic. Can I do so?
questions.text: Flexi-MediSave can only be used for your own or your spouse's outpatient medical treatment expenses.

questions.title: I am an ElderShield claimant who is recently approved on MediSave Care. Why am I asked to go for disability review when my application has just been approved?
questions.text:
Periodic reviews are carried out to check on some individuals’ severe disability status to ascertain their continued eligibility for payouts. As such, if there is a need for you to attend a severe disability review, Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will inform you.
Please note that disability review assessment fees are waived. Please bring along your disability review letter and show it to the MOH-accredited severe disability assessors.
topics: ElderShield / Government Administration of ElderShield in 2021

questions.title: I am an existing ElderShield insured. If I am eligible for ElderShield claims, should I claim from ElderShield or join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you have severe disability (i.e. unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living) and are an ElderShield insured, you should apply to claim under ElderShield so that you can receive your monthly claim payouts in a timely manner.
You will not be eligible for CareShield Life if you have severe disability.

questions.title: I am an existing ElderShield/ElderShield Supplement policyholder. Do I have to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born between 1970 and 1979, who were covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and did not develop severe disability, were auto-enrolled to CareShield Life from 1 December 2021.
Those who were not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life.
The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to those who join CareShield Life, to ensure that no one who joins the scheme loses coverage due to financial difficulties.
You may refer to the types of premium support available for more information. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Can I choose to receive the CareShield Life participation incentive as one lump sum?
questions.text: The participation incentive was provided to Singapore Citizens who joined and were covered under CareShield life by 31 December 2024. It was introduced to encourage Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier to join CareShield Life by helping to offset the annual premiums payable. As such, the Government has designed it to be spread over 10 years of premium payment. It cannot be received as one lump sum payment.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Why are there no subsidies for the catch-up component when it looks so substantial?
questions.text:
The catch-up component is not subsidised to ensure parity in premium subsidies across different groups within those born in 1979 or earlier.
If you are unable to afford your CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support to help you with your CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later and am terminally ill but do not have severe disability. Can I be exempted from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
As CareShield Life is universal for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, there are no exemptions even though you are terminally ill. As long as you are covered under CareShield Life, you can still receive monthly payouts in the event of severe disability.
The Government will support Singaporeans who are unable to afford their premiums, so that no one will lose their coverage due to financial difficulties.

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later, who can be covered under CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you are born in 1980 or later, you will be automatically covered under CareShield Life from 1 October 2020, or when you turn 30, whichever is later.

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later. If I have private insurance coverage similar to CareShield Life, can I be exempted from universal coverage?
questions.text: CareShield Life will be universal for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later. Private insurance can still play a complementary role by providing additional benefits above and beyond such basic coverage.

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later. What do I need to do to be covered by CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1980 or later, you are automatically covered under CareShield Life from 1 October 2020, or when you turn 30, whichever is later.
If you are born between 1980 and 1990 (i.e. aged 30 to 40 in 2020), you would have received a CareShield Life welcome package informing you of your CareShield Life cover, by 2 September 2020 or up to two months before your 30th birthday, whichever is later.
If you are born after 1990 (i.e. aged below 30 in 2020), you will receive a CareShield Life Welcome Package before you reach age 30.

questions.title: I am born in 1990 or later, when will I be notified of my CareShield Life cover?
questions.text: If you are born in 1990 or later, you will receive a CareShield Life welcome package about two months before your 30th birthday.

questions.title: I am concerned of the state of my health, and would like to go for some health screenings. Can I use my MediSave for them?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for your own or your approved dependants' outpatient scans or health screenings at the participating medical institutions. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. Please note that your grandchildren and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
The use of MediSave for mammograms are for female patients aged 50 years or above. This is in line with recommendations from the Screening Test Review Committee from The Academy of Medicine Singapore.
You may also use MediSave for colonoscopy if you are 50 years old or above, according to the withdrawal limits in the image above.

questions.title: I am eligible for both the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme and Matched MediSave Scheme but I have limited funds. Should I top up the Retirement / Special Account or MediSave Account?
questions.text:
If you and your loved ones have limited funds available for CPF top-ups and are eligible for both Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) and Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), you can consider which scheme better meets your needs. You may also wish to consider portioning your funds and top up to both your Retirement / Special Account (RA / SA) and MediSave Account (MA) to benefit from both schemes.
If you want to increase your retirement payout, you may consider topping up your RA / SA to benefit from MRSS. If you anticipate higher healthcare spending given your health circumstances, you may consider topping up your MA to benefit from MMSS.
You can refer to this comparison table to learn the key differences between the two schemes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am eligible for both the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme and Matched MediSave Scheme. Can I participate in both schemes to receive the maximum Government grants?
questions.text: Yes, if you are eligible for both schemes, you can top up in cash to your Retirement / Special Account to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) of up to $2,000 per year, as well as to your MediSave Account to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) of up to $1,000 per year. You can top up to these accounts, anytime throughout the year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme at the beginning of the year. Will I still be eligible if there are changes to my circumstances during the year?
questions.text:
Your eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) for the year is first determined at the beginning of the year. Changes to your financial circumstances (e.g. increase in monthly income) will not affect your eligibility for that year. Your eligibility for MMSS will be reassessed next year based on your new circumstances.
However, you will no longer be eligible for MMSS if:
You are no longer a Singapore Citizen within the year; or
You are a self-employed person (SEP) who has not fully settled or are not on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable
Find out more information on the conditions you need to meet to receive and keep the matching grant.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am going for a day surgery. How do I know if I can use my MediSave in that clinic/hospital?
questions.text:
You can refer to this list of medical institutions or day surgery centres participating in the MediSave scheme.
To use your MediSave, please inform the staff handling your hospital admission that you wish to do so. The staff will submit your claim for you after your authorisation.

questions.title: I am going to be 29 years old when CareShield Life is launched. If I have severe disability, will I be able to join the scheme earlier?
questions.text:
Under CareShield Life, premiums paid by insureds are designed to be risk-pooled within their own generation, and used to cover their claims in the event of severe disability.
As there is no risk pool for your cohort when the scheme is launched, your cohort will be covered under CareShield Life when you turn 30 years old, even if you have severe disability.
You may refer to Government support schemes specifically for younger Singaporeans who have developed disability and their caregivers on the SG Enable's website or speak to SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.

questions.title: I am holding two types of licences (e.g. LTA and ACRA). Do I have to make MediSave contributions for both licences?
questions.text:
Your MediSave contributions are computed based on your age and net trade income1 (NTI) for the year. Regardless of the number of licence(s) you hold, if you earn an annual NTI of more than $6,000, you are required to make mandatory MediSave contributions.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards

questions.title: I am making a reimbursement claim from my employer or insurer for my medical bills. Is it compulsory to provide a hardcopy Healthcare payments and claims statement?
questions.text: CPF Board does not require any documents from your employer or insurer to process the reimbursement. You are not required to provide a hardcopy Healthcare payments and claims statement when making a reimbursement claim. If your employer or insurer requests a statement, they should accept a digital copy.

questions.title: I am receiving my monthly payouts. Does the online Daily Withdrawal Limit affect my monthly payout amount?
questions.text: No, the online Daily Withdrawal Limit does not affect the monthly payout amount you are receiving. The online Daily Withdrawal Limit only applies to CPF lump sum withdrawals made under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: I am receiving other disability assistance schemes such as Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme or Home Caregiving Grant. Can I qualify for CareShield Life or ElderShield claims?
questions.text:
Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS) and Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) are moderate disability schemes, which support individuals who require some assistance with three or more Activities of Daily Living.
In contrast, CareShield Life and ElderShield are severe disability schemes that require individuals to be unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (i.e. they must require significant assistance) in order to be eligible for a claim.
As the eligibility criteria for CareShield Life and ElderShield are more stringent, an assessment by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor is required to determine if an individual qualifies for these claims.

questions.title: I am self-employed and have outstanding MediSave payable. Why am I not eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme grant?
questions.text:
It is a statutory requirement for self-employed persons (SEPs) to make their mandatory MediSave contributions*. Hence, SEPs who have not fully settled or are not on a monthly instalment plan for their MediSave payable will not be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) grant.
*For platform workers, this also applies if you have outstanding MediSave payable from your platform work prior to 2025.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am staying at a nursing home’s chronic sick unit. Can I tap on MediSave Care withdrawals to pay for the monthly bills?
questions.text: You can arrange for the MediSave Care withdrawals to be paid directly to approved healthcare institutions such as nursing homes to offset your nursing home bill.

questions.title: I am staying in a nursing home. Can I use MediSave Care/CareShield Life/ElderShield payouts to pay for the monthly bills?
questions.text: If you qualify to claim under MediSave Care/CareShield Life/ElderShield, you can arrange for the payouts to be paid directly to approved healthcare institutions, such as nursing homes, to cover your monthly bills.

questions.title: I am the family member or caregiver of a Mentally Incapacitated (MI) Patient. Can I receive CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts on their behalf?
questions.text:
You may nominate your own bank account to receive monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts on behalf of a Mentally Incapacitated (MI) patient. However, if the payout is not made to the patient or their nursing home, the family member or caregiver must obtain a deputyship within 12 months to prevent the suspension of payouts. This measure is in place to safeguard the patient’s interests.
For more details, please refer to the Frequently Asked Questions on AIC’s website.

questions.title: I am unable to make my MediSave contributions in full. What should I do?
questions.text:
If you are having difficulties making your MediSave contributions in full, you can request an instalment plan1 for your MediSave contributions via the Manage your MediSave payable form. This allows you to make your contributions conveniently in more manageable monthly instalments, with automatic deductions from your bank account.
1Please note that your request is subject to the Board’s approval. You may be required to provide additional information or supporting documents, if necessary.

questions.title: I can only see the amount of Merdeka Generation Package MediSave top-up I received in "Your Benefits" @LifeSG. Where can I see the rest of my Merdeka Generation Package benefits?
questions.text: To find out more about your Merdeka Generation Package benefits, visit http://go.gov.sg/mgpackage.

questions.title: I develop severe disability but not a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR). However, my spouse is a SC/PR. Can I make MediSave Care withdrawals from my spouse’s MediSave?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident with severe disability, you can make MediSave Care withdrawals from your own and your spouse’s MediSave.
Non-Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident who wish to make MediSave Care withdrawals from your own or your spouse’s MediSave may be assessed on a case-by-case basis and subject to approval.

questions.title: I develop severe disability. Can I use my existing disability assessment to qualify for CareShield Life/MediSave Care/ElderFund/IDAPE/ElderShield payouts?
questions.text:
Individuals who wish to apply for CareShield Life/ MediSave Care/ ElderFund/ IDAPE/ ElderShield payouts will need to undergo a severe disability assessment by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. A trained, accredited severe disability assessor will be able to assess whether the applicant meets the CareShield Life/ MediSave Care/ ElderFund/ IDAPE/ ElderShield severe disability criteria of being unable to perform three or more of the six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). We have expanded the list of accredited assessors to include therapists and nurses who have been trained.
All MOH-accredited assessors have undergone a rigorous training programme to learn how to assess an individual’s level of disability. Through the training, assessors are equipped to assess an individual’s ability to perform the six ADLs, including specific components of each ADL to take into account, what factors to consider when an individual is cognitively impaired, and what should be done if any individual’s functional ability fluctuates over time. As this is a complex process, the training and accreditation is necessary to ensure that disability assessments are conducted with a high degree of rigour and consistency.
The Government is also looking into recognising equivalent assessments that have been performed by a qualified healthcare professional (doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses) providing care to the individual. In such cases, the individual need not undergo a separate severe disability assessment. Today, those who are staying in a nursing home can already approach their nursing home for assistance to submit the Resident’s Assessment Form in place of the severe disability assessment.
MOH and AIC will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will make the information available via the MOH and AIC website.

questions.title: I develop severe disability. Can I withdraw up to $200/month each from my own MediSave and another $200/month from my spouse’s MediSave (i.e. withdrawing a total of $400/month) under MediSave Care?
questions.text:
If you are eligible to apply for MediSave Care, you can only withdraw up to a combined total of $200 per month from your MediSave and/or your spouse’s MediSave.
Example
1. Husband applies to withdraw $200 monthly from his own MediSave. That is the total maximum withdrawal limit allowed from his and his spouse’s MediSave.
2. If the husband has $12,000 in his MediSave, he is eligible to withdraw $100 monthly from his own MediSave. If his wife’s MediSave balance is at least $10,000, he can apply to withdraw an additional $100 monthly from his wife’s MediSave. The total monthly MediSave Care withdrawal from his and his spouse’s MediSave add up to a maximum of $200.
MediSave Balances and corresponding Monthly Withdrawal Quantum
MediSave Balance
Monthly Withdrawal Quantum
$20,000 and above
$200
$15,000 and above
$150
$10,000 and above
$100
$5,000 and above
$50
Below $5,000
NIL ($0)

questions.title: I do not have a CPF account. Can I still join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you do not have a CPF account, you will still be able to join CareShield Life. You can make your first premium payment via the following methods:
Opening a CPF account by making a top-up to your MediSave Account
A family member* can apply to take over as your premium payer using his/her MediSave savings. To do so, he/she may visit the Change Premium Payer e-Service and log in using his/her own Singpass to complete the "Change Premium Payer" transaction.
*Family member refers to the Insured's spouse, parents, children, siblings or grandchildren.

questions.title: I do not have a Singpass account. How will I be notified of my MediSave deduction?
questions.text:
You will be notified of your MediSave deduction digitally via your contact details maintained with CPF Board.
We strongly encourage you to update your contact details with us using Singpass to obtain timely notification of your MediSave deduction.
Having a Singpass account provides added convenience and security when accessing Singapore government services. You can register a Singpass account by following the instructions on the Singpass website.

questions.title: I do not have enough MediSave to pay for my hospitalisation expenses. Are there other ways to pay for it?
questions.text:
If you do not have sufficient MediSave for your hospitalisation expenses, you may consider tapping on one or more of your immediate family member's MediSave. Immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident if you wish to tap on your grandchildren or sibling's MediSave.
It is important to note that while you can tap on your immediate family members' MediSave, the amount you can use is still subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per hospitalisation episode basis. If you still have outstanding hospitalisation expenses after using up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, you would have to pay the remainder in cash.
For more information, please speak to the staff at the hospital's Business Office.
You should use your MediSave prudently to provide for your own and your approved dependant's hospitalisation needs. This is because you may require more medical care in your old age.

questions.title: I do not have enough MediSave to pay for my outpatient treatment expenses. How else can I pay for it?
questions.text:
If you do not have sufficient MediSave for your outpatient treatment expenses, you may consider tapping on one or more of your immediate family member's MediSave. Immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident if you wish to tap on your grandchildren or sibling's MediSave.
You may claim up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for non-complex chronic patients) per patient per year. Each MediSave claim is subject to a 15% co-payment in cash except for treatments received at your enrolled Healthier SG clinic. You may find out more about Healthier SG and search for a clinic near you to enrol into one.
While you can tap on your immediate family member's MediSave, the amount you can use is subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per patient basis regardless of the number of payers. If you still have outstanding medical expenses after utilising up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, you would have to pay the remainder in cash.

questions.title: I do not have outstanding MediSave payable as a self-employed person. Can I make MediSave contributions to offset my future payables?
questions.text:
You may make MediSave contributions to offset your future payables, up to the prevailing CPF Annual Limit, via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
The total CPF contributions (voluntary and mandatory CPF contributions) made for the calendar year should not exceed the prevailing CPF Annual Limit. Any contributions made in excess of the CPF Annual Limit will be refunded without interest.
You can enjoy tax relief on your MediSave contributions, if eligible.

questions.title: I do not have Singpass. Can I apply to join CareShield Life via a hardcopy form?
questions.text:
Please apply for Singpass via the Singpass website. Alternatively, you may contact the Singpass Helpdesk at support@singpass.gov.sg or 65 6643 0555.
Thereafter, you may apply to join CareShield Life with your Singpass.

questions.title: I earned income from platform work only and my platform operator(s) is/are making CPF contributions on my behalf. Why did I receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed person informing me to make mandatory MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
You will receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons if your annual net trade income (NTI) exceeds $6,000, after excluding net earnings from platform work declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.
For work year 2025 onwards, if you only earned income from platform work and received a notice of CPF contributions, please Write To Us so that we can assist with your case. Please provide us with your tax filing consolidated statement issued by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) and your earning slips issued by your platform operator(s). If you are on paper returns for tax filing and are not issued a consolidated statement, please provide us with a copy of your paper individual Income Tax Return (Form B) instead.
You may refer to the following steps or the steps to download notices issued by IRAS (including consolidated statement):
Log in to IRAS’ tax portal
Navigate to Inbox > View notices > Individual
Select the notice that you wish to download, and click “Download selected”
If you encounter any difficulties accessing the tax portal or locating notices issued by IRAS, please contact IRAS for assistance.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I earned income from self-employment and platform work. How can I check that the MediSave contributions in my notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons are only for my self-employment income and have excluded my platform work earnings?
questions.text:
In computing your self-employed MediSave contributions, we will first take your annual net trade income (NTI) assessed by IRAS [A], and deduct your net earnings from platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) [B]. The remaining income [C]* is stated in your notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons, and will be used to compute your mandatory MediSave contributions.
* [C] = [A] – [B]
To verify the income stated in your notice of CPF contributions [C], you should first ensure that you have declared each source of income from self-employment and platform work separately to IRAS. Refer to IRAS’ guide for details. You can then download your consolidated statement from IRAS to verify the income shown in your notice of CPF contributions:
Log in to IRAS’ tax portal
Navigate to Inbox > View notices > Individual
Select the notice that you wish to download, and click “Download selected”
Your consolidated statement will show the breakdown of your income (in the “Adjusted profit/loss” row), by nature of business.
E.g. assume you are a freelance tutor and private hire car driver. You can verify the NTI stated in your notice of CPF contributions [C] against the “Adjusted profit/loss” reflected under “Tutor/Lecturer” in your consolidated statement.
If you are on paper returns for tax filing and are not issued a consolidated statement, you can follow the same steps above and verify against your paper individual Income Tax Return (Form B) instead.
If you have difficulties accessing the tax portal, locating notices issued by IRAS, or need to redeclare your income for self-employment and platform work separately, please contact IRAS.
If the income reflected in your notice of CPF contributions [C] differs from the “adjusted profit/loss” stated in the consolidated statement (for the nature of businesses not relating to platform work), please Write to Us and provide us with:
Your consolidated statement (or Form B if you are on paper returns for tax filing); and
All your earning slips issued by your platform operator(s) for the year
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I have already made CPF contributions as a platform worker. Do I still need to contribute MediSave in the following year for my other self-employed work?
questions.text:
For work year 2025 onwards, if you are only receiving platform earnings in the year, platform operators would have deducted and paid the CPF contributions on your platform earnings for you every month. Therefore, you do not need to make your own MediSave contributions on such platform earnings in the following year.
If you derive self-employed income from non-platform work (e.g. giving tuition, or taxi street-hail jobs), you will still need to make MediSave contributions on these incomes in the following year on your own, as per status quo, after you have declared your net trade income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). Your MediSave contributions are computed on your NTI after excluding net earnings from your platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s). CPF Board will inform you of your mandatory MediSave contributions once IRAS has assessed your income.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I have an instalment arrangement for my MediSave contributions. Why do I need to continue with my instalment deductions if I am also making monthly contributions as a platform worker?
questions.text:
The monthly CPF contributions made by your platform operator are for your income earned from platform work from 2025 onwards. You will not need to make your own MediSave contributions on these platform earnings, since your platform operator would have deducted and paid the CPF contributions for you every month (see FAQ).
Your instalment arrangement via GIRO is for MediSave contributions on your income earned prior to 2025 (i.e. income earned in 2024 and before).
Hence, your monthly GIRO instalment deductions will continue, as this is for your past MediSave contributions.
If you are facing difficulties keeping up with your instalment, you may reach out to CPFB to arrange affordable instalment plans on your past MediSave obligations.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. Why does it not show up on the Healthcare dashboard – “CareShield Life/ElderShield” section?
questions.text:
Your CareShield Life policy details will only be displayed on your Healthcare dashboard – “CareShield Life/ElderShield” section after successful deduction of your first premium.
Please be assured that your coverage has already commenced from the date your application was approved. You will be eligible to claim if the onset of severe disability falls on or after this date.

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. Why is the coverage status reflected as ‘Waiting for Cover’ on my Healthcare dashboard?
questions.text:
Your CareShield Life coverage status will be reflected as 'Active' after your first premium is successfully deducted, which will take about two months after your application is approved.
However, please be assured that you will still be eligible for claims while your coverage status is 'Waiting for Cover'.

questions.title: I have applied to join CareShield Life online. When would I be informed of my application outcome?
questions.text:
We will notify you on the outcome of your CareShield Life application in approximately seven working days if your application has been approved, unsuccessful or pending assessment. You will be notified via the e-mail address that you have registered with a government agency (e.g. Singpass). If there is no e-mail address registered, an SMS will be sent instead.
A letter will only be sent out if both e-mail address and mobile number are unavailable.

questions.title: I have applied to join CareShield Life online. Where do I check my application status?
questions.text: You can view the status of your CareShield Life application through Activities.

questions.title: I have applied to opt out of CareShield Life as I belong to the optional group (i.e. born in 1979 or earlier) and the cover is still within my free-look period. When will my application be approved?
questions.text:
Your application to opt out of CareShield Life will be processed after one working day. You will receive a notification once your application has been processed.
You may view the status of your application via Activities (Singpass login is required).

questions.title: I have directed a medical institution to submit a claim on my behalf. However, I would like to make an amendment to that claim. What should I do?
questions.text: Please approach the medical institution that submitted the claim on your behalf for assistance.

questions.title: I have existing private insurance that covers permanent/total disability. Can I claim from both my private insurance and CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You can claim from both your private insurance and CareShield Life at the same time. These are separate insurance policies with different coverage terms, so claiming from one does not affect your eligibility to claim from the other.
The assessment criteria for disability may vary between your private insurance and CareShield Life. Please consult your private insurer for details on your specific coverage.

questions.title: I have mild or moderate disabilities or I can perform more than three Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). How can I get help for my long-term care costs?
questions.text:
If you have mild or moderate disabilities and need long-term care, you can tap on various means-tested Government subsidies and assistance schemes to complement your personal savings and family support.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare can provide further assistance to you if you are unable to pay for your care after Government subsidies and other means of support. The Government will continue to look at ways to support the needs of Singaporeans with less severe disabilities.
To find out more about long-term care services, specific Government subsidies for long-term care services and other Government assistance schemes for long-term care that Singapore Residents may tap on, you may reach out to the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) through the AIC website or 1800-650-6060. You can also speak to a Care Consultant at AIC Links located at the public hospitals and Maxwell.

questions.title: I have more than one source of trade income. Do I have to make MediSave contributions on all these sources of income?
questions.text:
Your MediSave contributions are computed based on the annual net trade income1 (NTI) from all your trades. If your total NTI from all your trades exceeds $6,000, you are required to make mandatory MediSave contributions.
You can refer to these examples of how MediSave contributions are computed on multiple sources of NTI.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.

questions.title: I have outstanding MediSave payable. Why am I not able to make voluntary top-ups to my or my loved ones' MediSave Account?
questions.text:
As a self-employed person, you are required to have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable when making top ups to your MediSave Account or your loved ones'. To do so, you can conveniently request for an instalment plan or make full payment for your MediSave payable via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
Conversely, you will be able to receive voluntary top-ups from your loved ones if they have fully settled or are on monthly instalment plans for their MediSave payable (if applicable).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: I have received a call claiming to be from CareShield Life. What should I do if this is a scam and my contact details are shared with external agencies?
questions.text:
The CareShield Life Team does not contact members to request sensitive personal information or engage any external agencies to call members on CareShield Life matters. The CareShield Life Team will not disclose members' contact details to external agencies without members' consent.
If you receive an unexpected phone call from someone who claims to be from the CareShield Life Team, please be vigilant and do not provide your sensitive personal information (e.g. Singpass ID/password, bank account or credit card details). When in doubt, end the conversation with the individual and check with the organisation which the caller claims to represent directly. To verify the authenticity of such calls, you can call us directly at 1800 222 3399 or write to us.
topics: Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I have received a notification on topping up MediSave savings. How do I know that this notification is indeed sent by CPF Board?
questions.text:
Members will receive email notifications at the email address registered with the Board. You may check or update your email address earlier registered with us using your Singpass.
To verify if the email you received is legitimate and avoid falling prey to phishing scams,
Ensure that the sender's email address is correctly spelt and ends with "@e.cpf.gov.sg".
Ensure that the hyperlinks or links you click on have a domain ending with “.gov.sg”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I have recovered from a severe disability. Can I join CareShield Life, even if I was previously receiving payouts from ElderShield?
questions.text:
You can join CareShield Life if you have recovered from your severe disability and are able to perform all Activities of Daily Living1 independently, regardless of whether you previously received payouts from ElderShield. You may need to undergo a disability assessment, and will be informed by the Agency of Integrated Care if this is required.
1 Activities of Daily Living refers to feeding, dressing, toileting, washing, walking or moving around, and transferring from bed to chair and vice versa.

questions.title: I have signed up for an approved chronic disease treatment package or an approved vaccination package with my healthcare provider. May I use my MediSave to pay for the package?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave for approved treatments under the MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit. Your healthcare provider will be able to help you to submit a MediSave claim for each treatment of the package. Please contact your healthcare provider for assistance.

questions.title: I have submitted my application to join CareShield Life and received a letter to attend a disability review. How do I go about it?
questions.text:
If you have submitted an application to join CareShield Life and received a letter requesting a disability review, please contact an MOH-accredited assessor to schedule your disability review. Your letter will include instructions on how to attend a disability assessment.
If you need further assistance, please contact Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) at 1800 650 6060 or submit an enquiry via "My Correspondences" with your Singpass Login.

questions.title: I have substantial balances in my Ordinary and Special or Retirement Accounts. Can I use the available funds to offset my MediSave payable?
questions.text: The Ordinary, Special, or Retirement Accounts, serve different purposes from the MediSave Account. While the Ordinary and Special or Retirement Account savings are meant for retirement or housing needs, your MediSave Account savings are for your healthcare needs. Thus, the balances in your Ordinary and Special or Retirement Accounts cannot be used to settle your MediSave payable, so as not to affect your retirement adequacy.

questions.title: I have used my MediSave for some outpatient medical treatments this year, and would like to know how much more I can use under Flexi-MediSave. How can I do so?
questions.text:
You can check how much more you can use under Flexi-MediSave through:
a. my cpf digital services
• Log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass
• Select 'Utilisation of healthcare benefits' from the menu bar or scroll down to the 'Utilisation of healthcare benefits' section for 'Additional benefits for the elderly (Flexi-MediSave)'
b. CPF Mobile app
• Download CPF Mobile app
• Log in using your Singpass
• Select 'Healthcare' from the menu bar for 'Flexi-MediSave'

questions.title: I have used my MediSave for some outpatient treatments of my chronic disease this year, and would like to know how much more I can use. How can I do so?
questions.text:
You can check how much more MediSave you can use for outpatient treatments of your chronic disease through:
a. my cpf digital services
• Log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass
• Select "Utilisation of healthcare benefits" from the menu bar or scroll down to the "Utilisation of healthcare benefits" section for "Treatments for chronic illnesses (MediSave500/700)"
b. CPF Mobile app
• Download CPF Mobile app
• Log in using your Singpass
• Select "My Healthcare" from the menu bar for "Outpatient Treatment"

questions.title: I intend to seek treatment at a general practitioner (GP) clinic at my void deck. How do I know if I can use my Flexi-MediSave there?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave can be used at:
Polyclinics,
Specialist Outpatient Clinics in the public hospitals and national specialty centres, and
Medical general practitioner (GP) clinics participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) scheme.
The list of participating CHAS medical GP clinics can be found at the following websites:
CHAS
Ministry of Health

questions.title: I intend to seek treatment in a hospital. How do I know if I can use my MediSave in that hospital?
questions.text:
Please refer to this list of medical institutions or day surgery centres participating in the MediSave scheme.
To use your MediSave, please inform the staff handling your hospital admission that you wish to do so. The staff will submit your claim for you after your authorisation.

questions.title: I intend to send my newborn child for health screenings. Which of the health screenings for newborns can be covered by my MediSave?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave for the following health screenings for your newborn:
Hearing test
G6P deficiency screening
Metabolic screening
Thyroid function test
You can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave for your newborn's health screenings.

questions.title: I intend to use my immediate family member's MediSave for my hospitalisation expenses. Do I need to produce any proof of my relationship with my family member?
questions.text:
You will not be required to produce documentary proof of your relationship with your family member at the point of admission. However, your family member will need to complete a Medical Claims Authorisation Form to use his/her MediSave for your hospitalisation expenses, where he/she will be asked to declare his/her relationship with you.
You and your family member may subsequently be asked to submit documentary proof of your relationship as part of an audit. Please note that legal action may be taken against any member who makes a false declaration.

questions.title: I just received my CareShield Life (CSHL) renewal letter. I do not remember receiving any notifications about being enrolled into CSHL and note that my free-look-period (FLP) has ended. Can I still opt out of the scheme?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979 who was covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme, you would have been enrolled in CareShield Life from 1 December 2021. A welcome notification package would have been sent to you in November 2021, informing you of your coverage and that after the end of the free-look-period (FLP) on 31 December 2023, you would continue to be covered under the scheme. We are unable to accede to opt-out requests for members whose FLP had ended on 31 December 2023.
CareShield Life offers lifelong protection against the costs of long-term care in the event of severe disability. Find out how CareShield Life protects you for life.

questions.title: I logged in to the Household Check e-Service but could only view my household information. How do I make changes to my household information?
questions.text:
We are currently processing changes to your household information submitted by a household member. During this time, you will not be able to make changes to your household information.
Please write to us or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 or +65 6222 3399 from overseas (after selecting your preferred language, press 3, and then 2), from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8) if you need more information.

questions.title: I visited a clinic for an outpatient medical treatment that can be paid by my Flexi-MediSave. How do I go about using my Flexi-MediSave?
questions.text:
To use your Flexi-MediSave for your outpatient medical treatment cost:
Inform the clinic that you wish to use MediSave to pay for your outpatient medical treatment. The staff will require your NRIC/Passport. If you are paying for your spouse, please also produce his/her NRIC/Passport.
The clinic may require information on how much MediSave is available for payment of the outpatient treatment. You will be able to obtain this information by logging in to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services, with your Singpass.
You and the patient (if applicable) will need to sign a Medical Claims Authorisation Form to allow the clinic to use your Flexi-MediSave to pay for the outpatient medical treatment bill.
If your employer or insurer is also paying for your outpatient treatment, please bring along your Letter of Guarantee or Employer Identity Pass (i.e. if your clinic already has an existing arrangement with your employer or insurer).

questions.title: I want to pay for my outpatient treatment for chronic disease using MediSave. How can I do so?
questions.text:
To use your MediSave for your outpatient medical treatment cost:
1. Inform the clinic that you wish to use MediSave to pay for your outpatient medical treatment. The staff will require your NRIC/Passport. If you are paying for your approved dependant, please also produce his/her NRIC/Passport. Approved dependants refer to spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
2. The clinic may require information on how much MediSave is available for payment of the outpatient treatment. You will be able to obtain this information by logging in to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services, with your Singpass.
3. You and the patient (if applicable) will need to sign a Medical Claims Authorisation Form to allow the clinic to use your MediSave to pay for the outpatient treatment bill.
4. If your employer or insurer is also paying for your outpatient treatment, please bring along your Letter of Guarantee or Employer Identity Pass (i.e. if your clinic already has an existing arrangement with your employer or insurer).

questions.title: I was born in 1979 or earlier. Can I join or upgrade to CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier and do not have any pre-existing disability, you can join CareShield Life. This applies whether you:
Previously opted out from ElderShield or did not qualify to join ElderShield
Are currently covered under ElderShield and wish to upgrade to CareShield Life
To join or upgrade to CareShield Life, you can apply via Application to join CareShield Life form using your Singpass. You may need to undergo a disability assessment, and will be informed by the Agency of Integrated Care if this is required.
For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you can access the CareShield Life Premium Checker using your Singpass.

questions.title: I was diagnosed with a complex chronic condition in the middle of the year. How does this affect my MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit?
questions.text: If you are diagnosed with a complex chronic condition in the middle of the year, your MediSave 500/700 withdrawal limit will automatically be increased from $500 to $700, and the new limit will apply for the entire year.

questions.title: I was told by my dentist that Flexi-MediSave does not cover all dental treatments. Why is that so?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave is meant to help with recurrent outpatient medical expenses, which many older Singaporeans have raised as a key concern due to significant accumulated bill sizes over the longer term.
Flexi-MediSave can be used for select restorative dental procedures, i.e. permanent crowns and root canal treatments which can be relatively more costly. Other dental expenses are not covered under Flexi-MediSave and patients can benefit from generous government subsidies to cover costs – for example, at CHAS dental clinics and public institutions such as the polyclinics and National Dental Centre.
Nevertheless, you can use MediSave under the MediSave withdrawal limits applicable for day surgeries for selected complex dental procedures.

questions.title: I wish to apply, retain, or renew a business registration or licence with my business partners. Do all of us need to have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for our MediSave payable?
questions.text:
Yes, all owners or partners who wish to apply, retain, or renew their business registration or licence are required to have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for their MediSave payable.
Existing business registrations and licences may be subject to cancellation if any of the owners or partners have not fully settled or are not on a monthly instalment plan for their MediSave payable. The relevant licensing agency (e.g., ACRA) will send a notice to all owners or partners to inform them of any early business registration or licence cancellations.

questions.title: I would like my monthly payouts for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care to be made to an overseas bank account. How can I do so?
questions.text: You are advised to nominate a local bank account as this is the default payment option.

questions.title: I would like my monthly payouts for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care to be made to an overseas bank account. How can I do so?
questions.text: You are encouraged to nominate a local bank account for your monthly payouts under CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care as this is the default payment option.

questions.title: I would like to donate my Pioneer Generation - MediSave Top-Ups. How can I do so?
questions.text:
Thank you for your kind spirit of generosity. We are glad that you are considering donating. However, we regret that you cannot donate your MediSave top-ups because they are meant for your healthcare needs.
Instead, we encourage you to donate an equivalent cash sum (if you wish) to those in need. You may do so via online fundraising platforms such as Giving.sg (by the National Volunteer & Philanthropy Centre) or to Community Chest (by the National Council of Social Service).

questions.title: If I am 66 years old in 2026 and my applicable Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is $75,500, am I allowed to maintain a balance greater than my applicable BHS in my MediSave Account?
questions.text: You can only save up to your applicable Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) in your MediSave Account (MA), which is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA. The BHS is designed to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and to prevent the excessive accumulation of funds in your MA.
