questions.title: If I am a non-profit organisation and want to top up to a specific member, how can my organisation make such top-up and how do I know if the recipient of the top up will benefit from Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: You can submit your request to make voluntary top-ups to specific members here and we will assess if the member is eligible and inform you accordingly.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: If I am a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR) with severe disability, can I make MediSave Care withdrawals from my non-SC/PR spouse’s MediSave?
questions.text: If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident with severe disability, you can make MediSave Care withdrawals from your own and your spouse’s MediSave. Non-Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident who wish to make MediSave Care withdrawals from your own or your spouse’s MediSave may be assessed on a case-by-case basis and subject to approval.

questions.title: If I am born in 1979 or earlier and have severe disability, can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are unable to perform one or more Activities of Daily Living (i.e. have disability), you will not be eligible to join CareShield Life.
If you are currently insured under ElderShield and have not made a claim yet, you may claim from ElderShield instead. Depending on the plan you have, ElderShield provides monthly cash payouts of $300 per month for up to 60 months (under ElderShield 300 plan), or $400 per month for up to 72 months (under ElderShield 400 plan).
If you have received all your ElderShield payouts, you may tap on Government subsidies and various Government assistance schemes (such as the Home Caregiving Grant, ElderFund) for assistance. You may also approach the Medical Social Workers at the health institution you are seeking medical treatment from or your nearest Social Service Office (SSO). For more information, please refer to this page on MediFund or this page on ComCare.

questions.title: If I am currently on ElderShield 300/400 and choose to upgrade to CareShield Life, can I opt out or downgrade to ElderShield 300/400 subsequently?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979, you will be automatically enrolled in CareShield Life from 1 December 2021, if you are currently covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and do not have severe disability at the point of auto-enrolment. You can opt out of CareShield Life by 31 December 2023 if you do not wish to join the scheme and you will automatically be placed back onto your ElderShield 400 scheme.
Those who are not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life. If you are an ElderShield insured in this group, you will have a 60-day free-look period from the commencement of your CareShield Life coverage, for you to review your decision. If you choose to opt out, you will be given a full premium refund and will be automatically placed back onto your original ElderShield 300/400 scheme.
You will not be able to opt out from the scheme after the applicable opt-out/free-look periods.

questions.title: If I am eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme this year, will I be automatically eligible in the following years?
questions.text: No, your eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is assessed annually. We will inform you at the beginning of the year if you are eligible. You can also check your eligibility for MMSS via Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: If I am not covered under CareShield Life and have developed severe disability, can I withdraw more than $200/month under MediSave Care?
questions.text:
The Government encourages individuals to review their severe disability insurance coverage carefully to ensure that they have adequate financial protection against severe disability, especially in old age.
Due to the personal savings nature of MediSave, there are no benefits of risk-pooling like CareShield Life, and the withdrawals are constrained by the savings over the working years. The withdrawal limit of $200 under MediSave Care was set to ensure that there would be enough MediSave set aside for other medical purposes such as hospitalisation expenses and selected outpatient treatments which MediSave is primarily designed for.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare can provide further assistance if you are unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.
The Government will also review the MediSave withdrawal limits regularly to ensure that basic long-term care costs remain affordable for Singaporeans.

questions.title: If I am not the payer for my health insurance policies, will I be able to use the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: Yes, you can use the Health Insurance Planner even if someone else pays for your policies. The planner will create projections as if you were the payer, allowing you to compare your current plan with other available options in the market.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: If I develop severe disability, can I withdraw up to $200 per month from my own MediSave and another $200 from my spouse’s MediSave under MediSave Care?
questions.text:
If you are eligible for MediSave Care, you can only withdraw up to a combined total of $200 per month from your own and/or your spouse’s MediSave.
Example
Husband applies to withdraw $200 monthly from his own MediSave. That is the maximum withdrawal limit allowed from his own and/or his spouse’s MediSave.
If the husband has $12,000 in his MediSave, he can withdraw $100 monthly from his own MediSave. If his wife’s MediSave balance is at least $10,000, he can apply to withdraw an additional $100 monthly from her MediSave, totalling $200 per month in MediSave Care withdrawals.
MediSave Balances and corresponding Monthly Withdrawal Quantum
MediSave Balance
Monthly Withdrawal Quantum
$20,000 and above
$200
$15,000 and above
$150
$10,000 and above
$100
$5,000 and above
$50
Below $5,000
Nil ($0)

questions.title: If I do not fully utilise my MediSave withdrawal limits for inpatient treatment, can I receive the unused amount in cash?
questions.text:
You will not be able to receive the unused amount in cash if you do not fully utilise your MediSave withdrawal limits for inpatient treatment.
Existing MediSave limits cater to well-defined care episodes and treatments. MediSave is hence intended to directly pay providers for the exact cost of treatment incurred, up to prevailing withdrawal limits.

questions.title: If I do not have enough MediSave balance, but am able to draw from my spouse's MediSave for MediSave Care, can I still qualify for ElderFund?
questions.text:
ElderFund is a discretionary assistance scheme targeted at assisting lower-income Singaporeans aged 30 and above who have developed severe disability and are not able to join CareShield Life or have low MediSave balances and inadequate personal savings to meet their long-term care needs.
If you are unable to meet your long-term care costs, even after receiving payouts under CareShield Life/ElderShield, MediSave Care or IDAPE, you may be considered for ElderFund on a case-by-case basis.
If you have challenges meeting your long-term care needs, you should approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), or a medical social worker at your long-term care provider, for more advice and assistance.

questions.title: If I do not have my cohort’s Basic Healthcare Sum when I reach my Payout Eligibility Age and I intend to start receiving my retirement payouts, do I need to top up my MediSave Account?
questions.text: You do not need to top up your MediSave Account (MA) to the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) in order to receive your retirement payouts. The BHS is the estimated savings you need in your MA to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA.

questions.title: If I do not intend to renew my licence, do I need to settle my outstanding MediSave payable?
questions.text: You’re required to pay your outstanding MediSave payable even if you do not intend to renew your licence.

questions.title: If I have CareShield Life/ElderShield 300/ElderShield 400/IDAPE/Supplements or I am able to withdraw under MediSave Care, can I still qualify for ElderFund payouts?
questions.text:
The target group for ElderFund recipients are Singapore Citizens who are not eligible for CareShield Life, ElderShield and IDAPE, or are no longer active recipients of ElderShield and IDAPE. Our focus is also on benefitting Singapore Citizens who have low MediSave balances, which means that the amount that they are able to draw under MediSave Care will not be the full withdrawal limit of $200/month.
However, Singaporeans who are unable to meet their long-term care costs, even after receiving payouts under CareShield Life/ElderShield, MediSave Care (from himself or his spouse) or IDAPE, may be considered for ElderFund on a case-by-case basis.
If you have challenges meeting your long-term care needs, you should approach a medical social worker at your long-term care provider, or the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for more advice and assistance.

questions.title: If I have developed severe disability, can I make MediSave Care withdrawals from my spouse's MediSave Account?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR) with severe disability, you can make MediSave Care withdrawals from your own and your spouse’s MediSave.
Non-SC or PR who wish to make MediSave Care withdrawals from your SC or PR spouse's MediSave may be assessed on a case-by-case basis and are subject to approval.

questions.title: If I have finished claiming my ElderShield 300/400 payouts, can I still join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You can choose to join CareShield Life even if you have already completed claiming your payouts under ElderShield 300/400. However, you may be required to undergo a disability assessment. Please note that you will not be eligible to join CareShield Life if you are unable to perform one or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
However, you can tap on Government subsidies and various Government assistance schemes such as Home Caregiving Grant and ElderFund, and MediSave Care to complement your personal savings and family support, in meeting your long-term care needs. Government assistance schemes such as the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund can also help defray the cost of consumables and assistive devices.

questions.title: If I have used $500 from my MediSave account for my treatment under MediSave500, can I still withdraw from my family members' MediSave accounts to pay for my treatment?
questions.text: From 1 January 2021, each patient is eligible to withdraw up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for non-complex chronic patients) for their own treatment, regardless of how many MediSave accounts are being withdrawn from.

questions.title: If my employer(s)/ platform operator(s) and I are not required to make CPF or MediSave contributions for my income with each employer(s)/ platform operator(s), can I still receive Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.text:
If you earn less than $500 per month (in total), you must meet the eligibility criteria for concessionary Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) in order to qualify for concessionary WIS payments.
If you earn $500 or more per month (in total) but work for multiple employers/platform operators and are not required to make CPF or MediSave contributions for your income with each employer/platform operator, you may be eligible for WIS.
If you are an employee and meet all the eligibility criteria:
(i) you will be automatically assessed for WIS if your employer is making CPF contributions for you. This is when you are earning more than $50 per month with the employer.
(ii) you may write to us to assess your eligibility if you are earning $50 or less per month with an employer.
If you are a self-employed person (SEP) and meet all the eligibility criteria:
You will receive WIS payments after you have made the required MediSave contributions.
If you are a platform worker and meet all the eligibility criteria:
(i) You will be automatically assessed for WIS if your platform operator is making CPF contributions for you. This is when:
you are mandated or opted-in to increased CPF contributions and are earning more than $50 per month with the platform operator.
you are not opted-in to increased CPF contributions and are earning more than $500 per month with the platform operator.
(ii) You may write to us to assess your eligibility if:
you are mandated or opted-in to increased CPF contributions and are earning $50 or less per month with a platform operator.
you are not opted-in to increased CPF contributions and are earning $500 or less per month with a platform operator.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: If my loved one has IDAPE, ElderShield 300/400, CareShield Life, supplements, or MediSave Care, can he/ she still qualify for ElderFund?
questions.text:
ElderFund supports Singapore Citizens who are not:
A CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholder / supplement plan policyholder
An active recipient of CareShield Life or ElderShield (including supplement claims)
Eligible for or currently receiving payouts from Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE)
It also seeks to support Singapore Citizens who have low MediSave balances (ie less than $10,000). This means that the amount that they are able to draw from MediSave will not be the full $200 monthly sum allowable under MediSave Care.
Singapore Citizens who are unable to meet their long-term care costs, even after receiving payouts under ElderShield/ CareShield Life, MediSave Care (from himself or his spouse) or IDAPE, may be considered for ElderFund on a case-by-case basis.
Please speak to a medical social worker or AIC for advice.
Please click here for more information on ElderFund.

questions.title: If my Supplements overlap with CareShield Life, will insurers provide a refund if I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
As Supplement policies are separately administered by the private insurers, they will remain active as long as you continue paying your premiums and do not terminate your coverage. Your existing Supplement policies will not be affected by CareShield Life. You will also be able to make a claim under both CareShield Life and your Supplement.
For further advice, consider speaking with your financial advisor.

questions.title: If the licensees had any contraventions with any healthcare financing schemes, what are the enforcement actions under the HCSA that can be imposed on the licensees to protect patient safety and welfare ?
questions.text:
Any contravention of healthcare financing schemes established by written law (e.g., MediShield Life Scheme Act) can be taken into account by MOH at licence renewal or if errant management decided to apply for a new licence.
In addition, regulatory action may be taken against the licensee if public interest so requires.
The regulatory actions range from censuring the licensee in writing, to paying a financial penalty (a sum of not more than $10,000 for each contravention).

questions.title: Is CareShield Life mandatory and do I have to join it?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is universal and mandatory for the following groups:
Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, are automatically enrolled on 1 October 2020, or when they turn 30, regardless of any pre-existing conditions or disabilities.
Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents born between 1970 and 1979 were automatically enrolled from 1 December 2021 if they were covered under ElderShield 400 and had not developed severe disability at the point of auto-enrollment.
Foreigners who become Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards and are born in 1979 or earlier are automatically enrolled provided they have no severe disability (if granted residency from 1 October 2020 to 31 December 2025). From 1 January 2026, automatic enrolment applies only to those with no disability at all.
The scheme is made mandatory to ensure that all Singaporeans, including those who are more vulnerable such as the lower-income group and those with pre-existing severe disabilities, have basic protection for long-term care needs. The Government will support Singaporeans who are unable to afford their premiums, so that no one loses their coverage due to financial difficulties.
If you were not automatically enrolled, you can apply to join CareShield Life. A 60-day free-look period applies from the start of coverage, after which you will not be able to terminate your coverage.

questions.title: Is Flexi-MediSave applicable only to the Pioneer Generation or all elderly?
questions.text: Flexi-MediSave applies to all elderly aged 60 and above.

questions.title: Is MediSave Care means-tested?
questions.text:
Means-testing is not required. However, to be qualified for MediSave Care, you need to fulfil all the following criteria:
a. Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.
b. Aged 30 and above.
c. Certified by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to have developed severe disability (i.e. unable to perform three (3) or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). You can find the list of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors here.
d. Have a minimum MediSave balance of $5,000.

questions.title: Is my voluntary top-up to the MediSave Account reversible?
questions.text: Voluntary top-ups made are irreversible.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of times I can use Flexi-MediSave for my outpatient treatments in a year?
questions.text: There is no limit to the number of Flexi-MediSave claims you may make in a year. However, you can only use up to $400 in a calendar year.

questions.title: Is there a minimum amount I need to top up to be eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: There is no minimum amount of cash top-up needed to be eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme. However, the more you top up, the more matching grants you can receive, up to $1,000 per year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Is there a minimum bill amount before I can use Flexi-MediSave?
questions.text: There is no minimum bill amount before Flexi-MediSave can be used. However, as smaller amounts of cash payment are generally affordable, patients may wish to conserve the use of their Flexi-MediSave for larger outpatient bills, e.g. above $20 - $30.

questions.title: My child is paying for my chronic disease treatment under the MediSave500/700 scheme. Can I also tap on my spouse's Flexi-MediSave to pay for the co-payment?
questions.text:
If both you and your spouse are aged 60 years old or above, you can use your spouse's Flexi-MediSave for the 15% co-payment.
Also, if you have reached the withdrawal limit for chronic disease treatment, you can tap on your own or your spouse's Flexi-MediSave to continue reducing the cash payment, provided that you have not reached the $400 withdrawal limit.

questions.title: My GIRO deduction for MediSave contributions has been stopped due to two unsuccessful deductions. How do I reinstate my GIRO deductions using my existing bank account registered with the Board?
questions.text:
To reinstate your MediSave GIRO deduction using your existing bank account, you can submit the “Reinstate GIRO deductions for MediSave contributions” form within 14 days from our notification. If we do not receive your application by the deadline, your current instalment plan will be terminated.
Your monthly deductions will resume once your application to reinstate your MediSave GIRO deductions has been processed. To avoid future interruption, please maintain sufficient funds in your bank account for the deductions.

questions.title: My top-up via PayNow QR is not reflected in my CPF account. Why is my CPF account balance(s) not updated immediately?
questions.text:
Your top-up via PayNow QR will generally be processed immediately upon successful deduction from your bank account.
If your top-up is not reflected in your CPF accounts, please check your CPF account balance after five working days as more time may be needed to process the transaction. Such cases may arise due to intermittent network connectivity issues beyond CPF Board's control.
Please alert us immediately if your payment is still not updated in your CPF account balance after five working days.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Should I join CareShield Life if I already have an existing ElderShield & ElderShield Supplement plan that provides similar coverage, e.g. lifetime payouts?
questions.text:
Your existing Supplement plan will not be affected, even if you join CareShield Life. You will continue to pay the same premiums for your Supplements and enjoy the same benefits for as long as you are covered. You will also be able to make claims under both CareShield Life and your Supplement plan.
You may refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support, and consider speaking to your financial advisor on whether you should upgrade to CareShield Life.

questions.title: Should I opt out of ElderShield if I would like to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You do not need to opt out of ElderShield if you wish to join CareShield Life. Your existing ElderShield cover will be upgraded to CareShield Life and the premiums paid for ElderShield will be taken into account.
Access the Application to join CareShield Life form using your Singpass. We will notify you on the outcome of your upgrade.

questions.title: Should I upgrade to/join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The Government encourages Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1979 or earlier without disability to consider joining CareShield Life for basic lifetime financial protection for long-term care. CareShield Life provides monthly cash payout in the event of severe disability, for as long as you are unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
The Government also provides support to help make premiums affordable.

questions.title: The current ElderShield scheme has a maximum entry age of 64 years old. Can I join CareShield Life if I am older?
questions.text:
You can join CareShield Life at any age as there is no maximum entry age for CareShield Life.
As premiums increase with age, please check your personalised premium payable using the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass before applying, so that you can make an informed decision.

questions.title: The MediSave withdrawal of $200 is significantly lower than the CareShield Life payout. Can I withdraw more as $200 a month is insufficient to cover long-term care needs?
questions.text:
Due to the personal savings nature of MediSave, there are no benefits of risk-pooling like CareShield Life and the withdrawals are constrained by one’s savings over one’s working years. The withdrawal limit of $200 under MediSave Care was set to ensure that there would be enough MediSave set aside for other medical purposes such as hospitalisation expenses and selected outpatient treatments which MediSave is primarily designed for.
The Government will also review the MediSave withdrawal limits regularly to ensure that basic long-term care costs remain affordable for Singaporeans.
The Government encourages individuals to review their severe disability insurance coverage carefully to ensure that they have adequate financial protection against severe disability, especially in old age. For other forms of assistance, you may wish to apply for means-tested Government assistance schemes such as the ElderFund, Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) in meeting long-term care needs. If you are still unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, there are other forms of assistance such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: Under Contribute As You Earn, how much MediSave contribution would I have to make from my service fee?
questions.text:
Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), the amount of MediSave contribution deducted from your service fee is based on your estimated annual revenue and expenses for the year.
Your CAYE contribution rate is computed by the following formula:
CAYE contribution rate = (A x B) / C
where
A is the MediSave contribution rate for your estimated annual Net Trade Income (NTI)1 and age for the year;
B is your estimated annual NTI1 for the year2; and
C is your estimated annual revenue for the year2
1 Your estimated annual NTI is derived using your estimated annual revenue less estimated annual expenses for the year.
2 If you did not provide your estimated annual revenue and expenses for the year, it will be based on your actual revenue and expenses assessed by IRAS in the preceding year.
A floor CAYE contribution rate of 2% will apply if you have earned more than $6,000 two years ago.
To ensure that your CAYE contribution rate reflects your business outlook for the year accurately, please estimate your revenue and expenses by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass, under Contribute As You Earn > Update contribution rate. You can adjust your CAYE contribution rate as and when there are changes to your estimated revenue and expenses. Generally, your updated rate will apply to payments made from the next day.
Otherwise, a personalised default CAYE contribution rate computed based on your NTI assessed by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) in the preceding year will apply.
From work year 2025, the NTI used to compute your default CAYE rate will exclude net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s).
Example on how the CAYE contribution rate will be computed
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme, will corporate service buyers only be making MediSave contributions for self-employed vendors?
questions.text: Under the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme, corporate service buyers do not need to make MediSave contributions for self-employed persons (SEPs) as SEPs are required to contribute to their MediSave Account.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What are CareShield Life and ElderShield Supplement plans?
questions.text:
CareShield Life (CSHL) and ElderShield (ESH) Supplement plans are plans which complement basic CSHL and ESH plan by offering additional benefits, such as higher monthly payout amounts or higher disability coverage, which enhance your coverage.
Supplement plans are offered by private insurers such as Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance. You need to be an existing policyholder under CSHL or ESH to purchase Supplement plans.
There is no restriction on the number of Supplement plans one can purchase. Supplement plans can be paid using MediSave, up to a limit of $600 per calendar year per person insured. Premiums for Supplement plans range widely and are commensurate with the type of benefits they offer. You may refer to the comparison of Supplement plans for more information.
For more information on your Supplement plans, please contact your insurer or log in to your insurer's web portal:

questions.title: What are the benefits of contributing to MediSave by GIRO?
questions.text:
GIRO lets you contribute to your MediSave Account through monthly instalments. Contributing to MediSave by GIRO provides:
Convenience - Automatic monthly deductions from your bank account to help you stay on track with your MediSave obligations without the risk of missing payments.
Hassle-free licence application and renewal – Your regular contributions ensure you meet MediSave requirements, making licence application and renewal processes smoother.
You can request an instalment plan for your MediSave contributions via the Manage your MediSave payable form.

questions.title: What are the benefits of the ElderShield scheme?
questions.text:
ElderShield is a long-term care insurance scheme targeted at severe disability, especially in old age. ElderShield provides monthly payouts of $300 or $400 per month, for up to 72 months. Your plan's benefits depend on when you joined ElderShield.

questions.title: What are the conditions for applying to limit my MediSave payable as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
You can apply to limit your MediSave payable if your total income from employment (excluding Additional Wages) or platform work for the year exceeds the maximum total annual income.
Additional Wages are wage supplements which are not granted wholly and exclusively for the month. Examples are the annual bonus, leave pay, incentive and other payments made at intervals of more than a month.
Please refer to the table below for the total income from employment (excluding Additional Wages) or platform work that qualifies you to limit your MediSave contributions as a self-employed person.

questions.title: What are the differences between topping up my retirement savings, making a Voluntary Housing Refund, topping up my MediSave Account and topping up my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
Find out the differences between the various types of top-ups in the table below:
Topping up your retirement savings
Voluntary Housing Refund
Topping up your MediSave Account
Topping up your 3 CPF accounts
Top up/refund to
Special Account (SA) for members below 55; or
Retirement Account (RA) for members 55 or above.
Ordinary Account (OA); and/or
RA for members 55 or above and have not met their Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in their RA.
MediSave Account (MA)
Ordinary Account (OA)
Special Account (SA) for members below 55 or Retirement Account (RA) for members 55 or above
MediSave Account (MA)
The CPF contributions allocated to the RA will be up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS). For members who have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to the OA.
Eligibility for tax relief
You can enjoy tax relief if you made cash top-ups to yourself or your loved ones up to the current year's FRS.
However, please note that tax relief would not apply if you made a CPF transfer.
You will not be eligible for tax relief.
For non self-employed persons:
You get to enjoy tax relief for voluntary top-ups to MA.
If you are self-employed, you will enjoy tax relief on your MediSave contributions based on your annual net trade income (NTI). There will be no tax relief for your MediSave contributions if your assessed NTI for the year of assessment is zero or negative.
For non self-employed persons:
You are not eligible for tax relief
For self-employed persons who made self top-up or received a top-up:
You can enjoy tax relief based on your assessable net trade income for the year.
Top-up limit
What is the maximum amount of top-ups I can receive?
If you are below 55, you may top up your SA up to the current year's FRS.
If you are 55 or above, you may top up your RA up to the current year's Enhanced Retirement Sum.
You can check your top-up limit in your Retirement Dashboard.
Can I voluntarily refund a portion of the CPF savings I used for my property?
You can make a refund of any amount, capped at the full principal amount you have withdrawn for the property, along with the accrued interest.
You may check the amount that you can refund through the Home Ownership Dashboard.
Do note that after making a full voluntary housing refund of the CPF savings withdrawn and accrued interest, all CPF withdrawals including monthly housing loan instalments (if any) for the property will stop.
What is the voluntary top-up limit to my MediSave Account?
The maximum amount you can voluntarily top up to your MA is the difference between your Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) and your current MA balance. Once your BHS has been reached, no further voluntary top-ups can be made to your MA. If you exceed your BHS from the top-up, the full amount of your top-up will be refunded to you.
You can check your top-up limit with these steps.
Top-ups cannot exceed the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740, which includes your mandatory CPF contributions for the calendar year.
When you make a cash top-up online, you will be shown the amount of top-up you can receive before you reach the top-up limit.
If you are making a top-up on another person’s behalf, please check with your recipient directly on the amount he can receive.
Top-ups in excess of the recipient’s Annual Limit will be refunded.
Withdrawal
Top-ups are meant to boost your retirement income. They will be streamed out to you as monthly payouts and cannot be used for other purposes.
You can continue to use your OA savings for the current or next property after making a voluntary housing refund.
However, if you would like to use your OA for the same property, after making a voluntary refund of the full principal amount used and the accrued interest, you will need to re-apply to use your CPF savings.
After turning 55 and setting aside the FRS, you can withdraw the remaining balance in your OA in full or in part at any time.
From 55, you can make retirement withdrawals from your OA in full or in part, at any time for your immediate needs, provided you have set aside your FRS.
MA savings are meant for your healthcare needs and cannot be withdrawn as cash.
From 55, you can make retirement withdrawals from your OA in full or in part, at any time for your immediate needs, provided you have set aside your FRS.
Top-ups to your SA and RA are meant to boost your retirement income while MA savings are meant for your healthcare needs and cannot be withdrawn in cash.
Application
Top-ups can be made using cash and/or CPF transfers.
How do I apply to make a top-up?
Refund can only be made via cash.
Can I voluntarily refund a portion of the CPF savings I used for my property?
Top-ups can only be made via cash.

questions.title: What are the payment options to do the top-up to MediSave under Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Currently, members can use PayNow to make a cash top-up to yourself or your loved ones’ MediSave Account. Your cash top-up will be credited upon successful payment.
For more information on how to make cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched MediSave Scheme, you may refer to how to make a cash top-up to MediSave Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What benefits do self-employed persons enjoy from making MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
When you contribute to MediSave, you enjoy:
Up to 6% interest per annum on your MediSave savings
Self-employed tax relief on your MediSave or CPF contributions, if eligible.
Use of MediSave to pay for medical expenses and healthcare insurance
Hassle-free licence application and renewal
You may also qualify for Workfare Income Supplement scheme for lower-income workers.

questions.title: What can I use Flexi-MediSave for?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave can be used for outpatient medical treatments (i.e. visits that do not involve a hospital stay or day surgery) received at polyclinics, public hospital Specialist Outpatient Clinics and general practitioner clinics participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).
Flexi-MediSave can cover consultation fees, select restorative dental procedures, tests and drugs, and other services such as physiotherapy, if ordered by your doctor for diagnosis or treatment of your medical condition.
Please refer to this FAQ for medical expenses that Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for.

questions.title: What can I use the Matched MediSave Scheme matching grant for?
questions.text: Matching grants granted under the Matched MediSave Scheme are credited to your MediSave Account (MA). You can use your MediSave savings to pay for approved healthcare insurance premiums (e.g. MediShield Life, CareShield Life) and approved medical treatments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What conditions must I meet in order to receive and retain the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
To receive and retain the matching grant, you must:
Be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) for the year; and
Have received cash top-ups to MediSave Account (MA) during the year; and
Still be a Singapore Citizen when the matching grant is credited to your MA at the beginning of the following year.
If you are self-employed, have fully settled your MediSave payable or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What conditions must my child meet to receive and retain the MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN)?
questions.text:
To receive and retain the MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN), the following conditions need to be met:
Your child must be a Singapore Citizen at birth, or become one by the age of 2 (the grant amount will depend on the date the citizenship is obtained).
If your child was born overseas, the child's birth must be registered with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) or through a Singapore Overseas Mission before the age of 12.
No request to return the MGN was made within two years of receiving the MGN. For more information on the request, please see this page.
For more information about the MGN, please visit madeforfamilies.gov.sg.

questions.title: What do I need to do to receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
To receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), simply make a cash top-up to your MediSave Account (MA) by 31 Dec of the year of eligibility.
You can top up any amount using PayNow. Top-ups can be made by anyone, including yourself or your loved ones.

questions.title: What does it mean that CareShield Life payouts remain fixed based on the year you start receiving them?
questions.text:
Your CareShield Life payouts will increase by 4%* each year, reaching $689 per month in 2026 and will stop increasing once you make a successful claim or turn 67 years old (whichever comes first).
For example, if you start claiming from CareShield Life in 2026 at age 67 or younger, you will receive $689 per month for as long as you have severe disability.
*The payouts will increase by 4% each year until 2030, after which they will be subject to review.

questions.title: What happens if I make multiple top-ups and exceed the annual matching cap of $1,000 for Matched MediSave Scheme? Will the excess top-ups be eligible for tax relief?
questions.text:
Givers of cash top-ups that attract the matching grant (up to $1,000 per year) under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) will not receive tax relief.
However, you may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for eligible cash top-ups that do not attract matching grants from MMSS and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones). For more information on how to compute my tax relief for voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave Account, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What happens if I stop paying for my Supplements if I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: Supplement plans will lapse if you stop paying premiums. For more information, refer to your specific Supplement policy documents or consult your insurer.

questions.title: What happens if my employer or insurer is paying part of my hospital expenses?
questions.text:
If you have given the hospital a Letter of Guarantee or Hospitalisation Identity Card at admission, the hospital will send the bill to your employer or insurer. Your employer or insurer will then work out the part of the bill to be paid by you. They will then ask you to sign a Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) if you wish to pay the amount from your MediSave Account (MA).
When your employer or insurer returns the MCAF to the hospital, the hospital will arrange to deduct the amount from your MA.
Some hospitals may request that you sign the MCAF at admission especially if your employer or insurer is paying only part of your hospital expenses.

questions.title: What happens if the amount of MediSave contributions the self-employed person has made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) is higher than his MediSave payable for the year?
questions.text:
The self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave payable for income earned in the year will be computed after the SEP has declared his actual income in the following year.
If the self-employed person (SEP) has outstanding MediSave payable from previous years, his excess CAYE contributions will be used to offset those payables1. Any excess thereafter will be refunded to him. He can also choose to retain the excess CAYE contributions in his MediSave Account (MA).
Example:
Based on his estimated income of $22,000 for 2023, Sam contributed $2,200 via CAYE. In the following year, he declared that he earned a lower Net Trade Income of $19,000 for 2023. As such, Sam’s MediSave payable for his work done in 2023 is $1,900. Hence, he has excess CAYE contributions of $300 for the year. Sam also has an outstanding MediSave payable of $100 incurred in 2022 which would be offset by the excess CAYE contributions, leaving a final excess amount of $200. This amount will be refunded to him2. He can also choose to keep this $200 in his MA.
This example is illustrated within the table below:

$22,000
CAYE contributions in 2023
$2,200
(After 2023 NTI declaration)
Declared 2023 NTI
$19,000
MediSave payable for work done in 2023
$1,900
Outstanding MediSave payable for 2022

Amount Sam will receive as a refund

(i.e. $2,200 - $1,900 - $100)
1This will take effect for CAYE contributions made from 2023. The SEP may write to us if he does not wish to use his CAYE contributions to offset his outstanding MediSave payable from previous years.
2Sam may also choose not to use his CAYE contributions to offset his outstanding MediSave payable of $100 incurred in 2022. In this case, he will be refunded $300 instead.

questions.title: What happens if the amount of MediSave contributions the self-employed person has made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) is lower than his MediSave payable for the year?
questions.text:
The self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave payable for income earned in the year will be computed after the SEP has declared his actual income in the following year.
If the SEP’s total Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution is lower than his MediSave payable for the latest year, he will be required to top up the shortfall.
Example:
Sam has made a total contribution of $2,100 via CAYE in 2023. The following year, Sam is informed that his MediSave payable for his work done in 2023 is $3,000. Sam will have to top-up the shortfall of $900.

questions.title: What happens if the child's mother passes away after receiving the Large Family MediSave Grant payment?
questions.text: For persons who have passed away after receiving the Large Family MediSave Grant payment, their Central Provident Fund (CPF) savings, including MediSave balance, will be distributed to their beneficiaries in cash according to their CPF nomination or through the Public Trustee's Office if no CPF nominations were made.

questions.title: What happens if the MediSave contributions I made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) are lower than my MediSave payable for the year?
questions.text:

questions.title: What happens to my CareShield Life coverage upon death?
questions.text: When an insured passes away, their CareShield Life policy will be terminated immediately. There is no death benefit for CareShield Life, so no payouts will be made upon the insured's passing. Any premiums paid will be refunded to the premium payer's MediSave if the insured passes away within the first 60 days of the first policy year. No premium refund will be made thereafter. If you wish to obtain insurance that provides death benefits, you can purchase Supplement plans that provide this option.

questions.title: What happens to my CareShield Life payout if I have been receiving payouts prior to 1 January 2026?
questions.text: Existing CareShield Life claimants will not be affected by the enhanced CareShield Life benefits and increased premiums, and will continue to receive their existing CareShield Life payouts for the duration of severe disability.

questions.title: What happens to my existing Supplement plan bought under ElderShield if I decided to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Your Supplement plan remains active as long as you continue paying its premiums and maintain coverage under CareShield Life or ElderShield. You can claim from both your Supplement plan and CareShield Life or ElderShield if you fulfil the respective claim criteria.
Since Supplement plans are administered by private insurers, any premiums you have already paid for these policies will not be considered when joining CareShield Life.
When upgrading to CareShield Life, only your paid ElderShield premiums will be taken into account when calculating your CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: What happens to the additional MediSave contribution if my employee has reached the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS)?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is adjusted yearly to ensure Singaporeans have sufficient savings to meet their basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age.
Any MediSave contributions in excess of the BHS will be transferred from the MediSave Account to the other CPF accounts to help with retirement expenses.

questions.title: What if I do not wish to receive the MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN)?
questions.text:
The MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN) and any interest earned on it will be recovered from the child’s CPF account if, within two years of receiving the MGN, the following person(s) notify the CPF Board or the Ministry of Health in writing that they want the MGN to be returned:
Where the child is aged below 21 years old: The parent or legal guardian, acting on behalf of the child.
Where the child is aged 21 years and above: The child.
Once the CPF Board or the Ministry of Health is notified in this manner, the condition to retain the MGN will no longer be met and the MGN and the interest earned on it will be recovered. For more information on the conditions to receive and retain MGN, please see this page.
For more information about the MGN, please visit madeforfamilies.gov.sg.

questions.title: What if I have insufficient MediSave balances for my healthcare and long-term care expenses?
questions.text:
If your MediSave Account is depleted, you may tap on your spouse's MediSave for MediSave Care withdrawals, and use your family members' MediSave for other healthcare treatments.
You may also apply for additional support through means-tested Government assistance schemes such as ElderFund and Home Caregiving Grant to cover your long-term care costs. If you are still unable to afford your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, further assistance are available through schemes such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: What if I need a treatment which is not on the Cancer Drug List (CDL), or is on the CDL but unsubsidised, and I cannot afford the treatment without insurance?
questions.text:
We encourage you to discuss with your doctor if there are suitable alternative treatments on the Cancer Drug List (CDL) that are subsidised and covered by insurance. However, if switching treatments is not feasible, there is support to help you if you face difficulty affording your treatment.
If you are a subsidised patient, you can approach a Medical Social Worker (MSW) in your public healthcare institution (PHI) for financial assistance such as MediFund. If you are a private patient, you can approach your doctor to refer you to a PHI for subsidised care. The PHI’s medical team will review your treatment plan and provide financial counselling (e.g., eligibility for subsidies) before you decide whether to transfer.
To help existing patients during this transition, MOH will provide additional financial support for all PHI patients without an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), and who had started treatments that are unsubsidised or not on the CDL before 1 September 2022. Insurers, on their part, will continue their current coverage until 30 September 2023 for patients with IP that are being renewed between 1 April 2023 and 30 September 2023, and who are on a course of cancer drug treatment as of 31 March 2023.

questions.title: What if I pass away before receiving the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: If you pass away, your matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme will still be credited to your CPF account and paid out to your beneficiaries together with any remaining CPF savings.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What if I prefer making MediSave contributions through the current payment modes (e.g. GIRO)?
questions.text:
The small and regular MediSave contributions made through Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) help self-employed persons (SEPs) to reduce the MediSave contributions payable in the following year (after SEPs declare their Net Trade Income and have their MediSave payable computed).
If you’ve made your MediSave contributions in full or are on GIRO instalment plan, you’ll be allowed to set your CAYE contribution rate to 0% and receive your service fee in full.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What if my hospital bill is more than what my MediSave can cover?
questions.text: The MediSave withdrawal limits are generally sufficient to cover bills incurred in B2 or C ward types in a public hospital. This restriction is necessary to prevent premature depletion of your MediSave, as your MediSave savings are to last through your lifetime. This is particularly important as elderly people may require more hospital stays and medical care than younger ones. If there is any part of the hospital bill that MediSave is unable to cover, you will need to pay in cash.

questions.title: What incentives are there for me to top up to my loved ones under the Matched MediSave Scheme given that there is no tax relief for me?
questions.text:
Topping up to your loved ones’ MediSave accounts helps them to grow their healthcare savings and provide them with greater peace of mind.
Recipients of cash top-ups who are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) can also receive a matching grant of up to $1,000 per year from the Government, which further boosts their MediSave savings.
You may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for eligible cash top-ups that do not attract matching grants from MMSS and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What is CareShield Life?
What is ElderShield?
questions.text:
ElderShield was first launched by the Ministry of Health in September 2002 as a severe disability insurance scheme which provides basic financial protection to those who need long-term care especially in their old age. It provides a monthly cash payout for up to 72 months to help pay out-of-pocket expenses in the event of severe disability.
ElderShield was offered to eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who had a MediSave Account when they turned 40 years old in 2019 or earlier.

questions.title: What is long-term care?
questions.text: Long-term care is the personal and medical care needed if an individual develops disability due to age or adverse health conditions. It includes a range of services which individuals may choose depending on their care needs and support available, either at home or institutions like nursing homes.

questions.title: What is MediSave Care (also known as MediSave Withdrawals for Long-Term Care)?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is a long-term care scheme which was launched on 1 October 2020. Under MediSave Care, Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged 30 and above who have developed severe disability will be able to make monthly cash withdrawals from their own and/or their spouse’s MediSave for their long-term care needs.
After setting aside a minimum amount to ensure adequacy for other medical expenses, Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with severe disability will be able to withdraw up to a total of $200/month from their own and/or their spouse’s MediSave. The table below shows the MediSave balances and corresponding monthly withdrawal quanta.

1 Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who have developed severe disability can withdraw from their spouse's MediSave Account if they have insufficient MediSave balances, and their spouse has MediSave balances of $5,000 or more. Withdrawals from their spouse's MediSave will also be subject to the same MediSave balance thresholds. The total withdrawal from their own and/or spouse's MediSave is capped at $200/month.

questions.title: What is MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is a long-term care scheme that allows Singaporeans and PRs who are severely disabled to make monthly cash withdrawals from their own and their spouse’s MediSave Accounts.
The withdrawals can be used for long-term care needs, such as hiring a helper, paying for care services, or daily expenses.
Click here to read more information about MediSave Care.

questions.title: What is MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is a long-term care scheme that allows Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged 30 and above with severe disability to make monthly cash withdrawals of up to $200 from their own and/or their spouse’s MediSave for their long-term care needs. This is provided they have set aside a minimum amount to ensure sufficient MediSave for other medical expenses.
The table below shows the required MediSave balances and the corresponding monthly withdrawal quantum for eligible individuals.1

Withdrawals from the spouse's MediSave are also subject to the same balance thresholds, and the total combined withdrawal from both accounts is capped at $200 per month.

questions.title: What is MediSave?
questions.text:
MediSave is a national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement.
Saving for future medical expenses is important, as the need for medical care and hospitalisation increases significantly as one grows older. It is important that you spend your MediSave savings prudently.
MediSave can be used for hospitalisation and day surgery expenses. MediSave can also be used to pay for certain costly outpatient treatments like dialysis, cancer drugs and radiotherapy, as well as treatment for a number of chronic diseases like diabetes and hypertension. Those with severe disability can also tap on MediSave Care for their long-term care needs. You can refer to the MOH website for the uses of MediSave and the withdrawal limits.
Additionally, MediSave can also be used to pay the premiums of approved medical insurance schemes like MediShield Life. If you want additional coverage for your bills in private hospitals, or A and B1 ward types in public hospitals, you can use your MediSave to help pay for an Integrated Shield Plan from an approved private insurer. These plans are integrated with MediShield Life to provide additional medical coverage on top of MediShield Life.
MediSave can also be used to pay the premiums of approved long-term insurance schemes like CareShield Life and ElderShield. For those under CareShield Life who would like additional coverage, you may also use your MediSave to help pay for Supplements from approved private insurers. You can refer to the CareShield Life for more information.

questions.title: What is the CareShield Life 2025 Review about?
questions.text: On 27 August 2025, Ministry of Health announced the changes related to the CareShield Life 2025 Review. You can read more about the changes by clicking on this link.

questions.title: What is the catch-up component under CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You will need to pay a catch-up component, on top of the base premium, if your ElderShield profile is any of the following prior to joining CareShield Life:
You are an existing ElderShield 300 insured.
You are not insured under ElderShield or have opted into ElderShield late.
You are an existing ElderShield 400 insured who joined CareShield Life from 1 January 2022 onwards.
Your ElderShield 300/400 policies have become reduced paid-up (i.e. you stopped paying premiums after a minimum number of years of premium payment, which qualifies you for a lower payout amount).
The catch-up component ensures consistency with those in the same cohort who had been consistently insured under the ElderShield 400 scheme and joined CareShield Life earlier.
The catch-up component will also be applicable to foreigners who become Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards.
The catch-up component is a flat amount paid across 10 years and is paid on top of the base premium.

questions.title: What is the CPF Withdrawal Lock, and how can I activate it?
questions.text:
The CPF Withdrawal Lock allows members aged 55 and above to instantly disable online CPF withdrawals by setting the Daily Withdrawal Limit to $0, and is part of CPFB’s suite of anti-scam measures.
If you do not need to withdraw immediately, you may want to consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock to better safeguard your CPF savings.
You can easily activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock at any time online under Account Settings. Follow the three simple steps below.
Please visit the FAQ below to find out more on how to deactivate the CPF Withdrawal Lock:
How do I deactivate the CPF Withdrawal Lock?
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What is the cut-off date for self-employed MediSave contributions to be eligible for tax relief?
questions.text:
To be eligible for tax relief for the year, MediSave contributions made by self-employed persons must be credited to their CPF accounts by the last calendar day of the year.
MediSave contributions amounts made during the year will be automatically transmitted to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) for tax relief in the following year.
Please refer to this FAQ for more information on the tax eligibility of your contributions.
For more details on tax deductions, please visit the IRAS website or call the Individual Income Tax / Property Tax Helpline at 1800-356-8300.

questions.title: What is the Daily Withdrawal Limit for online withdrawals?
questions.text: The Daily Withdrawal Limit is a limit that all CPF members aged 55 and above can set to determine the maximum daily amount they can withdraw online. The current maximum Daily Withdrawal Limit for online withdrawals is $50,000. There is no change in the current withdrawal rules under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What is the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) is an online tool that helps you make informed decisions about your health insurance coverage in about 15 minutes. Through a four-step process, HIP will allow you to:
have personalised projections of your long-term MediSave savings and health insurance premiums;
compare benefits, features, and premiums across Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) for your preferred ward type; and
have long-term premium projections for your selected IP and its rider.
These features provide you with a consolidated view to better review and plan your healthcare coverage.
To use the HIP, members will need to prepare the name of their IP and rider, as well as the number of years left to pay for their CareShield Life and ElderShield Supplements, if applicable.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: What is the healthcare hotline?
questions.text:
For healthcare-related enquires, you may call us at 1800 222 3399* / 65 6222 3399 (overseas) from Mondays to Fridays, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8, excluding public holidays). Alternatively, you can also write to us.
* Airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: What is the MediSave Grant for Newborns?
questions.text:
The MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN) is a MediSave grant to help parents defray their child’s healthcare expenses, such as MediShield Life premiums, recommended childhood vaccinations, hospitalisation, and approved outpatient treatments.
All Singapore Citizen newborns born on or after 26 August 2012 are eligible. Those born on or after 26 August 2012, but before 1 January 2015 are eligible for a grant of $3,000. Those born on or after 1 January 2015, but before 1 April 2025 are eligible for the MGN of $4,000. Those born on or after 1 April 2025 are eligible for the MGN of $5,000.
A CPF MediSave account will be opened for each newborn, and the grant will be credited automatically to your newborn's MediSave account within a week from the registration of birth1, or from the date when Singapore Citizenship was granted2.
For more information on the MediSave Grant for Newborns, please visit madeforfamilies.gov.sg.
1 If your child is a Singapore Citizen at birth.
2 If your child is a Singapore Citizen by registration

questions.title: What is the MediSave Maternity Package?
questions.text: The MediSave Maternity Package is a package that allows MediSave to be used to pay expenses incurred during delivery and pre-delivery medical expenses such as consultations, ultrasounds, tests, medications etc.

questions.title: What is the net trade income used to compute my MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
Your MediSave contributions are computed based on your age and net trade income assessed by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). This refers to your gross trade income minus all allowable business expenses, capital allowances and trade losses as determined by IRAS.
From work year 2025, if you are also a platform worker, your MediSave contributions will be computed on your net trade income after excluding net earnings from your platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s). This is because CPF contributions on your net earnings from platform work are payable by your platform operator(s).
You can use the Self-Employed MediSave Contribution Calculator to calculate the amount of MediSave you need to contribute or use the MediSave contribution rates to derive your MediSave contribution amount for the respective work years.

questions.title: What is the status of my request to make self-employed MediSave contributions via monthly instalments?
questions.text:
We will keep you informed about the status of your request to make self-employed MediSave contributions via monthly instalments, once it has been processed.
Please note our normal processing time:
· Requests made via online appeal: generally 12 working days
· Manual transactions: generally 15 working days
You can check the status of your request by clicking on this link.
You can view your approved GIRO instalment plan details on the Self-employment dashboard. To access my cpf Digital Services – Self-employment dashboard, please log in to the CPF website using your Singpass.

questions.title: What is the voluntary top-up limit to my MediSave Account?
questions.text:
The maximum amount you can voluntarily top up to your MediSave Account is the difference between your Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) and your current MediSave balance. Once your BHS has been reached, no further voluntary top-ups can be made to your MediSave Account. If you exceed your BHS from the top-up, the full amount of your top-up will be refunded to your registered bank account in our records.
Please keep your bank account in Account settings up to date. If your bank account details are not updated, the refund will be made to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account by default.
You can check your top-up limit with these steps.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: What outpatient treatments can be paid using MediSave and what are the withdrawal limits?
questions.text: Please refer to the MOH website for the list of outpatient treatments that can be paid using MediSave and their corresponding withdrawal limits.

questions.title: What should I consider before buying a CareShield Life or ElderShield Supplement plan?
questions.text:
If you are covered under CareShield Life or ElderShield, consider whether the current benefits suit your long-term care preferences. If you wish to have additional coverage or benefits on top of the CareShield Life or ElderShield scheme, consider purchasing a Supplement plan. You can purchase CareShield Life supplement plans immediately upon enrolling in CareShield Life - there is no waiting period required.
You may refer to a comparison of Supplement plans offered by private insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance). For more information about Supplement plans, you may consider speaking to a financial advisor from one of the private insurers.

questions.title: What should I do if I need to withdraw more than the maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit?
questions.text: The Daily Withdrawal Limit only applies to online CPF lump sum withdrawals made under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above. If you need to withdraw an amount above the maximum Daily Withdrawal Limit of $50,000, you may consider doing so online over multiple days. Alternatively, you may also wish to consider booking an appointment (Select ‘Retirement Income’ then ‘Withdrawal above maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit’) to withdraw your preferred amount in person at CPF Service Centres. Generally, the next available appointment would be in a week’s time; subsequently, members will receive their withdrawn CPF savings in their bank account registered with us generally within five working days. To minimise any potential delay during the withdrawal process, we encourage members intending to make large withdrawals to plan in advance.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What should I do if I need to withdraw more than the online Daily Withdrawal Limit of $2,000?
questions.text: Withdrawal of more than $2,000 can be done by first adjusting the online Daily Withdrawal Limit to your desired amount, then wait for 12 hours for the higher limit to take effect. Find out more about this 12-hour cooling period.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What sources of MediSave contributions are eligible for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution?
questions.text:
MediSave contributions1 made by the taxi principal hirer to offset MediSave payable will qualify him for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution. CPF contributions received as an employee (from both employer and self) for taxi principal hirers who are concurrently employed, as well as government top-ups are excluded.
1 You may make MediSave contributions as a self-employed person via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.

questions.text:

questions.title: What type of CPF withdrawals does the online Daily Withdrawal Limit apply to and how do I change the online Daily Withdrawal Limit?
questions.text:
The Daily Withdrawal Limit applies to online CPF lump sum withdrawals made under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above.
A default online Daily Withdrawal Limit of $2,000 a day is applied to all CPF members aged 55 and above. You can adjust the online Daily Withdrawal Limit up to a maximum of $50,000, at any time under Account settings via Singpass authentication. Please note that any increase to the online Daily Withdrawal Limit will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period and may require enhanced authentication.
If you do not plan to withdraw soon, you may wish to consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock or lowering your Daily Withdrawal Limit to better safeguard your CPF savings.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What types of hospital charges can be covered by my MediSave?
questions.text: You can use your MediSave for your hospitalisation, surgery, and rehabilitation charges.

questions.title: What vaccinations can MediSave be used for?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for the following vaccinations received at any of the approved medical institutions in Singapore. Please refer to the list of approved medical institutions that provide these vaccinations.
For a list of MediSave-approved clinics under the MediSave500/700 scheme, please visit the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) webpage.

questions.title: When am I eligible to make a CareShield Life/ElderShield claim?
questions.text:
You are eligible to make a claim if you are covered under CareShield Life/ElderShield and have been assessed by an MOH accredited assessor as being unable to perform three or more of the following six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
Washing – the ability to wash in the bath or shower (including getting into and out of the bath or shower) or wash by other means
Dressing – the ability to put on, take off, secure and unfasten all garments and, as appropriate, any braces, artificial limbs or other surgical or medical appliances.
Feeding – the ability to feed oneself food after it has been prepared and made available.
Toileting – the ability to use the toilet or manage bowel and bladder function through the use of protective undergarments, such as diapers or surgical appliances if appropriate.
Moving or Walking Around – the ability to move indoors from room to room on level surfaces.
Transferring – the ability to move from a bed to an upright chair or wheelchair, and vice versa.

questions.title: When am I eligible to withdraw under MediSave Care?
questions.text:
You are eligible to withdraw under MediSave Care if you have been assessed by an MOH-accredited assessor as being unable to perform three or more of these six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
Washing – the ability to wash in the bath or shower (including getting into and out of the bath or shower) or wash by other means.
Dressing – the ability to put on, take off, secure and unfasten all garments and, as appropriate, any braces, artificial limbs or other surgical or medical appliances.
Feeding – the ability to feed oneself food after it has been prepared and made available.
Toileting – the ability to use the toilet or manage bowel and bladder function through the use of protective undergarments, such as diapers or surgical appliances, if appropriate.
Walking or Moving Around – the ability to move indoors from room to room on level surfaces.
Transferring – the ability to move from a bed to an upright chair or wheelchair, and vice versa.

questions.title: When is the deadline to make my MediSave contributions?
questions.text: Your MediSave contributions are due 30 days from the date of issuance of the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons from CPF Board.

questions.title: When will I receive my monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts?
questions.text: You can expect to receive your monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts by the middle of each month.

questions.title: When will I receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: If you are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) and have received cash top-ups in that year, you can expect to receive the matching grant in your MediSave Account at the beginning of the following year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.text:
The revised payouts and premiums under the CareShield Life 2025 Review will take effect from 1 January 2026.
Changes to other aspects of the scheme such as improvements in scheme administration will take place progressively.

questions.title: Where can I seek advice on financial planning for old age or seek financial assistance for long-term care needs?
questions.text:
For an overview of options for long-term care financing and services, you may visit this link.
To find out more about long-term care services, specific Government subsidies for long-term care services and other Government assistance schemes for long-term care that older Singaporeans (age 65 and above) may tap on, you may reach out to the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) through AIC website or 1800-650-6060. You can also speak to a Care Consultant at AIC Links located at the public hospitals and Maxwell. You may find the list of AIC Link locations via this link.
For Government support schemes specifically for younger Singaporeans with severe disability and their caregivers, you may refer to SGEnable website or speak to SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.
