questions.title: Which agencies will administer ElderShield?
questions.text: ElderShield will be jointly administered by the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC).

questions.title: Which organisations are responsible for administering the CareShield Life, ElderShield and MediSave Care schemes?
questions.text: CareShield Life, ElderShield and MediSave Care are jointly administered by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB).

questions.title: Who are the MOH-accredited severe disability assessors for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care and where can I find the list of assessors if I need to arrange an assessment?
questions.text:
MOH-accredited severe disability assessors are Singapore-registered doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses who have undergone a rigorous training programme to assess a patient’s level of disability.
You can find the list of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors on the AIC website if you need to arrange a CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care assessment.

questions.title: Who can make cash top-ups to recipients who are eligible to receive the matching grant under Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Anyone, including the member himself/herself, his/her loved ones, employers or members of the community, can help the eligible member receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme by making cash top-ups to the member’s MediSave Account.
For more information on how to make a cash top-up to MediSave Account, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Who can still enrol in CareShield Life after 1 January 2026?
questions.text:
After 1 January 2026, individuals born in 1979 or earlier can still enrol into CareShield Life if they do not have any pre-existing disabilities.
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later will continue to be automatically enrolled when they turn age 30.

questions.title: Who can use the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) is available to members aged 16 to 85. The minimum age of 16 is in line with the minimum age required by Singaporeans to access other CPF post-login e-services such as top-ups to MediSave. This also accounts for the fact that children below 16 are typically covered under their parents' health insurance plans and do not make independent coverage decisions.
The planner provides projections up to age 90, which is in line with the general life expectancy in Singapore, allowing for a more meaningful comparison for the majority of members.
The planner supports your financial planning needs across different life stages. As a young adult, you can evaluate insurance options while managing other financial commitments like education loans and home purchases. As your responsibilities change over time, you can continue using HIP to review your coverage needs and long-term affordability through to retirement.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Who is eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens who meet the following criteria will be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme for the year. Eligibility is automatically assessed annually. Eligible members will be notified by CPF Board at the beginning of the year. No application is needed to participate in the scheme.
AgeBetween 55 and 70 (inclusive) as of 31 December of the year
MediSave Account SavingsLess than 50% of the current Basic Healthcare Sum
Average Monthly IncomeNot more than $4,000
Annual Value of ResidenceNot more than $21,000
Property OwnershipOwn not more than one property
Self-Employed Persons onlyMust have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for MediSave payable
For more information on how to check my and my loved ones’ eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Who is responsible for reimbursing my MediSave Account for hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text: Third parties with a contractual obligation (e.g. your employer or insurer) are required to reimburse your MediSave Account for your hospitalisation expenses.

questions.title: Who should I approach at the nursing home should I need assistance with application for schemes to support long-term care costs?
questions.text: If you are in a nursing home, you may wish to consult a medical social worker (or equivalent) from the nursing home for financial counselling and assistance to apply for long-term care schemes.

questions.title: Why am I not allowed to make a withdrawal under MediSave Care to meet the long-term care needs of my parent/child?
questions.text:
With MediSave Care, the Government is allowing cash withdrawals from MediSave for the first time. Hence, we have decided to start with a more cautious approach. Currently, MediSave Care only allows the applicant to withdraw from his/her own MediSave, supplemented by his/her spouse’s MediSave, for his/her long-term care needs. As the period that individuals could remain in severe disability can vary significantly, the period of withdrawal and amount withdrawn can be substantial. When coupled with other existing withdrawals, allowing those with severe disability to tap on their children’s MediSave for withdrawals could potentially impact their children’s MediSave adequacy and compromise their ability to afford their own healthcare needs. Similarly, allowing MediSave Care withdrawals from the parents of those with severe disability could affect the elderly’s ability to afford their own medical expenses in old age.
Singapore Citizens who are in need in need of financial assistance and have low MediSave balances may apply for ElderFund. If you remain unable to pay for the costs of your long-term care needs, there are additional forms of assistance such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: Why am I not allowed to make MediSave Care withdrawals to cover my parent or children’s long-term care needs?
questions.text:
The duration of severe disability can vary significantly, potentially leading to substantial withdrawals over a long period. Allowing individuals with severe disability to tap into their parent or children’s MediSave for withdrawals could potentially impact their parent or children’s MediSave adequacy and compromise their ability to afford their own healthcare needs.
Singaporeans who need financial assistance and have low MediSave balances may apply for ElderFund. If they are still unable to afford their long-term care costs, additional assistance is available through schemes such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: Why am I receiving digital notifications instead of the hardcopy MediSave transaction statement to inform me of a deduction from my MediSave?
questions.text:
As part of our commitment to protect members against fraudulent deductions and to reduce environmental footprint, we have transitioned to digital notifications to inform you of your MediSave deduction for medical expenses. You will receive notifications via one of the following modes:
a. If your email address is registered with CPF Board, you will receive an email notification;
b. If you do not have an email address registered, but have a mobile number registered, you will receive an SMS notification.
If you have installed the CPF Mobile App and enabled push notifications, you will receive push notification alerts on your mobile phone as an additional notification.
These digital notifications will ensure that you are informed of any deductions made from your MediSave in a timely manner. If you wish to update your contact details, you may do so via the Account settings page on CPF website, after logging in with your Singpass.

questions.title: Why am I receiving notifications for CareShield Life and ElderShield through email/SMS or at a contact detail different from what I expected?
questions.text:
As part of our continuous efforts to improve our members’ experience, we have made changes to the notifications we send. These updates ensure better alignment with other notifications members receive from us.
Starting 24 November 2025, we are notifying members of their CareShield Life/ElderShield policy and payouts via email or SMS, using the contact details they have maintained with CPF Board.
You will receive notifications via one of the following modes:
a. If your email address is registered with CPF Board, you will receive an email notification;
b. If you do not have an email address registered with CPF Board, but have a mobile number registered, you will receive an SMS notification.
If you have installed the CPF Mobile App and enabled push notifications, you will receive push notification alerts on your mobile phone as an additional notification.
This transition to digital notifications will ensure you are promptly informed of any premium deductions made from your MediSave, as part of our commitment to protecting members against fraudulent deductions and reducing our environmental footprint.
If you wish to update your contact details, you may do so via the Account settings page on CPF website, after logging in with your Singpass.

questions.title: Why am I receiving notifications for MediSave Care through email/SMS or at a contact detail different from what I expected?
questions.text:
As part of our continuous efforts to improve our members’ experience, we have made changes to the notifications we send. These updates ensure better alignment with other notifications members receive from us.
Starting 24 November 2025, we are notifying members of their MediSave Care withdrawals via email or SMS, using the contact details they have maintained with CPF Board.
You will receive notifications via one of the following modes:
a. If your email address is registered with CPF Board, you will receive an email notification;
b. If you do not have an email address registered with CPF Board, but have a mobile number registered, you will receive an SMS notification.
If you have installed the CPF Mobile App and enabled push notifications, you will receive push notification alerts on your mobile phone as an additional notification.
This transition to digital notifications will ensure you are promptly informed of any MediSave Care withdrawals, as part of our commitment to protecting members against fraudulent withdrawals and reducing our environmental footprint.
If you wish to update your contact details, you may do so via the Account settings page on CPF website, after logging in with your Singpass.

questions.title: Why am I unable to undergo a severe disability assessment for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care at a hospital?
questions.text:
While you are undergoing treatment in the hospital, your disability status may change, and this may impact your long-term care scheme application. As such, we do not recommend the Patients to attend the severe disability assessment while hospitalised.
Our focus is to accredit healthcare professionals in the community, including the GPs, and clinicians in the long-term care sector to assess individuals’ level of disability when their condition has stabilised.

questions.title: Why am I unable to undergo a severe disability assessment for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care at a hospital?
questions.text:
While you are undergoing treatment in the hospital, your disability status may change, and this may impact your long-term care scheme application. As such, we do not recommend patients to attend the severe disability assessment while hospitalised.
Our focus is to accredit healthcare professionals in the community, including the GPs, and clinicians in the long-term care sector to assess individuals’ level of disability when their condition has stabilised.

questions.title: Why am I unable to undergo a severe disability assessment for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care during my hospitalisation?
questions.text:
While you are receiving treatment at the hospital, your disability condition may still be changing, which can affect the outcome of your long-term care scheme application. As such, severe disability assessments are not recommended while you are hospitalised.
Instead, our focus is on accrediting healthcare professionals in the community, such as the GPs, and clinicians within the long-term care sector who can assess your disability status once your condition has stabilised.

questions.title: Why are CPF transfers not eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is designed to encourage cash top-ups to senior Singapore Citizens with lower healthcare savings to help them save more. Thus, only cash top-ups to eligible members will be matched.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why are Government subsidies provided for CareShield Life and not for ElderShield?
questions.text:
Government subsidies are provided for CareShield Life as it is a mandatory scheme for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or after, unlike ElderShield which is optional.
While CareShield Life is also optional for those born before 1979, they would not be able to cancel their CareShield Life cover after 60 days free-look period. Premium subsidies are provided to help the lower- to middle-income households pay their CareShield Life premiums. On the other hand, ElderShield policyholders have the option to opt out or cancel their policy anytime.

questions.title: Why are mandatory MediSave contributions made by Self-Employed Persons that can be used to offset MediSave payable not counted towards the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Contributions made through the Manage your MediSave payable (MMSP) form are specifically designated to fulfil your mandatory MediSave contributions as a Self-Employed Person (SEP), which is a statutory requirement that must be met first.
The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is designed to encourage additional voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave beyond these mandatory obligations. Hence, any contributions made through the MMSP form will not count towards MMSS.
Only voluntary cash top-ups made via the Top up MediSave Account (VCMA) form will be considered for MMSS, provided that SEPs have met the other eligibility criteria for MMSS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why are Singaporeans not covered by CareShield Life from birth?
questions.text:
The priority of CareShield Life is to provide protection against severe disability during old age, when Singaporeans are most likely to need long-term care.
There are various support schemes available for families caring for their loved ones below age 30 who have severe disability, e.g. subsidies for early intervention programmes under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), and subsidies for therapy services at KK Hospital and the National University Hospital.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare can provide further assistance to Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.

questions.title: Why did CPF Board and MOH launch the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) is a joint initiative by CPF Board (CPFB) and Ministry of Health (MOH) under PLAN with CPF, our one-stop guidance service for financial and retirement planning.
Making decisions about health insurance coverage and comparing Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) can be challenging due to the complexity of information. As healthcare costs rise, members need to ensure their coverage matches both their care preferences and financial circumstances.
The HIP uses members' personal data to generate long-term projections of their MediSave savings, healthcare expenses, and insurance premiums. Working alongside existing information on MOH, CPFB and insurers' websites, the planner helps members make better-informed decisions about their health insurance coverage.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why did my GIRO monthly MediSave instalment amount change?
questions.text:
The monthly instalment amount for your self-employed MediSave contributions may change when there are changes to your outstanding MediSave contributions, which could be due to:
Assessment or reassessment of your net trade income by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore
Previous unsuccessful GIRO deductions
Refunds of MediSave contributions
Additional MediSave contributions made or received

questions.title: Why do I have to go through the quarterly survivorship check for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care?
questions.text: The quarterly survivorship check for an individual living overseas is to verify one’s continued eligibility for payouts under CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care. If you are required to undergo this check, Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will send you a letter with the review date and instructions on how to complete it.

questions.title: Why do I need to log in with my Singpass to access the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: Singpass login is required for the Health Insurance Planner to access your personal information, including your MediSave Account balance, MediShield Life and CareShield Life or ElderShield premiums, and details about your dependants. This information is needed to be used for projections. Through the Singpass login feature, the planner can also save your personalised inputs for future sessions, making it more convenient when you return.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why do I need to make MediSave contributions as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
You are required to make mandatory MediSave contributions as a self-employed person if you earn a total net trade income of more than $6,000.
These MediSave contributions helps you to build up savings for your healthcare needs, especially in the absence of regular MediSave contributions from an employer.

questions.title: Why do I need to set aside the MediSave balance of at least $5,000 to be eligible for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave is designed to help Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents set aside sufficient savings for their hospitalisation expenses and certain high-cost outpatient treatments such as cancer treatments.
The minimum balance of $5,000 required by MediSave Care ensures that individuals have MediSave available to cover medical expenses such as MediShield Life premiums or hospitalisations.

questions.title: Why do I need to update my contact details to adjust the online Daily Withdrawal Limit or make a CPF lump sum withdrawal?
questions.text: Notifications via SMS or email will be sent to you whenever there are adjustments to the online Daily Withdrawal Limit, or when you make a CPF lump sum withdrawal. As such, you will have to update your contact details under Account settings to receive these notifications. These notifications help provide immediate alerts and prevent any unauthorised adjustments or CPF lump sum withdrawals without your knowledge.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: Why do I still have outstanding MediSave payable when I am already on Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: Your Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions is an estimate of your MediSave payable for the year and may be lower or higher than your MediSave payable for the year. If your CAYE contributions are lower than your MediSave payable for the year, you’ll be required to top up the shortfall. You’ll also be required to make MediSave contributions for any outstanding MediSave payable incurred in previous years.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why do I still need to contribute to MediSave as a self-employed person even though I have already bought insurance for myself?
questions.text:
All working Singapore residents are required to contribute to their MediSave as a form of savings for their own and their loved ones’ healthcare needs.
Many Singaporeans have bought private hospital insurance plans in the form of Integrated Shield Plans, or IPs. IPs comprise of two parts – MediShield Life (MSL) which is a universal basic health insurance plan, and additional private insurance coverage. MediSave can be used to pay the premiums for both MSL and private insurance, up to the current withdrawal limit.
Hence, private medical insurance serves to complement rather than replace your MediSave savings.

questions.title: Why do I still need to contribute to MediSave even though I already have enough savings for my healthcare needs?
questions.text: With rising healthcare costs, it is important to have enough savings for your healthcare needs. Contributing regularly to MediSave will help you build up your savings over your working life. These savings can help you meet your own as well as your loved ones’ hospitalisation expenses under unforeseen circumstances.

questions.title: Why does cash withdrawal not apply to existing MediSave uses?
questions.text:
The Government allows for cash withdrawals under MediSave Care, also known as MediSave Withdrawals for Long-Term Care, out of recognition that long-term care needs vary significantly across individuals. Allowing cash withdrawals will provide patients and their caregivers the flexibility to decide on their desired care arrangements and long-term care services.
Other existing MediSave limits cater to well-defined care episodes and treatments. MediSave is hence intended to directly pay providers for the exact cost of treatment incurred, up to prevailing withdrawal limits.

questions.title: Why does CPF Board take self-employed persons to court for not contributing to their MediSave?
questions.text:
Self-employed persons (SEPs) are required under the CPF Act to contribute to their MediSave. This ensures that SEPs have enough MediSave savings for their healthcare needs, especially during old age when they have stopped working. SEPs without enough MediSave savings and MediShield Life cover may need to tap on other sources of funds such as their family members’ MediSave savings should they be hospitalised.
The CPF Board will continue to be flexible towards those with genuine financial difficulties. SEPs can request instalment plans to settle the outstanding amounts over a reasonable period. The CPF Board will only take recalcitrant defaulters to court as the last resort.

questions.title: Why does the CareShield Life claim threshold remain at severe disability?
questions.text:
Expanding CareShield Life coverage to those with milder forms of disability would require premiums to at least double, due to the longer claim duration and higher claim incidences for these individuals. As this would have come at the expense of premium affordability for more policyholders, the CareShield Life Council has recommended not to vary the scheme’s scope of coverage.
Importantly, the CareShield Life Council notes that those with mild/moderate disability can continue to access Government subsidies and grants that have been designed with them in mind. These include long-term care subsidies and grants such as Home Caregiving Grant that the Government will enhance progressively from 2026.
Those who wish for additional insurance coverage can also consider Supplements offered by private insurers.

questions.title: Why is CareShield Life universal coverage not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier?
questions.text:
CareShield Life universal coverage is not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier due to several reasons:
This is a diverse group - some may have previously opted out of ElderShield, or decided not to upgrade to ElderShield. Others could have bought Supplements or insurance plans.
They would face higher entry premiums as they have fewer years to spread their premium payment over.
The higher prevalence of severe disability in older cohorts make it challenging to maintain affordable premiums for everyone.
From 1 January 2026, those who are born in 1979 or earlier and have disability will not be able to join CareShield Life. The Government will assist them through:
Government subsidies
Other schemes like the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund
Tap on ElderFund and MediSave savings
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund, ComCare can also provide further assistance to Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.

questions.title: Why is CareShield Life/ElderShield necessary for Singaporeans' long-term care needs?
questions.text:
Growing need for long-term care
As Singapore's population ages, more people will need long-term care. As one ages, the risk of severe disability increases. The expected median duration for which individuals with severe disability remain in disability is around four years, but three in ten remain in severe disability for 10 years or more.
Savings alone may not be enough
It is increasingly challenging to rely only on personal and family savings to pay for your long-term care needs, as not only are family sizes shrinking, the duration of severe disability and the costs of long-term care will vary for each individual.
Managing the cost of long-term care with CareShield Life/ElderShield
Long-term care insurance schemes like CareShield Life and ElderShield help Singaporeans to pool their risks together within their cohort so that each Singaporean within that cohort has basic financial protection against the uncertainty and variability of the cost of long-term care. They complement other long-term care financing sources, such as Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support.

questions.title: Why is making MediSave contributions important for self-employed persons?
questions.text:
As a self-employed person, it is important to set aside a portion of your income to build up your MediSave savings. These savings can be used for your healthcare needs such as MediShield Life premiums or hospitalisation costs, helping to safeguard your healthcare expenses especially when you are older or no longer working.
If you are having difficulties making your MediSave contributions, you can request an instalment plan1 for your MediSave contributions via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
1Please note that your request is subject to the Board’s approval. You may be required to provide additional information or supporting documents, if necessary.

questions.title: Why is MediSave Care restricted to individuals aged 30 and above?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is not applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents below the age of 30 as they are significantly less likely to develop severe disability and need long-term care. They also tend to have lower MediSave balances based on employment history.
Those under the age of 30 who require assistance can tap on various support schemes such as subsidies for early intervention programmes under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), subsidies for therapy services at the KK Women's and Children's Hospital and National University Hospital, and means-tested Government assistance schemes such as the Home Caregiving Grant (HCG), in meeting their long-term care needs.
For Singaporeans who are unable to afford care even after receiving Government subsidies and support from other schemes, additional help is available through Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare.

questions.title: Why is MediSave Care restricted to those age 30 years and above?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is less applicable for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents below the age of 30 as they are significantly less likely to develop severe disability and need long-term care. They also tend to have lower MediSave balances based on employment history.
Those under the age of 30 who require assistance can tap on various support schemes such as subsidies for early intervention programmes under Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), and subsidies for therapy services at KK Women's and Children's Hospital and the National University Hospital, and means-tested Government assistance schemes such as the Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) in meeting their long-term care needs.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare can provide further assistance to Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.

questions.title: Why is my final MediSave deduction amount different from the amount provided to me before my hospital admission/in my care cost form?
questions.text:
The final MediSave deduction amount may differ from the estimated amount provided during financial counselling at the medical institution due to various reasons, such as changes to the treatment, longer than expected stay etc.
For clarifications on your final medical bill, please approach the medical institution where you received treatment at for assistance.

questions.title: Why is my voluntary cash top-up to my MediSave Account not updated in my healthcare dashboard under "Matching Grant Received This Year" for Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: Voluntary cash top-ups to your MediSave Account for Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) require up to three working days to be processed and reflected in your healthcare dashboard. If you have recently made a top-up, the system may not have updated your matching grant status yet. We recommend checking your account after this processing period. Please note that top-ups eligible for MMSS cannot be claimed for tax relief purposes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why is the Basic Healthcare Sum adjusted yearly?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is adjusted annually for cohorts below age 65 to ensure it remains relevant and keeps pace with rising healthcare consumption, especially with increasing healthcare costs and expansions in MediSave usage.
For each cohort, the BHS is fixed from age 65 onwards and remains the same for the rest of their lives. This helps members save adequately for their basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age, while providing certainty on the amount they need to set aside in their MediSave Account.

questions.title: Why is the ElderFund payout ($250) higher than the MediSave Care payout ($200)?
questions.text:
The MediSave Account can be used for a wide variety of costly medical treatments (e.g. hospitalisation expenses, selected outpatient treatments), and MediSave Care. A higher withdrawal amount for long-term care would result in a faster depletion of MediSave Account balances, which may affect an individual’s ability to pay for other medical expenses in the future.
Instead, MediSave Care complements insurance schemes such as CareShield Life/ElderShield/Supplement payouts, existing Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support and other personal savings and family support, to help individuals better meet their long-term care financing needs. In deciding the MediSave Care withdrawal amount, the Government took into account the basic long-term care costs for a range of services and settings, other sources of long-term care funding such as those mentioned before, as well as the need to balance withdrawal amounts with MediSave adequacy.
Meanwhile, ElderFund is targeted at helping lower-income Singaporeans who cannot benefit from CareShield Life or ElderShield and have low MediSave balances to draw on for their long-term care needs.

questions.title: Why is the ElderFund payout ($250) higher than the MediSave Care withdrawal amount ($200)?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is designed to complement insurance schemes such as CareShield Life/ElderShield/Supplement payouts, Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support, to help individuals better meet their long-term care financing needs. The Government determined the MediSave Care withdrawal amount by considering the basic long-term care costs across various services and settings, other available sources of long-term care funding, and the need to maintain MediSave adequacy.
In contrast, ElderFund is targeted at helping lower-income Singaporeans who are unable to benefit from CareShield Life or ElderShield and have low MediSave balances for their long-term care needs.
That explains why the ElderFund payout of $250 is higher than the MediSave Care withdrawal amount of $200.

questions.title: Why is the enrolment criterion being reinstated for CareShield Life application?
questions.text:
When CareShield Life was launched, older Singaporeans with less severe disability were allowed to join as a time-limited concession, so that more seniors could enrol in and benefit from CareShield Life.
However, this also meant that premiums for all older Singaporeans had to be priced higher, to account for the possibility that those with milder forms of disability were more likely to join the scheme.
This concession period lasted 4 years, over twice as long as what MOH had announced when the concession was rolled out. In this time, application rates have also decreased over time.
Thus, the CareShield Life Council views that this is an appropriate juncture to reinstate the underwriting criteria, which will moderate the extent of premium increases for all older policyholders, keeping the scheme fair and sustainable.

questions.title: Why is the maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit set at $50,000?
questions.text: Since the implementation of the default online Daily Withdrawal Limit of $2,000 in November 2023, the vast majority of CPF members have maintained an online Daily Withdrawal Limit of $50,000 or less. Hence, CPF Board lowered the maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit to $50,000 on 25 September 2024 to provide more friction against scams and introduce more time between transactions to prevent further losses, while still ensuring minimal inconvenience for the vast majority of members making legitimate withdrawals.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: Why is the Trusted Contact notified when the appointer updates their bank account, contact details or daily withdrawal limit?
questions.text:
Scammers may deceive victims into updating their bank account, contact details or daily withdrawal limit. They may also attempt to update this information if they obtain unauthorised access to the victims’ CPF accounts. Therefore, it is crucial for Trusted Contacts to be alerted when such transactions are made.
Learn more about scammers’ latest tactics and tips to help your loved ones safeguard themselves against scams.

questions.title: Why is the withdrawal amount for MediSave Care capped at $200 monthly (or $2,400 yearly)?
questions.text:
In deciding the MediSave Care withdrawal amount for long-term care, the Government took into account the basic long-term care costs for a range of services and settings, other sources of long-term care funding such as Government subsidies and assistance schemes, community support, personal savings, family support and Government-funded safety nets, as well as the need to balance withdrawal amounts with MediSave adequacy.
The Government will continue to regularly review the healthcare financing framework, including MediSave withdrawal limits, to ensure that basic long-term care costs remain affordable for Singaporeans.
For other forms of assistance in managing your long-term care costs, you may wish to apply for Government support schemes such as CareShield Life and ElderFund. If you are still unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, there are other forms of assistance such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: Why is the withdrawal quantum under MediSave Care based on my MediSave Account balance?
questions.text:
MediSave is used to cover a wide range of expenses, including health insurance premiums, hospitalisation, day surgery and outpatient bills such as chemotherapy and dialysis.
The withdrawal quantum under MediSave Care is carefully calibrated to ensure that Singaporeans have sufficient savings in their MediSave Account to meet their basic healthcare needs.

questions.title: Why is the withdrawal quantum under MediSave Care based on my MediSave account's balance?
questions.text:
The MediSave Account is used for healthcare purposes, such as paying for hospitalisation expenses, approved outpatient medical care and approved medical insurance premiums.
The Central Provident Fund (CPF) is a social security system that allows members to set aside savings for retirement. The Ordinary Account is for housing, insurance, investment and education purposes. The Special Account is for retirement income and retirement-related investments.

questions.title: Why is the withdrawal under MediSave Care restricted to my own and/or my spouse’s MediSave?
questions.text: The Government recognises and encourages family members to support one another in healthcare and long-term care. Hence, Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are already allowed to use immediate family members’ MediSave for hospital expenses and premium payments for MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield.

questions.title: Why is there a combined tax relief cap for top-ups to the Special Account/Retirement Account and MediSave Account from 1 January 2022?
questions.text:
The combined tax relief for cash top-ups to the Special/Retirement Account and MediSave Account (MA) was introduced for greater consistency across CPF schemes. This allows members to better understand and take action to benefit from these schemes.
The tax relief eligibility conditions for cash top-ups made before 1 January 2022 had differed1 for top-ups to retirement savings and top-ups to MA. With this change2, the tax relief eligibility conditions for cash top-ups made on or after 1 January 2022 across both schemes have been aligned.
1Before 1 January 2022, the tax relief eligibility conditions for cash top-ups differed between both scheme in terms of (i) tax beneficiary [giver for Retirement Sum Topping-Up (RSTU); recipient for Voluntary Contribution to MediSave Account (VCMA)]; and (ii) tax relief cap for top-ups to self/loved ones (capped at $7k/$7k for RSTU, tax relief cap for VCMA depended on both the Basic Healthcare Sum and the amount of mandatory CPF contributions for the year).
2The changes related to cash top-ups to MA do not apply to MA contributions made as a self-employed person (SEP). If you would like to make MA contributions as a SEP, visit the Self-Employed Scheme page for more information on topping up your MA.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why is there a need to double CareShield Life payout growth rate?
questions.text: CareShield Life works alongside other Government subsidies and grants to support long-term care costs. With rising long-term care costs, the enhancements in the payout growth rate are necessary to ensure that CareShield Life continues to meaningfully support the varied care needs of those with severe disability.

questions.title: Why is there a need to start CareShield Life earlier at age 30?
questions.text:
Starting CareShield Life at age 30 provides insureds with earlier coverage protection and allows them to spread premium payments over a longer period, hence reducing the annual premiums payable.
By age 30, most Singaporeans would have started working and contributing to their MediSave. They should be able to cover their CareShield Life premiums without out-of pocket expenses. Hence, this is a good time to start planning for their long-term care needs.

questions.title: Why is there no tax relief for top-ups to the MediSave Account made to my children or non-immediate family?
questions.text:
Tax relief is an incentive given to encourage members to build up their healthcare savings for themselves or their immediate family members, particularly older Singaporeans who may have less healthcare savings.
However, your children have longer remaining working lifespans and would have more time to build up their healthcare savings for their own healthcare needs. Hence, there is no tax relief for top-ups made to your children or non-immediate family members.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: Why must self-employed persons contribute to MediSave to receive Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.text:
A key principle of the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme is personal responsibility in saving for future needs, with the government providing supplementary support.
Self-employed persons (SEPs) are required to contribute to their MediSave Accounts because they do not receive employer contributions. Regular Medisave contributions help ensure they have enough savings for healthcare needs, especially in old age.
To qualify for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS), SEPs must contribute to MediSave as WIS is intended to supplement both income and CPF savings for long-term financial security.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why not allow insureds to choose from different CareShield Life plans depending on their ability to pay?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is intended to provide better protection for basic long-term care needs, when payouts are taken together with other long-term care financing sources.
If you wish to have additional coverage beyond what CareShield Life provides, you can consider purchasing Supplements from private insurers.

questions.title: Why was I notified of my MediSave deduction via a different notification mode before and after 12 June 2023?
questions.text:
As part of our continuous effort to enhance our members’ experience, we have made changes to the notifications we send. These changes were made to ensure alignment with other types of notifications that our members receive from us.
With effect from 12 June 2023, we have started notifying members of their MediSave deductions for medical expenses via email or SMS using their contact details maintained with CPF Board. You may verify that the notification is legitimate by checking that that the sender’s email address ends with @e.cpf.gov.sg, and the SMS sender ID is 'gov.sg'. The SMS will also begin with "Central Provident Fund Board".
If you have installed the CPF Mobile App and enabled push notifications, you will receive push notification alerts on your mobile phone as an additional notification.
We encourage you to keep your contact details updated so that you can receive timely notifications. You may update your mobile number and/or email address via the Account settings page on CPF website, after logging in with your Singpass. An SMS or email One-Time PIN (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile number or email address for verification before the changes take effect.

questions.title: Will ElderShield insurers continue selling Supplements?
questions.text: The ElderShield insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern Life & Income Insurance) will continue administering Supplements that complement the current ElderShield schemes.

questions.title: Will I be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme if I am turning 55 later this year?
questions.text:
Yes, you will be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) as long as you are 55 years old at the end of the assessment year and you meet the eligibility criteria.
You can check your eligibility for MMSS via Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Will I receive hospitalisation subsidies if I choose A ward type in public hospital or choose to go to a private hospital?
questions.text: You will not receive any hospitalisation subsidy in an A ward type in a public hospital or at a private hospital. Hence, if you are inclined to stay in an A ward in a public hospital or go to a private hospital for treatment, you should consider an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) that covers the cost for the particular ward/hospital type.

questions.title: Will I still receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme if my healthcare savings exceed 50% of the current Basic Healthcare Sum after topping up?
questions.text: Yes, you will receive the matching grant for the amount you received in cash top-up to your MediSave account as long as you are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) for the year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Will my MediSave Care withdrawal limit automatically change as and when my MediSave balance changes?
questions.text:
The monthly cash withdrawal quantum is based on your MediSave balance, or the maximum withdrawal amount that you set when applying for MediSave Care (whichever is lower).
MediSave Balances and corresponding Monthly Withdrawal Quantum
MediSave Balance
Monthly Withdrawal Quantum

If you have received voluntary cash contribution from family members or Government top-ups, and the MediSave balance is in the higher tier once again, your corresponding withdrawal quantum will automatically increase.

questions.title: Will my MediSave Care withdrawal limit automatically change as and when my MediSave balance changes?
questions.text:

MediSave BalanceMonthly Withdrawal Quantum
$20,000 and above$200

questions.title: Will platform operators need to make additional deductions for platform workers with outstanding MediSave liability from past years?
questions.text: No, platform operators will not deduct the outstanding CPF contributions that platform workers have incurred as self-employed persons for work done in past years. Platform workers who have difficulties making these outstanding MediSave contributions can approach CPFB to arrange affordable instalment plans.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: Will the estimated income that I provided for the computation of my Contribute As You Earn contribution rate be used as the income to compute my MediSave payable?
questions.text:
The estimated income information you provided via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services is only used to compute the CAYE contribution rate. It will not be used as your actual income to compute your MediSave payable for the year.
You will still need to declare your actual net trade income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) in the following year. Your MediSave payable for the year will then be computed based on your NTI1.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why can't I find my Healthier SG clinic of choice? What do I do if my existing General Practitioner (GP) is not a Healthier SG clinic?
questions.text:
For Healthier SG, residents can enrol only with a clinic that is participating in Healthier SG. GP clinics that are not Healthier SG will not be available for selection.
As you will need to enrol with a Healthier SG GP clinic to access Healthier SG benefits, you are strongly encouraged to choose from the list of Healthier SG clinics in HealthHub.
You may continue to visit non-Healthier SG clinics even after your enrolment. However, Healthier SG benefits will not be applicable at clinics that you are not enrolled with, so you would only be able to enjoy the existing schemes such as CHAS and MediSave.
If your current GP is not on Healthier SG, you could also encourage your GP to onboard Healthier SG.

questions.title: Do I need to be a Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) cardholder to enjoy the Healthier SG Chronic Tier under Healthier SG from 2024?
questions.text:
You will need to be a CHAS/ Pioneer Generation (PG)/ Merdeka Generation (MG) cardholder and be enrolled with a Healthier SG GP clinic to be eligible for the Healthier SG Chronic Tier. In this tier, CHAS/PG/MG cardholders with high medication needs, can access subsidies for selected common chronic medications* at prices comparable to polyclinics. You or your household members can sign up at www.chas.sg.
Healthier SG benefits are available/ accessible at your enrolled Healthier SG Clinic.
*Additional subsides for Medication Assistance Fund (MAF) medications on the Healthier SG Medication List are available only for CHAS Blue and CHAS Orange cardholders (including PG/MG cardholders who also hold a CHAS Blue/Orange card).

questions.title: Where is the Healthier SG Enrolment Station nearest to me? How can I check if my GP / polyclinic is participating in Healthier SG?
questions.text: You may check for your nearest Healthier SG Enrolment Station and the list of participating clinics at https://gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg . Simply enter your postal code or name of clinic to search.

questions.title: Who is eligible to receive fully-subsidised COVID-19 vaccinations under the National Vaccination Programme?
questions.text:
The following groups of residents and pass holders are eligible to receive fully-subsidised COVID-19 vaccinations under the National Vaccination Programme:
• Singapore Citizen
• Permanent Resident
• Employment Pass
• S-Pass
• Work Permit holders (including Confinement Nannies)
• Student’s Pass
• Dependant’s Pass
• MFA-issued IDs
• Long Term Visit Pass (and LTVP+)
• Training Employment Pass
• Training Work Permit
• Work Holiday Pass

Holders of Training Employment Pass, Training Work Permit, Work Holiday Pass, Special Pass and Short-Term Visit Pass with a pass validity period of at least 60 days may call a participating General Practitioner (GP) clinic to book an appointment. The pass holder should bring along identification documents such as a passport or approval of extension of stay in Singapore for verification purposes.

questions.title: I would like to appeal for the Merdeka Generation Package. Can I do so, and how?
questions.text:
Citizens aged 60 years and above in 2019 (i.e. born on or earlier than 1959) who became Singapore citizens after 31 December 1996, but have good claims to be counted among the MG, can appeal for the MGP.
Similar to the Pioneer Generation Package, the Appeals Panel will not consider appeals from those who miss out on the age criterion (i.e. born after 31 December 1959 in this case).
You can send your appeals to contactus@merdeka.gov.sg or call 1800 2222 888. You can also mail to Robinson Road P.O. Box 3060 Singapore 905060.

questions.title: How can I apply? (CHAS)
questions.text:
You can apply for CHAS via the online application by using this link.
Alternatively, you can also pick up a CHAS application form at any Community Centre or Club (CC), Community Development Council (CDC), Public Hospital or Polyclinic or download the application form by using this link . Please send the completed and signed application form to Privy Box No. 920231, Singapore 929292.
If anyone in your household is not a Singapore Citizen, please also include copies of their foreign identification documents (e.g. work permit/long term visit pass).
If your application is successful, all eligible members of your household will receive an individual CHAS card in their name. The card indicates the subsidy tier you qualify for (CHAS Blue or Orange or Green) and is valid for two years. Simply present the card at a CHAS GP or dental clinic when seeking treatment. PG and MG cardholders can use their PG or MG card at any CHAS clinic to obtain CHAS subsidies. You will receive an itemised bill for your treatment.
If this is your first visit to a CHAS GP, please also present your NRIC upon registration (or birth certificate for cardholders under 15 years old).
By using your CHAS or Pioneer Generation or Merdeka Generation card at a CHAS clinic, you consent to allow your doctor/dentist to disclose your personal information to the Ministry of Health (including its authorised agents).

questions.title: Where can I access subsidised referrals to public specialist outpatient clinics (SOCs)?
questions.text:
Eligible individuals can access subsidised referrals to public specialist outpatient clinics (SOCs) regardless of their Healthier SG enrolment status, as follows:
Singapore Citizens: You can get subsidised referrals at polyclinics. If you hold a CHAS, Merdeka Generation (MG), or Pioneer Generation (PG) card, you can also get subsidised referrals at CHAS clinics.
Permanent Residents: You can get subsidised referrals at polyclinics.
Enrolment in Healthier SG is not required for subsidised referrals.

questions.title: How can I get a referral for subsidised care at public SOCs?
questions.text: A referral for subsidised care at public SOCs can be obtained from either CHAS clinics or polyclinics. Do note that you will need to be a PG/MG/CHAS cardholder to obtain subsidised SOC referrals from CHAS clinics.

questions.title: I would like to appeal for the Pioneer Generation Package. can I do so, and how?
questions.text:
The Appeals Panel was set up in May 2014 and has carefully considered the criteria for assessing appeals.
If you were born after 31 Dec 1949, please note that no appeals will be received. As explained in response to queries in Parliament and during the debate on the Pioneer Generation Fund Bill, the Appeals Panel recognised that the Government had already adopted a more inclusive approach by extending the Pioneer Generation Package to all those born in 1949 or earlier. Whatever the age set, there will always be those who marginally fall short of it. It would therefore not be feasible or fair to allow age-related appeals without extending the new age criterion to all Singaporeans. Hence, as provided under the Pioneer Generation Fund Act, the Panel decided that it would only consider appeals relating to the citizenship criterion.
For citizenship-related appeals, the Panel considers whether the person had obtained Singapore citizenship shortly after 1986 – the year set as the citizenship cut-off date for eligibility of the Pioneer Generation Package. In addition, it looks at factors such as whether he or she had been in Singapore since the early years of independence, contributed to our society, and had demonstrated clear efforts to sink roots in Singapore.
If you marginally missed the citizenship date of 31 Dec 1986 and you feel that you meet the criteria, please contact us at 1800-2222-888 or contactus@pioneers.gov.sg with your NRIC number to file an appeal. If you would like to appeal on behalf of a relative, please obtain your relative's consent first.

questions.title: Are there provisions to prevent a licensee from using names of MOH's related agencies in their advertisement? For example, can licensees use terms like “MOH’s Healthier SG” or "HSA's XXXX Program" when advertising their healthcare services?
questions.text:
HCSA does not govern the use of names of MOH’s related agencies in advertising. However, this will be controlled by the agencies whose programs the services purport to be a part of. Licensees will need to comply with the rules stipulated for the respective programs.
In general, licensees should ensure that their advertisements are factual and not deemed to be misleading to the general public and comply with all the requirements under Healthcare Services (Advertisement) Regulations.

questions.title: Are we eligible for higher subsidies if I/my family member am/is placed in a nursing home with higher fees?
questions.text:
For individuals who require nursing home care, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will work closely with the individual and family members to identify a suitable nursing home, taking into account the individual's needs and family's preferences, including financial considerations.
The Government provides subsidies to help with the costs of long-term care. The amount of subsidies each individual is eligible for is determined by means-testing and is not dependent on the fees charged by the nursing homes. Individuals from lower income households who meet the eligibility criteria will receive higher subsidies under the means-testing framework.
If you require additional assistance, you can tap on financial assistance schemes such as MediFund. Many nursing homes are also run by voluntary welfare organisations, and they may tap on charitable donations to provide further financial support to their residents after all other means of financial assistance and resources are exhausted.
topics: CareShield Life / Financing My Long-Term Care Needs

questions.title: Can a licensee advertise government programmes such as CHAS schemes, health screenings and vaccinations?
questions.text: Licensees are allowed to advertise government programmes if the substantive content comprises factual information about or relating to the healthcare services provided by a licensee, where the healthcare service is provided in relation to a programme that is funded (in whole or in part), initiated or endorsed by the Government or the Health Promotion Board.

questions.title: How is ElderFund different from Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE) and Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PG-DAS)?
questions.text:
Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE) and Pioneer Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS) are disability assistance schemes restricted to smaller cohorts of older Singaporeans. ElderFund provides wider coverage, and is targeted at assisting lower-income Singapore Citizens above the age of 30 who are unable to benefit from CareShield Life, ElderShield and IDAPE, and have insufficient MediSave balances to support their basic long-term care needs.
IDAPE was introduced in 2002 to benefit seniors who were not eligible for ElderShield at the time because they were aged 70 and above (born on/or before 30 September 1932) or had pre-existing disabilities. It provides $250 per month or $150 per month, depending on applicant's per capita household income, for a maximum of 6 years.
PioneerDAS is part of the Pioneer Generation package, and provides $100 per month for all Pioneers with moderate disability. There is no cap on the duration of payouts as long as they meet the eligibility criteria.

questions.title: Why is my clinic no longer a Healthier SG Clinic?
questions.text:

You are encouraged to continue your Healthier SG journey by enrolling to a new preferred Healthier SG clinic via HealthHub. If you need assistance with enrolment, you may approach a nearby Healthier SG Enrolment Station, a participating clinic at https://gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg. questions.title: Can I take a vaccination if I am currently unwell, such as having the flu?
questions.text:
It is generally recommended to postpone vaccinations if you are experiencing moderate to severe illness, such as a high fever or significant flu symptoms. However, if your symptoms are mild, you may still be able to take the vaccination.
To ensure your safety, consult your doctor or healthcare provider for advice tailored to your specific health condition before proceeding with the vaccination.

questions.title: I am receiving other disability assistance schemes such as Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme/Home Caregiving Grant. Can I qualify for CareShield claims?
questions.text:
Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS) and Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) are moderate disability schemes, where the individual only needs to always require some assistance with three or more Activities of Daily Living. CareShield Life and ElderShield are severe disability schemes, where the individual needs to be unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (i.e. require significant assistance) in order to make a claim.
As the eligibility criteria for CareShield Life and ElderShield are stricter, insureds who are eligible for CareShield Life/ElderShield claims can automatically receive PioneerDAS or HCG payouts without going for a separate assessment (subject to meeting the other non-disability eligibility criteria for these schemes).

questions.title: If vaccination is needed, are the vaccinations subsidised by MOH? If not, will the personnel be eligible for the National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS) subsidy for the measles and diphtheria vaccination?
questions.text: All Singapore Citizens (SCs) and Permanent Residents (PRs) for whom vaccination is recommended under the NAIS are eligible for subsidies for the relevant vaccinations. Under the NAIS, measles vaccination (as part of the Measles Mumps and Rubella vaccine) is recommended for adults who have not been previously vaccinated, or lack evidence of past infection or immunity, while Tdap is recommended for pregnant women during 16-32 weeks of each pregnancy. Licensees may also further subsidise the remaining cost of vaccinations for personnel, at their discretion.

questions.title: Is GPFirst applicable to CHAS patients, even though they have already received subsidised care at GP clinics?
questions.text: The subsidy under GPFirst will apply to patients, as long as they are referred to the emergency department by participating clinics with the original GPFirst Referral Form. This includes patients under CHAS.

questions.title: What are the common side effects for PCV20?
questions.text: The vaccine has been assessed to be safe for use. However, similar to other vaccines, individuals may experience common side effects which include injection site reactions (e.g., pain, redness, swelling), headache, body aches, fatigue and fever. While most side effects are mild or moderate and usually resolve within a few days, individuals should consult a doctor if the side effects persist or worsen.

questions.title: Why is the Merdeka Generation Package only extended to those born in the 1950s?
questions.text:
Compared to younger cohorts, the MG had fewer opportunities and lower wages, and they were less able to save up for their healthcare needs. The MGP provides additional support to this group, who are reaching their retirement years.
Younger cohorts of Singaporeans would have benefitted more from the schemes introduced over the years (e.g. MediSave in 1984), and are in a better position to look after their own healthcare needs. At the same time, we recognise that some will still need more help. The Government continues to provide substantial support through permanent healthcare schemes, to ensure that healthcare remains affordable for all.

questions.title: Will patients referred by polyclinics enjoy the GPFirst subsidy?
questions.text: GPFirst applies to General Practitioners participating under the programme, and does not include referrals from polyclinics. Patients referred by polyclinics will continue to be given priority at the emergency department.

questions.title: Are licensees allowed to advertise their business and services under MOH’s Healthier SG initiative?
questions.text:
Only licensees who are Healthier SG-registered providers can use the Healthier SG brand. Eligible licensees who would like to use the “Healthier SG” brand, which includes the name and logo (and its variations), would have to abide by the Healthier SG Brand Guidelines and submit a request to MOH for the use of the Healthier SG brand at https://www.healthiersg.gov.sg/resources/on-healthier-sg/brandguidelines/
Examples of products, services, businesses, events, treatment that cannot be used in conjunction with the Healthier SG brand include:
a) Companies/ products that make non-evidence based health claims, and/or sell unhealthy or unregulated products b) Vaccination and screenings that are outside of the list of nationallyrecommended vaccination/ screenings
c) Medical and aesthetics devices
d) Cosmetic/slimming services and products (e.g., facials, aesthetics treatments, massages)
e) IT systems or software for usage by hospitals and clinics that are not related to, or not supporting Healthier SG
The above listing is non-exhaustive.

questions.title: Are the requirements under HCSA and its subsidiary legislations applicable to local licensees who provide healthcare services overseas?
questions.text:
HCSA applies to local or foreign entities providing licensable healthcare services in Singapore. HCSA does not have extra-territorial reach. Local entities providing licensable healthcare services overseas are reminded to comply with the legislations in the foreign country.
Similarly, the provision of licensable healthcare services by foreign entities to local patients who travel overseas will also be outside the jurisdiction of HCSA.

questions.title: Can clinics refer patients to purchase items from a co-located retail pharmacy? Does this constitute a breach under the HCS (Advertisement) Regulations?
questions.text: The HCS (Advertisement) Regulations do not regulate such referrals as they are not advertisements. However, as stipulated in the HCS General Regulations, patients should not be compelled to patronise the co-located retail pharmacy as a pre-requisite for treatment.

questions.title: Can I apply for Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) if my loved one is unable to provide consent for the application due to e.g. lack of mental capacity or below 21 years old?
questions.text:
Yes.
For care recipient who lacks mental capacity
Care recipent’s donee/deputy# may provide consent on the care recipient’s behalf. If the care recipient does not have such a donee/deputy, the caregiver* may make the application on care recipient’s behalf.
# Donee/deputy must be appointed in accordance with the Mental Capacity Act (Cap 177) and is authorised to make decisions on behalf of the care recipient in relation to the care recipient’s property and affairs.
* For successful applications without a donee/deputy, the caregiver or another family member has 12 months to obtain a court order appointing him/her as a deputy, failing which the payouts will be suspended. For more information on how to apply for a deputyship, please visit SG Courts Website.
Doctor’s certification for mental incapacity is only valid for six months, unless stated permanent.
You will also need to submit the following additional supporting documents:
Doctor’s certification that the care recipient lacks mental capacity OR court order of deputy appointment OR recent medical report stating that the care recipient lacks mental capacity; and
Copy of bank book or statement IF you are nominating an account belonging to a deputy or trustee of the care recipient.
For care recipient below age of 21 years old
The care recipient’s parent or legal guardian^ may make this application on behalf of the care recipient.
^ Legal guardian refers to a person who has been lawfully appointed in accordance with the Guardianship of Infants Act (Cap. 122).
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

CareShield Life Supplements are products by private insurers who set the underwriting decisions based on commercial and actuarial considerations.
You may refer here for a comparison of Supplement plans offered by private insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance). You may also wish to speak to a financial advisor from one of the private insurers who can share more about their Supplement plans with you.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to purchase a short-lease 2-room Flexi Flat?
questions.text: You must first set aside your Basic Retirement Sum in your CPF accounts before you can use any excess Ordinary Account savings to purchase a short-lease-2-room Flexi Flat. This ensures that you have a monthly income to support a basic standard of living during your retirement.

questions.title: Can more than one caregiver tap on the grant to attend the same training programme?

questions.title: Do I need a valuation report to use my CPF savings for property purchase if I am not taking a loan?
questions.text:
Yes, a valuation report is mandatory when using CPF savings for property purchase, regardless of whether you are taking a loan. This report determines the maximum amount of CPF savings you can use for your property purchase.
For HDB flats: Only HDB's valuation will be accepted, and it must be dated within three months from your application date.
For private properties: The valuation report must be:
Conducted by a licensed valuer, which can be your bank’s valuer
Dated within three months from your property purchase date

questions.title: How are Healthier SG vaccinations selected for inclusion under NAIS?
questions.text:
Healthier SG vaccinations listed under NAIS are selected based on recommendations by the Drug Advisory Committee and Expert Committee on Immunisation which takes into consideration public health needs, local disease burden, vaccine efficacy and safety and cost-effectiveness. If the vaccine effectively prevents vaccinated individuals from infection or minimises complications if infected and is found to be cost-effective for its intended target population, the vaccine will be considered for inclusion under the NAIS.
MOH, in consultation with the Expert Committee on Immunisation, also monitors newly registered vaccines or those in the development pipeline to assess their relevance for Singapore, taking reference from international guidelines.

questions.title: How do I know how much subsidies I will receive for the long-term care service(s) that I use? How do I know how much subsidies I will receive for the long-term care service(s) that I use?
questions.text: Qualified healthcare professionals, medical social workers and/or administrative staff at public hospitals and/or Government-funded long-term care service providers can assist with your application for Government subsidies for long-term care services, and advise on the subsidy quantum you are eligible for.

questions.title: How do I know if the merchants allow me to make purchases using my GovCash?
questions.text: You can only make purchases using GovCash at merchants that accept PayNow/NETS QR code using the LifeSG app. You can look out for the PayNow/NETS logo on the SG QR label that is displayed by the merchants.

questions.title: How does Active Ageing Centres (AACs) play a part in Healthier SG?
questions.text:
As part of the Healthier SG initiative, AACs deliver the 2S (Social Connector for Social and Lifestyle Interventions, and Community Screening) which aims to empower Seniors towards healthy and active lifestyles.
As a Social Connector for Social and Lifestyle Interventions, AACs assist Seniors to join relevant active ageing programmes as recommended in their Healthier SG health plan.
AACs also serve as a community node for Community Screening, such as vitals screening and functional screening.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: How does the Home Purchase Planner compute my budget?
questions.text:
The Home Purchase Planner helps you compute a home purchase budget by considering:
your Ordinary Account (OA) balance, cash savings and cash proceeds (if you sell an existing property); and
key financial parameters (e.g. Mortgage Servicing Ratio, loan tenure, and Loan-To-Value limit). See assumptions via this link.
The calculated budget provides a conservative estimate that helps you buy a home within your means. Here is an example:
John has:
$50,000 in his OA
$30,000 in cash
Based on his profile, John qualifies for a maximum housing loan of $400,000. With a loan-to-value limit of 75%, he technically has a budget of $532,000.
However, John’s actual budget is lower because:
He needs to make a minimum downpayment of 25%.
Assuming John uses his capital consisting of OA savings and cash of $80,000 for his downpayment, the maximum he can afford is $320,000. This is based on a loan of $240,000 covering the remaining 75% of the property price.
Therefore, the planner shows John’s purchase budget as $320,000, ensuring he buys a property within his financial means.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Home Purchase Planner

questions.title: How does the Home Purchase Planner determine the impact of my home purchase on my future retirement payouts?
questions.text:
The Home Purchase Planner (HPP) determines the impact of your home purchase on your future retirement payouts by considering:
your retirement goal – the monthly payout you need at age 65 to support your retirement lifestyle, after factoring in inflation
your retirement savings – the amount of CPF savings you are projected to have at age 65, after paying for your property (e.g. downpayment, monthly instalments)
If your retirement savings at age 65 fall short of what is needed to meet your retirement goal after factoring the estimated purchase budget, you should consider:
using less CPF savings and more cash to service your monthly instalments where possible
buying a more affordable property
boosting your retirement savings by making cash top-ups or CPF transfers.
The HPP also allows you to see the impact of using less CPF savings for your monthly housing instalments on your retirement savings.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Home Purchase Planner

questions.title: How is income calculated for Student Care Financial Assistance (SCFA) subsidy?
questions.text:
For salaried employees:
Based on average gross monthly income derived from the CPF contributions made over the last 12 months or the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 calendar years).Includes: basic salary, bonuses, commissions, overtime pay, allowances, cash rewards, and employee CPF contributions.
For self-employed individuals:
Based on average trade income over 12 months from the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 calendar years), or income declared to CPF Board.

questions.title: How much CPF savings can I use for my property purchase?
questions.text:
The amount of CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings you can use depends on:
Remaining lease of the property
Type of property
Loan type
Whether it’s your first or subsequent property
Note: For members age 55 and above, your Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) is half of your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) which depends on the year you turn 55 and will remain the same for life. For members below 55, your BRS is half of the prevailing FRS in the year.
You can use our CPF Housing Usage Calculator to determine the total amount of CPF savings that you and your co-owner (if any) may use to buy your property.
Purchasing your second or subsequent property
You can only use your OA savings after setting aside the BRS or FRS (refer to Table B), up to the CPF housing limit of your property.
Table B: Amount to set aside
Property OwnershipAmount to set aside
