questions.text:
The launch of CareShield life will not affect your existing ElderShield and supplement plans.
However, you are encouraged to consider upgrading your ElderShield to CareShield Life if you do not have severe disability. If you choose to upgrade to CareShield Life, the ElderShield premiums that you have paid will be taken into account when computing your CareShield Life premiums, resulting in lower CareShield Life premiums.
The Supplements will also work with CareShield Life cover and do not need to be terminated.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: When will the Government take over the administration of ElderShield?
questions.text: The Government has taken over the administration of ElderShield from 1 November 2021.
topics: ElderShield / Government Administration of ElderShield in 2021

questions.title: Where can I find the list of accredited assessors for ElderFund?
questions.text: The lists of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors can be found at the AIC’s website.

questions.title: Where can I get more information about disability support and resources?
questions.text: Visit SG Enable’s Enabling Guide, an online resource for persons with disabilities and their caregivers, as well as professionals looking for disability support.

questions.title: Where can I seek advice on financial planning for old age or seek financial assistance for long term care needs?
questions.text:
For an overview of options for long term care financing and services, you may visit the CareShield Life website (under “Long-Term Care Financing”) for more information.
If you wish to find out more about long term care services, specific Government subsidies for long-term care services and other Government assistance schemes for long term care that older Singaporeans (age 65 and above) may tap on, you may reach out to the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) through the AIC website or 1800-650-6060. You can also speak to a Care Consultant at AIC Links located at the public hospitals and Maxwell. For a list of AIC Link locations, visit the AIC website.
For Government support schemes specifically for younger Singaporeans with severe disability and their caregivers (age 65 and below), you may refer to the website here or speak to SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.
For more information on retirement planning, Singaporeans can visit the following websites:
•CPF website to learn about CPF schemes.
•Are You Ready? outreach website to understand how CPF savings can support Singaporeans through the key stages of their life and learn how they can work towards a better retirement.
topics: CareShield Life / Financing My Long-Term Care Needs

questions.title: Which agencies will administer ElderShield?
questions.text: ElderShield will be jointly administered by the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC).
topics: ElderShield / Government Administration of ElderShield in 2021

questions.title: Who administers ElderFund?
questions.text: The Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) administers ElderFund.

questions.title: Who are the members of the CareShield Life council?
questions.text: The CareShield Life Council has been appointed on 1 April 2020 and has 14 members from a variety of disciplines (e.g. actuaries, investment/finance expertise, accounting/auditor, doctor, law, medical social worker, and union/grassroots).
topics: CareShield Life / Government Administration and Independent Council

questions.title: Who can still enroll in CareShield Life after 1 January 2026?
questions.text:
After 1 January 2026, individuals born in 1979 or earlier can still enrol into CareShield Life if they do not have any pre-existing disabilities.
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later will continue to be automatically enrolled when they turn age 30.

questions.title: Who should I approach at the nursing home should I need assistance with application for schemes to support long-term care costs?
questions.text: If you are in a nursing home, you may wish to consult a medical social worker (or equivalent) from the nursing home for financial counselling and assistance to apply for long-term care schemes.

questions.title: Who’s covered under CareShield Life?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible to join, but when you can join depends on the year you were born.
Born in 1980 or after
Automatically covered once you turn 30
You’re automatically covered once you turn 30, or from 1 October 2020, whichever is later, regardless of any pre-existing medical conditions and/or disability.
If you were born in 1990 or later, we’ll write to you with more information about two months before your 30th birthday.
Born in 1979 or earlier
Optional participation
Your participation in CareShield Life is optional^.
If you were born between 1970 and 1979, insured under ElderShield 400, and have not developed severe disability, you had been automatically enrolled into CareShield Life from 1 December 2021. No action is required if you wish to join CareShield Life.
If you were not automatically enrolled and wish to join CareShield Life, you may access the Application to join CareShield Life e-Service with your Singpass and enjoy a 60-day free-look period.
Apply for CareShield Life
^ Except foreigners who become Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards, for whom participation is mandatory, provided they do not have severe disability (if granted residency status from 1 October 2020 to 31 December 2025) or any disability (if granted residency status from 1 January 2026 onwards).
Click here for more information on CareShield Life.

questions.title: Why am I not able to receive claims disbursements via cheque under Government administration?
questions.text:
As part of the Government’s efforts to go paperless and safeguard the payments process, the Government encourages you to nominate a bank account for interbank GIRO payments.
To nominate a bank account, please log in to Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS) portal at https://efinance.aic.sg using your Singpass.
topics: ElderShield / Government Administration of ElderShield in 2021

questions.title: Why are Singaporeans not covered by CareShield Life from birth?
questions.text:
The priority of CareShield Life is to provide protection against severe disability during old age, when Singaporeans are most likely to need long-term care.
There are various support schemes for families who need support for their loved ones who are younger than the starting age (of 30) for CareShield Life but have developed severe disability, e.g. subsidies for early intervention programmes under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), and subsidies for therapy services at KK Hospital and the National University Hospital.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare can provide further assistance to Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: Why call the enhanced scheme “CareShield Life”?
questions.text:
The new name, CareShield Life will better signal the intent of the scheme to provide protection for long-term care.
The current ElderShield scheme will continue to be known as “ElderShield”.
topics: CareShield Life / Government Administration and Independent Council

questions.title: Why do I have to go through the quarterly survivorship check?
questions.text: The quarterly survivorship check for an individual living overseas is to verify one’s continued eligibility for payouts. If you are required to undergo quarterly survivorship check, AIC will send you a letter to inform you when the review is required. Details on how to complete the quarterly survivorship check are included in the letter.

questions.title: Why does CareShield Life Team refer my case to another organisation?
questions.text:
CareShield Life Team is committed to providing the best possible assistance to those in need. To make sure you get the right kind of support, we’ll look at your situation and assess whether there are other organisation(s) with more appropriate assistance tailored to your needs. If the situation warrants, we will refer your case to our partner organisation(s) that have the right assistance programme(s) and expertise to better assist you. Please inform us explicitly if you do not want us to refer your case to our partner organisation(s).
CareShield Life Team is committed in ensuring your data is protected. You may refer to our privacy statement for more details.

questions.title: Why does the CareShield Life claim threshold remain at severe disability?
questions.text:
Expanding CareShield Life coverage to those with milder forms of disability would require premiums to at least double, due to the longer claim duration and higher claim incidences for these individuals. As this would have come at the expense of premium affordability for more policyholders, the CareShield Life Council has recommended not to vary the scheme’s scope of coverage.
Importantly, the CareShield Life Council notes that those with mild or moderate disability can continue to access Government subsidies and grants that have been designed with them in mind. These include long-term care subsidies and grants such as Home Caregiving Grant that the Government will enhance progressively from 2026.
Those who wish for additional insurance coverage can also consider Supplements offered by private insurers.

questions.title: Why is my participation incentive $0?
questions.text: Participation Incentive is only extended to Singapore Citizens (SCs). However, both SCs and Permanent Residents (PRs) will be entitled to Government subsidies, if you are from a lower- to middle-income household. PRs enjoy half the applicable subsidies that SCs enjoy.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Why is the enrolment criterion being reinstated for CareShield Life application?
questions.text:
When CareShield Life was launched, older Singaporeans with less severe disability were allowed to join as a time-limited concession, so that more seniors could enrol in and benefit from CareShield Life.
However, this also meant that premiums for all older Singaporeans had to be priced higher, to account for the possibility that those with milder forms of disability were more likely to join the scheme.
This concession period lasted 4 years, over twice as long as what MOH had announced when the concession was rolled out. In this time, application rates have also decreased over time.
Thus, the CareShield Life Council views that this is an appropriate juncture to reinstate the underwriting criteria, which will moderate the extent of premium increases for all older policyholders, keeping the scheme fair and sustainable.

questions.title: Why is there a need to start CareShield Life earlier at age 30?
questions.text:
Starting CareShield Life at age 30 allows a longer period for premiums payment to be spread over. A longer duration of premium payment allows insureds to spread premium payment over more years, so as to reduce annual premiums payable. Consequently, insureds will benefit from additional years of coverage starting from age 30.
By the age of 30, most Singaporeans would have started working and many would have worked for a few years. It is also a good time to start planning for their long-term care needs. They would have started contributing to their MediSave, and should be able to cover their CareShield Life premiums without out-of-pocket expenses.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later

questions.title: Why is universal coverage not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier?
questions.text:
Universal coverage is not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier as this is a diverse group - some may have previously opted out of ElderShield, or decided not to upgrade to ElderShield. Others could have bought Supplements or insurance plans. Those born in 1979 or earlier would also likely face higher entry premiums as they have fewer years to spread their premium payment over. The prevalence of those who already have severe disability in the older cohorts is also much higher, which would make it harder to cover everyone while still keeping premiums affordable. Hence, universal coverage is not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier.
Those who are born in 1979 or earlier and who already have severe disability will not be able to join CareShield Life. The Government will help them through other ways e.g. Government subsidies and other Government schemes such as the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund. They can also tap on ElderFund and their MediSave savings.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund, ComCare can also provide further assistance to Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Why not allow insureds to choose from different CareShield Life plans depending on their ability to pay?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is intended to provide better protection for basic long-term care needs, when payouts are taken together with other long-term care financing sources.
If you wish to have additional coverage beyond what CareShield Life provides, you can consider purchasing Supplements from private insurers.

questions.title: Will CareShield Life/ElderShield disability assessment data be shared with the private insurers?
questions.text: With the insured’s consent, the disability assessment data will be shared with relevant Supplement insurers to avoid the need for patients to undergo multiple assessments.
topics: CareShield Life / Government Administration and Independent Council

questions.title: Will community care entities e.g., Adult Disability Homes, Shelters, Boys’ Home, and Girls’ Home, Assisted Living Facilities (ALFs), Senior Care Centres (SCCs), Senior Activity Centres and Social Day Care Centres need to be licensed under HCSA?
questions.text:
These entities provide services that are predominantly social in nature and to that extent will not be regulated under HCSA.
However, if these entities also deliver services that are clinical in nature, then the clinical services will have to be licensed. For example, if the senior activity centre has a doctor providing clinical services, either the doctor will require an Outpatient Medical Service licence, or the doctor has to be employed by a clinic licensee.

questions.title: Will ElderShield insurers continue selling Supplements?
questions.text: The ElderShield insurers will continue administering Supplements that complement the current ElderShield schemes.

questions.title: Will ElderShield Supplements remain with the insurers?
questions.text: The three private insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern Life & Income Insurance) will continue to administer ElderShield Supplements. The Government will administer CareShield Life and ElderShield, which provide basic protection against long-term care costs, while leaving the private insurers to innovate in the provision of CareShield Life/ElderShield Supplements which provide additional protection.
topics: ElderShield / Government Administration of ElderShield in 2021

questions.title: Will I need to verify my disability status every year to qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text: No, verification of your disability status will be a one-time process. If you are a person with disability below 55 and are verified with MSF, we will automatically assess your eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) at the beginning of each year. If you are eligible, we will notify you via email or post at the beginning of each year. You can also check your eligibility via the Retirement Dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Will I receive the Participation Incentives of up to $4,000 as long as I apply to join by 31 December 2023?
questions.text:
It depends on whether you will be required to undergo a disability assessment as part of the underwriting process.
If you are not required to undergo a disability assessment by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and apply to join CareShield Life using our eService by 31 December 2023, you will be eligible for Participation Incentives of up to $4,000.
If you are required to undergo a disability assessment by AIC and attend your disability assessment after 31 December 2023, you will not be eligible for the Participation Incentives of up to $4,000 as your application will only be approved as per your disability assessment date.
Therefore, you are encouraged to apply to join CareShield Life early if you are planning to do so.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Will it become more difficult for me to claim under my Supplements since the Government will be administering CareShield Life?
questions.text: The Government will work with private insurers to ensure that the claims process for insureds with CareShield Life and Supplement policies can be made as seamless as possible.
topics: CareShield Life / Government Administration and Independent Council

questions.title: Will my loved one be automatically included for ElderFund if he/ she is receiving payouts from other moderate disability schemes like PioneerDAS or Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)?
questions.text:
No. ElderFund’s eligibility criteria are stricter as it is a severe disability scheme.
If your loved one is eligible for ElderFund, you may apply for PioneerDAS or HCG without going for a separate assessment (if you meet those schemes’ criteria).
Please click here for more information on ElderFund.

questions.title: Will Singapore Permanent Residents be eligible for ElderFund?
questions.text: The focus of ElderFund is to provide support for Singapore Citizens living in Singapore. Singapore Permanent Residents will not be eligible for ElderFund.

questions.title: Will the ElderFund payouts rise over time, like CareShield Life payouts?
questions.text:
The regular increase in payouts for CareShield Life are supported by regular premium increases. Once an insured under CareShield Life makes a claim, the payout stays fixed.
ElderFund will be a government financial assistance scheme, funded through taxes. Eligible Singapore Citizens can receive up to $250 per month in cash. There will be no cap on payout duration for the duration of their severe disability. The Government will review the payout amount over time to ensure that payouts remain relevant for beneficiaries.

questions.title: Will the Government administer both CareShield Life and the current ElderShield schemes?
questions.text: The Government will work with the agencies, Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB) and the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), to operationalise and administer CareShield Life and ElderShield schemes. These agencies have a good record in implementing insurance and long-term care support schemes.
topics: CareShield Life / Government Administration and Independent Council

questions.title: Will the Government be allowing more insurers to sell Supplements for CareShield Life/ElderShield?
questions.text: The Government will review the CareShield Life/ElderShield Supplement market and assess the entry of new insurers into the Supplement market, if there is interest from other insurers.

questions.title: Will the Government be more lenient in its underwriting and claims processes compared to the insurers if it administers CareShield Life/ElderShield?
questions.text: CareShield Life/ElderShield will still be targeted at severe disability, i.e. no change from. insurer’s previous criteria for ElderShield. However, as a single administrator, the Government can achieve better consistency in the implementation of underwriting and claims processes across insureds.
topics: CareShield Life / Government Administration and Independent Council

questions.title: Would someone with dementia or other cognitive challenges automatically qualify for CareShield Life claims?
questions.text:
No, as such conditions affect people’s ability to carry out the six activities of daily living at different levels.
In order to qualify for a CareShield Life claim, your loved one still needs to undergo a disability assessment by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. The assessor will consider the impact of your loved one’s cognitive challenges as part of the assessment.

questions.title: Can a licensee appoint a third-party administrator (based overseas) to advertise its licensable healthcare services in other jurisdictions, i.e. promoting medical tourism?
questions.text:
The rules on advertising under HCSA are aimed at protecting the safety and welfare of patients in Singapore, and hence apply to advertisements that are accessible by persons physically located in Singapore.
HCSA licensees that advertise their services in other jurisdictions will have to comply with the prevailing laws in that jurisdiction.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to buy properties overseas?
questions.text:
CPF savings can only be used to buy properties in Singapore.
If you are looking to buy a property in another country, you will not be able to use your CPF savings to fund the purchase. It is important to keep this in mind when planning your property purchase and to ensure you have enough savings or financing options available for a property purchase outside of Singapore.

questions.title: Can overseas-trained or retired doctors and dentists who are not registered in Singapore use the title “Dr” in healthcare service advertising?
questions.text:
Overseas-trained or retired doctors/dentists who are not registered in Singapore and do not hold a valid practising certificate, must comply with the following when using the title “Dr” in their healthcare service advertising:
state their qualifications, and
include a disclaimer that he/ she is not holding a valid practising certificate issued by the relevant local healthcare professional board.
Examples as follows:
Example 1: Overseas-trained dentist who is not registered with SDC: Dr ABC, BDS (NUS, Singapore), does not hold a valid practising certificate under the Dental Registration Act 1999
Example 2: Registered retired doctor in Singapore with no valid practising certificate Dr XYZ, MBBS (Singapore), does not hold a valid practising certificate under the Medical Registration Act 1997
This advertising control would apply when any of these doctors/dentists are featured in advertisements of healthcare services

questions.title: What are the benefits of the new framework under the HCSA as compared to the previous framework under the PHMCA? Are there any overseas countries that utilise a similar licensing framework?
questions.text:
The PHMCA was premises-based whereas the HCSA adopts a service-based licensing structure. This is similar to the healthcare systems in the United Kingdom (UK) and Malaysia.
This allows licensees the flexibility to provide a range of services and take on new licences in a modular fashion.

questions.title: What is a Singapore Overseas Mission?
questions.text:
Singapore Overseas Missions located in certain countries can help CPF members residing overseas in witnessing and certification of application forms and documents.
You will need to visit the Singapore Overseas Mission in person. Find out where the overseas mission nearest to you is.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs
Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What should I do if I am currently overseas and unable to attend the Home Protection Scheme medical examination appointment?
questions.text:
We are unable to assess your eligibility for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) and process your application, if you are unable to attend the HPS medical examination.
You can submit a new HPS application online, using your Singpass, when you have returned to Singapore. A medical examination would be arranged for you thereafter.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Will the HCSA be able to take an errant healthcare service provider located overseas treating a local patient to task?
questions.text:
HCSA requires that local or foreign entities providing healthcare services in Singapore be licensed and that all foreign doctors working for the provider be registered with SMC. HCSA does not have extra-territorial powers.
The provision of healthcare services to local patients who travel overseas is also outside the jurisdiction of HCSA.

questions.title: What should I do if I suspect the call claiming to be from ICA to be a scam?
questions.text:
If you have reason to believe that the call is a scam, you are advised to take the following precautions:
Ignore such calls and the caller’s instructions
Do not provide personal information such as your name, identification number, passport details, contact details, or banking and credit card details
Report to Police if you suspect any fraudulent act or wrongdoing.
ICA takes a serious view of such scam calls as it undermines public trust in ICA. Members of the public can seek scam-related advice by calling the anti-scam centre at 1800-722-6688 or go to scamshield.gov.sg.

questions.title: What is Singpass Face Verification?
questions.text:
Singpass Face Verification is a method of verifying your identity using a face scan compared against the government's records.
Please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly for more information on Singpass Face Verification.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: How to spot a scam call?
questions.text:
1. Official callers will never request your personal or financial information over the phone.
2. Official callers will never send you a recorded message.
3. Official local calls will usually not have a “+” prefix - this is likely to be a spoofed call which you should not answer.
4. Only incoming international calls have the “+” sign prefix.
MOH is aware of calls falsely informing recipients that the caller is from MOH, requesting your personal or financial information over the phone. We urge recipients not to respond to such calls.
Be vigilant. Always be sure of the authenticity of instructions before offering any personal or financial information.
To verify the authenticity of calls from MOH, call MOH General Line 6325 9220 to verify the authenticity of the MOH number and full name of the caller.
If you suspect you have been scammed, contact the police at 1800 255 0000 or submit a report via www.police.gov.sg/iwitness

questions.title: I have updated my email address/mobile number with Singpass. Why are my Singpass contact details not updated with CPF Board?
questions.text:
Updates to your Singpass mobile number and email address will not be automatically updated with the Board.
You can update your mobile number and/or email address via my cpf digital services – Account settings with your Singpass. An SMS or email One-Time PIN (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile or email address for verification before the changes can be submitted.
Please note that any changes to your contact details will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period and you may be subject to enhanced authentication measures to verify your identity.
You can also watch the instructional video on how to update your contact details with CPF Board.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: What should I do if I accidentally reported a number as scam?
questions.text:
Please note that the ScamShield app only blocks phone numbers that have been marked as scam in the ScamShield database. These numbers are marked by the authorities based on reports from the community about suspicious or scam-related activity.
Please be assured that a single report alone does not automatically mark a phone number as a scam. Our system uses multiple data points and verification processes to determine if a number is suspicious.
If this is a legitimate phone number, you don't need to worry. The phone number won't be incorrectly marked as a scam based on a single report.
If you've accidentally reported a number as "scam", you may use the Check for Scams feature to check if the phone number is marked as scam in the ScamShield database.
A phone number is only blocked if the check outcome appears red with the message "Beware, this looks like a scam."
Only phone numbers from government and healthcare institutions that have been whitelisted will be marked as "Safe".
If you get an outcome saying “Be careful, we're not sure about this one”, the number has not been marked as "Scam" or blocked.
If you believe a phone number has been wrongly marked as scam, please reach out to the ScamShield Helpline at 1799 to request an unblock.
In addition, please submit a new scam report on the ScamShield app for the suspicious phone number you have come across.
Hope this helps!

questions.title: What should I do if I fall prey to a malware/phishing scam?
questions.text:
In the unfortunate event that you fall prey to a scam, we recommend taking the following actions immediately:
Alert your bank to freeze the affected bank account.
Reset your Singpass password if you think your Singpass has been compromised. For further assistance, please contact the official Singpass helpdesk at 6335 3533.
If you are 55 and above, activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to disable online CPF withdrawals instantly.
File a police report and provide all details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: Why is Singpass Face Verification failing for me?
questions.text:
There may be several possible reasons for this. For ways to improve the success of Singpass Face Verification, you should ensure that:
Your face is not covered
You keep still while scanning is in progress
Your environment is not too dark
There is no strong lighting in the background
You use a minimum resolution of two megapixels for the camera. If you are using a laptop, you may wish to try again using a mobile phone which has a better camera
If you require assistance with Singpass Face Verification, please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: Why do I need to update my registered bank account with CPF Board to my PayNow NRIC-linked bank account to make PayNow withdrawals if I have already withdrawn via PayNow previously?
questions.text:
With PayNow, you can withdraw CPF savings for immediate retirement needs from age 55 to your bank account almost instantly. As part of CPF Board’s ongoing efforts to better safeguard CPF members against scams, to make a PayNow withdrawal, you will need to do a one-time update of your registered bank account with CPF Board to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account via Account settings. This update will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period and may require enhanced authentication, similar to existing safeguards when you update your personal account details. Once your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account has been activated with CPF Board, it will be used to receive your CPF withdrawals and monthly payouts.
This update is required even if you have withdrawn via PayNow previously, as a one-time exercise to strengthen security against scams. We recognise the inconvenience but seek your understanding that this additional safeguard is necessary to provide a greater level of security to CPF members.
topics: Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: As a Trusted Contact, what should I do upon receiving notifications regarding transactions on my appointer’s CPF account?
questions.text:
As a Trusted Contact, you will receive copies of your appointer’s notifications whenever important transactions occur in your appointer’s CPF account. When you receive these notifications, check with your appointer to confirm they made the transaction.
If unsure whether your appointer may have fallen for a scam, STOP and CHECK with 24/7 ScamShield anti-scam helpline via 1799. To learn more about common scam signs and scam types, please visit the ScamShield website.
If your appointer has fallen victim to a scam, advise or guide them to take the following steps immediately:
Alert the bank to freeze any affected bank account(s)
Call Singpass helpdesk at +65 6335 3533 to reset their Singpass
Activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock to disable online CPF withdrawals (applicable for members aged 55 and above)
Lodge a police report and inform CPF Board

questions.title: How do I avoid falling prey to phishing scams?
questions.text:
Your financial safety matters to us.
Here are some tips on how to protect yourself against phishing scams pretending to come from CPF Board:
Do not share your Singpass or bank log-in details with anyone. CPF officers will NEVER ask for your Singpass or bank log-in details.
Check the source of the message. CPF Board will only contact you through these official channels:
Calls from CPF Board will only be made from 6227 1188.
SMSes will only be sent from "gov.sg" sender ID.
Sender's email address will end with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg. Check that the email address is spelt correctly.
WhatsApp sender is "CPF Board Text Us" with the blue badge. This is our official business account with the phone number 6031 5753.
Stay vigilant and examine the links embedded in the message. Messages from CPF Board may contain links to Government websites. Before clicking on such links, please check that the domain of the link ends with “.gov.sg” by hovering your mouse over the link to view the full address. For mobile devices, you can hold your finger down on the link so that a window pops out and shows you the full address.
Report any suspicious messages spoofing CPF Board via our CPF official hotline or Write to us. If unsure, check with the ScamShield app or call the 24/7 ScamShield anti-scam helpline via 1799.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: How do I deactivate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
You may request to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch through one of the following methods:
Call the CPF hotline at 1800-227-1188 (+65-6227-1188 if calling from overseas) and select option ‘8’ after choosing your language during operating hours
Make an appointment to visit any of the CPF Service Centres during operating hours
Note that your deactivation request will take around three to five working days to process, after we successfully verify your identity.

questions.title: How do I set up Singpass Face Verification (SFV)?
questions.text:
Singpass Face Verification (SFV) does not require any setup. It will automatically be triggered for potentially suspicious or higher-risk logins and transactions.
Please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly for more information on Singpass Face Verification.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: I received an SMS/email informing me that I will receive CPF notifications via my Singpass registered email address and/or mobile number. Is this legitimate?
questions.text:
Your Singpass contact information was shared with us so that we can update you on your CPF matters in a timely and efficient manner. This is part of the whole of government effort to provide you with a seamless digital experience.
If you prefer us to contact you via a different email address or mobile number, you can update your mobile number and/or email address via the Account settings page with your Singpass. An SMS or email One-Time PIN (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile number or email address for verification before the changes can take effect.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: Why am I prompted for Singpass Face Verification when performing transactions using my cpf digital services?
questions.text:
This is an additional safeguard against unauthorised usage of your Singpass account on transactions that require Singpass.
Please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly for more information on Singpass Face Verification.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: A loved one has appointed me as their Trusted Contact. How do I accept?
questions.text:
You can accept the appointment request under “Added you as a Trusted Contact” in the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings.
You may also refer to the instructional video below on how to accept a Trusted Contact request.

questions.title: An unknown party has appointed me as their Trusted Contact. What should I do?
questions.text: If you have received a Trusted Contact appointment request from a person not known to you, you can decline the request at the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings.

questions.title: Can anyone else, including Trusted Contacts, activate the CPF Safety Switch on behalf of a member?
questions.text: No, the CPF Safety Switch requires members to verify their identity before activation. CPF Board staff may also contact members via their registered contact details by the next working day to better understand their situation and provide further support as required.

questions.title: Can anyone else, including Trusted Contacts, request to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch on behalf of a member?
questions.text: No. Deactivation can only be performed by the member, who must complete our authentication process.

questions.title: Can CPF Board notify Trusted Contacts about other types of transactions made by their appointers?
questions.text: Only notifications for critical transactions or updates that may expose an account to higher scam risk (e.g. when a withdrawal is made, or when bank account information is changed) are copied to Trusted Contacts. This avoids overwhelming Trusted Contacts with less critical notifications regarding their appointer’s account.

questions.title: Can I appoint a new Trusted Contact or remove existing Trusted Contact on someone’s behalf?
questions.text:
No, Trusted Contact appointments or removal of existing Trusted Contact appointments must be made by the CPF member personally.
However, if the CPF member loses their mental capacity, their Deputy or Donee may apply to remove existing Trusted Contacts on their behalf.

questions.title: Can I appoint a Trusted Contact who is not based in Singapore?
questions.text:
You may appoint a person who is not based in Singapore as your Trusted Contact as long as they meet the eligibility criteria.
Your Trusted Contact must:
be a CPF member aged 21 and above;
be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (with Singpass account); and
have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board

questions.title: Can I appoint someone who is not my next-of-kin to be my Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can appoint a person who is not your next-of-kin to be your Trusted Contact. We highly recommend that you carefully review and only choose someone you trust, as they will help monitor important CPF transactions and provide an additional layer of security against potential scams.
Do note that your appointee will also need to accept the appointment before they become your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: Can I be a Trusted Contact for someone who is not my next-of-kin?
questions.text: Yes. You can be the Trusted Contact for someone who is not your next-of-kin if they appoint you. You must also meet these eligibility criteria to be a Trusted Contact.

questions.title: Can I make further changes to my contact details while my current request is still in the 12-hour cooling period?
questions.text:
Yes, you can submit further changes to your contact details via the Account settings page with your Singpass.
Please note that your most recent request will supersede the previous submission and the changes will take effect after the 12-hour cooling period.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars
Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: Can I submit more than one Trusted Contact appointment request within the same day?
questions.text:
Yes, you can submit up to two Trusted Contact appointment requests within the same day, which is the maximum number of Trusted Contacts you can appoint.
If you wish to submit a new Trusted Contact appointment request when you already have reached the maximum of two Trusted Contacts, you must first withdraw one of your pending requests or remove an existing Trusted Contact, before submitting a new appointment request.

questions.title: Do CPF volunteers conduct house visits or door-to-door services?
questions.text: No, CPF volunteers do not make house visits or conduct door-to-door activities. All CPF Volunteering activities take place at designated venues such as community centres or official events. CPF volunteers will never approach you at your home.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: How can I check the status of my application to remove an appointed Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your Trusted Contact removal application via your Activities page using your Singpass.
The removal of your Trusted Contact will take immediate effect upon successful submission of the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form. You may also refer to the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings and check that the Trusted Contact you have removed is not shown under “Your Trusted Contacts”.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my application to remove my appointment as a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your application to remove your appointment as a Trusted Contact via your Activities page using your Singpass.
Upon successful submission of the Remove yourself from your appointer's Trusted Contact list e-form, your name will be removed from the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your Trusted Contact appointment request via your Activities page using your Singpass.
You may also view your appointed Trusted Contacts at the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings. Only Trusted Contacts who have accepted your appointment request will be listed under “Your Trusted Contacts”.

questions.title: How can I differentiate the notifications I receive as a Trusted Contact from notifications for my own CPF account?
questions.text:
You can look out for the label in the notifications sent to you:
SMS Notifications: Begins with “(To Trusted Contact)”
Email: Contains “You are receiving this notification as an appointed Trusted Contact”
Push Notifications via CPF Mobile app (if enabled): Contains “You are receiving this notification as an appointed Trusted Contact of <Name of your appointer>”

questions.title: How can I make a Trusted Contact appointment if I failed the enhanced authentication verification?
questions.text:
If you failed the enhanced authentication when trying to submit a Trusted Contact appointment request, please try again later.
Otherwise, you may visit any CPF Service Centre with your intended appointee for assistance. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: How can I remove a Trusted Contact appointment if I failed the enhanced authentication?
questions.text:
If you fail the enhanced authentication when trying to remove a Trusted Contact, please try again later.
Otherwise, you may visit any CPF Service Centre for assistance. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: How can I remove my appointment as a Trusted Contact if I failed the enhanced authentication?
questions.text:
If you failed the enhanced authentication when trying to remove yourself as a Trusted Contact, please try again later.
Otherwise, you may visit any CPF Service Centre for assistance. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: How can I tell if the Workfare SMS I received is real?
questions.text:
Given the recent rise in scams and phishing attempts, it is important to verify that the message you received is genuinely from an official source.
As of 1 July 2024, all government SMS communications are sent under the sender ID “gov.sg”. The SMS will begin with the full name of the sending agency (e.g. “Central Provident Fund Board”) and end with “This is an automated message sent by the Singapore Government”, meaning you should not reply to the message.
This is only an example of a Workfare SMS. The actual SMS you receive may be different.
Here are some tips to help protect yourself against phishing SMSes that appear to be sent from CPF Board:
check that the SMS is sent from “gov.sg”to the mobile number registered with CPF Board. If you are unsure of whether you had registered your mobile number, log in to the CPF website with your Singpass and check your account settings.
verify that the last four characters of the masked NRIC number match your NRIC number.
We will never ask you to reply to a Workfare SMS or direct you to a non-Government website. If you receive suspicious SMS please report it at the CPF official hotline or write to us.
Be Cautious, Pay attention to scams and don't be the next victim of Fraud.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: How can I verify if someone claiming to be a CPF volunteer is genuine?
questions.text:
All CPF volunteers at events carry official identification displaying CPF Board and CPF Volunteering (CPFV) logos. If someone claims to be a CPF volunteer, always ask to see their identification or contact CPF Board to verify their identity. If you have any doubts about their authenticity, do not engage with them.
CPFV lanyard and identification card:
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: How do I activate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
You may activate the CPF Safety Switch by calling the CPF hotline at 1800-227-1188 (+65-6227-1188 if calling from overseas) and selecting option ‘8’ after choosing your preferred language.
Should you require any assistance in activating the CPF Safety Switch, you may make an appointment to visit any of the CPF Service Centres during operating hours.
Please note that we will require members to verify their identity before activation.

questions.title: How do I appoint a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can easily appoint a Trusted Contact via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form. You will need to log in with your Singpass to access the e-form.
You may also refer to the instructional video below on how to appoint a Trusted Contact.
Before you proceed:
Ensure that you and your appointee’s contact details registered with CPF Board are complete and up to date. You may update your contact details via Account settings before returning to this form.
Important notes:
You may need to verify your identity using enhanced authentication measures to complete the submission of Trusted Contact appointment.
Your appointee has seven days to respond to your Trusted Contact appointment request, after which the request will automatically expire.
If the Trusted Contact appointment request has expired, you will need to submit a new request. We strongly encourage you to personally inform your appointee about the Trusted Contact appointment request to ensure they are aware of it and understand their role as a Trusted Contact.
Steps to appoint:
Select the ‘Add a Trusted Contact’ option at Step 1 of the form.
Provide the following details of the person you wish to appoint:
Full name (as per NRIC)
NRIC number
Relationship to you
Review your input before submitting the e-form.
What happens next:
Both you and your Trusted Contact appointee will be notified upon successful submission. The Trusted Contact appointment will only take effect once your appointee accepts the request. Please remind your appointee to accept your Trusted Contact appointment request within seven days of submission. You may go to the Activities page to view the status of your request.
Once your Trusted Contact appointment request has been accepted, your Trusted Contact will receive a copy of your notifications whenever important transactions occur in your CPF account.

questions.title: How do I avoid falling prey to malware scams?
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: How do I become a Trusted Contact for a loved one?
questions.text:
Your loved one can appoint you as their Trusted Contact via the Add or remove Trusted Contact
e-form. They will need to login with their Singpass when they begin the e-form.
To be a Trusted Contact, you must:
Be a CPF member aged 21 or above; and
Be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (with Singpass account); and
Have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board.
Before accepting the role of a Trusted Contact, please review the Terms and Conditions of the Trusted Contact service and understand the role of a Trusted Contact. Please refer to the Trusted Contact information page for more details.

questions.title: How do I inform CPF Board if I have changed my contact details?
questions.text:
Notifications will be sent to you whenever you make a transaction. Also, we may contact you to perform further verification checks on your transactions for added security. Hence, it is important to check and keep your contact details updated.
You can update your mobile number and/or email address via the Account Settings page with your Singpass. An SMS or email One-Time Password (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile or email address for verification before the changes can be submitted.
Please note that any changes to your contact details will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period and you may be subject to enhanced authentication measures to verify your identity.
You can also watch the instructional video below on how to update your contact details with CPF Board.
Watch it in Chinese, Malay, Tamil
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars
Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: How do I know if my CPF Safety Switch activation request is successful?
questions.text:
You will receive an email and SMS to your registered contact details notifying you of the outcome of your activation request. Note that we will not be able to reach you if you have no registered contact details with us.
If you wish to update your contact details, you may do so via the Account settings page on CPF website, before activating CPF Safety Switch.
SMS notifications from CPF Board will only be sent from the “gov.sg” sender ID, and the email address will end with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg.
After CPF Safety Switch has been activated, you will not be able to log in to your CPF account.

questions.title: How do I know if my deactivation request is successful?
questions.text: You will receive an email and SMS to your registered contact details notifying you once your deactivation request is successful. Generally, this may take three to five working days, and we may contact you for more information during this period.

questions.title: How do I know whether the emails I receive are genuinely sent by CPF Board?
questions.text: To ensure that an email is genuinely sent by the CPF Board, remember to always check that the sender’s email address ends with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: How do I remove my appointed Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can easily remove a Trusted Contact via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form. You will need to login with your Singpass when you begin the e-form.
Before you proceed:
Verify that your contact details registered with CPF Board are correct. If you need to update your contact details, you can do so via Account settings before returning to this form.
Steps to remove:
To remove a Trusted Contact, select the ‘Remove a Trusted Contact’ option at Step 1 of the form.
Next, select the Trusted Contact you wish to remove.
Review your input before submitting the form.
What happens next:
The removal of your Trusted Contact will take immediate effect.
Notifications will be sent to both you and the Trusted Contact you have removed.
Important notes:
You may need to verify your identity using enhanced authentication measures to complete the submission.

questions.title: How do I update my registered bank account details with CPF Board?
questions.text:
You can update your registered bank account details with CPF Board to receive payments such as withdrawal of CPF savings and monthly payouts via my cpf digital services - Account settings with your Singpass.
You may need to verify your identity using enhanced authentication measures to update your registered bank account details.
To guide you on how to update your registered bank account details with CPF Board, watch the instructional video in your preferred language, or follow the steps below:
Log in to your CPF account with your Singpass.
On the website menu, click on ‘Account services’ > ‘Your account information’ > ‘Update account settings’.
Click the ‘Bank account’ tab and click ‘Update’.
For PayNow, select ‘PayNow NRIC-linked bank account’ and submit the form. The bank account will be updated after 12 hours
For Interbank GIRO, key in your bank account details and submit the form. The bank account will generally take up to two working days to be activated after your bank confirms that the bank account belongs to you.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars
Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: How do I verify that the CPF Contribution Alert email I received is legitimate?
questions.text:
The CPF Contribution Alert is a notification service to inform CPF members who are Singapore Citizens and 3rd year onwards Singapore Permanent Residents when their monthly CPF contributions are credited.
Members will receive the email notification at the email address registered with the Board. You may check or update your email address which you have earlier registered with us using your Singpass.
If you have the CPF Mobile app installed, you will be directed to view your details via the app.
To verify if the CPF Contribution Alert email you received is legitimate and avoid falling prey to phishing scams,
Ensure that the sender's email address is correctly spelt and ends with "@e.cpf.gov.sg".
Ensure that the hyperlinks or links you click on has a domain ending with “.gov.sg”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: How is the Trusted Contact different from a Court-appointed Deputyship?
questions.text:
A Deputy is an individual appointed by the court to make decisions on behalf of a person who lacks mental capacity. The type of decisions a Deputy can make are specified in the Deputyship appointment court order.
In contrast, a Trusted Contact is a trusted person that a CPF member can appoint, while they have mental capacity, to receive a copy of their notifications whenever important transactions occur in their CPF account. Unlike a Deputy, a Trusted Contact is not legally empowered to make decisions on the person’s behalf.

questions.title: How is the Trusted Contact different from a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)?
questions.text:
An Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) allows a person to appoint someone (Donee) to make decisions on their behalf, should they lose mental capacity in the future. A Donee can be appointed to act in the two broad areas of personal welfare and/or property and affairs matters. The LPA also gives the authority to the Donee to sign deeds on the Donor's behalf.
While both Donee and Trusted Contact appointments are initiated by the CPF member, unlike a Donee, a Trusted Contact is not legally empowered to make decisions on the person’s behalf. The Trusted Contact can only receive a copy of their appointer’s notifications whenever important transactions occur in their CPF account.
You should also consider appointing an LPA as part of your legacy planning if you have not done so already.

questions.title: How is the Trusted Contact notification service different from CPF nomination?
questions.text:
The Trusted Contact notification service and CPF nomination are two separate CPF services:
The Trusted Contact notification service: Allows you to appoint a trusted individual such as a family member, to receive a copy of your notifications whenever important transactions occur in your CPF account.
A CPF nomination allows you to specify who will receive your CPF savings and the proportion of your savings each nominee will receive when you pass away.
Appointing a Trusted Contact does not affect your CPF nomination. Likewise, making a CPF nomination does not affect your Trusted Contact appointment(s) too. If you wish, you may appoint the same individual as both your nominee and your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: How long does a Trusted Contact appointment remain valid for?
questions.text:
Trusted Contact appointments will remain valid until either you or your appointed Trusted Contact terminates the arrangement. The CPF Board will also remove Trusted Contact appointments when either party can no longer use the service, such as upon demise.
Do note that Trusted Contact(s) you have appointed will not be affected and remains valid even after you lose mental capacity.

questions.title: How long does it take to remove an appointed Trusted Contact?
questions.text: The removal of your Trusted Contact will take immediate effect upon the successful submission of the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form.

questions.title: How long does it take to remove my appointment as a Trusted Contact?
questions.text: You will be removed as a Trusted Contact with immediate effect upon a successful submission.

questions.title: How long does my appointee have to accept my Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text:
Your appointee has seven days to respond to your Trusted Contact appointment request, after which the request will automatically expire. If the request has expired, you will need to submit a new appointment request.
We strongly encourage you to personally inform the appointee about the appointment request to ensure that they are aware of the appointment request and understand their role as your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: I am a deputy/donee for a CPF member. How can I remove their Trusted Contact appointment(s)?
questions.text:
As a deputy/donee, you can write to us via Singpass to request the removal of Trusted Contact on a member’s behalf, by providing the following documents:
For Donee appointed under a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA): Submit the LPA document and a medical report certifying your donor’s loss of mental capacity
For Deputy appointed by the Singapore Court: Submit the Deputyship court order

questions.title: I am a Trusted Contact. Why am I not allowed to transact on my appointer’s behalf or view the CPF account balances and statements?
questions.text:
As a Trusted Contact, you serve as an extra pair of eyes to help safeguard your appointer from potential scams. To meet this objective, you will receive a copy of the notifications whenever important transactions occur in your appointer’s CPF account.
We strike a balance between enabling you to support your appointer and protecting their privacy. You can only receive key transaction information through notifications to help you monitor for suspicious transactions - you cannot view your appointer's full CPF account details, make transactions, or change any account settings on their behalf. This ensures you can help identify suspicious transactions while your appointer's account privacy remains protected.

questions.title: I am not a scam victim. Should I still activate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
You should only activate the CPF Safety Switch if you suspect you have fallen victim to a scam.
If you wish to protect yourself against scams and do not need to withdraw immediately, consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock instead. Activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock will maintain your online access to your CPF account while disabling online CPF withdrawals. Find out more about the CPF Withdrawal Lock.

questions.title: I am providing caregiving to a loved one with medical conditions. I would like to make changes to their Trusted Contact appointment(s). How can I do so?
questions.text:
Trusted Contact appointments or removal of existing Trusted Contacts must be made by the CPF member personally. Your loved one can make changes to their Trusted Contact appointment online via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form.
As a third party, you cannot make decisions concerning another member’s CPF account unless you have been legally authorised to do so.
If your loved one has lost mental capacity and you are their Deputy or Donee, you can write to us via Singpass to request the removal of appointed Trusted Contacts on their behalf, by providing the following documents:
For Donee appointed under a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA): Submit the LPA document and a medical report certifying your next-of-kin’s loss of mental capacity
For Deputy appointed by the Singapore Court: Submit the Deputyship court order
If your loved one has mental capacity but you wish to act on their behalf, you will need to write to us via Singpass and furnish a court order authorising you to make such changes.

questions.title: I am the appointed Trusted Contact of someone who has lost their mental capacity. Will my appointment as the Trusted Contact be affected?
questions.text:
If a person who appointed you loses their mental capacity, your appointment as their Trusted Contact will not be affected and remains valid.
A Court-appointed Deputy or Donee appointed under a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) are legally empowered to manage the affairs of your appointer (who has lost his mental capacity). They may remove you as the Trusted Contact if they deem it necessary and you will be informed accordingly. If you wish to remove yourself from the Trusted Contact’s list, you may do so via the Remove yourself from your appointer's Trusted Contact list e-form.

questions.title: I did not perform any removal for my Trusted Contact appointment. Why was my Trusted Contact appointment / appointment as a Trusted Contact removed by CPF Board?
questions.text: The CPF Board may remove your appointed Trusted Contact or your appointment as a Trusted Contact when either you or your Trusted Contact are no longer eligible to use the service. You are advised to check with your appointer or your Trusted Contact if there has been a change in their circumstances affecting their eligibility. You may refer to our FAQs on Member eligibility and Trusted Contact eligibility for more information.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that I cannot remove my appointed Trusted Contact because their contact details are incomplete. What should I do?
questions.text:
Please inform the person you are trying to remove as your Trusted Contact to register both a Singapore-registered mobile number and an email address with CPF Board. Once your Trusted Contact has successfully updated their contact details, you may proceed to remove the Trusted Contact via the e-form.
If this is not possible, you may write to us via Singpass with the following details:
A screenshot of the error page,
The name and NRIC number of the Trusted Contact you wish to remove
You may also visit any CPF Service Centre to remove the Trusted Contact in person. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre, as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that I cannot remove my appointment as Trusted Contact because my appointer’s contact details are incomplete. Can CPF Board assist to remove my appointment?
questions.text:
Please inform your appointer to update their contact details with CPF Board. Once your appointer has successfully updated their contact details, you may proceed to remove your appointment as a Trusted Contact via the Remove yourself from your appointer's Trusted Contact list e-form.
If this is not possible, you may write to us via Singpass with the following details:
A screenshot of the error page,
The name and NRIC number of the appointer you wish to remove
You may also visit any CPF Service Centre to remove your Trusted Contact appointment in person. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that the name I keyed for my appointee was different from his NRIC/CPF Account Number. How can I resolve this?
questions.text:
You should key in the full name of your appointee as per his NRIC. This includes any punctuation such as the comma (,), hyphen (-), and slash (/).
However, you should exclude the Hanyu Pinyin, Alias and Married name. See examples of NRIC names.
If you are still encountering problems in submitting your Trusted Contact appointment request, we recommend that you check the following:
Check for the correct spacing of characters in the names of your appointee.
For example:
John⎵Tan should not be written as John⎵⎵Tan or John⎵Tan⎵
D/O should not be written as D / O, and likewise for S/O
Avoid copy-pasting the details from another program or app as there might be hidden characters that might get copied. Key in the appointee’s particulars manually instead.
If you are using an iOS device (such as iPhone or iPad), disable the “Smart Punctuation” feature in iOS (iOS device Settings > General > Keyboard > Turn off Smart Punctuation). This feature might create unrecognisable characters in the application form.
Avoid opening multiple browser tabs. Use only one browser tab and clear your browser cache.
Consider using a different device to submit your Trusted Contact appointment request if submission via your original device is still unsuccessful.
If you continue to encounter the same error despite the above, you can write to us via Singpass with the following details for assistance:
A screenshot of the name of your appointee,
The time and date when the error occurred, and
Details of the device that you are using to submit your Trusted Contact appointment request.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that the person I intend to appoint as my Trusted Contact cannot be appointed because their contact details are incomplete. What should I do?
questions.text:
To better safeguard you from potential scams, your Trusted Contact must have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and an email address registered with CPF Board, as they will receive a copy of your transaction notifications whenever important CPF transactions or updates are made in your CPF account.
You should inform the person you are trying to appoint to update their contact details with CPF Board. If this is not possible, you should consider appointing a different person as your Trusted Contact instead.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that the person I intend to appoint as my Trusted Contact has reached their appointment limit. What should I do?
questions.text: The person you are trying to appoint is already a Trusted Contact of several other individuals. We recommend appointing someone else for better monitoring of your important CPF transactions or updates. If you still prefer to appoint this person, you can ask them to remove one of their existing appointments. However, do consider that spreading their attention across multiple members might affect their focus and effectiveness in spotting suspicious activities promptly.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that the person I intend to appoint as my Trusted Contact is not eligible. What should I do?
questions.text:
The person you are trying to appoint as your Trusted Contact is not eligible to use the service.
Your Trusted Contact must:
Be a CPF member aged 21 and above
Be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident
Have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board
Please consider appointing a different person as your Trusted Contact instead.

questions.title: I have submitted my Trusted Contact appointment request. How will my appointee be informed to accept my appointment request?
questions.text: Notifications will be sent to your appointee via email, SMS and push notifications via the CPF Mobile app (if enabled) to inform them of your appointment request. While CPF Board will notify your appointee, we strongly encourage you to personally inform them of your appointment request beforehand. This helps to ensure that they are aware of the appointment request and understand their role as your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: I no longer wish to be appointed as a Trusted Contact. How do I remove my appointment?
questions.text:
You can easily remove your appointment as a Trusted Contact via the Remove yourself from your appointer's Trusted Contact list e-form. You will need to login with your Singpass when you begin the e-form.
Before you proceed:
Verify that your contact details registered with CPF Board are correct. If you need to update your contact details, you can do so via Account settings before returning to this form.
How to remove yourself as Trusted Contact:
Select the person from whose Trusted Contact list you wish to remove yourself.
Review your selection before submitting the form.
What happens next:
The removal will take immediate effect after successful submission.
Both you and your appointer (from whom you have removed your appointment as Trusted Contact) will be notified.
Important notes:
You may need to verify your identity using enhanced authentication measures to complete the submission.

questions.title: I received a call from CDA notifying me of contact tracing. How do I verify if this is not a scam call?
questions.text: To verify the authenticity of calls from CDA, call CDA Hotline 6461 5340 to verify the authenticity of the CDA number and full name of the caller.

questions.title: I received a call/email/letter claiming they are from the Household Means Eligibility System (HOMES). Are they legitimate?
questions.text:
HOMES is a Government system supporting the Silver Support (SS) Scheme in conducting household means-tests, which are used to assess a senior’s eligibility for the SS Scheme. If you or your family member had asked for a reassessment of SS eligibility, and there is a need for further clarification regarding your household information, the HOMES team may contact you via phone, email or letter to find out more on your household circumstances.
If you are unsure of the authenticity of the mobile number that you have received, please call their hotline 6818 1422 for confirmation.
If you have any query on HOMES, you may visit the HOMES website to provide your contact details and a brief description of your query.
topics: Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received a call/email/SMS from the CPF Board regarding my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS). How do I know if it is legitimate?
questions.text:
We understand your concern on phishing. Given the recent rise in scam and phishing attempts, it is important to verify that the message you received on your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is genuine.
Remain vigilant and cautious when receiving calls/emails/messages. Government officials, including CPF Board officers, will never:
Ask you to withdraw CPF or transfer money to them (or to other persons);
Ask you to provide personal or banking IDs/passwords
Ask you to download and install non-Government mobile apps from sources other than official app stores; or
Transfer your call to SPF, except when necessary in life-threatening emergencies
If you receive such requests from anyone claiming to be a CPF Board officer, do not act on them. End the conversation, call the 24/7 ScamShield anti-scam helpline via 1799, and inform CPF Board.
To receive notification on your PCTS, it is important to check and keep your contact details updated under Account Settings.
You can further protect yourself against scams by doing the following additional checks:
Sender's email address will end with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg. Check that the email address is spelt correctly.
SMSes will only be sent from “gov.sg” to the mobile number registered with CPF Board.
Calls from CPF Board will only be made from 6227 1188.
Messages from CPF Board may contain links to the CPF website or other Government websites (NEVER to non-Government). Please check that the domain of such links end with ".gov.sg" before clicking on them. To determine if a link will lead you to a malicious website or is reliable, you can hover your mouse over the link to view the full address. For mobile devices, you can hold your finger down on the link so that a window pops out and shows you the full address.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received a call/email/SMS/WhatsApp message from the CPF Board. How do I know if it is legitimate?
questions.text:
Check the source of the message
CPF Board will only contact you through these official channels:
Calls from CPF Board will only be made from 6227 1188.
SMSes will only be sent from "gov.sg" sender ID.
Sender's email address will end with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg. Check that the email address is spelt correctly.
WhatsApp sender is "CPF Board Text Us" with the blue badge. This is our official business account with the phone number 6031 5753.
CPF Board Text Us
Messages from CPF Board may contain links to the CPF website or other Government websites. Please check that the domain of such links end with ".gov.sg" before clicking on them. To determine if a link will lead you to a malicious website or is reliable, you can hover your mouse over the link to view the full address. For mobile devices, you can hold your finger down on the link so that a window pops out and shows you the full address.
Scammers may impersonate Government Officials
Be aware that scammers may impersonate CPF Board staff or Government officials and:
Cite your personal information like name or NRIC number to appear legitimate
Insist that you are involved in crimes like money laundering
Pressure you to hand over valuables like cash or gold bars for “investigation”
Instruct you not to tell anyone about the “investigation"
Government officials, including CPF Board officers, will NEVER:
Ask you to withdraw CPF or transfer money;
Ask you to disclose bank log-in details;
Ask you to install mobile apps from unofficial app stores; or
Transfer your call to Police
If you receive such requests from anyone claiming to be a CPF Board officer, do not act on them. STOP and CHECK with 24/7 ScamShield anti-scam helpline via 1799, and inform CPF Board.
Update your Contact Details
We will send notifications to you whenever you make a transaction and may contact you to perform further verification checks on your transactions for added security. Hence, it is important to check and keep your contact details updated under Account Settings (Singpass login required).
For more information
To learn more about protecting yourself against scams, please visit the ScamShield website and find out more about the anti-scam security measures available to CPF members.
topics: Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received a notification indicating that my CPF Safety Switch activation request is not successful. What should I do next?
questions.text: If you have been scammed, please call us at 1800-227-1188 (+65-6227-1188 if calling from overseas) for assistance. You should also contact your bank to freeze your bank account immediately, and reset your Singpass (for assistance, call Singpass helpdesk at +65 6335 3533).

questions.title: I received a notification informing me of a Trusted Contact appointment request. What should I do?
questions.text:
Someone has requested you to be their Trusted Contact. Please verify that this appointment was correctly made by checking the requestor’s name.
You can accept or decline the appointment request at the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings. Please note that the Trusted Contact appointment request will expire seven days after your appointer made the request, after which you will no longer be able to accept or decline it. Your appointer will be notified after you accept or decline the Trusted Contact appointment request.

questions.title: I received a notification informing me that a pending Trusted Contact appointment request has been withdrawn. What should I do?
questions.text: No further action is required from you as the pending appointment request has been withdrawn by the appointer.

questions.title: I received a notification informing me that my Trusted Contact appointment was declined. What should I do?
questions.text:
The notification was sent to inform you that the person you had tried to appoint as your Trusted Contact has declined your appointment request. You should try to contact your appointee to explain your request and help them understand their role as your Trusted Contact before submitting a new appointment request.
Alternatively, you may consider choosing a different person to appoint as your Trusted Contact. We strongly encourage you to personally inform them of your appointment request beforehand. This helps to ensure that they are aware of the appointment request and understand their role as your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: I received a notification stating my Trusted Contact appointment request has expired. What should I do?
questions.text:
The notification was sent to inform you that the person you had tried to appoint as your Trusted Contact did not respond to your appointment request within seven days of your submission.
Your appointee must agree to be your Trusted Contact by accepting your appointment request at the “Trusted Contact” section under their Account settings via Singpass login.
