The Trusted Contact appointment will only take effect once your appointee has accepted the Trusted Contact appointment request.
If you wish to appoint the same person as your Trusted Contact, you should personally inform them before resubmitting your appointment request, so that they can respond promptly. You will receive a notification when your appointee accepts the Trusted Contact appointment request to be your Trusted Contact.
Alternatively, you may consider choosing a different person to appoint as your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: I received an anonymous call claiming that I can sign up for a new CPF Scheme that allows me to withdraw my CPF savings, and the caller offered to meet me to sign an application form. Is it a scam?
questions.text:
Yes, it is a scam. CPF Board officers will not solicit sign-ups for CPF Schemes which involve the withdrawal of CPF savings. Members who wish to perform transactions with the Board should use my cpf digital services instead.
In the unfortunate event that you fall prey to a scam, we recommend taking the following actions immediately:
Alert your bank to freeze the affected bank account.
Reset your Singpass password if you think your Singpass has been compromised. For further assistance, please contact the official Singpass helpdesk at 6335 3533.
If you are 55 and above, activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to disable online CPF withdrawals instantly.
File a police report and provide all details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of Trusted Contacts I can appoint? How many Trusted Contacts can I appoint?
questions.text: You may appoint up to two individuals as your Trusted Contacts. Both Trusted Contacts will have the same role and responsibilities with no primary or secondary designation. If you wish to appoint a new Trusted Contact but have already reached the limit, you must first remove one of your existing Trusted Contacts or withdraw one of your pending appointment requests.

questions.title: Is there a time limit for how long the CPF Safety Switch remains active?
questions.text:
No. The CPF Safety Switch will remain activated until we receive your instruction to deactivate it.
However, we recommend that you deactivate the CPF Safety Switch after you have performed the necessary actions to secure your CPF account. We will send periodic email and SMS reminders to members who may have forgotten to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch.

questions.title: My appointed Trusted Contact is not receiving a copy of my notification when I perform CPF transactions. Why is this so?
questions.text:
The Trusted Contact service only sends notifications to your Trusted Contact for transactions below:
CPF lump sum withdrawals for immediate retirement needs
Contact details update
Bank account update
Daily withdrawal limit update
If your Trusted Contact did not receive a notification, it may be because the transaction you performed is not covered by the Trusted Contact service.
However, if your Trusted Contact is not receiving notifications for any of the above transactions, please write to us via Singpass with the following details:
Name of your Trusted Contact
The type of transaction you performed, including the time and date
Screenshot of the notifications sent to you

questions.title: Should I disclose my personal details to a CPF volunteer?
questions.text:
No. Our volunteers will never ask for your personal details such as NRIC, phone number and email address. If you have account-specific queries, they are best addressed by our trained staff via our various customer service channels.
If you encounter such a situation, it is important that you report so that appropriate action can be taken.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: What are the anti-scam security measures available to CPF members?
questions.text:
CPF Board adopts a multi-pronged approach in safeguarding members' CPF savings from scams. This includes empowering members with self-help measures and working with other Government agencies and banks to enhance the overall ecosystem's scam detection capabilities. We prioritise security above convenience and continually review the evolving scam landscape and enhance our measures accordingly.
For example, in addition to our existing safeguards such as ensuring that CPF savings are credited to bank accounts that are verified to belong to the members, Singpass Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) and enhanced authentication measures, we have implemented a suite of measures to better partner our members in safeguarding their CPF savings from scams. These measures include:
Trusted Contact notification service
Members can appoint a trusted individual, such as a family member, to receive a copy of their notifications for the following important CPF transactions:
CPF lump sum withdrawals for immediate retirement needs
Contact detail update
Bank account update
Daily withdrawal limit update
This gives members an additional safeguard by allowing a trusted individual to help identify unusual transactions and act quickly if needed. To find out more about the Trusted Contact notification service, please visit cpf.gov.sg/trustedcontact.
CPF Safety Switch
Members aged 55 and above who suspect their CPF account has been compromised or have fallen victim to a scam can immediately secure their CPF accounts by activating the CPF Safety Switch. Once activated:
All disbursements to members' registered bank account will cease, including any withdrawals currently being processed; and
Access to CPF online services through the CPF website and mobile app will be disabled, preventing unauthorised future withdrawals from members’ CPF accounts.
However, all incoming CPF contributions or recurring payments to organisations for housing and insurance will remain unaffected to minimise disruptions.
Daily Withdrawal Limit
A limit that all CPF members aged 55 and above can set to determine the maximum daily amount they want to withdraw online. The amount withdrawable by CPF members aged 55 and above remains subjected to the current withdrawal rules.
All CPF members aged 55 and above will have their online Daily Withdrawal Limit defaulted at $2,000 for a start. Members who prefer a different Daily Withdrawal Limit can adjust it up to a maximum of $50,000, at any time under Account settings. Increases to the Daily Withdrawal Limit may require enhanced authentication. There will also be a 12-hour cooling period to provide sufficient time for members to react in the event of unauthorised adjustments.
CPF Withdrawal Lock
CPF members who wish to disable online withdrawals or do not plan to withdraw soon can consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock, which instantly sets the Daily Withdrawal Limit to $0. Please refer to the three simple steps to activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock.
To re-enable online withdrawals, members would need to increase the online Daily Withdrawal Limit under Account settings. This requires 12 hours to take effect and may require enhanced authentication. Online CPF withdrawals can be made after 12 hours from the time members re-adjust their Daily Withdrawal Limit upwards.
Alternatively, members can also make an appointment to withdraw in person at CPF Service Centres if they do not want to adjust their online limit. Generally, the next available appointment would be in a week’s time; subsequently, members will receive their withdrawn CPF savings in their bank account registered with us generally within five working days. To minimise any potential delay during the withdrawal process, we encourage members intending to make large withdrawals to plan in advance.
Please visit the FAQs below to find out more on the Daily Withdrawal Limit and the CPF Withdrawal Lock:
What type of CPF withdrawals does the Daily Withdrawal Limit apply to and how do I change the Daily Withdrawal Limit?
What is the CPF Withdrawal Lock, and how can I activate it?
Can I choose to opt-out of the Daily Withdrawal Limit?
What should I do if I need to withdraw more than the maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit?
Enhanced authentication and 12-hour cooling period when updating contact details via the Update Contact Details (UCD) form
Members who are updating their contact details via the UCD e-form under Account settings will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period. Members may also be prompted to verify their identity before submitting the update form.
Enhanced authentication when updating bank account details via the ‘Update Bank Account’ e-service
Members can update their bank account details with CPF Board to receive payments such as withdrawal of CPF savings and monthly payouts via my cpf digital services - Account settings with their Singpass.
Members may be prompted to verify their identity through enhanced authentication to update their bank account details. PayNow NRIC-linked bank accounts will be activated after a 12-hour cooling period, and all other bank accounts will generally take up to two working days to be activated after your bank confirms that the account belongs to you.
Please visit the FAQs below to find out more about the new “Update Bank Account” e-service:
How do I update my bank account details with CPF Board?
Why do I need to update my registered bank account with CPF Board to my PayNow NRIC-linked bank account to make PayNow withdrawals if I have already withdrawn via PayNow previously?
Do I have to provide my bank account details to CPF Board if I do not have any upcoming payments from CPF Board?
Which CPF payments will I receive in the bank account provided under my Account settings?
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: What are the Trusted Contact notification service Terms and Conditions?
questions.text:
You may refer to the terms and conditions for the Trusted Contact notification service below:
Terms and Conditions.

questions.title: What can my Trusted Contact view or do?
questions.text:
Your appointed Trusted Contact will receive a copy of the notifications sent to you whenever you perform any of the following transactions and updates in your CPF account. Their role is limited to receiving a copy of your transaction notifications and alerting you when they notice any unusual or unexpected transactions or updates made in your CPF account.
Notifications from the following CPFB services are copied to your Trusted Contact via their registered email address, mobile number, and push notifications (if enabled):
CPF lump sum withdrawals for immediate retirement needs
Contact details update
Bank account update
Daily withdrawal limit update
You will continue to receive these notifications at your own registered email address and mobile number, and push notifications (if enabled).
Please note that your Trusted Contact cannot view your CPF account details beyond the information included in these notifications, make transactions, or change any account settings on your behalf.

questions.title: What happens if I genuinely need to make an urgent withdrawal after activating CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
We understand that members may have legitimate urgent transactions even after activating the CPF Safety Switch. Members can call the CPF hotline or make an appointment to visit any CPF Service Centre during operating hours to request to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch. During this process, CPF Board staff will work with the member to verify their identity, understand their situation and provide guidance on safe practices before reactivating access to CPF online services.
Deactivation of the CPF Safety Switch can only be performed by CPF Board staff after the member’s identity has been verified. This ensures that only the genuine account holder can regain access to their account and helps safeguard members' CPF savings from scammers who might otherwise pressure victims to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch.
Do note that after deactivation, you will still need to update your bank account, which will take 12 hours for a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account or two working days for Interbank GIRO.

questions.title: What happens if my appointed Trusted Contact loses their mental capacity?
questions.text:
You should revoke their Trusted Contact appointment via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form when your appointed Trusted Contact loses their mental capacity.
You may also wish to submit a new appointment request to appoint a different person to be your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: What happens to my Trusted Contact appointment(s) if I lose my mental capacity?
questions.text: Your Trusted Contact appointment will not be affected and remains valid even after you lose mental capacity. The CPF Board will uphold any decisions made by members prior to the loss of mental capacity.

questions.title: What happens to my Trusted Contact appointment(s) upon my demise?
questions.text: CPF Board will revoke your appointed Trusted Contact(s) as well as your appointment(s) as a Trusted Contact upon your demise.

questions.title: What information do I need to prepare to activate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
If you are calling the CPF hotline to activate the CPF Safety Switch, you will need to provide your personal details for us to verify your identity.
If you have made an appointment to CPF Service Centre, please be reminded to bring your identification documents (such as NRIC).

questions.title: What information does my Trusted Contact see in the notifications copied to them?
questions.text:
Successfully appointed Trusted Contacts receive copies of the same notifications that are sent to you when transactions are made. The information in these notifications will differ for each CPF service used and transaction made.
You cannot customise the notifications or information sent to your Trusted Contacts. They will receive copies of the same notifications you receive to ensure they can effectively detect any unusual or unexpected activities in your CPF account. We recommend appointing someone you trust to help monitor important CPF transactions as an additional layer of security against potential scams.
Information included in the notifications:
CPF service Information included
CPF lump sum withdrawals for
immediate retirement needs
Transaction date, withdrawal amount, details of Bank Account used for withdrawal, reason(s) for unsuccessful withdrawal (where applicable)
Contact details update
Transaction date, Transaction time
Bank account update
Transaction number, Transaction date, Transaction time, Update option (PayNow or Interbank GIRO), details of new Bank Account
Daily withdrawal limit update
Transaction date, previous Daily Withdrawal Limit, updated Daily Withdrawal Limit
You can also view a sample of the notification content.

questions.title: What is my role as a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
As an appointed Trusted Contact, you play a role in helping to protect your appointer from potential scams. You will receive a copy of the notifications sent to your appointer when important transactions and updates occur in their CPF account. By monitoring these notifications, you can help to spot and alert them to any suspicious activities in their CPF account that may not be performed by them.
Notifications from the following CPF services will be copied to you when triggered by transactions in your appointer’s CPF account:
CPF lump sum withdrawals for immediate retirement needs
Contact details update
Bank account update
Daily withdrawal limit update
Your appointer will still receive notifications at their own registered contact.
It is important to note that as a Trusted Contact, you cannot transact or make changes to your appointer’s CPF account on their behalf as your appointer has sole control of their CPF account. Your role is limited to receiving a copy of their transaction notifications and alerting your appointer when you notice any unusual or unexpected transactions or updates made in their CPF account. Learn how to differentiate notifications you receive as a Trusted Contact from notifications meant for your own CPF account.

questions.title: What is the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
CPF Safety Switch is a security feature that allows you to immediately secure your CPF account if you suspect you have fallen victim to a scam.
Upon activation, the CPF Safety Switch will stop in-progress withdrawals meant to be credited to your Registered Bank Account, and prevent any future withdrawals from your CPF account, while disabling access to CPF online services through the CPF website and mobile app.

questions.title: What is the difference between CPF Safety Switch and CPF Withdrawal Lock?
questions.text:
While both measures effectively disable online CPF withdrawals, the CPF Safety Switch also prevents online access to your CPF account and stops all disbursements to your registered bank account from our records.
Hence, we encourage you to only activate the CPF Safety Switch if you suspect you have fallen victim to a scam. Doing so will immediately cease any unintended monetary outflows and prevent informational loss in the event that your Singpass has been compromised.
If you wish to protect yourself against scams and do not need to withdraw immediately, consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock instead which will allow you to maintain your online access to your CPF account.

questions.title: What is the Trusted Contact notification service?
questions.text:
Trusted Contact notification service is a digital service that allows you to appoint a trusted individual, such as a family member to receive a copy of your notifications whenever important transactions and updates occur in your CPF account.
Please refer to the list of notifications that are copied to your Trusted Contact to see what information they can view.

questions.title: What security measures should I take when I transact using my cpf digital services?
questions.text: Please refer to the e-Security Guidelines for useful tips on transacting online with us.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: What services do CPF volunteers NOT provide?
questions.text:
CPF volunteers do not:
call members
make unannounced house visits or door-to-door calls
collect money, CPF-related payments, or personal information
request personal login details and passwords
sell financial products or provide investment advice
Should you encounter any of these attempts, do not engage with them and report it via the whistleblowing form.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: What should I do after deactivating the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
For security reasons, the bank account you previously registered with CPF Board would be removed when the CPF Safety Switch was activated. Your bank account will not be automatically reinstated after deactivating the CPF Safety Switch, as your bank account may also have been compromised.
In order to receive CPF payments to your bank account again, you will need to register your bank account with CPF Board. You may also wish to review your registered contact details to ensure that they are up to date. If you are not intending to withdraw soon, you may consider lowering your Daily Withdrawal Limit or activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock.
Find out more about updating your registered bank account, Daily Withdrawal Limit, and activation of CPF Withdrawal Lock. Please note that increasing the Daily Withdrawal Limit, updating your contact details and registering a PayNow-NRIC linked bank account will require a 12-hour cooling period. All other bank account updates will generally take up to two working days to be activated after your bank confirms that the account belongs to you.

questions.title: What should I do if I wish to amend my Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text:
If your Trusted Contact appointee has not accepted your request and you wish to change the appointee, you can do so by withdrawing your appointment request and submitting a new one.
To withdraw the request:
Go to your Activities page and locate the pending request that you wish to withdraw. The “Add or remove Trusted Contact” transaction should still be “In-Progress”.
Click into the “In-progress” transaction record and click the “Withdraw this request” button at the bottom of the page.
If your Trusted Contact request has been accepted, you will not be able to withdraw your appointment. Instead, you will need to remove the existing Trusted Contact appointment first. You may do so via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form before submitting a new appointment request. Your Trusted Contact will be notified of the changes.

questions.title: What transactions/services are affected when the CPF Safety Switch is activated?
questions.text:
While the CPF Safety Switch is active:
Access to your CPF online services will be disabled
All in-progress withdrawals will be stopped, and you will not be able to make any further withdrawals
Disbursements to your registered bank account will be stopped
You can only obtain information related to your CPF account at CPF Service Centre
Please note that CPF contributions and recurring payments to third-party organisations will not be affected by the CPF Safety Switch. In order to regain access to these services, find out more about deactivating the CPF Safety Switch.

questions.title: When should I activate CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text: Please activate the CPF Safety Switch only if you suspect you have fallen victim to a scam. Activating the CPF Safety Switch will stop in-progress withdrawals meant to be credited to your Registered Bank Account, and disables online access to your CPF account. This would help to mitigate monetary losses and safeguard your personal data. Do note that deactivation of Safety Switch will take around three to five working days.

questions.title: Where can I see an overview of my Trusted Contact appointment and appointment requests?
questions.text:
You may view your appointed Trusted Contacts at the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings. Only Trusted Contacts who have accepted your appointment request will be listed under “Your Trusted Contacts”. For pending appointment requests, you may track the status via your Activities page. Pending requests have the “In-Progress” transaction status.
If someone has appointed you as their Trusted Contacts, you will be able to see the pending request(s) under “Added you as a Trusted Contact” in the Account settings – Trusted Contacts section.

questions.title: Who can activate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text: The CPF Safety Switch is available to members aged 55 and above, as it is meant to help members who are eligible to withdraw their CPF savings safeguard their CPF savings when they suspect they have fallen victim to a scam.

questions.title: Who can appoint a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can appoint a Trusted Contact if you are:
A CPF member aged 21 and above; and
A Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (with Singpass account); and
Have at least a Singapore-registered mobile number or email address registered with CPF Board.

questions.title: Who can I appoint as my Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You should only appoint someone you trust, such as a family member, to help monitor important CPF transactions as an additional layer of security against potential scams.
Your Trusted Contact must:
Be a CPF member aged 21 and above;
Be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (with Singpass account); and
Have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board.

questions.title: Why am I not allowed to appoint more than two Trusted Contacts?
questions.text: Your Trusted Contacts help to protect your CPF account by helping to detect any unexpected activity in your CPF account. The two-person limit is designed to provide optimal protection from potential scams while keeping your CPF information within a close, trusted circle. We encourage you to carefully select your most reliable and trusted contacts, ensuring focused and effective monitoring of your CPF transactions for suspicious activities.

questions.title: Why am I receiving SMSes from the CPF Board with the sender ID 'gov.sg'?
questions.text: The Singapore Government has launched a new security measure – ‘gov.sg’, a single SMS Sender ID to be used across Government agencies. This is to help the public identify authentic Government communications sent by SMSes, and safeguard themselves against Government Official Impersonation Scams. The ‘gov.sg’ SMS Sender ID will be used by all Government agencies from 1 July 2024.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: Why do I need my appointee to accept the Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text: A Trusted Contact will receive copies of your notifications when you make important transactions and updates in your CPF account. As the role of Trusted Contact is a voluntary one, your appointee must understand their role before accepting your appointment request.

questions.title: Why do I need to have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board to be a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
As an appointed Trusted Contact, you play an important role in helping to protect your appointer from potential scams. You will receive a copy of the notifications sent to your appointer when they make important transactions and updates to their CPF account.
It is crucial for Trusted Contacts to spot and flag any unusual or unexpected activities in your appointer’s CPF account. As such, you would need to maintain both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address with CPF Board, so that you can receive your appointers’ notifications via both channels and take timely action.

questions.title: Why do I need to maintain contact details to use the Trusted Contact notification service?
questions.text:
You will receive SMS and email notifications whenever there are changes to the status of your Trusted Contact appointment. To ensure you receive these alerts and can detect any unauthorised modifications, you need to register or update your contact details under Account settings.
Keeping your contact details up to date is crucial for your account security, as it ensures you receive timely notifications for your account activities. Regularly reviewing your contact details, especially after changing phone numbers or email addresses, helps maintain your account security.

questions.title: Why do I need to provide the Name and NRIC number of my appointee in the Trusted Contact appointment form?
questions.text: Providing the Name and NRIC number of your appointee helps CPF Board correctly identify the person you wish to appoint as your Trusted Contact. CPF Board will also check if your appointee is eligible to be a Trusted Contact.

questions.title: Why is my appointed Trusted Contact not allowed to view my CPF account balances / statements? Why are they not allowed to transact using my CPF account?
questions.text:
As the account holder, you maintain complete control over your CPF account. This is of critical importance as your CPF account holds your retirement savings and payout arrangements.
Your Trusted Contact can only receive key transaction information through notifications to help you monitor for suspicious transactions - they cannot view your full CPF account details, make transactions, or change any account settings on your behalf. This ensures your Trusted Contact can help identify suspicious transactions while your account privacy remains protected.

questions.title: Why is the Trusted Contact notified when the appointer makes a withdrawal transaction?
questions.text:
Scammers may deceive victims into withdrawing their CPF savings or attempt to withdraw victims’ CPF savings if they obtain unauthorised access to the victims’ CPF accounts. Therefore, it is crucial for Trusted Contacts to be alerted when such a transaction is made.
Learn more about scammers’ latest tactics, and tips to help your loved ones safeguard themselves against scams.

questions.title: Why is there a 12-hour cooling period?
questions.text:
The 12-hour cooling period is a safeguard that provides members sufficient time to take action to prevent any unauthorised adjustments to the CPF online Daily Withdrawal Limit, or changes to important personal information and bank account details from taking effect. The 12-hour duration is aligned with industry practice.
To minimise any delays when making withdrawals, we advise you to plan ahead and regularly ensure that your bank account and contact details are updated with the Board.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: Why should I appoint a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
Anyone can fall prey to scams or have their personal devices compromised by malicious software. When life gets busy, it becomes easy to overlook suspicious interactions.
By receiving a copy of your transaction notifications, your Trusted Contact provides an additional layer of scrutiny for your CPF transactions. Your Trusted Contact can spot unusual or unexpected activities that you might miss and alert you promptly, allowing for early intervention to potentially mitigate losses.
Please refer to the list of notifications that are copied to your Trusted Contact to see what information they can view.

questions.title: Will my Trusted Contact(s) be held accountable if they fail to notify me about the unusual or unexpected transactions in my CPF account?
questions.text:
Although your Trusted Contact(s) will receive a copy of your CPF transaction notifications, they cannot be held accountable if they do not alert you to unusual or unexpected activities. You remain responsible for all activities which take place through the use of your Singpass, and for managing your CPF account.
Apart from appointing a Trusted Contact, the CPF Board strongly encourages you to update your contact details so that you can be notified when transactions occur in your CPF account. You can also download CPF Mobile on your mobile device and turn on push notifications to receive alerts on transactions performed in your CPF account.

questions.title: Will the appointer be informed when I accept or decline their Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text: Yes, the person who has appointed you as their Trusted Contact will be notified via email, SMS and push notifications (if enabled) when you accept or decline their Trusted Contact appointment request.

questions.title: What is the maximum amount of top-ups I can receive?
questions.text:
The maximum amount of top-ups you can receive depends on your age and your CPF savings. You can easily check your top-up limit in the “Top-ups” section of your Retirement Dashboard.
If you are below 55, you can refer to the “Maximum amount you can top up using cash” to reach the Current Full Retirement Sum.
If you are 55 or above, you can refer to the “Maximum amount you can top up using cash” to reach the Current Enhanced Retirement Sum.
Here is a breakdown of how the maximum top-up amount is calculated:

2 Excludes, generally, interest earned and includes retirement withdrawals.
You can refer to these examples on how the maximum top-up amount is computed.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How much CPF payouts can I get every month?
questions.text:
Your monthly payout amount depends on the amount of savings in your Retirement Account (RA) and your age at the point you start your payouts. Under CPF LIFE, you can receive up to $3,440 per month for life starting from age 65. For each year that you defer, your payouts will increase by up to 7%. This means that you can receive up to $4,580 if you choose to start your payout at age 70. You can use the Retirement Payout Planner to estimate how much you need every month to support the retirement lifestyle you want and project your CPF payout based on your CPF balances.
The table below provides a reference on how much you will receive under the CPF LIFE1 Standard Plan based on the amount of savings in your RA at age 55, if you start your monthly payouts from age 65 or 70.

questions.title: How can I check my top-up limits?
questions.text:
You can check your top-up limit in your Retirement Dashboard.
Find out how the top up limit is computed.

questions.title: What is the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)?
questions.text:
The Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) in 2026 is $440,800. This is the maximum amount that members aged 55 and above can top up their Retirement Accounts (RA) to in 2026. From 1 January 2026, the ERS amount is double the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS) and provides members the option to top up more for higher payouts.
The ERS amount is not dependent on your age or the year you turn 55 years old. It increases yearly on 1 January. Here are the ERS amounts for 2026 to 2027.
Year
2026

$440,800

You can top up more to your RA every year when the ERS increases. To illustrate, a member aged 55 and above in 2026 would be able to top up to $440,800. In 2027, when the ERS is increased to $456,400 the member will be able to top up a further $15,600 (i.e. $456,400 - $440,800).
You can top up your RA with cash or your Ordinary Account (OA) savings. Topping up your RA allows you to receive higher monthly payouts in retirement. This allows members to get higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts through CPF top-ups. For example, a member who is 55 in the current year could receive up to $3,440 monthly for life when they turn 65. Learn more about the payouts you can receive if you top up to the ERS.
You may check the maximum amount you can top up on your Retirement Dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Will I still receive the full matching grant of $2,000 if my retirement savings exceed the current Basic Retirement Sum after topping up?
questions.text: Yes, you will receive the full matching grant of $2,000 as long as you are eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme for the year, and the total amount of cash top-ups you received was at least $2,000.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How will I receive my payouts?
questions.text:
You will receive your payouts through your PayNow-NRIC linked account, GIRO or GovCash. You are encouraged to link your NRIC to PayNow to receive your payouts earlier.
For step-by-step guidance on setting up your PayNow-NRIC account, please visit: CPFB | What is PayNow and how do I link my NRIC to PayNow?

questions.title: What happens to my savings used for CPF LIFE when I pass away? Will it go to my beneficiaries?
questions.text:
Upon your passing, your CPF LIFE premium balance and any remaining balances in your CPF accounts will be paid to your beneficiaries. The remaining CPF LIFE premium balance refers to the amount of Retirement Account (RA) savings deducted for the CPF LIFE premium when you joined CPF LIFE minus the total amount of CPF LIFE payouts you received during your lifetime.
*Not applicable to members under the CPF LIFE Income Plan, which does not have a refund feature. As such, beneficiaries will not receive any unused CPF LIFE premium balance upon the member's passing.
Refer to the infographic for detailed examples of how the CPF LIFE premium balance amount is computed, as well as steps to check your CPF LIFE premium balance in the Retirement Dashboard.
You can also access the following links for more information:
Retirement Dashboard: Check your CPF LIFE policy details, including your premium balance.
CPF Nomination: Make a CPF nomination to ensure your savings are distributed according to your wishes quickly.
Check CPF Nomination Details: Review or update your CPF nomination details.

questions.title: Can I withdraw my CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments when I reach 55 years old?
questions.text:
A. If you have set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account, you can apply to withdraw your CPFIS by closing your CPF Investment Account with your agent bank and ceasing your participation under the CPFIS. To apply, please submit your application through the Investment dashboard. After submission, your agent bank and/or product providers will proceed with the following actions:
Convert the investments in your CPF Investment Account under CPFIS-OA or investments under the CPFIS-SA to cash investments, to be held in your personal accounts with the respective product providers / CDP*. Should you subsequently liquidate your investments, the sale proceeds will be paid to you directly.
Close the CPF Investment Account with agent bank and pay out the balance (if any) in the CPF Investment Account in cash to you.
*Your agent bank would require you to provide your personal Central Depository (Pte) Ltd (CDP) account number to facilitate the transfer of any exchange-traded products. Do note that CDP imposes a transfer fee of $10.00 (excluding GST) for every exchange-traded product counter transferred from your CPF Investment Account to your CDP personal account.
Generally, the agent banks/product providers will take about 1- 2 weeks for processing. Once withdrawn, your CPFIS investments and cash balance in your CPF Investment Account will no longer be protected from any claims by your creditors and/or the Official Assignee.
B. If you have not set aside the FRS in your Retirement Account, you would not be able to withdraw your CPFIS investments. However, you can still liquidate the investment holdings under your CPF Investment Account. The sale proceeds will be credited to your CPF Investment Account and thereafter returned to your CPF Ordinary Account. If you had used your Special Account for the investments, once the investments are liquidated, the sale proceeds will be credited to your Retirement Account up to the FRS, with any remaining balance paid to your CPF Ordinary Account.
As long as you do not have investment holdings in your CPF Investment Account, you can instruct your agent bank to close your Investment Account. See this FAQ for more details.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I withdraw my CPF savings before I turn 55?
questions.text: You can apply to withdraw your CPF savings earlier if you have a medical condition that reduces your life expectancy or causes you to be permanently unfit for work or lack mental capacity permanently.

questions.title: How much CPF savings can I withdraw from age 55 to 64?
questions.text:
You can check the CPF savings you can withdraw from age 55 by logging into your Retirement dashboard.
The amount that you can withdraw is determined as follows:
If you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), fully in cash or with a mixture of property and cash:
You can withdraw any amount from your Ordinary Account (OA)
If you have not set aside your FRS:
You can withdraw $5,000 from your OA
Upon your withdrawal, non-withdrawable amounts in your OA may be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to make up your FRS. This transfer occurs with each withdrawal until you have set aside your FRS.
For example: John turned 55 in 2026 with $100,000 in his RA and $5,000 in his OA. His OA savings later grew by $2,000 from contributions and interest earned, bringing the total to $7,000. As he has not set aside his FRS of $220,400, he can only withdraw up to $5,000 from his OA. The remaining $2,000 in his OA cannot be withdrawn and will be transferred to his RA subsequently to help him set aside his FRS.
You can withdraw an additional amount of your retirement savings from 65. The amount you can withdraw depends on your birth year and generally excludes any cash top-ups, CPF transfers and government grants.

questions.title: How much Retirement Account savings do I need for my desired CPF LIFE monthly payout?
questions.text: You can easily use the Monthly payout estimator to estimate the amount of Retirement Account savings you need, based on your desired monthly payout and choice of payout start age.

questions.title: What are the retirement sums - Basic Retirement Sum (BRS), Full Retirement Sum (FRS) and Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)?
questions.text:
The CPF Retirement Sum is the principal amount1 of savings in your CPF Retirement Account (RA). The more savings you have in your RA, the higher your monthly payouts will be in retirement.
There are three Retirement Sum reference points to guide you on the Retirement Sum to set aside based on your retirement needs.
Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) provides you monthly payouts for basic living needs, excluding rental expenses2.
Full Retirement Sum (FRS) is double your BRS and is the default amount to set aside in your RA when you turn 55.
Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) is double the current year’s FRS and is the maximum amount you can top up to your RA if you are aged 55 and above. The ERS increases yearly, and topping up to the current year’s ERS allows you to get the highest CPF monthly payouts.
If you are age 55 and above, visit the Retirement Dashboard to find out whether you have set aside your FRS and the amount you can top up to your RA for higher monthly payouts.
1This includes CPF contributions, top-ups and transfers from other CPF accounts to the RA, but generally excludes government grants. Interest earned on RA savings is excluded.
2If you own a property in Singapore with remaining lease that lasts you until you are 95 or older, you may apply to withdraw RA savings down to your BRS.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Who can join CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
All CPF members can join CPF LIFE anytime from age 65. The latest age to join CPF LIFE is one month before age 80.
There is no minimum CPF savings required to join, but the amount of payout you get is dependent on your Retirement Account balances when you join CPF LIFE.
You will be automatically included in CPF LIFE when you start your CPF monthly payouts if you were born on or after 1 January 1958 and have at least $60,000 in your CPF retirement savings when you start your monthly payouts.
If you are not automatically included in CPF LIFE, you can still choose to join the scheme.
Tip: Use the Monthly payout estimator to see which LIFE plan suits you and see the estimated monthly payout based on your choice. Consider topping up your retirement savings in your Retirement Account(RA), to increase your monthly payouts.

questions.title: Can I apply for ComCare assistance if I have refunded my SIRS payout?
questions.text:
Low-income households that are unable to afford their basic living expenses can approach MSF’s Social Service Offices (SSOs) to apply for ComCare.
If you need financial assistance, you may email Ask_SSO@msf.gov.sg, call the ComCare hotline at 1800-222-0000, or approach the nearest Social Service Office.

questions.title: Can I change my plan type after I have joined CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
You can request to change your CPF LIFE plan type within 30 days from the date of your first* policy letter. If you wish to do so, please write to us.
Currently, the Board is granting concessions to allow plan changes beyond the 30-day grace period for the following members:
Original plan (Basic, Balanced, Plus or Income Plan) members who are concerned about a drop in their monthly payouts can change to the Escalating or Standard Plan.
Original and Standard Plan members who are concerned about a reducing retirement lifestyle as prices rise can change to the Escalating Plan.
Otherwise, changing of CPF LIFE plan after the grace period is not allowed as this will affect the payouts of other members on the scheme.
As changing of CPF LIFE plan is irrevocable, we encourage you to consider your options carefully.
*The letter sent to you when your original CPF LIFE plan was first issued.

questions.title: How can I make monthly transfers of my CPF employment contributions from my Ordinary Account to Retirement Account?
questions.text:
If you are aged 55 and above and would like to transfer your monthly CPF employment contributions regularly from your Ordinary Account (OA) to Retirement Account (RA), you can do so by setting up recurring CPF transfers . With this recurring transfer service, you can conveniently earn higher interest on your CPF employment contributions credited to your OA and build up your retirement savings in your RA.
Upon successful application, your recurring transfer will take effect from the following month on the 18th.
Please note that CPF transfers are irreversible. The savings are set aside to boost your monthly payouts in retirement and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How does the CPF LIFE Basic Plan work?
questions.text:
The CPF LIFE Basic Plan provides payouts that will get lower when the CPF balances drop below $60,000. It is suitable if you do not mind lowering your lifestyle as prices increase over time. Consider the Escalating or Standard Plans if you want to generally maintain your desired lifestyle or receive higher-level payouts.
Premium
New CPF LIFE members: When you join CPF LIFE, about 10% to 20% of your Retirement Account (RA) savings will be used as your CPF LIFE premium.
Existing CPF LIFE members: When you receive additional inflows into your RA after starting payouts, it will automatically increase your CPF LIFE premium if the revised monthly payouts increase by at least $10.
Generally, the proportion of RA savings deducted for CPF LIFE increases with age. We will notify you of the exact RA savings deducted and your revised monthly payouts.
Your CPF LIFE premium will continue to earn the CPF interest rates, which are factored into your monthly payouts. This allows you to receive higher payouts from the start, compared to if there were no interest earned.
Monthly Payouts
Your monthly payouts are calculated based on various factors and will be paid to you for as long as you live.
CPF LIFE works by risk-pooling, like other forms of insurance. The pooling of interest earned on the CPF LIFE premiums enables members to receive lifelong payouts.
For the CPF LIFE Basic Plan, your CPF LIFE monthly payouts will first be paid from your RA savings until age 90. Thereafter, you will receive the monthly payout from your CPF LIFE premium.
Your RA savings that are first used for your monthly payouts will continue to earn 4% interest, with an extra interest of up to 2% earned on the first $60,000 of your CPF balances (across all your CPF accounts). This interest is paid to your RA and included in your monthly payouts. As your RA savings are gradually withdrawn to provide you with monthly payouts, the extra interest you earn will decrease when the total balances fall below $60,000. Your monthly payout will then get progressively lower as the extra interest earned decreases over time.
Premium Balance
Upon your passing, your remaining CPF LIFE premium balance will be paid to your beneficiaries.

questions.title: How does the CPF LIFE Standard Plan work?
questions.text:
The CPF LIFE Standard Plan provides level payouts for life. It is suitable if you are comfortable with buying less and maintaining a modest lifestyle to cope with rising prices.
Compared to the CPF LIFE Escalating Plan, the Standard Plan provides higher payouts at the start, but don’t increase over time to keep up with the rising prices. Hence, the payouts will eventually be lower than Escalating Plan payouts.
Premium
All your Retirement Account (RA) savings will be used as your CPF LIFE premium when you join CPF LIFE.
Subsequent inflows into your RA after starting the monthly payout will automatically increase your CPF LIFE premium and monthly payouts.
Your CPF LIFE premium will continue to earn CPF interest rates, which is factored into your monthly payouts. This allows you to receive higher payouts from the start, compared to if there were no interests earned.
Monthly Payouts
Your monthly payouts are calculated based on various factors and will be paid to you for as long as you live.
CPF LIFE works by risk-pooling, like other forms of insurance. The pooling of interest earned on the CPF LIFE premiums enables members to receive lifelong payouts.
Premium Balance
Upon your passing, your remaining CPF LIFE premium balance will be paid to your beneficiaries.
