questions.title: What are the CPF LIFE plans available and which is the right plan for me?
questions.text:
There are three CPF LIFE plans to choose from – Escalating Plan, Standard Plan and Basic Plan.
Do plan for your retirement with inflation in mind. For example, if your monthly expenditure is $1,000 today, you may need about $1,500 monthly payouts to maintain the same lifestyle in 20 years’ time. Choose your CPF LIFE plan based on how willing you are to adjust your retirement lifestyle, as things become more expensive.
If you are worried about the rising costs of living, you can consider the Escalating Plan which provides monthly payouts that start lower initially but grow by 2% every year for life. The growing payouts protects you against inflation and generally helps you maintain your retirement lifestyle. Read more about how the CPF LIFE Escalating Plan works.
If you are willing to live a more modest lifestyle and buy less as years pass, you may find the Standard Plan which provides steady payouts suitable for you. Payouts do not grow to protect you against inflation so you'll have to lower your lifestyle to buy less as things get more expensive in the years ahead. Payouts start higher than the Escalating Plan, but will eventually become lower than the Escalating Plan. Read more about how the CPF LIFE Standard Plan works.
If you don’t mind starting with lower monthly payouts which will be lower later on, then the Basic Plan is good enough. The Basic Plan is an original plan carried over from the time CPF LIFE was first introduced in 2009. Compared to the Standard Plan which gives higher and steady monthly payouts, Basic Plan payouts are lower and will get lower when your combined CPF balances eventually fall below $60,000. Read more about how the CPF LIFE Basic Plan works.
In all three plans, you will enjoy payouts no matter how long you live, your premiums will enjoy risk-free CPF interest rates, and any remaining CPF LIFE premium balance will be given to your beneficiaries, together with your remaining CPF savings when you pass on. In other words, you and your loved ones will always get back the premium that you have put into CPF LIFE.

questions.title: What will happen to my CPF savings when my monthly payouts start?
questions.text:
If you are born on or after 1958, the following will happen when your monthly payouts start:
Transfer of Ordinary Account savings: If you have not set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), your Ordinary Account savings will be transferred to your Retirement Account to make up your FRS in cash. This will help you receive higher payouts.
CPF LIFE premium deduction: When you join CPF LIFE, your Retirement Account (RA) savings will be used to pay your CPF LIFE premium. Your premium will continue to earn interest and the interest earned will be factored into your lifetime monthly payouts.
Additional withdrawable amount of up to 20% of RA savings at 65: Up to 20% of your RA savings at 65 will be available for your immediate withdrawable from age 65. If this withdrawable amount is not withdrawn nor used to increase your payouts, it will be transferred to your Ordinary Account for future cash withdrawals.

questions.title: Can I choose how much I want to withdraw from my retirement savings if I have an alternative pension/annuity?
questions.text: The amount that can be withdrawn from your retirement savings will depend on the monthly payout you are receiving from your pension/annuity. You can withdraw your retirement savings in full if the pension/ annuity monthly payout is more than the minimum monthly payout.

questions.title: Can I choose to retain my Ordinary Account savings instead of automatically disbursing them as payouts when my Retirement Account is depleted?
questions.text:
No, you cannot choose to retain your Ordinary Account (OA) savings. CPF is designed to provide you with an income in retirement. The auto-disbursement of your OA savings ensures that you continue to receive a steady stream of retirement income even when your Retirement Account has been depleted.
With the monthly payouts, you also have greater flexibility for your daily living expenses or your monthly housing instalments (if applicable).
If you wish to retain the monies in your CPF accounts to earn higher interest, you should consider options outside of CPF.

questions.title: Can I request a higher CPF LIFE monthly payout based on my current Retirement Account balance?
questions.text:
If there are no new inflows into your Retirement Account (RA), we are unable to increase your CPF LIFE monthly payout. This is because CPF LIFE payouts are determined by an independent actuarial consultant based on various factors, including your RA savings used to join CPF LIFE.
Find out how changes to your RA can affect your monthly payouts

questions.title: Can I still make top-ups or receive top-ups to my retirement savings if I have withdrawn my savings using my pension/annuity?
questions.text: No, you cannot top up or receive top-ups to your retirement savings if you have already withdrawn your retirement savings using your pension/annuity. However, you can top up your retirement savings if you choose to join CPF LIFE.

questions.title: Can I top up my retirement savings to the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)?
questions.text:
If you are aged 55 or above, you have the option to top up your Retirement Account (RA) up to the current year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) as retirement becomes an even higher priority.
If you are aged below 55, you can start building up more retirement savings by topping up your Special Account up to the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS). Once you reach age 55, you can then choose to set aside more in your RA, up to the current year’s ERS.
You can check your top-up limit on your Retirement Dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Do I need to top up my Retirement Account and will I receive monthly payouts if I am unable to set aside my Full Retirement Sum?
questions.text:
It is not mandatory for you to top up your Retirement Account (RA) if you are unable to set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). You can still receive monthly payouts anytime from your payout eligibility age, and the payout amount will be based on your RA savings.
However, you may wish to top up your RA for higher monthly payouts. You can also enjoy tax relief for cash top-ups up to the FRS.
Did you know? You can use the Monthly payout estimator to estimate how much you need to top up to reach your desired monthly payouts.
If you receive contributions, government grants or other refunds in your CPF accounts after 55, they will be transferred to your RA up to your FRS (or Basic Retirement Sum if you own a property) on your next withdrawal.
If you are born in 1958 or after and wish to start your monthly payouts, there will be another transfer of your Ordinary Account (OA) savings, up to your FRS, to your RA, if you have not met your FRS. This transfer allows you to receive higher monthly payouts.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: How are the CPF LIFE payouts calculated?
questions.text:
CPF LIFE payouts are computed based on the following factors:
FactorHow it affects your monthly payout
Your Retirement Account (RA) balance when you join CPF LIFEYour RA savings are used to pay for the CPF LIFE premium. The higher your RA balance when you join CPF LIFE, the higher your payout will be.
When you start payouts For each year that you defer starting payouts, your payouts will increase by up to 7%.
CPF interest ratesCPF LIFE payouts factor in the CPF interest rate, with a floor of 4%, and up to 2% extra interest on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances.
Life expectancy / Mortality rates
Since CPF LIFE pays monthly payouts for life, longer life expectancies would result in lower monthly payouts as the payout duration is longer on average.
Hence, males receive higher payouts compared to females as they have a shorter average life expectancy.

questions.title: How can I change the amount or delete my recurring CPF transfer arrangement?
questions.text:
You can change the amount of your existing recurring CPF transfer arrangement by following the steps below:
Delete your existing recurring CPF transfer arrangement in the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form.
Create a new recurring CPF transfer arrangement via the same form with the revised amount. The transfer will take effect from the following month on the 18th upon successful application.
You can delete your existing recurring CPF transfer arrangement via the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form.
Your deletion application will generally be processed instantly. For example, if you delete your recurring CPF transfer arrangement on 17 May, no transfer will take place on 18 May.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my existing recurring cash top-up arrangements?
questions.text: You can check your existing recurring cash top-up arrangements, including the recipients, amount of cash top-ups, and frequency (monthly or yearly) by accessing the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form, under “Who you are making recurring top-ups to”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I check the status of my cash top-up and/or CPF transfer application?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your online application via Activities. Once your cash top-up and/or CPF transfer application is successful, you will be able to find the details of the transaction on your Retirement Dashboard under the Retirement Sum Topping-Up History section.
If you have submitted multiple applications, you can also review the status of each application under Activities. This will help you identify which transactions have been successfully processed, and you can also submit a new application if necessary.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How long will my monthly payouts last if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
If you are not automatically included CPF LIFE and did not opt to join CPF LIFE to enjoy lifelong payouts, you will receive monthly payouts which will stop when your CPF savings run out. Your monthly payouts are calculated to last you up to 20 years, with the extra interest earned on your retirement savings helping to extend the payout duration up to 90 years old.
Find out how can I prolong my monthly payouts if I am not on CPF LIFE?

questions.title: How will the top-ups to my retirement savings be used?
questions.text:
Top-ups to your Special or Retirement Account will form part of your retirement sum. If you are on CPF LIFE, top-ups will increase your CPF LIFE monthly payouts. If you are not on CPF LIFE, top-ups will allow you to receive higher payouts or receive payouts for a longer time.
As such, top-up monies cannot be withdrawn as a lump sum, withdrawn from your Retirement Account savings using property, or transferred to your loved ones.
Additionally, top-up monies cannot be used for other CPF schemes, such as withdrawal for immediate retirement needs, withdrawal on exemption from setting aside a retirement sum, and other CPF schemes for education, investment, insurance, housing etc.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How will topping up my Special or Retirement Account increase my CPF LIFE monthly payouts?
questions.text:
If you are on CPF LIFE, the top-ups to your Special or Retirement Account will be used for your CPF LIFE premium in order to increase your CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
The extent of increase depends on a few factors including your age when you make the top-up. The earlier you make the top-up, the more your monthly payouts will increase. This is because your top-up amount grows with compound interest over time, which means it earns interest, and then that interest also starts earning interest.
Here are some examples of the expected increase in payouts:
One-Time Top-Ups:
A $2,000 top-up made at age 65 will increase your monthly payout by about $10*.
The same $2,000 top-up made at age 25 will increase your monthly payout by about $50.
Regular Monthly Top-Ups of $100:
Monthly top-ups from age 55 to 65 (over 10 years) will result in an increase of about $70 in your monthly payout.
Monthly top-ups from age 25 to 35 (over 10 years) will result in an increase of about $240 in your monthly payout.
For personalised estimates, use the CPF Retirement Payout Planner. This tool helps you project your monthly CPF payouts in retirement and simulate the effect of different top-up amounts on your monthly payout.
*The actual revision may take up to two months following your top-up, and we will notify you on the changes in your monthly payouts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I am on one of the original CPF LIFE plans (Basic, Balanced, Plus or Income). Can I change to one of the newer plans (Standard or Escalating)?
questions.text:
The Basic, Balanced, Plus and Income plans were introduced when CPF LIFE was first launched in 2009. Under these plans, extra interest earned on the first $60,000 of your CPF balances is credited to your Retirement Account (RA) and factored into your monthly payouts. As your balances are withdrawn over time to provide you with monthly payouts, the amount of monthly payouts and extra interest will decrease when your balances fall below $60,000.
If you are currently on any of the above original plans, you have the option to change to either the Escalating Plan or Standard Plan. Changing to the Escalating Plan will provide you with increasing payouts over time, while changing to the Standard Plan will provide you with level payouts. You can make the change anytime.
It is important to note that:
Once you have changed to the Standard or Escalating Plan, you cannot change back to an original plan.
All your RA savings, including the premium refunded from your original plan, will be deducted as CPF LIFE premium when the Standard or Escalating Plan is issued to you.

questions.title: I do not wish to wait for the next automatic transfer of non-withdrawable monies from my Ordinary Account to my Retirement Account. Can I perform the transfer manually and boost my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
Yes, you can. Here are the steps to perform the transfer of your non-withdrawable monies from your Ordinary Account (OA) to your Retirement Account:
1) Access the Plan my monthly payouts service.
2) Under ‘Use more CPF savings to increase payouts’ in the second page, select the OA amount to be transferred to increase your CPF LIFE payout.
You may perform the above any time, as long as you have monies in your OA.

questions.title: I have made a PayNow QR payment but I am not able to see an immediate update to my CPF balance(s). Why is my CPF account balance(s) not updated immediately?
questions.text: Such cases are extremely rare and may arise due to intermittent network connectivity issues beyond CPF Board's control. As a result, the status of your PayNow payment may be delayed, and your CPF account balance(s) may not be updated instantly. Please do not worry as your CPF account balance(s) will be updated within 3-5 working days and you will receive an email notification if you have registered your email address with us. Please check your CPF account balance(s)/E-form status again after 3-5 working days and alert us immediately if your payment is still not updated.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: If I am eligible to receive monthly payouts under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, when will the monthly payouts be paid to me?
questions.text: The monthly payouts of all members are deducted on the 2nd of the month, and the crediting of the monthly payouts to members’ bank accounts will depend on the bank's processing time. You will receive the monthly payouts in your bank account generally by the 4th working day of the month. You will generally receive your payouts earlier if your bank supports Fast And Secure Transfer (FAST).

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of top-ups I can make or receive in a year?
questions.text:
There is no limit to the number of top-ups you can make or receive as long as the recipient can still receive top-ups.
It is important to note that once you make a top-up, it cannot be reversed. Therefore, we advise you to review that you have sufficient cash or CPF savings for other expenses before making the top-up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What happens if I have used my CPF savings to pay for my home and do not have enough CPF savings left to set aside Full Retirement Sum when I turn 55?
questions.text:
You can set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with a mixture of CPF savings in your Retirement Account (RA) and CPF savings used for your property. At age 55, if your RA savings is less than your FRS, the CPF savings used for your property (including accrued interest) will automatically be counted towards meeting up to half of your FRS.
For example: John turns 55 in 2025 and has $113,000 in his RA. He had used $200,000 of his CPF for his property (including accrued interest). His FRS of $213,000 would be set aside with the $113,000 in his RA and $100,000 of the CPF used for his property.
When you sell your property, you will need to refund the CPF savings (including accrued interest) used for your property to your CPF accounts. This will be used to set aside your FRS in cash.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What is CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
The CPF Lifelong Income For The Elderly (CPF LIFE) is a national longevity insurance annuity scheme that insures you against running out of your retirement savings, by providing you with a monthly payout no matter how long you live.
Unlike investment products which are meant to grow our wealth, insurance products, like CPF LIFE, help to protect us against life's uncertainties.
With CPF LIFE, you can have peace of mind knowing that you will have a steady stream of lifelong income to support your retirement needs. This way, you can enjoy your golden years without having to worry about financial uncertainties, no matter what age you live to.

questions.title: What is PayNow QR?
questions.text:
PayNow QR is a convenient and faster way for you to make payments by scanning a QR code using your mobile banking app. It is also secure as it adopts the same high security standards adopted by the Singapore banking industry for fund transfers such as FAST and GIRO.
You can use PayNow QR if you have accounts with any of the following banks in Singapore: Citibank Singapore Limited, DBS Bank/POSB, HSBC, Maybank, OCBC Bank, Standard Chartered Bank, United Overseas Bank, Bank of China, and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is the current Enhanced Retirement Sum?
questions.text:
The current Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) for 2026 is $440,800.
The ERS is increased yearly. For members 55 and above who wish to have higher monthly payouts in retirement, they can top up their Retirement Account up to the current ERS. To find out how much you can top up, log in to your Retirement dashboard.
From 1 January 2025, the ERS was raised to double the current year’s Full Retirement Sum to enable members to voluntarily commit more savings for even higher payouts. This allows members to get higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts of up to $3,440 for life from age 65 through CPF top-ups. Learn more about the payouts you can receive.
Here are the ERS amounts for 2026 to 2027 to enable you to plan your top-ups:
Year
Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)
2026 (Current)
$440,800
2027
$456,400
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What is the latest age to join CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
If you are not automatically included in CPF LIFE, the latest age to join CPF LIFE is one month before you turn 80.
If you are automatically included in CPF LIFE, find out when you have to choose your CPF LIFE plan.

questions.title: What is the maximum amount I can top up via PayNow QR?
questions.text:
The daily transaction limit with PayNow QR is capped at $200,000, which is further subject to monthly and daily transaction limits imposed by your bank.
See guides on how to change your bank’s transfer limits if you need to do so.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When can I start my monthly payouts if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
You have the flexibility to decide when to start your monthly payouts, anytime from 65 to 70.
Note: If you are born before 1958, you are past your payout eligibility age and can choose to start your payouts anytime.

questions.title: When do I have to choose my CPF LIFE plan?
questions.text:
You only need to choose your CPF LIFE plan when you wish to start receiving your CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
If you are automatically included in CPF LIFE, you can start your payouts any time from 65 to 70 and choose your CPF LIFE plan then. If you do not choose a plan before 70, you will be automatically placed on the CPF LIFE Standard Plan and your payouts will start at 70.
If you are not automatically included in CPF LIFE, you can choose your CPF LIFE plan when you wish to join the scheme, any time from 65 to one month before you turn 80.
To help you better decide on which CPF LIFE plan is suitable for you, find out more details on what are the CPF LIFE plans available.

questions.title: When is the best time to top up to grow my savings?
questions.text:
You should top up as early as possible to maximise the growth of your CPF savings through the power of compound interest.
Additionally, you can earn more interest if you top up earlier in the year. For example, if you top up in January each year instead of in December, you can earn up to 20%* more interest on your top-ups in 10 years.
* Based on the current 4% interest rate floor on Special and Retirement Account monies and extra interest of up to 2% per annum on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances, with $8,000 annual top-up and $0 starting balance.
Do top up early in the year to ensure that your top-ups are processed before the year end as the normal processing time may take longer in December if there is a surge in applications.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When will the automatic transfer of non-withdrawable monies from my Ordinary Account to my Retirement Account take place?
questions.text: For members who are eligible, the automatic transfer will take place once a year. You will receive a notification one month before the transfer occurs.

questions.title: Where can I find records of past top-ups made by me?
questions.text: You can view top-ups made by you in the last five years directly from Retirement Savings Topping-Up History under “Given to” tab.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why am I not able to top up my Special/Retirement Account beyond the current Full Retirement Sum (FRS) (below 55) or Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) (55 or above)?
questions.text:
The CPF system is designed to cater to the basic retirement needs of the broad majority of Singaporeans.
If you are below 55, you can top up your Special Account up to the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS) to build up your retirement savings. If you wish to save beyond the FRS, you can choose to tap on the Supplementary Retirement Scheme, where contributions are also eligible for tax relief.
If you are 55 or above, retirement becomes a higher priority. As such, members have the option to voluntarily top up beyond the FRS up to the current year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) for higher payouts. This could help the middle-income group better meet their retirement needs.
Find out more about what the retirement sums are.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why am I not eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme if my retirement savings are above the current Basic Retirement Sum?
questions.text: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is designed to help senior Singapore Citizens with lower retirement savings save more and boost their retirement payouts. If your retirement savings are more than the current Basic Retirement Sum, you will not be eligible for the scheme as it is intended to provide additional support to those who need it the most.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Why is there no tax relief for top-ups made to my children or non-immediate family?
questions.text:
Tax relief is an incentive given to encourage members to build up retirement savings for themselves or their immediate family members, particularly older Singaporeans who may have less retirement savings.
Your children have more time to accumulate savings in their working years for their own retirement needs. Hence, there is no tax relief for top-ups made to your children or non-immediate family members.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why was the cash top-up to my / my loved one's Special or Retirement Account refunded or partially refunded?
questions.text: Your top-up was refunded as you / your loved one had received other inflows at the same time as the cash top-up was made. These inflows had resulted in you / your loved one to meet the current Full Retirement Sum or Enhanced Retirement Sum (for members age 55 or above).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Am I eligible for tax reliefs when I make a cash top-up to my/my loved ones' retirement savings?
questions.text:
You can enjoy tax relief if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident and make cash top-ups* within the current year’s Full Retirement Sum for yourself, your loved ones, employees or platform workers.
Find out more about the amount of tax relief you can enjoy.
Find out more on the conditions to qualify for tax relief.
*From 1 January 2025, givers of cash top-ups that attract the matching grant (up to $2,000 per year) under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) will no longer receive tax relief. Find out more on how this works.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on insurance payout given to my employee?
questions.text: CPF contributions are not payable on insurance payout made by insurer to your employee if he is the insured person and the payout is for his benefit.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on payouts from retirement savings held by a trust fund to my employee who is still in employment?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable on the payouts from funds set aside for pensions or retirement given to your employee who is still in employment with you.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Can I access the Monthly Payout Estimator if I do not have a Singpass?
questions.text:
You will need to log in via Singpass to access the Monthly Payout Estimator.
If you do not have a Singpass account, you can register for one by following the instructions on the Singpass website. Alternatively, if you have questions on your payout amounts, please write to us.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Can I access the Retirement Payout Planner on behalf of my spouse or family member?
questions.text: The Retirement Payout Planner is personalised to each member, so each member will need to log in with their own Singpass to access the planner. If you would like to help your spouse or family member plan for their retirement, you can guide them through the planner while they are logged in to their own Singpass account.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Can I be exempted from CPF LIFE?
questions.text: If you are automatically included under CPF LIFE, you cannot be exempted from CPF LIFE unless you have a pension or commercial annuity that pays the same or higher monthly payout as CPF LIFE. For more information, please refer to the conditions for withdrawing your retirement savings.

questions.title: Can I cancel my CPF LIFE plan after I have joined?
questions.text:
You can only cancel your CPF LIFE plan if you are withdrawing your CPF savings for the following reasons.
You have a reduced life expectancy due to a medical condition, as certified by an accredited doctor. Severe medical conditions that cause you to be permanently unfit for work or to lack mental capacity permanently can also be considered.
You have closed your CPF account as you are a non-Singapore Citizen or a non-Permanent Resident.
You are fully exempted from setting aside the retirement sum in your Retirement Account because you are receiving a monthly pension / annuity payout.
Upon cancellation of your CPF LIFE plan, you will receive a refund of your CPF LIFE premium balance. If your CPF LIFE premium has been fully paid to you as monthly payouts, there will be no remaining premium balance to refund.

questions.title: Can I choose to set aside my Full Retirement Sum with a mixture of property and cash, and withdraw part of my Retirement Account savings if I own a foreign property?
questions.text: No, you are not able to withdraw part of your Retirement Account savings if you own a foreign property. To secure the refund of your CPF savings when your property is sold or transferred in the future, your property must be located in Singapore.

questions.title: Can I continue to use my CPF savings for the property or withdraw my Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum in cash after discharging the CPF charge?
questions.text: No, after the CPF charge is discharged, no further CPF savings can be used for the property. If you are above 55, the property cannot be pledged for the withdrawal of your Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum. If you wish to do so, a new CPF charge is required, and legal costs will be incurred in the creation and lodgement of the new CPF charge.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Voluntary Housing Refund

questions.title: Can I defer my monthly payouts beyond 70 if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
You will not be able to defer your monthly payouts beyond 70. The purpose of your retirement savings is to provide you with a stream of retirement income.
If you have no immediate need for the payouts, you can consider investing them outside the CPF system. Do note that investing outside of CPF carries a certain level of risk and requires careful consideration.

questions.title: Can I defer the start of my CPF LIFE monthly payouts beyond 70?
questions.text:
The purpose of CPF savings is to provide members with monthly payouts in their retirement. Hence, you will have to start your CPF LIFE monthly payouts, including any Additional Monthly Payouts (AMP), latest by age 70.
We understand that some members think of their savings in CPF as an investment to enjoy the interest rates. If you have no immediate need for the payouts, you can consider investing them outside the CPF system. Do note that investing outside of CPF carries a certain level of risk and requires careful consideration.

questions.title: Can I make recurring CPF transfers to my loved ones?
questions.text: The recurring CPF transfer e-Service is currently only available for members aged 55 and above to make CPF transfers to their own Retirement Account. If you wish to make CPF transfer to your loved ones, you may make a one-time CPF transfer instead.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I opt out of receiving CPF monthly payouts and withdraw all my retirement savings?
questions.text: Yes, you can opt out of receiving CPF monthly payouts and withdraw your retirement savings in full if you have other sources of lifelong income. Alternatively, you can consider enjoying lifelong payouts under CPF LIFE, in addition to your other sources of retirement income.

questions.title: Can I retain my Ordinary Account savings instead of having them transferred to my Retirement Account to increase my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
You can retain your Ordinary Account (OA) savings for immediate withdrawal needs if you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account (RA).
If you have not set aside your FRS, your OA savings will be automatically transferred to your RA to provide you with higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
If you have housing obligations, you can use your CPF LIFE monthly payouts or any CPF savings in excess of your FRS to meet these needs.

questions.title: Can I reverse my top-up?
questions.text: No, cash top-ups and CPF transfers are irreversible. The top-ups/CPF transfers to your Special Account or Retirement Account savings earn a higher interest rate as the savings are locked in for the long-term. This is similar to the market practice where the interest earned on fixed deposits is higher compared to interest earned on savings deposits that are withdrawable anytime.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I set up more than one recurring cash top-up arrangement?
questions.text:
Yes, you can make multiple recurring cash top-up arrangements for different recipients. You can add recurring top-up via the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form if you have already set up GIRO to make cash top-ups for retirement.
If you have not set up GIRO to make cash top-ups for retirement, you may do so via this link.
Please note that only one GIRO bank account can be used for your recurring cash top-up arrangements to your various top-up recipients.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I set up yearly CPF transfers from my Ordinary Account to Retirement Account?
questions.text:
The recurring CPF transfer e-Service currently allows monthly CPF transfers only. By setting up recurring CPF transfers, you can easily transfer your monthly CPF working contributions received in your Ordinary Account to your Retirement Account.
If you intend to make a CPF transfer once a year, you may wish to do so via the one-time CPF transfer form.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I share my scheme payout details with my family members and friends?
questions.text:
While you may choose to share the details of your benefits with others, we wish to highlight that such information in “Your Benefits” is private and confidential to you.
We strongly advise against sharing your Singpass credentials or allowing others to access your account directly as this may compromise the security of your Singpass account, which contains many personal details. If you need to share “Your Benefit” details, you should explore other ways such as using a statement screenshot.

questions.title: Can I still receive top-ups if I have started my monthly retirement payouts?
questions.text:
Yes, you can receive top-ups as long as you have not reached the current Enhanced Retirement Sum.
Find out how much top-ups you can receive.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I top up using cash or CPF transfers?
questions.text:
Yes, you can top up your retirement savings using cash or by making CPF transfers. Please take note that CPF transfers do not qualify for tax relief or matching grant from the government under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.
If you wish to increase your own or your loved ones' retirement savings, you can find out more here:
Who you can make top-ups to
Who you can receive top-ups from
How much you can top up via cash
How much you can top up via CPF transfer
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I transfer my top-ups made to my Special Account/ Retirement Account to other CPF accounts if I need to use them for other purposes such as housing or healthcare?
questions.text:
No, such cash top-ups and CPF transfers are meant to boost your retirement savings to enable you to receive higher payouts. Hence, they cannot be used for other purposes or transferred to other CPF accounts such as your Ordinary Account or MediSave Account.
Consider whether you would require the monies for other purposes (e.g. housing or healthcare expenses) before topping up to your Special Account/ Retirement Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I use the Retirement Payout Planner if I am self-employed?
questions.text: Yes, you can. The Retirement Payout Planner is accessible by members from age 16, up to 4 months before turning 65. Self-employed members can input their monthly net taxable income (NTI) under the monthly salary field. As the projections are based on working contributions from employment calculated using the salary figures provided, they may not fully reflect the circumstances of self-employed members.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Can I withdraw the top-up monies if I have the Full Retirement Sum, or the Basic Retirement Sum if I own a property?
questions.text: You will not be able to withdraw the top-up monies as the higher interest rate and tax incentives are given to encourage members to build up their retirement savings. Allowing withdrawals after members have enjoyed these incentives would defeat the purpose of the topping-up scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can parents determine the amount of monthly payouts for their nominated child with disabilities?
questions.text: Parents can determine the amount of monthly payout for their nominated child with disabilities at the point of application, subject to a minimum payout of $250 per month with a minimum duration of at least one year.

questions.title: Does the interest earned on my retirement savings form part of the retirement sum that I am required to set aside at age 55?
questions.text: No, the interest earned on your retirement savings does not form part of the retirement sum that you are required to set aside at 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: How accurate are the projections within the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
The results provided in the Retirement Payout Planner are estimates, based on various assumptions and your inputs. They are meant to facilitate your planning of your CPF retirement savings and payouts, and should not be regarded as advice by CPF Board.
For more information on assumptions used within the Retirement Payout Planner, refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: How are monthly payouts calculated if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
If you are not on CPF LIFE, your monthly payouts are calculated to last for up to 20 years from your Payout Eligibility Age (PEA) – the age at which you can start receiving your monthly payouts, based on the prevailing base interest rate earned on your Retirement Account (RA) savings when you start your payouts.
If you chose to defer your payouts to a later age i.e. up to age 70, your monthly payouts will similarly be calculated to last for up to 20 years from your PEA. This allows you to receive a higher monthly payout.
As Singaporeans live longer, more than half of those aged 65 today are expected to live more than 20 years. To protect you against the risk of outliving your payouts, the extra interest paid by the Government (up to 2% per year) on your retirement savings is used to extend your payouts beyond 20 years, up to age 90* or another five years, whichever ends later.
*Up to age 90, or another five years, whichever ends later.
You can use the Monthly payout estimator to estimate the amount of monthly payouts you can receive from your retirement savings.

questions.title: How are the Basic Retirement Sum and Full Retirement Sum determined for each cohort?
questions.text:
The Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) takes reference from a person's expenditure from a lower-middle retiree household, according to the latest Household Expenditure Survey (HES). It assumes that the member owns a property that lasts him up to 95 and he does not need to pay rent in retirement.
The Full Retirement Sum (FRS) is set at two times of the BRS.
The BRS or FRS you need to set aside depends on when you turn 55 and is fixed for the rest of your life.
Find out why the retirement sums are adjusted yearly for successive cohorts.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: How can I apply for internet or mobile banking?
questions.text:
Applying for internet or mobile banking is easy and convenient. To get started, you can refer to the digital banking resources compiled by Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA). This list provides a comprehensive guide on how to apply for internet or mobile banking with various banks in Singapore.
You can also visit any SG Digital community hub to enjoy one-on-one guidance from IMDA’s digital ambassadors, who would be happy to assist you in setting up your internet or mobile banking account and answer any questions you may have.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I change or delete my recurring cash top-up arrangement?
questions.text:
You can change your existing recurring cash top-up arrangement such as the amount and frequency of top-ups by following the steps below:
Delete your existing recurring cash top-up arrangement in the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form.
Create a new recurring arrangement via the same form with your revised amount and/or frequency of the top-ups.
You can delete your existing recurring cash top-up arrangement via the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form. Your application will generally be processed instantly upon submission.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my existing recurring CPF transfers arrangements?
questions.text: You can check your existing recurring CPF transfer arrangement by accessing the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form, under “Who you are making recurring top-ups to”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I check the amount that I can top up to my Retirement Account to reach the raised Enhanced Retirement Sum in 2026?
questions.text:
You may check your top-up limit on your Retirement Dashboard on 1 January 2026 once the Enhanced Retirement Sum is raised.
Find out how the top-up limit is computed.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I check the status of my application to withdraw my retirement savings using my pension/annuity?
questions.text: If your application to withdraw your retirement savings using your pension/annuity is approved, you will receive a withdrawal advice by mail after we have processed the payment to your bank account. Alternatively, you can also check the status of your application by logging on to cpf.gov.sg.

questions.title: How can I find out if I have reached the personal income tax relief cap?
questions.text: You can use the tax calculator on Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website to find out if you have reached your personal income tax relief cap.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I increase my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
You can consider the following options to increase your monthly payouts:
Boost your retirement savings:
Make cash top-ups or CPF transfers to grow your retirement savings up to the current Enhanced Retirement Sum. The more retirement savings you have, the higher your monthly payouts.
If you are born in 1957 or after, you can use the additional amount of retirement savings you can withdraw from age 65 to increase your monthly payouts via the Plan my monthly payouts service.
Defer your monthly payouts up to age 70:
Start your monthly payouts later to allow your retirement savings to grow with risk-free interest rates of up to 6% per annum.
If your payouts have already started, you can defer them via the Plan my monthly payouts service.
Monetise your property:
Consider options like the Lease Buyback Scheme or Silver Housing Bonus Scheme to supplement your monthly payouts.
If you wish to enquire on your revised payout, please write to us.

questions.title: How can I make cash top-ups to my child's CPF retirement savings?
questions.text:
To make cash top-ups to your child's CPF retirement savings (regardless his or her age), simply:
1. Indicate your identification number as the giver of the cash top-up in the application
2. Indicate your child's identification number as the recipient
3. Select the relationship as "Others"
Do note that givers of cash top-ups need to be at least 16 years old and cash top-ups to children will not qualify for tax relief. Find out more about the types of cash top-ups which can enjoy tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I make recurring monthly or yearly top-ups conveniently via GIRO?
questions.text:
You can make small and recurring cash top-ups via GIRO by following the steps below:
Step 1: Set up a GIRO arrangement
Step 2: Submit a request to make recurring cash top-ups for retirement.
Please note that you must complete both steps for recurring cash top-ups via GIRO to be successful.
Currently, the online application to set up a GIRO arrangement is only available for these participating banks.
Check out our GIRO setup guide.
If you encounter any difficulties in setting up GIRO, you may write to us for assistance.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I monetise my property and which option is suitable for me?
questions.text:
Here are some ways to monetise your property for additional source of retirement income:
Silver Housing Bonus
If you own an HDB flat or a private residential property up to an annual value (AV) of $31,000 and do not mind moving to a 3-room or smaller flat, you can supplement your retirement income through Silver Housing Bonus.
Lease Buyback Scheme
If you prefer to live in your existing flat, you can consider the Lease Buyback Scheme.
Rental
You can consider renting out a spare bedroom, or your entire property if you have an alternative accommodation. If you own a HDB flat, find out more about renting out a flat/bedroom.
If you own a private property, consider speaking to a financial institution or advisor to learn about the different products available in the market that can help you monetise your property and supplement your retirement income, while ageing in place.
As with all financial decisions, it is important to understand the nature of the monetisation option, and assess your situation and retirement needs before deciding if the option is suitable for you. You may use HDB’s Enquire Housing Monetisation Options e-Service to check your eligible Housing Monetisation options.

questions.title: How can I prolong my monthly payouts if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
You can consider the following options to prolong your monthly payouts:
Join CPF LIFE: CPF LIFE provides lifelong monthly payouts, unlike payouts that stop when your retirement savings are depleted if you are not on CPF LIFE. You can join CPF LIFE anytime from age 65 to one month before turning 80 via the Plan my monthly payouts service.
Reduce your monthly payouts: You can reduce your monthly payouts to extend the duration of your retirement income up to age 90. Submit your request via 'Write-to-us' with your Singpass.

questions.title: How can I update or terminate my GIRO bank account for recurring cash top-ups?
questions.text:
You can update your GIRO bank account for your recurring cash top-up by setting up a new GIRO arrangement. If you have existing recurring top-up arrangements, the deductions could still be from your previous GIRO bank account for the current month. Find out more.
You can terminate your GIRO arrangement for your recurring cash top-up by submitting this form. All monthly and/or yearly GIRO deductions for top-ups to your recipient(s) will cease.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I view or download my CPF LIFE monthly payout statement?
questions.text:
You can access your CPF LIFE monthly payout information through these steps:
Log in to cpf.gov.sg with your Singpass
Click on "my cpf" at the top navigation bar
Under "My dashboards", select the Retirement dashboard
Scroll to the 'Monthly payouts' section
Click on “Monthly payout history”
Select your preferred period to view the payout history
You may click the “PDF icon” to download your monthly payout statement for your selected period.

questions.title: How do I apply for Lease Buyback Scheme or Silver Housing Bonus?
questions.text:
You can apply for the Lease Buyback Scheme or Silver Housing Bonus through HDB:
Silver Housing Bonus
Lease Buyback Scheme

questions.title: How do I apply to withdraw my retirement savings if I have a pension/annuity?
questions.text:
For CPF Members in Singapore
Make an appointment to visit any CPF Service Centre and bring along your:
Identity card for verification; and
Pension or annuity documents (see table below).
TypeDocuments required
Pension
Original pension letter bearing the Pension Office’s letterhead, dated within six months, stating the following:
You are currently receiving your monthly pension payouts; and
The guaranteed monthly pension payouts must be payable for life and only be terminated upon death.
You can visit the Pensioner’s Portal for more information.
Annuity
Original annuity policy (administered by Monetary Authority of Singapore-registered insurance companies) bought using cash or through the CPF Investment Scheme and its terms and conditions satisfying the following conditions:
You are currently receiving your annuity payouts which is guaranteed for life;
The guaranteed monthly annuity payouts must be payable and only be terminated upon death; and
You must be the sole policyholder and sole recipient of the annuity payouts and will not be able to change the recipient of the annuity payouts in your lifetime.
Note: Your insurer must endorse the two clauses in your policy and you will need to submit a certified true copy of the endorsement to us before you can withdraw your retirement savings:
Where the Annuitant cancels the policy for cash surrender value, the Company is required to refund to the Annuitant’s CPF account an amount determined by the Board in accordance with the laws in force at the time the refund is required to be made.
Where a loan of the cash surrender of the policy is granted to the Annuitant, the Board shall have a first charge on the policy to secure the refund to the Annuitant’s CPF account of an amount determined by the Board in accordance with the laws in force at the time the refund is required to be made. The Company shall not be entitled to use part or all of any annuity payment to repay the outstanding loan.
For CPF Members Overseas
Please write to us using your Singpass with the required supporting documents. We will write to you after our assessment. If you can withdraw your retirement savings, you will need to bring along your identity card, the documents and your application for verification by any of the Singapore Overseas Missions.

questions.title: How do I defer or restart my CPF LIFE monthly payouts?
questions.text:
You can defer your monthly payouts using our Plan My Monthly Payouts service.
You can use the same service to restart your monthly payouts any time before age 70. Please note that your payouts will automatically start at age 70, even if you have not submitted any instruction to do so.

It is important to make payment as soon as possible, as the QR code will expire at the end of the day of application. If the QR code expires, you will need to submit a new application and make payment using the new QR code generated at the end of the application.

questions.title: How does CPF Board guard against premeditated early CPF withdrawals?
questions.text: There are policy safeguards to ensure givers' retirement adequacy before they can make CPF transfers to their loved ones. In addition, we have put in place a set of mechanisms to detect potential premature withdrawals. When such cases are detected, the CPF transfers will be refunded to the giver's CPF account, instead of being received by the recipient (for closure of CPF account upon leaving Singapore permanently) or the recipient's beneficiaries (for deceased cases) in cash.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How does the CPF LIFE Escalating Plan work?
questions.text:
The CPF LIFE Escalating Plan provides payouts that increase by 2% each year. It is suitable if you want to protect your retirement income from rising prices. Although the payouts start lower, they will eventually become higher than the Standard Plan and Basic Plan payouts.
For example, if you start with a monthly payout of $1,000 at age 65, it will reach around $1,500 when you turn age 85. The 2% increase takes place every year in the same month that you receive your first payout.
Premium
All your Retirement Account (RA) savings will be used as your CPF LIFE premium when you join CPF LIFE.
Subsequent inflows into the RA after starting the monthly payout will automatically be used to increase your CPF LIFE premium and monthly payouts.
Your CPF LIFE premium will continue to earn the CPF interest rates, which is factored into your monthly payouts. This allows you to receive higher payouts from the start, compared to if there were no interests earned.
Monthly Payouts
Your monthly payouts are calculated based on various factors and will be paid to you for as long as you live.
CPF LIFE works by risk-pooling, like other forms of insurance. The pooling of interest earned on the CPF LIFE premiums enables members to receive lifelong payouts.
Premium Balance
Upon your passing, your remaining CPF LIFE premium balance will be paid to your beneficiaries.

questions.title: How is tax relief computed for my cash top-ups to Special Account/Retirement Account?
questions.text:
If your recipient is not eligible for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS):
You can enjoy tax relief of $8,000 per year on cash top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year on cash top-ups to your loved ones, up to the prevailing Full Retirement Sum (FRS).
For more information on the conditions for tax relief, you may refer to this FAQ.
Below are some examples of tax relief computation:
Example 1: If you make a cash top-up of $10,000 to a recipient (self/loved one) whose limit to the prevailing FRS is less than $8,000.
For example, if the recipient’s limit to the prevailing FRS is $2,000
Estimated tax relief amount = $2,000
Example 2: If you make a cash top-up of $12,000 to a recipient (self/loved one) who has already reached the prevailing FRS.
Estimated tax relief amount = $0
If your recipient is eligible for MRSS:
Your cash top-up will first enable the recipient to enjoy the matching grant of up to $2,000 per year from the Government and will thus not be eligible for tax relief. You can continue to enjoy tax relief on cash top-ups that do not attract the MRSS matching grant ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).
For more information on the conditions for tax relief, you may refer to this FAQ.
Below are some examples of tax relief computation.
Example 1: If you make a cash top-up of $3,000 to an MRSS-eligible recipient (self/loved one), who has yet to receive any cash top-ups this year:
Estimated matching grant your recipient will enjoy = $2,000
Estimated tax relief amount = Total top-up amount - Matching grant amount = $3,000 - $2,000 = $1,000
Example 2: If you make a cash top-up of $3,000 to an MRSS-eligible recipient (self/loved one) who has already received $2,000 of cash top-ups this year:
Estimated matching grant your recipient will enjoy = $0
Estimated tax relief amount = Total top-up amount - Matching grant amount = $3,000 - $0 = $3,000
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How long does it take to process my application to start my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
Our normal processing time for applications to start monthly payouts from retirement savings is three days to two weeks*.
* Your application may take up to two weeks to process if you have submitted multiple payout decisions via the Plan my monthly payouts service.
Monthly payouts will start at 65 or within one month (whichever is later) after your instruction is processed.

questions.title: How long does it take to process my application to withdraw my retirement savings using my pension/annuity?
questions.text: Your application will be processed within one month after we receive all the required information and documents. The retirement savings will then be paid to your registered bank account.

questions.title: How long does it take to process my top-up application?
questions.text:
Please refer to the table for our normal processing time for processing top-up applications:
Type of top-ups
Method
Normal Processing time
Processing
Deduction and Crediting
Cash
One-time cash top-up via:
PayNow QR
OCBC Digital (CPF Mobile app only)
In general, almost instantly
Recurring cash top-ups via GIRO
(participating bank users)
Upon successful application to set up GIRO to make cash top-ups, your GIRO bank account will be updated in the Board's record.
In general, the deduction will start from the following month after your recurring arrangement is successfully processed.
If you are updating your GIRO bank account, find out more on the GIRO deduction for your existing recurring top-up arrangements.
We will deduct the monies from your bank account on the 15th of the month (or the next working day if 15th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday).
In general, your top-up will be credited within seven working days after we receive your payment.
Note: Please ensure that you maintain sufficient funds in your bank account for GIRO deductions. Some banks may charge an administrative fee for each unsuccessful deduction.

However, a longer processing time may be required for certain transfers, such as first-time transfers to loved ones, as checks to verify relationships will need to be conducted. The processing time for such scenarios is generally five working days upon receipt of application.
Recurring CPF transfers to self for members aged 55 and above
Monthly CPF transfers will take effect from the 18th of the following month upon successful application.
In some cases, we may require additional time to verify your application. We will contact you within five working days to request for more information.

questions.title: How long will it take for my top-up to be credited via PayNow QR?
questions.text: Top-ups via PayNow QR are generally credited almost instantly, upon successful payment.
