questions.title: How much CPF savings can I transfer to myself or my loved ones?
questions.text:
You can easily check the maximum amount of CPF savings you can transfer in your Retirement Dashboard.
If you would like to learn more about how the amount shown on your Retirement Dashboard is computed, please refer to the table below.
Do note that the actual amount of CPF savings you can transfer may also depend on your recipient's available top-up limit.
Recipient of CPF TransferAvailable CPF Savings for Transfer
If you are below 55If you are 55 or above
Self
Any amount of your Ordinary Account (OA) savings.
Any amount of your Ordinary Account (OA) savings.
Spouse
Your OA savings after setting aside the current Basic Retirement Sum (BRS)1.
Example (PDF, 72KB)
Your CPF savings4 after setting aside your Basic Retirement Sum (BRS)5.
Example (PDF, 72KB)
Parents and/or grandparents
If you own a property3, you can transfer your OA savings after setting aside the current BRS1, provided you can meet the current Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with your OA savings, SA savings, the net amount withdrawn for investments2 and property3.
If you do not own a property3, you can transfer your OA savings after setting aside the current FRS1.
Example (PDF, 91.7KB)
If you own a property8, you can transfer your CPF savings4 after setting aside your BRS5, provided you can meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with your OA savings, RA savings7, net amount withdrawn for investments2 and property8.
If you do not own a property8, you can transfer your CPF savings4 after setting aside your FRS5.
Example (PDF, 91.7KB)
Siblings, parents-in-law and/or grandparents-in-law
Your OA savings after setting aside the current FRS1.
Example (PDF, 25.9KB)
Your OA savings after setting aside your FRS5.
Example (PDF, 25.9KB)
Find out what are the retirement sums applicable to you.
1Can be set aside using your OA savings, SA savings and net amount withdrawn for investments2.
2Refers to amounts withdrawn for (i) an active investment account under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)-OA, and (ii) investments under the CPFIS-SA and discounted Singtel shares that have not been completely disposed of.
3Refers to the CPF savings used for property, including accrued interest (P+I). If you have set aside the BRS and own a property bought using CPF savings, the P+I can be considered towards meeting the FRS for making CPF transfers to your parents and/or grandparents. The property you own must have remaining lease that can last you to at least 95 years old.
4Your OA savings will be transferred first, followed by the amount available to transfer from your RA6, if applicable. You can write to CPF Board to specify the CPF accounts from which to transfer to your spouse, parents and/or grandparents. Please note that if you use your RA6 for the transfer, the sum of your RA savings7 and property8 may be less than your FRS. As a result, when you make a withdrawal from your OA, a portion of the savings will be used to meet your FRS in the RA.
5Can be set aside using your OA savings, RA savings7, and net amount withdrawn for investments2.
6Refer to RA balances excluding interest earned, any government grants, and any top-ups received.
7Refer to the cash set aside in the RA (excluding amounts such as interest earned, plus retirement withdrawals.
8Refers to the CPF savings used for property, including accrued interest (P+I). If you have set aside the BRS and own a property bought using CPF savings, the P+I can be considered towards meeting the FRS for making CPF transfers to your parents and/or grandparents. The property you own must have remaining lease that can last you to at least 95 years old. If you have pledged your property for purposes of setting aside part of your retirement sum or to withdraw your retirement savings, the amount secured by the property can be considered towards meeting the FRS for this CPF transfer.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How much monthly payout will I receive if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
If you've reached age 65, you can check your monthly payout in your Retirement dashboard.
If you’ve not reached age 65, we will notify you three months before your 65th birthday regarding your options on your monthly payout and the decisions that you need to make.
Do note that if you are born in 1958 or after, you may be automatically included in CPF LIFE, which provides lifelong monthly payouts.

questions.title: How much Ordinary Account savings will be transferred to my Retirement Account to increase my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
You can choose to transfer all your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to your Retirement Account (RA), up to the current Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS).
If you have not set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) and have started your monthly payouts, your OA savings will be automatically transferred to your RA, up to your FRS. You will receive a notification before the transfer.
For example: Jane is born in 1960 and the principal amount in her RA is $148,000, which is below her FRS of $161,000. As she has started her monthly payouts, assuming she has $20,000 in her OA, $13,000 will be automatically transferred to her RA to set aside her FRS and increase her CPF LIFE monthly payouts. The remaining $7,000 will remain in her OA and she can choose to transfer it to her RA to increase her CPF LIFE payouts further or to withdraw anytime.

questions.title: How much tax relief can I enjoy when I make cash top-ups?
questions.text:
You can view the estimated tax relief when making top-up via the Cash Top-ups and CPF Transfers for Retirement Form.
You can enjoy tax relief on cash top-ups made each calendar year, up to:
$8,000 when you or your employer/ platform operator tops up your own Special Account (SA)/ Retirement Account (RA); and
Another $8,000 when you top up your loved ones' SA/RA.
This means you can receive up to $16,000 in tax relief per year by topping up both your own account and those of your loved ones.
Here are some important things to note:
NotesElaboration
Tax relief up to Full Retirement Sum (FRS) onlyTax relief is only granted up to the current year's FRS.
Giver enjoys tax reliefTax relief is enjoyed by the giver of the cash top-ups, not the recipient.
Tax deduction for employers/ platform operatorsEmployers/ platform operators may also claim tax deductions on cash top-ups made separately.
Shared cap with MediSave top-upsThe $8,000 tax relief cap on cash top-ups to your own SA/RA is shared with cash top-ups to your MediSave Account (MA). This shared cap also applies to the $8,000 cap on tax relief for top-ups to loved ones' SA/RA.
From 1 January 2025, cash top-ups that qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) (up to $2,000 matching per year) will no longer enjoy tax relief. Find out more.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How much will my CPF LIFE monthly payouts increase after my non-withdrawable Ordinary Account savings are annuitised?
questions.text: After your non-withdrawable Ordinary Account savings are successfully annuitised, we will send you a notification to inform you of the revised CPF LIFE monthly payout.

questions.title: How will changes to my Retirement Account affect my CPF LIFE monthly payouts?
questions.text:
Changes to your Retirement Account (RA) can affect your monthly payouts. This is because your RA savings is one of the factors in determining your CPF LIFE payouts.
Outflow from your RA, such as lump sum withdrawals will reduce your CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
On the other hand, inflows to your RA (such as top-ups or refunds from selling your property or investments) will be automatically used to increase your CPF LIFE premium and monthly payouts, provided they are sufficient to increase your monthly payouts by at least $10*.
*This is to avoid small and non-meaningful increase in payouts for members.
Please note that the actual revision may take up to two months, and we will notify you on the changes in your monthly payouts.

questions.title: How will I be eligible for the automatic transfer of non-withdrawable monies from my Ordinary Account to my Retirement Account?
questions.text: To be eligible for the automatic transfer, your non-withdrawable monies in your Ordinary Account must be sufficient to increase your CPF LIFE monthly payouts by at least $10.

questions.title: How will I receive my monthly payouts if my combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are less than the minimum sum of $350?
questions.text: You will receive monthly payouts as long as you have at least $350 in your combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings. If your combined RA and OA savings are less than $350, the balance will be paid to you next January (e.g., if your balance falls below $350 in August, you will receive your payout next January).

questions.title: How will I receive my retirement savings if my application to withdraw my retirement savings using my pension/annuity is approved?
questions.text: If your application to withdraw your retirement savings using your pension/annuity is approved, your retirement savings will be paid to your bank account provided under your Account settings.

questions.title: How will the annuitisation of the non-withdrawable Ordinary Account (OA) savings as CPF LIFE monthly payout affect my eligibility to withdraw or service the housing commitments that are financed by my OA savings?
questions.text:
Your eligibility to make lump sum withdrawals from your Ordinary Account (OA) will not be affected. This is because only the OA savings that cannot be withdrawn in a lump sum will be annuitised to provide you with higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
The purpose of your CPF savings is to provide you with a stream of retirement income. If you still have housing obligations after starting your monthly payouts, you can use your monthly payouts or monies in excess of your Full Retirement Sum after this transfer to meet your housing needs.

questions.title: How will top-ups boost my CPF monthly payouts?
questions.text:
If you are on CPF LIFE* in retirement, topping up your Special or Retirement Account will allow you to enjoy higher monthly payouts for life. Please refer to this FAQ for examples on the increase in payouts.
If you are not on CPF LIFE* in retirement, the top-ups will generally allow you to receive higher payouts or receive payouts for a longer time. Find out more.
*Members born in 1958 or later will be placed on CPF LIFE if they have at least $60,000 in their Retirement Account when they commence their monthly payouts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How will topping up my Special or Retirement Account boost my monthly payouts if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
If you are not on CPF LIFE* in retirement, topping up your Special or Retirement Account will generally increase your monthly payouts. However, if your remaining payout duration is short, the top-up will extend your payout duration instead so that your Retirement Account can continue to provide you with monthly payouts during your retirement.
For more personalised estimates, use the CPF Monthly Payout Estimator. This tool helps you project your monthly CPF payouts in retirement and simulate the effect of different top-up amounts on your monthly payout.
*Members born in 1958 or later will be placed on CPF LIFE if they have at least $60,000 in their Retirement Account when they commence their monthly payouts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I am an employer or platform operator who made cash top-ups to my employees or platform workers’ CPF Accounts on their behalf. How do I claim corporate tax deductions?
questions.text:
Cash top-ups made to your employees or platform workers’ CPF Retirement Accounts/ Special Accounts only or MediSave Account only, on the employees or platform workers’ behalf, are tax-deductible.
You are able to claim tax deduction on the cash top-ups as part of your allowable business expenses when filing the income tax return (Form B) for self-employed person or (Form C-S/ Form C-S (Lite)/ Form C) for company.
For more information, you may refer to the IRAS website on Top-Up of Employees’ CPF Retirement Accounts/ Special Accounts/ MediSave Accounts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I am below 55 years old. Can I set up recurring CPF transfers from my Ordinary Account to Special Account?
questions.text: The recurring CPF transfer e-Service is currently only available for members aged 55 and above. If you are below 55 years old, you may wish to make a one-time CPF transfer from your Ordinary Account to Special Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I am below 55. Can I use this Monthly Payout Estimator to estimate my monthly payout?
questions.text:
The Monthly Payout Estimator is designed to help members between the ages of 55 and 79 to estimate their monthly payout based on their desired retirement lifestyle.
If you are below 55, you can log in with your Singpass and try out the Retirement Payout Planner. This online tool can help you in setting your retirement income goal, visualising your projected retirement savings and payouts, and simulating the impact of actions you can take to achieve your goal. You may also perform selected transactions such as making retirement top-ups.
With the planner, retirement planning is easy with just a few steps and takes only 15 minutes to complete.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: I am currently receiving Additional Monthly Payout (AMP). Will my AMP be converted to higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts automatically?
questions.text:
You will continue to receive Additional Monthly Payout (AMP) from your Retirement Account (RA). The AMP is not part of CPF LIFE and will cease when your RA balances are depleted. To avoid a sudden decrease in your overall monthly income when your AMP ends, you may consider using your available balances in your RA to increase your CPF LIFE premium and boost your lifelong monthly payout. To do this, please submit your request via FormSG.
Starting from November 2021, any new Retirement Account inflows will automatically be used to increase your CPF LIFE premium. This will allow you to receive higher monthly payouts for life, providing you with greater financial security during your retirement years.

questions.title: I am making a top-up to myself from overseas. How can I set up a Singpass account if I do not have a mobile phone number registered in Singapore?
questions.text: If you wish to set up a Singpass account for your top-up application but do not have a mobile phone number registered in Singapore, you may contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly for assistance.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I am not on CPF LIFE. How will my monthly payouts be adjusted if there are changes to my retirement savings?
questions.text: We will review your payouts monthly to take into account the changes to your retirement savings. Generally, topping up your Retirement Account will increase your monthly payouts. Your payouts will be revised in the following month after the inflows or outflows are made to your retirement savings. However, if your remaining payout duration is short, the top-up will extend your payout duration instead so that your Retirement Account can continue to provide you with monthly payouts during your retirement.

questions.title: I am reaching age 65. How do I start my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
We will send you a notification three months before your 65th birthday, to guide you to explore your monthly payouts options and submit your instructions through the Plan my monthly payouts service.
If you do not submit any instructions on your payouts by 70, your monthly payouts will automatically start in the month of your 70th birthday.

questions.title: I am the appointed donee/deputy for my next of kin under the Mental Capacity Act. How can I receive monthly payouts on behalf of my next of kin?
questions.text:
Make an appointment to visit any of our CPF Service Centres and bring along the following original documents:
Medical report* from an accredited doctor stating that the member lacks mental capacity permanently;
Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order;
Trust bank account statement or passbook; and
Your NRIC/Foreign Passport.
*If the Court Order was applied through iFAMS, you can retrieve a copy of the medical report via iFAMS. Please note that fees may apply for the request:
Click on "Mental Capacity Act Application"
Click on the tab "Other Matters"
Click on "File Other Applications or Requests"
Log in via Singpass (when prompted) as Individuals
Select "File request for copy of documents" and fill up the required information.
Please ensure that you have all the necessary documents so that your application can be processed promptly for you to receive your next-of-kin’s CPF savings.

questions.title: I am unsure whether to start my monthly payouts now. How can I find out how much monthly payouts I can receive?
questions.text:
You may use the Plan my monthly payouts service to find out more about your monthly payout details, provide your payout instructions and confirm your bank account details.
The Plan my monthly payouts service is available to you three months before you reach 65.
With this service, you can find out your estimated monthly payouts when you:
start at 65 or defer to a later age
join CPF LIFE and/or
use more of your CPF savings to increase your monthly payouts.

questions.title: I belong to the generation born before 1958 and can withdraw a portion of my Special Account (SA) savings even though I have not set aside my Full Retirement Sum. Will I continue to be able to withdraw after my SA is closed?
questions.text:
When your Special Account (SA) is closed, the amount you could have withdrawn from your SA will be transferred to your Ordinary Account, and you can continue to withdraw this amount anytime.
If you continue to work after your SA is closed, any new contributions that used to be allocated to your SA will instead be allocated to your Retirement Account (RA), up to your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). This will go towards meeting your long-term retirement needs, by allowing you to receive higher monthly payouts from your Payout Eligibility Age. If you have immediate needs, you can choose to set aside up to half the FRS using your property and withdraw your savings above the Basic Retirement Sum in your RA.
If you require further assistance, you may write to us.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: I did not use CPF savings for the matrimonial property but pledged the property to set aside my retirement sum. Can the Court order a transfer of this property to my ex-spouse
questions.text: Yes, the Court can still order the transfer of the property to your ex-spouse upon the refund of your pledged amount to your CPF account. The Court may also order for the transfer with a partial refund or without a refund. For such orders, upon the subsequent disposal of the property by your ex-spouse, the unrefunded pledged amount will have to be refunded to your ex-spouse’s CPF account (since it was not earlier refunded to your CPF account).
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: I have bought an annuity in place of the retirement sum when I turned 55. Will my nominees receive the remaining guaranteed sum from my annuity when I pass away?
questions.text: If you had bought an annuity in place of the retirement sum when you turned 55, your nominees will receive the remaining guaranteed sum from your annuity when you pass away.

questions.title: I have not joined CPF LIFE yet. How can I increase my future monthly payouts?
questions.text:
There are a few ways to increase your future CPF LIFE monthly payouts:
Topping up your Retirement Account (RA) under the Retirement Sum Topping-up Scheme
You or your loved ones can make cash top-ups and CPF transfers to your RA up to the current Enhanced Retirement Sum by logging in with your Singpass at cpf.gov.sg/rstuform. The more RA savings you use to join CPF LIFE, the higher your monthly payouts.
Deferring your monthly payouts (up to 70)
Consider deferring your payouts if you are still working or have other income. Your monthly payouts will increase by up to 7% for each year that you defer. If you choose to defer until 70, you could get up to a 35% increase in payouts as your CPF savings would have accumulated more interest. You will only need to decide your CPF LIFE plan when you wish to start your payouts. The latest age you can start your payouts is 70, after which they will automatically begin.
Monetising your property
If you own a property, you can also consider monetising your property.
You can use the Monthly payout estimator to find out how much RA savings you need, or the age you need to start your payouts to get your desired monthly payout.

questions.title: I live in a private property. Are there ways for me to monetise my property without selling my home?
questions.text:
You can consider speaking with your financial institution or advisor on the available products in the market that allow you to monetise your private property to supplement your retirement income while ageing in place.
As with all important financial decision, it is important to understand the nature of the product and assess your own risk tolerance and retirement needs/preferences before deciding if the monetisation option is suitable for you.
Alternatively, you can consider renting out a spare bedroom, or your entire property if you have an alternative accommodation. This can provide you with an additional source of retirement income.

questions.title: I made top-ups to my Special Account before turning 55. What will happen to the top-ups when I turn 55?
questions.text:
When you turn 55, the top-ups made to your Special Account and accrued interest will be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) up to your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) and your Special Account will be closed.
Please note that top-up monies are meant to build up your retirement savings and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes. Read more on how the top-ups will be used.
If you are 55 or above and have excess savings above your FRS, you can apply to withdraw them for your immediate needs anytime. Alternatively, you can make top-ups to your RA (up to the current year's Enhanced Retirement Sum) to enjoy higher monthly payouts in retirement.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I plan to top up my Retirement Account to the raised Enhanced Retirement Sum. When can I make the top-up?
questions.text:
You can make your top-up anytime from 1 January 2026 onwards, once the Enhanced Retirement Sum is raised.
Find out how you can check the amount that you can top up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I received an email notification on topping up my and/or my loved ones’ retirement savings. How do I know if the notification is indeed sent by CPF Board?
questions.text:
Members will receive email notifications at the email address registered with the Board. You may check or update your email address which you have earlier registered with us using your Singpass.
To verify if the email you received is legitimate and avoid falling prey to phishing scams,
Ensure that the sender's email address is correctly spelt and ends with "@e.cpf.gov.sg".
Ensure that the hyperlinks or links you click on has a domain ending with “.gov.sg”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I was a foreigner who was on CPF LIFE. What happened to my CPF LIFE plan?
questions.text:
The purpose of the CPF system is to help Singapore Citizens (SC) and Permanent Residents (PR) retire with peace of mind. In line with this, CPF members who are not SC or PR will have to close their CPF accounts and their participation in CPF schemes such as CPF LIFE will cease.
Find out more about closing your CPF accounts.

questions.title: If I am 55 and would like to make a CPF transfer to my loved ones, in what order will my savings be transferred?
questions.text:
If you are 55 or above, your CPF savings will be transferred to your loved ones in the following order:
OA
RA*
*If you use your RA savings for the transfer, you may no longer have enough savings to meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). In that case, the next time you apply for a withdrawal from your OA, a portion or all of the savings will be used to meet your FRS in the RA.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: If I have a pension or annuity, can I withdraw my retirement savings?
questions.text:
You can apply to withdraw your retirement savings if your pension or annuity provides you with monthly payouts for life. The withdrawal amount depends on the monthly payouts you receive from your pension or annuity.
For Pensions:
Generally, only pensions under the Singapore Government will be considered.
Pension providers must have a credit rating comparable to CPF LIFE, which invests in AAA-rated Special Singapore Government Securities.
Pensions without recognised credit ratings (e.g., Standard & Poor's, Moody's, or Fitch Ratings) will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.
For Annuities:
Must be purchased using cash or through the CPF Investment Scheme.
Must be administered by Monetary Authority of Singapore-registered insurance companies and satisfy the Insurance Act requirements.
You must be the policyholder and sole insured person.
All applications are subject to the Board’s approval.
Please note that Investment instruments such as endowments and bonds are not eligible as they generally do not provide the policy holder with a lifelong income.

questions.title: If I have withdrawn under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, can I still apply to withdraw a lump sum from age 55 and payout eligibility age for my immediate retirement needs?
questions.text: No, you will no longer be able to make lump sum withdrawals from age 55 and payout eligibility age for your immediate retirement needs as the withdrawable savings are already paid out to you earlier under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme.

questions.title: If I wish to make both a CPF transfer and a cash top-up to myself / my loved one, which should I do first?
questions.text:
If you wish to enjoy tax relief on your cash top-up to help you or your loved one up to the Full Retirement Sum, please make the cash top-up first, before the CPF transfer. If you prefer using your CPF savings over cash, please make the CPF transfer first.
You may wish to take note that only cash top-ups to self and loved ones within the Full Retirement Sum can enjoy tax relief. Learn more about tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: In setting aside the Full Retirement Sum in my Retirement Account, why are my Special Account savings transferred before my Ordinary Account savings?
questions.text: The savings in your Special Account (SA) are meant for your retirement needs, while your Ordinary Account (OA) savings can be used to meet shorter-term expenditure needs such as housing. Hence, when you turn 55, SA savings are first transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to help you set aside the retirement sum, which will eventually be streamed out as monthly payouts when you reach your payout eligibility age.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Is the CPF payout eligibility age linked to the retirement/re-employment ages?
questions.text:
The CPF payout eligibility age is not linked to either the retirement or re-employment age.
Today, you can start your CPF payouts at any time from age 65. There is no link to the current retirement age of 63* or the re-employment age of 68. Even if the retirement age and the re-employment age are raised, the CPF payout eligibility age would remain unchanged.
* The current retirement age and re-employment age of 63 and 68 will be raised to 64 and 69 respectively from 1 July 2026.
For more information:
Information on the CPF Payout Eligibility Age
Information on the retirement age
Information on re-employment age

questions.title: Is there a minimum or maximum age for making or receiving top-ups?
questions.text:
There is no maximum age for making or receiving top-ups.
However, you will need to be at least 16 years old to be a giver of cash top-ups.
You can make cash top-ups to a child who is not yet 16 years old, and you can find out how to do so here.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: My child is below 16 years old. How do I transfer his Ordinary Account savings to his Special Account on his behalf?
questions.text: If your child is below 16 years old and wishes to transfer his Ordinary Account savings to his Special Account, you can complete this application on his behalf.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: My Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) claim has been approved. How will I receive my DPS claim payout?
questions.text: Upon approval of the Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) claim, Great Eastern Life (GEL) will disburse the DPS claim benefits to your PayNow account, which is linked to your Singapore NRIC and bank account. If you prefer not to receive your DPS claim benefits via PayNow, you may contact GEL directly. If payment made via PayNow is unsuccessful, GEL will contact you to check with you on your preferred payment mode.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: My Special Account (SA) savings were transferred to the Ordinary Account (OA) after SA closure, as I have set aside the Full Retirement Sum. With the OA having lower interest, what can I do to earn the interest that the SA pays?
questions.text:
If you wish to earn higher interest and receive higher retirement payouts, you may transfer your Special Account (SA) savings that were channelled to the Ordinary Account (OA) due to the closure of SA, to the Retirement Account (RA), up to the prevailing Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS). The RA interest rate is the same as the SA.
If you are still receiving monthly employment contributions in your OA after age 55, consider setting up monthly recurring CPF transfers from your OA to your RA to earn higher interest on your CPF contributions.
Find out more about how you can make the transfer at cpf.gov.sg/rstu.
Please note that CPF transfers are irreversible and the savings are set aside to boost your monthly payouts in retirement. Thus, the amount transferred cannot be withdrawn for any other purpose such as housing, investment, or immediate needs after age 55. Read more on how the top-ups will be used.
You can also invest the OA savings in low-risk investments, such as T-bills and fixed deposits, under the CPF Investment Scheme.
Did you know? From 1 January 2025, the ERS will be raised to four times of the Basic Retirement Sum to allow members to save more in the RA and receive higher payouts, if they want.
With the change, the ERS in 2025 would be $426,0001, up from $308,700 in 2024. Hence, if you are aged 55 and above in 2025, you can save up to $426,000 in the RA.
1 This is the limit for the savings set aside in the RA (excluding amounts such as interest earned, government grants received, plus retirement withdrawals).
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: My Special Account (SA) will be closed when I turn age 55 in the middle of the year. If I have the Full Retirement Sum, where does interest earned on my SA (before SA closure) go? Do I lose any interest for the remaining months till the end of the year?
questions.text:
The process for crediting CPF interest remains unchanged even after your Special Account (SA) closes at age 55. CPF interest is computed on a monthly basis and credited annually to all our CPF members.
If you have already set aside the Full Retirement Sum, the interest earned on your SA prior to its closure will be allocated to your Ordinary Account (OA) after your SA is closed, which is in line with the principle that short term funds earn the lower short-term interest rates. After your SA is closed on your 55th birthday, your CPF savings will continue earning interest in their respective accounts till the end of the year. All the interest you have earned for the whole year will then be credited by the following year.
To earn the higher long-term interest rate, you can transfer your OA savings to your Retirement Account (RA) up to the current year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum. The transfer is irreversible and will be paid to you as monthly payouts and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes. The transfer can be made anytime from age 55.
If you are receiving monthly employment contributions in your OA after 55, consider setting up monthly recurring CPF transfers from your OA to your RA to earn higher interest on your CPF contributions.
Find out more at cpf.gov.sg/RSTU.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: My top-up is not reflected in my CPF account. Was the top-up unsuccessful?
questions.text:
If your top-up is not reflected in your CPF accounts after the expiry of our usual processing time, it might be due to one of the following reasons:
You may have missed out in making payment for your cash top-up application. Find out how to submit a new application.
You may have missed out in submitting supporting documents for first-time CPF transfers to a loved one. Find out what the required supporting documents are.
We may require additional time to verify your application. We will contact you within five working days to request for more information.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Under a transfer order, do I need to set aside my retirement sum before my ex-spouse can receive their entitlement?
questions.text:
The transfer of CPF savings to your ex-spouse can take place without you setting aside your retirement sum* first. This gives your ex-spouse certainty over the amount they can receive and they can use them immediately for approved purposes such as housing, investment and education. Your ex-spouse may also withdraw the CPF savings when they are entitled to.
In the event of a transfer of CPF savings upon the making of housing refunds pursuant to a disposal of the property, the Board will first transfer the amount to your ex-spouse. Thereafter, the remaining refunds will be used to make up your retirement sum, up to your applicable Full Retirement Sum. Any balance housing refunds will remain in your Ordinary Account, and you can decide how to manage it.
*Only applies to members aged 55 and above.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What actions do I need to take to file and claim tax relief for my cash top-up?
questions.text:
You do not need to file or claim tax relief for your cash top-up as we will automatically inform Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) if you have instructed to claim tax relief in your top-up application and are eligible.
Please note that only givers who make cash top-ups are eligible for tax relief. If you make cash top-ups to your loved ones, the tax relief does not apply to your receipients. Find out the conditions to enjoy tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What are the assumptions used in the projections within the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text: For more information on assumptions used within the Retirement Payout Planner, refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What are the benefits of making top-ups via the PayNow QR?
questions.text:
Making top-ups via PayNow QR is hassle-free.
All you need to do is scan the QR code provided at the end of your online application, and the required details such as payment amount and transaction type will be automatically included. You do not have to manually enter any details, so you can complete the payment quickly and conveniently.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What are the conditions for me to enjoy tax relief to Special Account or Retirement Account?
questions.text:
Use Cash Top-ups and CPF Transfers for Retirement Form to view the tax relief you will receive on your top-up and make your cash top-up.
Only cash top-ups qualify for tax relief, and it depends on who you are topping up to and whether the amount is up to current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS).
Who you top up for
Maximum tax relief per year
Conditions
Yourself
Up to $8,000 for both
Only up to current year’s FRS
Employee/platform workers
Loved one
Up to $8,000 across all loved ones
Only up to current year’s FRS
Spouse/sibling must have annual income ≤ $8k in previous year or is handicapped*
*Handicapped refers to people who are incapacitated because of physical or mental infirmity.
Important notes
Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS): From 1 Jan 2025, top-ups that qualify for the MRSS matching grant (up to $2,000/year) will no longer enjoy tax relief. Find out more on how this works.
Shared cap with MediSave Account (MA): $8,000 tax relief cap shared across top-ups to Special Account (SA)/ Retirement Account (RA) or MA.
Overall tax relief cap: Your total personal income tax relief (including CPF top-ups) is capped at $80,000/year.
Learn more about tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What are the different features found in the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
The Retirement Payout Planner is organised into three features.
“Your Options” suggests personalised actions to help you reach your retirement payout goal. You can access this feature once you have completed both “Your Projection” and “Your Goal”.
“Your Projection” allows you to project your monthly retirement payouts based on your preferred payout start age and CPF LIFE plan.
After saving your projection, you will be able to simulate the impact of actions such as CPF top-ups, withdrawals and Ordinary Account (OA) reservation on your projected payouts, where applicable to you.
“Your Goal” allows you to set your retirement payout goal. You can set your own goal or use the retirement payout guide, a short questionnaire, to estimate how much you’ll need every month to support your desired retirement lifestyle.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What are the features of CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
CPF LIFE offers several key features to support your retirement:
Payouts that never run out:
It provides you with a monthly income no matter how long you live. With more Singaporeans living beyond 85 years old, this addresses concerns about outliving retirement savings.
Higher payouts with up to 6% interest:
Your premium continues to earn CPF interest of up to 6% per annum, risk free. The interest is factored into your monthly payouts, allowing you to receive higher monthly payouts from the start.
Capital guaranteed:
It guarantees that the total amount of payouts you receive over your lifetime plus the amount paid to your beneficiaries will be equal or more than your CPF LIFE premium.

questions.title: What conditions do I have to meet to set aside my Full Retirement Sum with a mixture of property and cash, and withdraw part of my Retirement Account savings using my property?
questions.text:
You can withdraw part of your Retirement Account (RA) savings (excluding interest earned, any government grants received and top-ups to your retirement savings) down to your Basic Retirement Sum if:
You are 55 and above;
You own a completed property* with a remaining lease that can last you to at least 95; and
The expected CPF housing refund (if you have used CPF for property or if you pledge your property) is able to restore the withdrawn amount or your RA to your FRS when you sell/transfer the property in the future.
* Including studio apartments, and flats bought under the short-lease 2-room Flexi scheme.
It is important to note that the amount of RA savings you can withdraw excludes, generally, interest earned, government grants received and top-ups to your retirement savings. It also depends on your RA balance at the point of withdrawal. For example, if you are on CPF LIFE and have started your monthly payouts, any new inflows received in your RA will be used to increase your CPF LIFE premium to provide you with higher monthly payouts, and you will not be allowed to withdraw them in a lump sum.
Find out how withdrawing with your property works if:
you have used CPF savings for your property
you did not use CPF savings for your property

questions.title: What happens if I scan the generated PayNow QR code multiple times?
questions.text:
To ensure that your cash top-up is processed smoothly, please only scan the PayNow QR code and make payment once as the code is only valid for a single payment. For subsequent or duplicate payments made using the same QR code, the payment will be refunded.
If you need to make another top-up, you will need to submit a new application and obtain a new PayNow QR code.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What happens if I surrender my pension/annuity after I have withdrawn my savings?
questions.text:
If you surrender your pension/annuity after you have withdrawn your retirement savings, the surrender value of your pension/annuity, up to your Full Retirement Sum with accrued interest, will be refunded to your Retirement Account. Any excess amount will be refunded to you in cash.
It's important to note that you will not be able to use your annuity to obtain a loan. This is because we need to ensure that we can refund the surrender value when you surrender your annuity.

questions.title: What happens if my Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are depleted and I receive new inflows in my RA and OA?
questions.text: If you are not on CPF LIFE, your monthly payouts will stop when your combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are depleted. When you receive any new inflows in your RA or OA, your monthly payouts will automatically resume from the following month. However, if your combined RA and OA savings are less than $350, the balance will be paid to you next January (e.g., if your account balance falls below $350 in August, you will receive your payout next January).

questions.title: What happens to my CPF LIFE plan if I am approved to withdraw under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme?
questions.text:
If you are approved to withdraw your retirement savings under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, you can decide whether to:
(i) terminate your CPF LIFE plan and receive a refund of the premium balance (if applicable); or
(ii) keep your CPF LIFE plan and receive monthly payouts for as long as you live.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF LIFE plan if my application to withdraw all my retirement savings using my pension/annuity is approved?
questions.text:
If your application to withdraw all your retirement savings using a pension or annuity is approved, your CPF LIFE plan will be terminated. Any remaining CPF LIFE premium balance1 will be refunded to your Retirement Account (RA) and disbursed to you. You can view your remaining CPF LIFE premium balance via your retirement dashboard under monthly payouts section.
1The remaining CPF LIFE premium balance is the amount deducted from your RA when you joined CPF LIFE, minus the total payouts you received under the plan before its termination.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF LIFE plan when my CPF account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text: Your CPF LIFE plan will be terminated, and you will receive your CPF LIFE premium balance (if any) together with your CPF savings when you transfer your savings to your bank account.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my CPF when I turn 65?
questions.text:
You can start to receive monthly CPF payouts from age 65.
Three months before your 65th birthday, we will notify you about your monthly payouts options. You will be guided to the personalised Plan my monthly payouts (PMP) service where you can:
1. choose to start or defer your payouts
2. view your estimated payouts
3. explore ways to increase your payouts using available CPF savings.
Find out more about what happens when you are reaching age 65.

questions.title: What happens to my recurring CPF transfer arrangement if I have reached my top-up limit or have insufficient Ordinary Account savings?
questions.text: If you have insufficient top-up limit or Ordinary Account (OA) savings, we will transfer up to your remaining top-up limit or available OA savings. Please note that your recurring arrangement will be stopped after two consecutive unsuccessful transfers (where no amount is transferred).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What happens to my Retirement Account savings when I join CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
It is dependent on the CPF LIFE plan you choose. If you opt for the Escalating or Standard Plan, all your Retirement Account (RA) savings will be used as your CPF LIFE premium.
If you opt for the Basic Plan, about 80-90% of your RA savings will be directly used to provide payouts until age 90. The remaining 10-20% will be deducted as your CPF LIFE premium when you join CPF LIFE and used to provide payouts from age 90 for the rest of your life. As less is used for your CPF LIFE premium, the monthly payout will be lower compared to the Standard Plan. The Basic plan payouts will also decrease correspondingly as your balances are withdrawn over time to provide you with monthly payouts and earn less extra interest*.
* The extra interest is earned on the first $60,000 of your CPF balances and is used to increase your payouts.

questions.title: What happens to my saved details from the previous version of the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text: Your saved details from the previous Retirement Payout Planner are automatically carried over to the enhanced planner, so you do not need to re-enter your information. You can go directly into any feature and continue your retirement planning from where you left off.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What happens to my unused CPF transfers and cash top-ups to my recipient upon his demise or if he closes his CPF account upon leaving Singapore?
questions.text: Cash top-ups and CPF transfers will generally be treated as gifts to the recipient. Any unused cash top-ups or CPF transfers will be paid to the recipient's beneficiaries upon his demise, or to the recipient himself if he closes his CPF account and withdraws his CPF savings upon leaving Singapore. This is subject to safeguards to prevent premature withdrawals.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What if my banking app is unable to scan the PayNow QR for my top-up application?
questions.text: If you are having trouble scanning the PayNow QR code for your top-up application, you should reach out to your bank for assistance.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is my payout eligibility age?
questions.text:
Your payout eligibility age is the age where you can start receiving your retirement monthly payouts.
If you were born in 1954 or later, your payout eligibility age is 65. This means that you can start receiving your monthly payouts any time between the ages of 65 and 70.
If you were born before 1954, the table below shows your payout eligibility age.
Year of birth
Payout eligibility age
Before 1944
60
1944 to 1949
62
1950 and 1951
63
1952 and 1953
64
Please note that your payout eligibility age is not linked to your retirement or re-employment age. You can still receive payouts from your payout eligibility age even if the retirement age or re-employment age is raised.

questions.title: What is Silver Housing Bonus?
questions.text:
The Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) enables you to supplement your retirement income if you're moving to a 3-room or smaller flat.
By committing your housing refunds towards your retirement payouts, you can enjoy lifelong income through CPF LIFE and receive a cash bonus of up to $40,000.
Find out more about SHB.
You may also use HDB’s Enquire Housing Monetisation Options e-Service to check your eligible Housing Monetisation options.

questions.title: What is the “Your Options” feature in the Retirement Payout Planner and how does it work?
questions.text:
The new “Your Options” feature in the Retirement Payout Planner suggests options on the actions you can consider (e.g. top-ups to your CPF retirement savings), personalised based on your projected payouts and retirement payout goal. You can access this feature once you have completed both “Your Projection” and “Your Goal”.
As with any financial decision, do consider your personal financial situation before committing to any action. The suggestions are meant to serve as a guide for your consideration, and you are not obligated to act on them.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What is the amount I can withdraw from my retirement savings when I have an alternative lifelong income, such as pension or annuity?
questions.text:
The amount you can withdraw from your retirement savings when you have alternative lifelong income, such as a pension or annuity is subject to the Board’s approval and depends on the following factors:
Total guaranteed lifelong monthly payout:
The total guaranteed monthly payout amount may include multiple pension/annuities.
Instruments such as endowments, whole life policies and bonds are not considered as sources of lifelong income.
Comparison to CPF LIFE Standard Plan Payout computed based on your Full Retirement Sum:
If your total guaranteed lifelong monthly payout equals or exceeds the monthly payouts under CPF LIFE Standard Plan, you may withdraw all your CPF retirement savings*.
If your total guaranteed lifelong monthly payout is less than the monthly payouts under the CPF LIFE Standard Plan, you may withdraw your CPF retirement savings* partially.
*Withdrawable amount excludes any cash top-ups, CPF transfers to the Retirement Account (RA) and government grants.

questions.title: What is the change to the Enhanced Retirement Sum in 2026?
questions.text:
The Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) was raised on 1 January 2026 to double the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS). This provides CPF members aged 55 and above the option to voluntarily top up more to their Retirement Account (RA) for even higher monthly payouts in retirement.
You can top up your RA with cash or your Ordinary Account (OA) savings. Topping up your RA allows you to receive higher monthly payouts in retirement. This allows members to get higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts through CPF top-ups.
For example, a member who is 55 in the current year could receive up to $3,400 monthly for life when they turn 65. Learn more about the payouts you can receive.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is the fastest way to make a cash top-up?
questions.text: The fastest way to make a cash top-up would be via PayNow QR or OCBC Digital (for applications via CPF Mobile app or online form). Your cash top-up will generally be credited almost instantly upon successful payment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is the GIRO bank account used for my recurring cash top-up arrangement?
questions.text: If you have an existing GIRO arrangement, you can view your current bank account used for your GIRO by accessing Set up GIRO for cash top-ups for retirement form, under “Select bank”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is the Lease Buyback Scheme?
questions.text:
The Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) enables you to supplement your retirement income by selling part of your HDB flat’s lease while you continue to live in it.
By participating in the LBS, the proceeds from selling part of your flat's lease will be used to top up your Retirement Account to boost your lifelong monthly payouts under CPF LIFE. You can also enjoy a cash bonus of up to $30,000.
Find out more about the LBS.
You may also use HDB’s Enquire Housing Monetisation Options e-Service to check your eligible Housing Monetisation options.

questions.title: What is the Monthly Payout Estimator?
questions.text:
The Monthly Payout Estimator is an online tool designed to help CPF members aged 55 to 79 plan their monthly payouts. It allows you to estimate your monthly payouts based on your Retirement Account balances and desired retirement lifestyle.
Key Features:
Estimate Monthly Payouts:
Calculate your monthly payouts based on your current Retirement Account balance.
Choose from different CPF LIFE plans to see how they impact your payouts.
Simulate Deferred Payouts:
Explore how different payout start ages could impact your monthly payouts.
Top-Up Calculator:
Simulate the amount you need to top up to achieve your desired monthly payout.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What is the personal income tax relief cap and why is there a cap on this relief for cash top-ups made?
questions.text:
The personal income tax relief cap sets a limit on the total amount of tax relief you can claim.
Even though each relief serves a good purpose, some individuals may end up with a significantly reduced taxable income when multiple reliefs are combined. Therefore, tax relief on cash top-ups is also subjected to the personal income tax relief cap.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is the Plan my monthly payouts service?
questions.text:
The Plan my monthly payouts service is an online service for CPF members reaching age 65 (Payout Eligibility Age) and above to apply to start their monthly payouts and customise their monthly payouts to suit their desired retirement lifestyle. This online application allows you to submit your instructions, view your estimated payouts and find out how your choices will affect your payouts.
Key Features:
1. Choose to start your monthly payouts anytime between 65 and 70:
Explore how different payout start ages impact your monthly payouts.
2. Choose your CPF LIFE plan and receive payouts for life:
Visualise how different CPF LIFE plan impact your payouts.
3. Option to increase your monthly payouts:
Discover how much more you can receive monthly if you use your withdrawable savings to increase your payouts.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What is the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
The Retirement Payout Planner is a digital tool that helps you plan for your retirement in three ways:
Set your retirement payout goal
Project your retirement savings and payouts, and
Explore how different actions could bring you closer to your goal.

questions.title: What is the sequence of disbursement for Special Needs Saving Scheme's monthly payout from CPF account? (i.e. which of the deceased's CPF account will be disbursed first?)
questions.text: The CPF savings nominated under Special Needs Savings Scheme will be paid via monthly payouts, starting from the lowest interest earning account, i.e. the Nominee Ordinary Account (NOA) first before moving to Nominee Special Account (NSA) and then Nominee Retirement Account (NRA).

questions.title: What will cause my CPF LIFE monthly payouts to be adjusted and when will payout adjustments be effected?
questions.text:
We want to ensure that your CPF LIFE monthly payouts are sustainable over the long term. As such, our actuarial consultant reviews them yearly and take into account the following:
Deviations in mortality experience. If more people live longer than expected in the long term, the monthly payouts might be lower, and vice versa.
Deviations in interest rates. If interest rates are higher than expected, the monthly payouts might be higher, and vice versa.
The revised payout, if any, will take effect every July of the year. We will notify you if there is an adjustment in your monthly payouts. Rest assured that any changes are expected to be small and gradual.

questions.title: What will happen if I do not instruct CPF Board to start my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
If you do not provide instructions to the CPF Board using the "Plan my monthly payouts" service, your monthly payouts will start automatically when you reach age 70. These payouts will be paid to the registered bank account provided in your Account settings.
Find out more on what happens to your CPF savings when your monthly payout starts.

questions.title: What's new in the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
The Retirement Payout Planner has been enhanced with three new features to help you plan your retirement more easily:

Make progress in minutes

Get personalised suggestions
Not sure how to reach your retirement goal? The new "Your Options" feature shows you personalised actions to help you get there.

questions.title: When can I apply to start my monthly payouts?
questions.text: You can submit your instructions to start your monthly payouts anytime from three months before the month you turn 65, up to age 70. We will notify you three months before you turn 65 to guide you in exploring the options for your monthly payouts.

questions.title: When can I apply to withdraw my retirement savings if I have a pension/annuity?
questions.text:
You can apply for withdrawal of your CPF retirement savings if you have a pension/annuity, as long as you are:
i. 55 or above; and
ii. currently receiving lifelong monthly payouts from your pension/annuity.

questions.title: When can I start receiving my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
You can choose to start receiving your CPF LIFE payouts anytime between the ages of 65 and 70 using our Plan my monthly payouts service. Consider starting later as your monthly payout will increase by up to 7% for each year that you defer starting.
CPF Board will send you a notification three months before your 65th birthday to explain your options and guide you in choosing your CPF LIFE plan. Your payouts will automatically start when you turn 70 if you have not instructed CPF Board regarding your payouts by then.

questions.title: When does my recurring CPF transfer take place?
questions.text:
The transfer from your Ordinary Account (OA) to Retirement Account (RA) takes place on the 18th of each month.
If you set up a new recurring CPF transfer, the transfer will take effect from the following month upon successful application.
Note: Please ensure that you maintain sufficient funds in your OA for the transfer. The recurring CPF transfer arrangement will be stopped if there are two consecutive unsuccessful transfers. There is no penalty for unsuccessful transfers.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When is the deduction date of my recurring cash top-up arrangements?
questions.text:
The deduction from your bank account takes place on the 15th of the month (or the next working day if 15th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday).
If you set up a new GIRO to make recurring cash top-ups:
GIRO deduction for your recurring cash top-up will take effect from the following month upon successful application of your recurring top-ups.
If you have an existing GIRO arrangement and have updated your GIRO bank account for recurring cash top-ups:
Deductions from your GIRO bank account for your recurring cash top-up(s) will take effect from the current month if you have updated your bank account before the 8th of the month. Otherwise, the deductions will be made from your new bank account from the following month.
Note: Please ensure that you maintain sufficient funds in your bank account for GIRO deductions. Some banks may charge an administrative fee for each unsuccessful deduction.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When should I submit my application for my top-up to be processed within the same month?
questions.text:
One-time cash top-up
Both your application and payment should be made by the following timings:
Payment mode
When payment should be made
PayNow QR
Within last day of the month
OCBC Digital (available for applications via CPF Mobile app only)
One-time CPF transfer
In general, online transfers from Ordinary Account to Special Account/Retirement Account are processed within the same day. However, a longer processing time may be required for certain transfers, such as first-time transfers to loved ones, as checks to verify relationships will need to be conducted. The processing time for such scenarios is generally five working days upon receipt of application. We encourage submitting your application before the 5th last working day of the month.
Recurring cash top-up and CPF transfer
The deduction or transfer will start from the following month after your recurring arrangement is successfully processed.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When should I submit my top-up application if I want to be eligible for tax relief in the next assessment year?
questions.text:
Your online top-up application and payment will need to reach us by 31 December of the year.
It is important to note that the tax relief is granted based on the calendar year in which the top-up is made, regardless of the actual date of submission.
We would also encourage you to top up earlier in the year. Find out why you should top up as early as possible.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When will I receive my monthly payouts?
questions.text: The monthly payouts of all members are deducted on the 2nd of the month, and the crediting of the monthly payouts to members’ bank accounts will depend on the bank's processing time. You will receive the monthly payouts in your bank account generally by the 4th working day of the month. You will generally receive your payouts earlier if your bank supports Fast And Secure Transfer (FAST).

questions.title: When will the top-ups received in my CPF Special/Retirement Account start to earn interest?
questions.text:
If you receive a cash top-up this month, it will start earning interest in the next month.
For CPF transfers of your existing CPF savings from your account to yourself or your loved ones, the transferred savings will start earning interest in the receiving account from the month of transfer. However, if the transferred savings are fresh injections (e.g. working contributions credited in the current month), it will start earning interest in the receiving account from the next month.
Illustration: $1000 is transferred in January from Ordinary Account (OA) to Special or Retirement Account (SA/RA) of the recipient (self or loved ones).
(A) If the $1,000 is existing OA savings (e.g. giver did not have new working contributions in January), it will start earning SA/RA interest in the recipient's SA/RA from January.
(B) If the $1,000 is January working contributions from OA savings, it will start earning SA/RA interest in the recipient's SA/RA from February.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Where can I find more information on what happens to my CPF accounts when I turn 55 and the available options I have in planning for my retirement?
questions.text:
You can log in to the Retirement Payout Planner to view your personalised retirement details before turning 55. This information is available from six months before your 55th birthday up to the day before you turn 55.
You will receive a notification from CPF Board around three months before your 55th birthday, providing you with information about the CPF rules that will affect you when you turn 55. It will include details on how to make an appointment to attend the CPF Retirement Planning Service, a one-to-one session at our CPF service centres where our Customer Service Executives will walk you through the CPF rules and options available to you when you turn 55.
You can also watch our webinars to learn more about planning for your retirement.

questions.title: Who can use the Monthly Payout Estimator?
questions.text:
The Monthly Payout Estimator is primarily designed for CPF members aged 55 to 79. However, you can also adjust the details and use it to simulate payouts for your family members or loved ones.
How It Works:
For Yourself: If you are aged 55 to 79, you can log in using your Singpass and estimate your monthly payouts based on your Retirement Account balance.
For Others: You can simulate payouts for your family members or loved ones by:
logging in with your Singpass.
updating the birth year in the tool to match the person you are helping.
entering their Retirement Account balance or the amount you wish to simulate.
If you are below age 55, you can use the Retirement Payout Planner to set your retirement payout goal, project your payouts, and explore personalised actions to help you reach your goal.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Who can use the Plan my monthly payouts service?
questions.text:
You can use the Plan my monthly payouts service if you are turning 65 within the next three months, or if you are currently 65 years old or older. It allows you to customise your monthly payouts to suit your desired retirement lifestyle.
If you are younger, you can use the Retirement Payout Planner to set your retirement payout goal, project your payouts, and explore personalised actions to help you reach your goal.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Who can use the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text: The Retirement Payout Planner is available for members from age 16, up to 4 months before 65. Members who are reaching or have reached 65 can use the Plan my monthly payouts service to make key decisions related to their payouts.
